authors: Robinson P, Yokote M, Bar-On O.
ai_summary: A global survey of 120 clinicians across 90 centers found that while imaging practices for Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia vary, chest X-ray is most common in young children at diagnosis and during exacerbations, whereas CT is preferred for older patients and routine assessments, highlighting opportunities for standardized guidelines.

title: Preclinical human models of primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Ong JWY, Jackson CL, Arbi M, Hart SL, Mill P, Paff T, Rubbo B, Shahaj E, Shoemark A, Lucas JS.
journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
ai_summary: This review examines human preclinical models for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), including air-liquid interface cultures, organoids, and lung-on-a-chip platforms, which are needed to evaluate emerging genetic therapies. The authors highlight the use of patient-derived and CRISPR-edited models for multiple PCD genes and emphasize the need for field-wide standardization to accelerate translation to clinical treatments.

Disease: Joubert Syndrome or non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa

title: Utilising human cellular models of primary ciliary dyskinesia: a scoping review.
authors: Ong JWY, Tsang W, Lucas JS, Jackson CL, Rubbo B.
journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
ai_summary: This scoping review identifies and describes knowledge gaps in the use of human cellular models for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD). The authors found that while various models exist (e.g., air-liquid interface cultures, organoids), there is a lack of standardized protocols and inconsistent reporting of outcome measures like ciliary function, which limits reproducibility and comparability of findings. They conclude that consensus on minimum characterization requirements is needed to advance therapeutic and exposure research.

title: Respiratory bacterial epidemiology at three primary ciliary dyskinesia clinical centers.
authors: Ziminski A, Zimbric M, McCaffery H, Freij J, Machogu E, Thompson M, Horani A, Wehmeijer L, Caverly LJ, Saba TG.
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
ai_summary: This study found that enhanced infection prevention and control (IPC) protocols, which reduce Pseudomonas aeruginosa in cystic fibrosis, did not significantly affect P. aeruginosa prevalence in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) patients across three pediatric centers. P. aeruginosa prevalence was 37-47% and did not differ significantly between centers with standard precautions, clinic cohorting, or enhanced IPC. The findings suggest that CF-based IPC strategies may not similarly influence bacterial epidemiology in PCD.

title: Pulmonary Exacerbations and Treatment in PCD: A Narrative Review.
authors: Anagnostopoulou P, Thee S, Kouis P, Yiallouros P.
ai_summary: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder causing chronic lung disease, and this narrative review summarizes current knowledge on pulmonary exacerbations (PEx) in PCD, including definitions, frequency, pathophysiology (focusing on common microorganisms and sputum inflammatory markers), risk factors (female sex, age, Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection), and the prognostic value of lung clearance index. The review highlights the need for more research on PEx mechanisms, treatment, and long-term outcomes.

ai_summary:
This abstract describes a new diagnostic tool (LMBA) for measuring kidney biomarkers NGAL and CysC, but it does not establish a link between a specific gene and a disease. The application to a mouse model of polycystic kidney disease is mentioned only as a validation step, without naming a specific gene.

The authors developed a rapid, self-contained microfluidic device (LMBA) that can quantify the early-stage kidney biomarkers NGAL and cystatin C from a small blood or urine sample in 20 minutes. The platform was validated against standard ELISA and successfully detected elevated biomarker levels in a neonatal mouse model of polycystic kidney disease, suggesting its potential for both preclinical research and future point-of-care diagnostics.

journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

title: CYSTSCAN-PKD: a comprehensive pipeline for automatic cyst segmentation and counting on µCT scans from PKD animal models.
authors: Mangili A, Arrigoni A, Sangalli F, Fest-Santini S, Corna D, Cerullo D, Xinaris C, Tomasoni S, Santini M, Remuzzi A, Caroli A.
ai_summary: This paper describes CYSTSCAN-PKD, an automated pipeline for segmenting kidneys and cysts and counting cysts on µCT scans from rat models of polycystic kidney disease (PKD). The pipeline uses a 3D U-Net ensemble for segmentation and a morphological algorithm for cyst counting, achieving high accuracy and reproducibility while drastically reducing processing time compared to manual methods. The tool is designed to support preclinical research on autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).

title: A C. elegans model for functional analysis of conserved ADPKD variants in cilia, extracellular vesicles, and sensory signaling.
authors: Wang J, Nava Cruz C, Walsh JD, desRanleau E, Nikonorova IA, Barr MM.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD2
Finding: The C. elegans ortholog of the human PC2C331S variant (PKD-2C180S) reduces protein levels, abolishes ciliary and extracellular vesicle localization, and eliminates sensory function, acting as a recessive null allele that also disrupts PC1 homolog LOV-1 trafficking.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Halting cyst progression in ADPKD using long-term ketogenic metabolic therapy and supplementation with exogenous ketones and alkaline citrate-a case series.
authors: Messing M, Muensterman E, Marcon S, Weimbs T.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Long-term ketogenic metabolic therapy, including carbohydrate restriction, intermittent fasting, and supplementation with exogenous ketones and alkaline citrate, stabilized or reduced total kidney volume and preserved kidney function in four individuals with truncating PKD1 variants.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: ComicGTN infers disease-associated rare cell states from single-cell multiomic data using DNA sequence-augmented graph transformer networks.
authors: Yang B, Hua J, Zhou G, Feng Y, Qi J, Guo Y, Sheng D, Jin S.
ai_summary: ComicGTN is a computational framework that uses graph transformer networks to integrate single-cell multiomic data with DNA sequence information, enabling accurate detection of rare cell states. It outperforms existing methods and identifies disease-relevant rare cell populations in mouse breast cancer, epilepsy patient cortex, and polycystic kidney disease organoids, including a rare glomerular subgroup with pathological pathways.

title: Mechanosensing in the Renal Tubule: Ion Channels, Ca 2+ Signaling, and the Integration of Mechanical Cues along the Nephron.
authors: Scorza SI, De Zio R, Certini M, Svelto M, Moccia F, Procino G, Gerbino A.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2  
Finding: Mutations in polycystins disrupt ciliary Ca2+ homeostasis, linking mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling dysfunction to autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.  
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

title: Multi-Modal, Machine Learning-Driven Framework Integrating Multi-Omics for Personalized Chronic Kidney Disease Management.
authors: Rutka B, Danieluk A, Wiewiórska-Krata N, Mucha K.
ai_summary: This review discusses the use of multi-omics profiling (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics) and machine learning to enable personalized management of chronic kidney disease (CKD), moving from traditional to precision medicine approaches for early detection, patient stratification, and treatment planning.

title: Serum activin A and bone metabolism in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
authors: Nakagawa Y, Takahashi H, Takahashi Y, Hyodo T, Hida M, Suga T, Kakuta T, Tomita Y, Nakamura M, Komaba H.
journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
ai_summary:
Gene: <no specific gene established>

Finding: In hemodialysis patients, higher serum activin A levels are associated with increased bone turnover markers (TRACP5b and BALP) independently of parathyroid hormone, but not with bone mineral density or fracture risk.

Disease: Kidney failure with high bone turnover

title: Multi-scale computational models of intervillous blood flow in fetal growth restriction: implications of anatomical changes on syncytiotrophoblast shear stress.
authors: Lee TC, Gamage TKJB, Spring M, Ramanlal I, Jackson T, Clark AR, James JL.
ai_summary:
Gene: DYNC1H1, KIF3A, TRPV6, IFT88, PKD2, PIEZO1  
Finding: In fetal growth restriction, impaired spiral artery remodeling and villous tissue changes increase syncytiotrophoblast shear stress, with altered expression of mechanosensing proteins (higher Dynein-1, lower Kinesin-2 and TRPV6, but no change in IFT88, Polycystin-2, or Piezo-1).  
Disease: Fetal growth restriction (FGR)

title: Procyanidin C1 modulates microglia cellular iron homeostasis via targeting HuR/ACSL4 pathway and alleviates high-glucose-induced ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy.
authors: Liu Q, Wang SM, Jiao T, Gao XM, Xie CQ, Hu XR, Liu Q, Yang JT, Zhang L.
ai_summary:
Gene: HuR (ELAVL1), ACSL4  
Finding: Procyanidin C1 alleviates high-glucose-induced ferroptosis in diabetic retinopathy by targeting the HuR/ACSL4 pathway, where HuR stabilizes Acsl4 mRNA to promote ferroptosis.  
Disease: Diabetic retinopathy

title: PRKAR1A-related acrodysostosis with partial growth hormone deficiency: 18-month response to recombinant human growth hormone.
authors: Katsoudas S, Kokkinou A, Nikolopoulou A, Tsitsekli E, Polychroni I, Zosi P.
ai_summary:
Gene: PRKAR1A  
Finding: Recombinant human growth hormone therapy for 18 months in a child with PRKAR1A-related acrodysostosis and partial growth hormone deficiency improved height SDS from -2.92 to -1.52 with a first-year growth velocity of 11 cm/year and no adverse effects.  
Disease: PRKAR1A-related acrodysostosis with partial growth hormone deficiency

title: Integrative screening of plant volatiles through transient receptor potential channel docking, olfactometry, and field validation in Bemisia tabaci.
authors: Paschapur AU, Pandey D, Singh L, Marella SM, Nebapure SM, Subramanian S.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1 (TRPP-PKD1)

Finding: Docking of 51 plant volatiles against TRPP-PKD1 and other TRP channels identified binding energies from -3.2 to -7.6 kcal/mol, with TRPM and TRPA1 showing the most stable interactions; RNAi knockdown of TRPA1 and TRPM reduced behavioral attraction to volatiles from ~0.58-0.65 to ~0.02-0.19, and field trials with thymol, β-caryophyllene, and cuminaldehyde achieved 2.1-3.2× higher catches than controls.

Disease: Bemisia tabaci (whitefly) pest infestation

title: Distribution and Evolutionary Implications of Flagellum-Associated Gene Families in Representative Algal Genomes.
authors: Jia L, Hou Y, Zhang M, Li L, Zhang Y, Wang J, Yuan Z, Fan G, Shi C, Zhao H.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS9, WDR35
Finding: BBS9 and WDR35 show lineage-specific expansion in dinoflagellates, with WDR35 enriched 3.6-5.8-fold and BBS9 identified as a candidate acquired via horizontal gene transfer.
Disease: Not applicable (evolutionary study in algae)

title: Modulation of Cilia Motility by Vortex-Ultrasound-Induced Shear Stress.
authors: Phan TN, Wang HC, Fan CH, Huang CH, Fang Y, Luo Y, Ma Z, Lin IH, Wang WJ, Lin YC, Yeh CK.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: Vortex ultrasound generates localized shear stress that induces cilia deflections up to 80°, triggering calcium influx via TRPV4 and TRPP2 channels and directly activating primary ciliary mechanotransduction.
Disease: Cilia-associated signaling pathways (general ciliopathy context)

title: Centriole Duplication, Maturation, and Transformation During Mammalian Spermatogenesis.
authors: Ishida M, Shibuya H.
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology
ai_summary: This review summarizes the specialized roles and molecular mechanisms of centrioles during mammalian spermatogenesis, including their duplication, maturation, and transformation in spermatogonia, spermatocytes, and spermatids, as well as their function in the first zygotic division.

title: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome
authors: Patri JR, Chamarthi VS.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS (multiple genes)
Finding: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding proteins essential for primary nonmotile cilia cause Bardet-Biedl syndrome, a multisystem ciliopathy with six cardinal features including rod-cone retinal dystrophy, obesity, polydactyly, renal anomalies, hypogonadism, and neurodevelopmental impairment; diagnostic criteria have been refined in 2024 and 2026, and setmelanotide was FDA-approved as the first targeted therapy.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: Estimation of the genetic susceptibility prevalence of primary ciliary dyskinesia via the gnomAD v4.1.0 database.
authors: Dai R, Dao Y, Zhang X, Ma Y, Zhu X, Gao Y, Wu J, Sun L.
ai_summary:
Gene: multiple PCD-associated genes (31 genes with "Definitive" or "Strong" associations)

Finding: Using gnomAD v4.1.0 data from 807,162 individuals, the estimated global genetic susceptibility prevalence of primary ciliary dyskinesia is approximately 1 in 20,103, with an overall carrier frequency of about 1 in 25, showing significant ethnic heterogeneity and a lower prevalence than previous estimates.

Disease: primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Clinical and Genetic Study of a Pseudo-Dominant Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia Pedigree: The First DNAAF1-Associated Family Reported in Chinese Population.
authors: Guo Z, Li P, Jiang G, Chen W.
ai_summary:
Gene: DNAAF1
Finding: Two loss-of-function variants (c.1930A>T and c.1022_1023del) co-segregate with primary ciliary dyskinesia in a pseudo-dominant inheritance pattern, causing absent outer and inner dynein arms, immotile cilia, and variable laterality defects and pulmonary involvement.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: Insights from a Portuguese tertiary centre cohort.
authors: Teixeira-Oliveira S, Pais-Cunha I, Lopes SS, Seixas S, Ferraz C, Amorim A, Azevedo I.
ai_summary:
Gene: DNAH5, DNAH11  
Finding: In a Portuguese tertiary centre cohort, DNAH5 (31.3%) and DNAH11 (12.5%) were the most frequent mutations, and earlier diagnosis (median age 7 years in children vs 38.5 years in adults) was associated with better pulmonary function and less extensive bronchiectasis.  
Disease: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia

title: Biallelic RSPH4A loss-of-function variants cause primary ciliary dyskinesia in a Chinese patient.
authors: Lu YT, Tang HY, Chen K, Lai DY, Wang DC, Yang F.
ai_summary:
Gene: RSPH4A  
Finding: Compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants (c.2T>C and c.854delA) impair RSPH4A protein expression via distinct mechanisms (translation initiation failure and nonsense-mediated decay), causing defective motile cilia function.  
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Atypical Kartagener syndrome in a 40-year-old woman: Computed Tomography findings of situs inversus with bronchiectasis and infertility.
authors: Zewdie YG, Tabor BB, Yesuf EF, Genetirune HY.
ai_summary:
Gene: <not specified>
Finding: A 40-year-old woman with recurrent respiratory infections, primary infertility, and computed tomography findings of situs inversus and bronchiectasis but no sinusitis represents an atypical presentation of Kartagener syndrome.
Disease: Atypical Kartagener syndrome (primary ciliary dyskinesia)

title: A Personal Health App and Wearable Co-Design Framework for Rare and Complex Diseases: User-Centered, Collaborative Co-Design Study.
authors: Goodday SM, Karlin E, Sorensen M, Yang R, Gordon P, Opoku C, Vuong D, Wilson J, McKenzie D, Piccotti J, Tavanti M, Fitzgerald M, Re'em Y, Wei H, Golden M, Morgan D, Manion M, Mosquera R, Shivas T, Hoover E, Peck A, Peck N, Yavarow Z, Bjornson-Pennell H, Stratton A, Anova Sahoo S, Arbittier D, Arbittier E, Goff R, Harvin-Graham D, Howard N, Knudsen C, Oldham M, Friend S.
ai_summary: A co-design framework involving patients, clinicians, and developers was used to create five prototype personal health apps for rare/complex diseases including primary ciliary dyskinesia. The apps tracked subjective symptoms and objective health measures, and a beta test with 239 participants showed high enrollment and retention, with feedback emphasizing customization.

title: The orchestration of ciliary opus: Interplay of signalling molecules, GTPases, and trafficking machinery.
authors: Piyush R, Giri P, Shinde SR.
ai_summary: This review discusses how IFT machinery, the BBSome, small GTPases, and secondary messengers like cAMP and Ca2+ cooperate to regulate ciliary composition and signalling, including hedgehog and insulin pathways. A mechanistic understanding of these integrated systems is presented as a framework for elucidating ciliopathy pathogenesis and identifying therapeutic targets.

title: Basal body docking failure triggers centriole clustering and elimination in mammalian spermatogenesis.
authors: Chen JJ, Gong X, Mak M, Li FQ, Takemaru KI.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP164
Finding: Loss of CEP164 causes basal body docking failure, leading to absence of zygotene cilia and sperm flagella, centriole clustering, and centriole elimination via residual bodies, resulting in male infertility.
Disease: Male infertility (ciliopathy-related)

title: Human Organoids as Drug Development Tools for Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Fu H, Freedman BS.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2
Finding: Human kidney organoids derived from PKD1-/- or PKD2-/- pluripotent stem cells recapitulate PKD-specific cystogenesis in vitro, revealing cell-intrinsic mechanisms and enabling therapeutic strategy development.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: Variants and variability - a cohort of Omani children sheds more light on autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Burgmaier K, Liebau MC.

title: Corrigendum to "Real-World Outcomes of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Therapy in Nondiabetic Autosomal-Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Effects on Progression to Dialysis in a TrinetX Cohort".
journal: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes
ai_summary: This is a corrigendum correcting a previously published article. It does not present new findings linking a specific gene to a disease or phenotype. The original study examined real-world outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy in nondiabetic autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), but this notice only corrects errors in that prior publication.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Octreotide, Lanreotide, and Pasireotide in ADPKD and PLD: A Network Meta-analysis with Real-world Evidence from the FAERS Database.
authors: Mei Z, Chen J, Fan J, Fan Z, Xi M, He Q.
ai_summary: This network meta-analysis compared three somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide, and pasireotide) for treating autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) or polycystic liver disease (PLD). Octreotide and pasireotide reduced kidney and liver volumes within 1 year, while lanreotide showed effects only after more than 2 years. Cholelithiasis was the most common side effect, with younger age and pasireotide use being independent risk factors.

title: Metabolomics in renal cystic disease: links to mechanisms and identification of pathways for potential pre-diagnosis.
authors: Chen L, Broadhurst D, Shafaei A, Phillips JK, Tang S, Abbiss H.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Metabolomics reveals that arginine biosynthesis; alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism; glycine, serine and threonine metabolism; and the citrate cycle are top-ranked pathways in renal cystic disease, with glycine, serine and threonine metabolism specifically linked to ADPKD/Pkd1 mouse models, indicating a shift from carbohydrate to amino acid metabolism.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: Whole exome sequencing identified a novel compound heterozygous mutation of nephrocystin 4 in a child with nephronophthisis-a rare case report.
authors: Li W, Cao GH, Li NN, Long JY, Tang YQ, Liu JS, Fan LL.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHP4
Finding: A novel compound heterozygous mutation (c.2611C>T/p.R871X and c.2768G>A/p.R923H) in NPHP4 was identified in a Chinese patient with nephronophthisis and proteinuria.
Disease: Nephronophthisis

title: Considerations on BMI Stratification in ADPKD Body-Composition Research.
authors: Hu X, Long L.
journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

title: A proposed classification for standardized reporting of liver disease in children with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Kurkal K, Gupte GL.

title: Impact of race-based and race-free CKD-EPI equations on estimated glomerular filtration rate in a multicenter retrospective cohort of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Oto ÖA, Yildiz A, Koçyiğit İ, Yazici H, Güllülü Boz SE, Kurtuluş Y, Demiray A, Doksan M, Suleymanova V, Ük E, Akin A, Bastani B, Edwards JC, Lentine KL, Çalişkan YK.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2 (implied by ADPKD diagnosis)
Finding: The 2021 race-free CKD-EPI equation significantly alters eGFR estimation and CKD staging compared to the 2009 race-based equation, increasing eGFR in Caucasian patients and decreasing it in African-American patients with ADPKD.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Kidney organoids as models for hereditary kidney diseases: Toward precision medicine (Review).
authors: Cui S, Chen T, Zou Y, Li M, Zhou H, Jiang J, Yang M.
ai_summary: Kidney organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells are valuable tools for modeling hereditary kidney diseases, including polycystic kidney disease, and for testing potential therapeutics, though challenges remain in achieving complex disease modeling and transplantable organs.

title: Cefepime-Induced Delirium in a Patient With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Case Report.
authors: Gomes H, Pires M, Freitas C, Freitas RM.
ai_summary: A 63-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease due to autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease developed delirium (temporal disorientation and visual hallucinations) within 24-48 hours of starting cefepime for a urinary tract infection; symptoms resolved within 24 hours of stopping the drug, consistent with cefepime-induced neurotoxicity.

title: Prognostic Systematic Reviews: Challenges and Insights-An Example.
authors: Khawandi J, Rayner DG, Rao V, Grimaji N, Azzam M, Hamarsha Q, Kawtharany H, Choaib A, Yu ASL, Perrone RD, Foroutan F, Mustafa RA.
ai_summary: This article discusses the challenges of conducting systematic reviews of prognostic factors, using a review of biomarkers for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) as an example. The main difficulties included variability in data reporting, which complicated analysis and interpretation, and the large number of studies that contained relevant data but were not primarily prognostic studies, making screening and extraction challenging. The authors provide insights and tips to help researchers conducting similar reviews in the future.

title: Pregnancy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Maternal and Fetal Considerations: A Narrative Review.
authors: Sarmadian PJ, Pirooz AD, Al Baghdadi M, Kamgar M, Afshar Y, Nobakht N.
ai_summary: Pregnant individuals with ADPKD face increased risks of hypertension, preeclampsia, and preterm delivery. Strict blood pressure targets and medications like ACE inhibitors or tolvaptan are contraindicated; pregnancy-appropriate monitoring and multidisciplinary care are essential.

title: Diagnosing Mendelian Kidney Disease: Hidden Niches in the (Kidney) Genome.
authors: Ekici AB, Knaup KX, Schaeffer C, Schneider K, Wopperer FJ, Wiesener A, Dieterle A, Buchholz B, Schiffer M, Saake M, Vasko R, Wons A, Schuhmann S, Vasileiou G, Reis A, Rampoldi L, Pasutto F, Wiesener MS.
journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: A pathogenic PKD1 variant (c.2180T>C, p.(Leu727Pro)) causing autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease was missed by exome sequencing but identified by long-range amplification and whole genome sequencing.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Analysis of host factors for internal ribosomal entry site-mediated translation of foot and mouth disease virus and classical swine fever virus: an in vivo evaluation in single- and double-knockout mice.
authors: Utsunomiya M, Momohara K, Sato R, Nagatomo S, Hifumi T, Sakoda Y, Tsukiyama-Kohara K.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1L3, USP31
Finding: Deletion of Pkd1l3 and/or Usp31 in knockout mice suppresses IRES-mediated translation of FMDV and EMCV, reduces CSFV replicon replication, and attenuates viral pathology and titers upon EMCV infection.
Disease: Foot-and-mouth disease, classical swine fever

title: Phenotypic spectrum and molecular characteristics of variants of uncertain significance in copy number variations associated with fetal cardiac malformations: a case series of 9 patients.
authors: Yin J, Wang Q, Lan T, Ou H, Zhou X, Zhong L, Cao H, Zhang L, Luo Y.
ai_summary: This study examined 9 fetuses with congenital heart malformations (CHMs) who had copy number variants of uncertain significance (VUS-CNVs). VUS-CNVs were more common in fetuses with non-isolated CHMs (those with additional structural anomalies or soft markers) and tended to be larger and contain more genes in these cases. Trio analysis reclassified 3 of 7 VUS-CNVs, and all live-born infants showed no major postnatal abnormalities, highlighting the challenges of interpreting VUS-CNVs in prenatal counseling and the need for trio testing and follow-up.

title: Case Report: ROSAH syndrome presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.
authors: Shunyakova J, Reynolds M, Taylor A, Sieck EG, Walsh JT, Hassman LM.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALPK1  
Finding: A heterozygous missense mutation (c.710C>T) in ALPK1 causes ROSAH syndrome, characterized by optic disc edema, uveitis, retinal degeneration, and macular edema that may respond to local steroids and immune suppression, but retinal degeneration can progress despite treatment.  
Disease: ROSAH syndrome (retinal dystrophy, optic nerve edema, splenomegaly, anhidrosis, headache)

title: The centrosome-cilium-centriolar satellite axis in neurodegenerative diseases.
authors: Sahin U, Firat-Karalar EN.
ai_summary: This review discusses how dysfunction of the centrosome-cilium-centriolar satellite axis contributes to neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's disease. The authors outline the structure and neuronal specializations of this axis, examine its reported dysfunction in NDD models, and highlight centriolar satellites as an underexplored area in classical NDDs. They conclude that this axis provides a framework for understanding context-dependent organelle dysfunction in neurodegeneration and discuss potential therapeutic strategies.

title: A human corticospinal organoid-slice connectoid model informs enhancer strategies for post-injury axon regrowth.
authors: Gibbons GM, Fuchsberger T, Abdelgawad M, Giandomenico SL, Szebényi K, Petrova V, Wenger LMD, Olschewski DN, Chabros J, Muresan L, Feord RC, Asif M, Fawcett JW, Mierau SB, Paulsen O, Lancaster MA, Lakatos A.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified
Finding: A human corticospinal organoid-slice connectoid model was developed to study developmental axon elongation and its decline, and compounds targeting maturation-associated transcriptional shifts were shown to promote post-injury axon regrowth.
Disease: Central nervous system injury

title: Intramuscular adipose tissue: from progenitor to pathology.
authors: Jones HG, Kopinke D, Meyer GA.
journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
ai_summary: Intramuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) is an active contributor to muscle decline, not just a passive biomarker. It impairs muscle function through physical disruption and unbalanced paracrine signals, and originates from fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) that differentiate into adipocytes when the signaling balance between proadipogenic triggers and inhibitory brakes is disrupted.

title: Integrative bioinformatics and experiments identify RIBC2 as a key regulator in the esophageal cancer.
authors: Zheng X, Cui Y, Yao X, Wu Y, Ge Y, Jin Y, Gan J, Yao W, Bi Y, Sun G.
ai_summary:
Gene: RIBC2  
Finding: RIBC2 is upregulated in esophageal cancer and promotes proliferation, migration, and invasion; its high expression is linked to an immune-excluded tumor microenvironment.  
Disease: Esophageal cancer

title: Growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRH-R) and its signaling.
authors: Halmos G, Szabo Z, Dobos N, Juhasz E, Schally AV.
ai_summary: This review discusses the GHRH receptor (GHRH-R) and its signaling pathways, focusing on its splice variants (especially SV1) and their roles in various tissues. The authors summarize the potential clinical applications of GHRH analogs (agonists and antagonists) in a wide range of diseases, including oncology, endocrinology, metabolic disorders, and others, supporting their future therapeutic use.

title: Prominin-1 Regulates Retinal Pigment Epithelium Homeostasis: Transcriptomic Insights into Degenerative Mechanisms.
authors: Huo W, Yin J, Ghose P, Schafer JC, Chaum E, Bhattacharya S.
ai_summary:
Gene: Prom1
Finding: Prom1 knockout in mouse RPE cells disrupts mitophagy, phagocytosis, and junctional stability while activating stress and inflammatory pathways, indicating a role in RPE homeostasis.
Disease: Inherited retinal degenerations and atrophic age-related macular degeneration

title: Multi-omics integration of F<sub>st</sub>, GWAS, TWAS and transcriptomics revealed candidate genes and pathways associated with pneumonia lesion scores in pigs.
authors: Zhao G, Yin Y, Han J, Chen J, Li M, Han X, Ma J, Yu J, Zhou J, Chen C, Huang R, Li P, Zhao Q.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRAF3IP1
Finding: TRAF3IP1, identified by Fst and GWAS, contributes to ciliary transport, epithelial defense, and regulation of NF-κB and MAPK signaling in association with pneumonia lesion scores.
Disease: Pneumonia lesion scores (respiratory disease susceptibility) in pigs.

title: Melanocortin-4 Receptor Regulation of Endocrine Axes and Clinical Effects of Setmelanotide.
authors: Hühne T, Steidel E, Holland J, Finkelberg I, Kiewert C, Pape L, Dinkelbach L, Cetiner M.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
ai_summary:
Gene: MC4R
Finding: Setmelanotide treatment in Bardet-Biedl syndrome patients modulates multiple endocrine axes—increasing gonadotropins, testosterone/estradiol, and IGF-1, while decreasing TSH—partially independent of weight loss.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: Kidney Transplant in Joubert Syndrome: A Human-Centered Case Series From a Single Center.
authors: Abdultawab K, Badawi M, Alawaday M, Shaker M, Adel M, Balaha M, Alotaibi T, Gheith O.
journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (Joubert syndrome, ciliopathy)
Finding: Kidney transplant is feasible and generally effective in 5 patients with Joubert syndrome and end-stage kidney disease, though all experienced delayed graft function and infectious complications led to one graft loss and one death.
Disease: Joubert syndrome with end-stage kidney disease

title: Advanced MRI methods for children and young adults with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) to support future multi-center clinical trials.
authors: MacAskill CJ, Smothers JB, Kretzler ME, Heilman J, Pepin K, Kuehn B, Liu KC, Tirumani SH, Chen Y, Dell KM, Hartung EA, Serai SD, Flask CA.
ai_summary: This review highlights the potential of advanced quantitative MRI techniques as non-invasive imaging biomarkers for children and young adults with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). These methods can characterize structural and functional changes in both the kidney and liver, addressing the current lack of sensitive biomarkers needed to support multi-center clinical trials and the development of disease-modifying therapies.

title: Detection of the NPHP4 c.2999_3005del (p.Asn1000SerfsTer4) variant in an Iranian family with nephronophthisis-4.
authors: Jadidi M, Booali S, InanlooRahatloo K.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHP4
Finding: A homozygous deletion variant, c.2999_3005del (p.Asn1000SerfsTer4), was identified via whole-exome sequencing and co-segregated with the disease in an Iranian family, with protein modeling predicting significant structural changes due to C-terminal truncation.
Disease: Nephronophthisis type 4 (NPHP4)

title: Genotype and Ultrastructure Correlation in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia Among Saudi Children: A Case Series.
authors: Althakfi WA.
ai_summary:
Gene: DNAAF3, DNAAF4, RSPH9, GAS2L2, NME5
Finding: Whole exome sequencing identified variants in these genes, with transmission electron microscopy showing class 1 defects in 3 patients, class 2 in 2, and abnormalities of uncertain significance in 3, supporting genotype-ultrastructure correlation in Saudi children with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Comparing Multiple Breath Washout Parameters in a Matched Cohort of Children With Cystic Fibrosis and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Vanvuchelen L, Vermaut A, Proesmans M, Vermeulen F, Boon M.
ai_summary:
Gene: CFTR
Finding: In age- and FEV1-matched children, those with cystic fibrosis show more abnormal lung clearance index (LCI) values than those with primary ciliary dyskinesia, indicating greater peripheral airway involvement in CF.
Disease: Cystic fibrosis and primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: The primary cilium as a compartmentalized signaling hub in tissue immunity and homeostasis.
authors: Zhang A, Huo C, Song T.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: Primary cilia are signaling hubs that regulate immune receptor dynamics, inflammatory pathways such as cGAS-STING, and immune homeostasis; defects in ciliary assembly or signaling contribute to immune dysregulation, viral infections, chronic inflammation, and ciliopathy-related immune dysfunction. This review synthesizes ciliary signaling pathways in host defense and highlights gaps and future directions for mechanistic and translational research.

title: Centriolar Protein POC5 Regulates Human Adipogenesis and Cellular Senescence: Insights From a Novel Metabolic Ciliopathy.
authors: Pistorio V, Vatier C, Capel É, Beaupère C, Auclair M, Steunou V, Morichon R, Joubert M, Vigouroux C, Gautheron J, Jéru I.

ai_summary:

Disease: POC5-related metabolic ciliopathy (centrosomal metabolic disorder)

title: Clinical Utility of NGS-Based Diagnosis in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: Experience from a Brazilian Pediatric Cohort at a Reference Center for Rare Diseases.

Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Screening of a Novel Synonymous DNAH5 Variant in Histopathologically Confirmed Adenomyosis Cases from Turkiye.
authors: Guzelbag B, Aydin S, Eser Ma N, Topbas Selcuki NF, Oral E, Tuncer FN.

Finding: A novel synonymous DNAH5 variant (NM_001369.3:c.9258C>T, p.(Leu3086=)) was detected in 52.1% of histopathologically confirmed adenomyosis cases from Turkiye, but was absent from population reference databases, suggesting a potential but unconfirmed association.

title: PKD1 upstream open reading frames affect Polycystin-1 expression and polycystic kidney disease phenotypes.
authors: Li Z, Guo Z, Cho S, Bhardwaj R, Dong K, Fedeles S, Besse W.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Disruption of conserved PKD1 upstream open reading frames (uORFs) via start codon removal or antisense oligonucleotides increases Polycystin-1 (PC1) protein expression 2-4-fold and prevents kidney cyst formation in Dnajb11 and Pkd1 missense mouse models.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: β-hydroxybutyrate: A Renoprotective Hormone In Polycystic Kidney Disease.

journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (ADPKD generally)
Finding: β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), a ketone body produced during ketogenic metabolic therapy, acts as a renoprotective signaling hormone that reduces cyst proliferation, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis while enhancing mitochondrial function in polycystic kidney disease.
Disease: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)

title: Compression of the Porta Hepatis in a Patient With Hepatic Cysts Secondary to Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Case Report.
authors: Santharam Y, Ali K, Reddy AD, Ali AA, Jaikaransingh V.

Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with hepatic cyst-related biliary obstruction

title: Peritoneal Dialysis Outcomes in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Gunning S, McGill RL, Chapman AB, Garimella PS.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
ai_summary:

Finding: Peritoneal dialysis is associated with lower mortality and greater likelihood of kidney transplantation compared to hemodialysis in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with end-stage kidney disease.

journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

Finding: Reduced polycystin dosage destabilizes epithelial homeostasis, creating a self-reinforcing network of cAMP, Ca2+, and purinergic signaling that drives chloride secretion, proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, and HIF-1α-mediated transcriptional programs, all of which promote cyst growth.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Phosphate and Phosphate Transporters in Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Torres VE, Wang X, Hanna C.

title: A cross model single-cell atlas reveals conserved involvement of osteopontin in polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Miller SJ, Zhong H, Wu W, Cordova AM, Yashchenko ME, Yashchenko A, Li Z, Jafree DJ, Zimmerman CN, DeVette CI, Do V, Hignite ME, Park Y, Nusrat F, Maryam B, Lu S, Li X, Gipson JR, Li X, Long DA, Weiser-Evans MC, Yoder BK, Cowley BD, Hopp K, Stubbs JR, Ma Q, Ma A, Zimmerman KA.

title: Renal Cyst Sclerotherapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Long-Term Follow-Up and Evaluation in a Porcine Bladder Model.

Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Plasma Amino Acid Signatures Associated with Disease Progression and Hypertension in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Targeted Metabolomics and Machine Learning Approach.

title: Success of Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy with Variable-view Rigid Endoscopy for Large Polycystic Liver in a Patient with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.

title: Comparison of eGFR based on Serum Cystatin C or Creatinine in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Roth J, Vaughan L, Ghanem A, Debeh FGM, Kennedy A, Gregory AV, Kline TL, Chebib FT, Zoghby Z, Titan SM, Dahl NK.

The combined creatinine-cystatin C equation was the least biased and most precise compared to measured GFR, suggesting it may be a reasonable alternative for estimating kidney function in ADPKD.

title: Genome and transcriptome sequencing reveal pathogenic activation of a pseudoexon in PKD1 via a de novo-common variant complex allele.

title: Gene-transcription factor regulatory networks implicate primary cilia in the evolution of vertebrate sex determination and expand models of epigenetic regulation.
authors: Gessler TB, Adams DC, Valenzuela N.
ai_summary:

Disease: Sex determination and developmental plasticity (non-disease phenotype)

title: From cystogenesis to carcinogenesis in ADPKD: risk modeling and a multistep precision surveillance.
authors: Margoni A, Papavassiliou KA, Papavassiliou AG.

authors: Angeloni LL, Jorente J, Oliveira Sobrinho RP, Gil-da-Silva-Lopes VL, Vidoti-Nascimento CG, Guaragna MS, Vieira TP, Steiner CE, Brazilian Rare Genomes Project Consortium, Teixeira ACB, Coelho AVC, Quaio CRAC, Moreno CA, Perrone E, Nascimento Junior JBD, Espolaor JGA, Prota JRM, Oliveira Filho JB, Ceroni JRM, Chen K, Ferreira LT, Santana LS, Mofatto LS, Virmond LDA, Silva MFB, Migliavacca MP, Minillo RM, Yamada RY, Sitnik R, Almeida TF, Silva TYT, Cintra VP.

title: Increased Excitability of Renal Sensory Neurons by Vasopressin in Male and Female Sprague Dawley Rats.

Disease: Hypertension and polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: Prenatal Diagnosis and Perinatal Outcomes of Posterior Fossa Anomalies in a Tertiary Referral Center: A Five-Year Experience.

title: Ciliary ARL13B Is Essential for Body Weight Regulation in Mice.

Disease: Obesity (associated with hyperphagia)

title: Microtubule-Associated Proteins: From Dynamic Regulation of Microtubules to Cellular Architecture.
authors: Pais E, Schou KB.
ai_summary: Microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs) regulate microtubule dynamics, stability, and organization, governing processes such as cell division, centriole assembly, and the transition between centrosomal and ciliary states. The review highlights emerging links between MAP dysfunction and human diseases, including ciliopathies, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders, and integrates structural, proteomic, and imaging advances to propose a unifying framework for MAP function.

title: NIMA-related kinase family at the nexus of skeletal development and congenital arthrogryposis: coordinated regulation of cell cycle and ciliary dynamics.

Disease: Skeletal and joint developmental abnormalities, including congenital arthrogryposis

title: The tetraspanin disc proteins, peripherin-2 and ROM1, facilitate CNG channel localization to the rod outer segment.

Disease: Rod photoreceptor degeneration (associated with peripherin-2 knockout, Rds-/-)

Disease: Lens physiology and accommodation (lens power regulation)

title: Assessment of cardiometabolic risk using single point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) in pediatric Bardet-Biedl Syndrome: a pilot study.
authors: Kandemir T, Yildiz M, Tercan U, Demirel OB, Yanik H, Karaman V, Aslanger AD, Kardelen AD, Poyrazoglu S, Darendeliler F, Toksoy G, Bas F.

Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) with early cardiometabolic risk

title: Lipid ciliology: specialized ciliary membrane lipids in physiology and disease.
authors: Hasan A, Morita T, Hirosawa M, Kitamura N, Murakami R, Mikuni M, Kobayashi D, Itabashi T, Miyamoto T.

Disease: Ciliopathies (including polycystic kidney disease, retinal degeneration, cerebellar hypoplasia, metabolic disorders, Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, Zellweger spectrum disorders)

title: Systematic Reanalysis of Whole-Exome Sequencing in Genetically Unsolved Pediatric Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Hakçıl Öz T, Şişmanlar Eyüboğlu T, Aslan AT, Kula N, Kayhan G.

Finding: Systematic reanalysis of whole-exome sequencing data from 34 previously unsolved pediatric primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) cases identified molecular diagnoses in 3 patients (8.8%) via known PCD genes and prioritized rare variants in biologically plausible candidate genes in 8 additional cases (23.5%).
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Unsupervised home spirometry versus supervised clinic spirometry: analysis of longitudinal participant-level data from the CLEAR trial in patients with bronchiectasis.
authors: McChrystal R, McLeese RH, O'Neill B, McAuley DF, Elborn JS, Clarke M, Norrie J, Linden D, Stewart J, Jackson A, Man WD, De Soyza A, Chalmers JD, Anand R, Copeland F, Bradley JM, CLEAR Investigator Team.
ai_summary: Home spirometry in adults with bronchiectasis showed close agreement with supervised clinic spirometry (mean FEV1 difference 20 mL), with measurement variability decreasing over time. It detected lung function declines during exacerbations, though individual-level variability may limit interpretation. With support to sustain adherence, home spirometry is a viable tool for remote monitoring and decentralised trials in bronchiectasis.

title: Papillary Hyperplasia in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Multi-Institutional Study With Immunohistochemical and Molecular Characterization.

Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

Disease: Congenital hepatic fibrosis with Von Meyenburg complex and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

title: Functional vs Structural Renal Outcomes of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
authors: Naeem F, Ong SC, Daoud Butt M, Khan AH, Adnan AS, Shaukat S.
ai_summary: SGLT2 inhibitors show functional renal benefits in ADPKD—improving blood pressure, proteinuria, and metabolic measures—but their effect on structural outcomes like cyst growth remains inconsistent and unproven. Preclinical rodent models demonstrate reduced cyst load, inflammation, and fibrosis, while clinical data are limited and heterogeneous, preventing meta-analysis. Short-term safety appears reassuring, but long-term efficacy requires validation in randomized controlled trials.

title: Prognostication in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Current Tools, Clinical Gaps, and Future Directions.
authors: Min J, Zhu C, Palma L, Vena N, Krishna Murthy S, Milo Rasouly H, Han H.

Disease: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)

title: Defining and Diagnosing Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: McCain MN, Fulcher ML, Clapp PW, Thorp BD, Senior BA, Davis SD, Ferkol TW, Randell SH, Kimple AJ.

authors: Pelaz SG, Mitsui K, Kolosowska N, Fritch H, Neupane C, Casha VH, Alonso-Gardón M, Pandey V, Wang L, Kawaguchi R, Wohlschlegel JA, Guo J, McCarroll SA, Berretta S, Khakh BS.

title: Exploring the BICC1 Interactome in HEK293T Cells: Insights Into RNA-Mediated Protein Networks and Biomolecular Condensates.

title: Metabolism of citrate-mediated PI3K-Akt signaling and primary cilium regulates spatiotemporal craniofacial mineralization.

authors: Wei Z, Gu J, Somlo S.

title: The trypanosome flagellum as model for parasitology, cell biology and ciliopathies.
authors: Hecquet A, Bonnefoy S, Bastin P.
ai_summary: Trypanosoma brucei is presented as a powerful model organism for studying cilia and flagella, whose defects cause human ciliopathies. The review highlights how trypanosome research has advanced understanding of flagellum construction and intraflagellar transport, and how mutations in flagellar genes contribute to ciliopathies.

ai_summary:
