title: Clinical, Genetic, and Endocrine Features of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome in a Pediatric and Adult Cohort.
authors: Hassan D, Salama M, Muthusamy K, Haqq AM, Scruggs BA, Lanpher BC, Tan QKG, Cramer CH, Biggs B, Rabatin AE, Koball A, Darr K, Bratcher PM, Lamothe K, Tenley JB, Schimmenti LA, Kumar S.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS1
Finding: Biallelic BBS1 variants were the most common genetic cause (36%) in a cohort where obesity affected 86% of children and 100% of adults, with diabetes/prediabetes, dyslipidemia, thyroid abnormalities, chronic kidney disease, and retinal dystrophy more prevalent in adults than children.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: A Novel NPHP5 Gene Mutation in Three Siblings With Nephronophthisis Without Retinitis Pigmentosa: A Case Report.
authors: Dahlan RA, Fairoozy RH.
ai_summary:
Gene: IQCB1 (NPHP5)
Finding: A novel homozygous IQCB1 p.(Ala486Asp) variant causes nephronophthisis with end-stage renal disease but without retinitis pigmentosa, unlike previously described IQCB1 mutations.
Disease: Nephronophthisis

title: Molecular and clinical heterogeneity in an Iranian case series of Joubert syndrome.
authors: Khalilian S, Fathi M, Farbood Z, Dehghanian F, Masoudi M, Ghafouri-Fard S, Dastgheib SA, Miryounesi M.
ai_summary:
Gene: AHI1
Finding: AHI1 was the most frequently mutated gene in an Iranian cohort of Joubert syndrome patients, with variants also identified in KIAA0586, CSPP1, CC2D2A, and TMEM67, though many variants were of uncertain significance.
Disease: Joubert syndrome

title: Precision Medicine in patients with rare forms of genetic obesity: Necessity for coordinated and structured care.
authors: Clément K, Farooqi IS, Kühnen P, Wabitsch M, Cetiner M, Argente J, Grueters A.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
ai_summary:
Gene: MC4R (melanocortin-4 receptor)
Finding: MC4R agonists are approved for treating hyperphagia and obesity in monogenic disorders (POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiencies) and Bardet-Biedl syndrome, but require coordinated expert care and structured monitoring to ensure equitable access and optimize therapy.
Disease: Monogenic obesity (including POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiencies) and Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Selçuk Balcı M, Yıldız CA, Erdem Eralp E, Ersu R.
ai_summary: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is increasingly recognized as a comorbidity in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), with obstructive sleep apnea prevalence reported between ~33% and 100% in most studies, though one large pediatric cohort found only ~1.2%. Upper-airway abnormalities are nearly universal, and lower-airway disease can cause nocturnal hypoxemia even without apneas; polysomnography remains the diagnostic standard, while questionnaires correlate poorly. Management focuses on optimizing upper-airway function and lung health, with positive airway pressure therapy for residual SDB, and the review calls for routine sleep assessment and multicenter, genotype-informed research.

title: Physiotherapy in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia-What Is the Evidence?: A Narrative Review and Personal Experience.
authors: Huenaerts E, Vreys M, Vermeulen F, Proesmans M, Lorent N, Boon M.
ai_summary: Physiotherapy, particularly airway clearance therapy, is considered a cornerstone of management for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a rare hereditary disorder of impaired motile ciliary function that leads to bronchiectasis. However, evidence supporting specific regimens is limited, with no standardized guidelines and no clear superiority among techniques such as PEP, ACBT, or HFCWO. The review concludes that current recommendations rely largely on expert opinion and extrapolation from cystic fibrosis and non-CF bronchiectasis, underscoring the need for robust evidence and international guidelines.

title: Advances in Health-Related Quality of Life in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Quittner AL, Davalillo IP, Cragun DM, Saunders J.
ai_summary: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder causing impaired mucociliary clearance and progressive sino-pulmonary disease. This review examined health-related quality of life (HRQoL) measures, particularly the condition-specific QOL-PCD instrument developed using FDA guidelines. Findings show that upper and lower respiratory symptoms worsen over time, ear and hearing symptoms improve moderately in adolescence, and disease severity increases in adulthood with lower HRQoL scores; strong associations exist between QOL-PCD scores and physical, psychological, and social functioning, though sensitivity to change in clinical trials remains unproven. The authors recommend embedding QOL-PCD in clinical care, registries, and trials, and call for research on longitudinal HRQoL trajectories, genotype-HRQoL links, and interventions targeting chronic cough, ENT symptoms, treatment burden, and psychological functioning.

title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: A Suggested Pathway to Transition From Pediatric to Adult Care.
authors: Castro A, Collins MS, Jain R, Walsh JB, Alba-Suárez J, Rivera-Sánchez YM.
ai_summary: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare, genetically heterogeneous disorder of motile ciliary dysfunction that impairs mucociliary clearance, leading to chronic respiratory symptoms, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. There are currently no established guidelines for transitioning PCD patients from pediatric to adult care, despite the adult PCD population being estimated at four times the pediatric population. The authors propose using the Six Core Elements of Health Care Transition framework, which has been shown to reduce care dropouts and increase engagement, and outline a specific pathway for transitioning pediatric PCD patients to adult care, noting unique challenges compared to other chronic diseases.

title: Hearing loss and tympanostomy tube outcomes in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Arida-Moody L, Solis RN, O'Connor MG, Virgin FW.
ai_summary: Hearing loss is common in primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), affecting 65% of patients in this retrospective review of 40 children. Tympanostomy tubes were frequently used (77.5% of patients, median 3 procedures) but were associated with a high complication burden, including otorrhea in 74.2% of cases and prolonged otorrhea (>12 months) in 41.9%. Hearing loss was fluctuant, with pure tone averages significantly worse after tube extrusion or removal compared to when tubes were in place, and many affected children required speech intervention (57.7%), educational support (19.2%), or hearing amplification (19.2%). The authors suggest that hearing amplification may offer more consistent functional support than tympanostomy tubes given the fluctuating nature of PCD-related hearing loss and tube complications.

title: A Novel Frameshift Variant in SPAG1 Likely Causes Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia in Cocker Spaniels in Australia.
authors: Mead SE, Hambrook LE, Suryadinata R, Robinson P, Wade CM.
ai_summary:
Gene: SPAG1
Finding: A 29 bp frameshift insertion in exon 11 of SPAG1 is likely causative for primary ciliary dyskinesia in Cocker Spaniels, inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Restoring the Balance: CRISPRa-Driven β-Tubulin Compensation as a Strategy for Tubulinopathy Treatment.
authors: Steiman S, Kinsella C, Zhang Y, Omer S, Brown C, Forguson G, Elbakr L, Pastore S, Ivakine EA.
ai_summary:
Gene: TUBB
Finding: CRISPRa-mediated upregulation of non-mutated beta-tubulin isotypes restores microtubule network integrity and primary cilia formation in cells with pathogenic beta-tubulin mutations.
Disease: Tubulinopathies (including ciliopathies)

title: Dysregulated Ferritin and Iron Homeostasis in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Sommer N, Placide S, Weatherly E, Wang W, Begum R, Dunfield M, Singh S, Ward CJ, Tran PV, Bolisetty S, Wallace DP, Sharma M.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
ai_summary:
Gene: FTH (ferritin heavy chain)
Finding: Conditional deletion of ferritin heavy chain in collecting duct or myeloid cells does not alter renal cyst growth in PKD mice, but ferritin infusion reveals dysfunctional ferritin trafficking with focal iron accumulation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis in PKD kidneys.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: SGLT2 inhibitors in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: rationale, evidence gaps, and ongoing clinical trials.
authors: Spatola L, Maccarrone R, Oddo G, Granata S, Zeiler M, Granata A.
ai_summary: SGLT2 inhibitors are being explored as a potential treatment for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), but evidence is limited because ADPKD patients were excluded from major randomized controlled trials. Observational studies show mixed results, and ongoing trials aim to clarify their safety and efficacy in this population.

title: Kidney outcomes and safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kanbay M, Mizrak B, Cig E, Karakaya E, Copur S, Covic A, Ortiz A, Mallamaci F, Zoccali C.
ai_summary: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy in ADPKD patients was associated with a modest attenuation in the rate of eGFR decline compared to each patient's own pre-treatment slope, but showed no significant benefit over non-SGLT2 inhibitor therapy for eGFR slope or total kidney volume change. Current evidence is insufficient to establish a beneficial effect on kidney outcomes, though no major safety concerns were identified; the findings are limited by small sample sizes, observational designs, and heterogeneity.

title: Hand-Assisted Laparoscopic Native Nephrectomy for Polycystic Kidney Disease Before Transplantation: A Single-Centre Case Series with a Technique-Stratified Focused Scoping Review.
authors: Kanani F, Shwaartz C, Meller M, Horowitz R, Baytner Zamir Yosilevsky T, Tennak V, Imam A, Khalaileh A, Gravetz A, Nesher E.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1/PKD2 (implied by ADPKD diagnosis, not directly tested in this study)
Finding: Hand-assisted laparoscopic native nephrectomy for ADPKD before transplantation is rapid and feasible but carries a bowel-predominant complication rate (35%), with bowel events clustering in right-sided procedures and potentially linked to free intraperitoneal cyst rupture rather than the surgical approach itself.
Disease: Autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Gas in a cyst: emphysematous infection in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease post-transplant.
authors: Sabe MG, Paul Davies MR.

title: Renal Volume Reduction on Magnetic Resonance Imaging During Tolvaptan Therapy in Patients with ADPKD: A Case Series.
authors: Koçyiğit İ, Aydın E, Baloğlu İ, Kılıç K, Demiray A.
ai_summary: Tolvaptan therapy in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is primarily known to slow kidney volume growth, but this observational case series of four patients demonstrates that actual kidney volume reduction can occur during treatment, with the most pronounced reduction seen in the patient with the highest baseline height-adjusted total kidney volume. Despite these volume changes, renal function changes were minimal (eGFR differences ranging from -9 to 0 mL/min/1.73 m²), and no patients required additional interventions. The findings highlight heterogeneity in treatment response, showing that kidney volume changes do not always parallel other clinical parameters, and underscore the need for larger studies to understand variability in tolvaptan response.

title: Kidney-specific deletion of the BicC family RNA-binding protein 1 triggers an ADPKD-like cystogenic program.
authors: Gagnieux C, Bernet F, Kroese L, Guiet R, Burns A, Combe R, Huijbers I, Constam DB, Rothé B.
ai_summary:
Gene: BICC1
Finding: Kidney-specific deletion of Bicc1 in adult renal tubules or distal nephron segments triggers an ADPKD-like cystogenic program, with activation of YAP signaling and transcriptional overlap with PKD and injury-repair signatures.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)-like phenotype

title: Dynamic regulation of hypothalamic NPY2R-positive primary cilia by nutritional states.
authors: Hamamoto A, Nishimura N, Saito Y, Kobayashi Y.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary:
Gene: NPY2R
Finding: Nutritional states and neuropeptide Y directly regulate the structural length of NPY2R-positive primary cilia in the hypothalamus via Gi/o-dependent Akt/JNK signaling, with region-specific remodeling in response to fasting and high-fat diet.
Disease: Hypothalamic regulation of feeding and energy homeostasis (metabolic regulation)

title: Selective loss of primary cilia and neurotrophic signaling in G51D α-synuclein mice highlights a common pathway to Parkinson's disease.
authors: Lin YE, Jaimon E, Kim Y, Loftman A, Vijayakumaran A, Belfort BDW, Chiang CY, Arenkiel BR, Zoghbi HY, Pfeffer SR.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
ai_summary:
Gene: SNCA (α-synuclein, G51D variant)
Finding: G51D α-synuclein knock-in mice show selective loss of primary cilia and neurotrophic signaling (including Neurturin downregulation) in striatal cholinergic interneurons, piriform cortex parvalbumin neurons, and olfactory horizontal basal cells, correlating with phospho-Ser129 α-synuclein accumulation.
Disease: Parkinson's disease

title: Vaptans: A Narrative Review of Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacogenetics, and Clinical Applications.
authors: Lica-Miler M, Miler K, Kostrzewa-Nowak D, Ciechanowicz A, Brodkiewicz A, Różański J, Stępniewska J.
ai_summary: This narrative review summarizes the pharmacokinetics, pharmacogenetics, and clinical applications of vaptans (AVP receptor antagonists), focusing on tolvaptan, conivaptan, and mozavaptan. It highlights tolvaptan's role as a disease-modifying therapy for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and its efficacy in SIADH, and discusses how pharmacogenetic factors, particularly CYP3A5 and SVEP1 polymorphisms, may influence inter-individual treatment response, pointing toward personalized aquaretic therapy.

title: Pediatric middle ear actinomycosis: report of two cases.
authors: Almalki MA, Almalki AH, Yaqoub N, Alaraifi A, Nassar J.
ai_summary: Middle ear actinomycosis is a rare cause of persistent ear discharge in children, often presenting as chronic suppurative otitis media that resists standard antibiotic treatment. This report describes two pediatric cases: a 7-year-old boy with Joubert syndrome who developed actinomycosis after ventilation tube insertion, and a 10-year-old girl with no prior medical history who had prolonged otorrhea. In both cases, diagnosis was confirmed by histopathology after surgical debridement, and infections resolved with a combination of surgery and a 3-month course of antibiotics. The authors conclude that actinomycosis should be suspected in children with treatment-resistant otorrhea.

title: Polycystin-1 suppresses apoptotic signalling in endothelial cells and protects from atherosclerosis.
authors: Tardajos Ayllon B, Gras Font J, Winks TAE, Grimwood H, Roddie H, Ariaans M, Wright C, Chico TJA, Fragiadaki M, Francis S, Ong ACM, Evans PC, Serbanovic-Canic J.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Endothelial-specific loss of PKD1 increases atherosclerosis by promoting endothelial apoptosis and reducing eNOS expression via THBS1 and CCN1, whereas PKD2 loss does not affect atherosclerosis.
Disease: Atherosclerosis (associated with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease)

title: Use of Next-Generation Sequencing and Whole-Exome Sequencing in the Diagnosis of Adult-Onset Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis: Challenges in Interpreting Variants of Uncertain Significance.
authors: Conti A, Gabrielli F, Ferrari S, Vaisfeld A, De Masi C, Azzaroli F, Piscaglia F, Vitale G.
ai_summary:
Gene: DCDC2, NPHP3, PKHD1, TTC21B
Finding: Emerging evidence implicates ciliopathy-associated genes in adult-onset cholestatic liver disease, expanding the genetic spectrum beyond classic PFIC genes.
Disease: Adult-onset familial intrahepatic cholestasis / cryptogenic cholestatic liver disease

title: Quantitative analysis of d-amino acids in renal samples using derivatization.
authors: Yin X, Decuypere JP, Mekahli D, Bammens B, Vennekens R, Adams E, Van Schepdael A.
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
ai_summary:
Gene: D-serine (not a specific gene)
Finding: Plasma D-serine levels progressively increase while urinary D-serine markedly decreases during kidney disease progression, and cyst fluid from an ADPKD patient shows elevated D-serine, suggesting D-serine as a potential metabolic biomarker of kidney dysfunction.
Disease: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Broadening horizons: Pathogenesis and therapeutics of renal ciliopathies.
authors: Zhang Q, Xue S, Gao Z, Shi P, Wang L, Feng Q, Kong X, Zhu X.
journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
ai_summary: Renal ciliopathies are a group of genetic disorders caused by defects in primary cilia, leading to cyst formation, fibrosis, and progressive kidney failure. The review highlights challenges in diagnosis and treatment, including incomplete understanding of molecular mechanisms, genetic heterogeneity, and limited prenatal diagnostic accuracy. It calls for a more integrated approach to studying signaling networks rather than focusing on individual pathways, aiming to improve prenatal diagnosis and develop novel therapies.

title: TBC1D23-AAVR interaction drives endosome-to-TGN trafficking required for rAAV transduction.
authors: Zhang X, Habib A, McFarlin S, Richart D, Park SY, Cheng F, Wang J, Yan Z, Qiu J.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
ai_summary:
Gene: TBC1D23
Finding: TBC1D23 binds the cytosolic domain of the AAV receptor (AAVR/KIAA0319L) via its C-terminal scaffold domain, mediating endosome-to-TGN retrograde transport of adeno-associated virus capsids, and its knockout impairs rAAV transduction across human cell types.
Disease: Adeno-associated virus transduction (viral infection model; no specific human disease phenotype)

title: Zero-Fluoroscopy Radiofrequency Ablation of a Right Ventricular Outflow Tract PVC in a Patient With Situs Inversus Totalis: When Precision Matters.
authors: Sanhueza E, Hanson M, Neira V, Chacko S, Enriquez A, Oli R, Saramago M, Burak C.
ai_summary: Zero-fluoroscopy radiofrequency ablation using high-definition 3D electroanatomic mapping and intracardiac echocardiography was successfully performed in a 60-year-old man with situs inversus totalis and symptomatic premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) refractory to medical therapy. The procedure, aided by reversed precordial lead placement, was safe and effective despite the complex congenital anatomy. This case demonstrates that a systematic zero-fluoroscopy approach is feasible even in patients with significant anatomical variation.

title: Genetic Heterogeneity in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Diagnostic Yield, Recurrent Genes, and Rare Variant-Phenotype Associations from Whole-Exome Sequencing.
authors: Gaouzi Z, Spoto G, Polito F, Festali R, Gasparo I, Licitri L, Mirabello AM, Romano S, Macaione V, Dini N, El Fahime E, Boutayeb S, Kriouile Y, Diawara I, di Rosa G, Aguennouz M.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: PKD1 was among the most frequently recurrent genes identified in children with autism spectrum disorder, though no specific phenotype association was reported for this gene.
Disease: Autism spectrum disorder

title: DOMINICA protocol: A study of benralizumab for severe eosinophilic asthma in children.
authors: Guilbert TW, Jison M, Sjö LB, Werkström V, Grindebacke H, Durżyński T, Lal A, Grigg J.
journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology

title: The genetic landscape of hypospadias: clinical insights into inherited and de novo risk factors.
authors: You Y, Luo Y, Zhou H, Liang Q, Xue J, Li Z, Zhao Y, He T, Wang K, Wang H, Chen Z, Wu L.
ai_summary:
Gene: PRKCZ, HRNR
Finding: Recurrent de novo loss-of-function variants in PRKCZ and HRNR disrupt cell proliferation, migration, and androgen signaling, and de novo LoF variants are enriched in ciliopathy-associated genes in hypospadias patients.
Disease: Hypospadias

title: Methylglyoxal Attenuates Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP)-Induced Pro-Inflammatory Macrophage Programming Associated with NRF-2 Antioxidant Responses and Reduced MCT4/Lactate-Linked Inflammatory Markers.
authors: Alrefaey HR, Naser SA.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Low-dose methylglyoxal treatment of Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis-infected macrophages reduces pro-inflammatory markers and downregulates PKD1 expression alongside glycolysis- and lactate-associated inflammatory signaling.
Disease: Crohn's disease

title: Five-year Incidence Trends and the Status of Major Rare Diseases in 2023 in the 「Annual Report on the Rare Disease Patients in Korea」.
authors: Park IS, Lee K, Lee J, Ji JH, Choi EJ, Kim JY, Park DH, Choi KH.
ai_summary: This study analyzed five-year trends (2019–2023) in rare disease incidence, deaths, and medical expenditures in Korea using the Annual Report on Rare Disease Patients. Newly registered cases rose to 62,420 in 2023, with the highest incidence among people in their 60s and in Gyeonggi-do. The most common rare diseases varied by age and sex—idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in older adults and males, systemic lupus erythematosus in females, Crohn's disease in teens and twenties, and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in middle age—with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis incurring the highest medical costs. The authors recommend moving beyond incidence-focused statistics toward a longitudinal data infrastructure tracking incidence, survival, and prevalence.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of Daratumumab in Recurrent and De Novo Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis After Kidney Transplant.
authors: Mehta RV, Evans KB, Shah CV, Shukla A, Belal A, Ibrahim H, Alquadan K, Leghrouz M, Vrakas G, Mehta R, Santos A.
ai_summary: Subcutaneous daratumumab was effective and well tolerated in 3 kidney transplant recipients with recurrent (n=1) or de novo (n=2) focal segmental glomerulosclerosis who were plasma exchange-dependent and/or rituximab-resistant. All patients achieved remission with sustained reductions in albuminuria and stable graft function; one developed transient neutropenia and oral ulcers. The findings suggest daratumumab may be a feasible option for refractory post-transplant FSGS, though prospective studies are needed.

title: Redox-Driven Precision Medicine for Life-Course Prevention of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
authors: Hsu CN, Tain YL.
ai_summary: Redox imbalance, particularly perturbation of the reactive oxygen species–nitric oxide axis during development, is a central integrative mechanism linking adverse early-life environments to persistent multi-organ vulnerability and the life-course development of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKMS). The authors propose a paradigm shift toward redox-driven precision medicine that integrates biologically informed phenotyping, life-course risk stratification, early developmental reprogramming, and phenotype-guided therapeutics to interrupt intergenerational risk transmission and improve cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health.

title: Technological Innovations and the Translational Path of Kidney Organoids.
authors: Li A, Chai Z, Jandeleit-Dahm K, Jha JC.
ai_summary: Kidney organoids are three-dimensional structures derived from human pluripotent stem cells that mimic kidney cellular heterogeneity, spatial organization, and physiological functions, offering a window into kidney development and disease. This review covers advances in stem cell differentiation, biomaterial-based culture systems, disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine applications, while highlighting key translational challenges—namely lack of vascularization, insufficient functional maturity, and obstacles in standardized production—that must be overcome to move organoids toward clinical therapeutic use.

title: Hospitalisations for bronchiectasis compared to COPD and asthma in the USA.
authors: El Labban M, Al-Itelat A, Aksamit TR, Chalmers SJ, Kanj AN.
ai_summary: Hospitalisations for bronchiectasis exacerbations in the USA are associated with worse outcomes than those for COPD or asthma, including longer hospital stays, higher costs, and greater mortality risk. Using a US all-payer database from 2017–2021, the bronchiectasis cohort (median age 72 years) had a median stay of 5 days and median cost of $50,393, and after adjustment, mortality was 1.2 times higher than for COPD and 3.0 times higher than for asthma. These findings highlight the need for improved care strategies for bronchiectasis hospitalisations.

title: Case Report: Efficacy and safety of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with Alström syndrome: a follow-up report of two siblings from the same family.
authors: Xue B, Li K, Guo Y, Wu Y, Peng H, Fu L, Jiang H.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALMS1
Finding: Ertugliflozin treatment in two siblings with Alström syndrome improved glycemic control, lipid metabolism, and early insulin sensitivity, with no adverse events over an 11-month follow-up.
Disease: Alström syndrome

title: Endothelin-1/endothelin B receptor signalling mediates Prx1<sup>+</sup> skeletal stem cells senescence: A driver of osteoporotic bone loss.
authors: Zou Z, Gong W, Lu X, Zhang Y, Au M, Lin J, Ouyang H, Xiao G, Tang B, Wen C.
ai_summary:
Gene: EDNRB (endothelin B receptor)
Finding: ET-1/ETBR signalling drives Prx1+ skeletal stem cell senescence via ROS accumulation and PI3K-AKT/p53 pathway dysregulation, and genetic knockout or pharmacological blockade of ETBR preserves bone mass in osteoporotic mouse models.
Disease: Osteoporosis (postmenopausal and age-related bone loss)

title: Tetralogy of Fallot: Genetic, Epigenetic and Clinical Insights into a Multifactorial Congenital Heart Disease.
authors: Gagliardi MF, Micaglio E, Micheletti A, Benedetti S, Negura DG, Bevilacqua F, Guglielmi G, Pasqualin G, Giamberti A, Chessa M.
ai_summary:
Gene: NOTCH1, FLT4, KDR, GATA6, TBX1, PUF60, DVL3
Finding: Variants in these genes, along with epigenetic mechanisms, contribute to the variable penetrance and expressivity of Fallot-type conotruncal malformations, which form a phenotypic continuum from Trilogy to Pentalogy of Fallot.
Disease: Tetralogy of Fallot (and related Fallot-type conotruncal malformations)

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing Reveals Breed-Specific SNPs, Indels, and Signatures of Selection in Royal White and White Dorper Sheep.
authors: Liao M, Kravitz A, Haak DC, Sriranganathan N, Cockrum RR.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
ai_summary:
Gene: NRXN1, HERC6, TGFB2, JADE2 (RW); TRIM14, PLXDC2, STPG3 (WD)
Finding: Whole-genome sequencing identified breed-specific SNPs and indels, with selective sweep analysis revealing candidate genes under positive selection linked to health, parasite resistance, growth, immune response, body weight, and reproduction in Royal White and White Dorper sheep.
Disease: Not applicable (livestock traits, no disease phenotype)

title: Tumor heterogeneity as a driver of drug resistance and its implications for personalized therapy.
authors: Da E, Zhu R, Xi B, Zhang L, Tang G.
ai_summary: Tumor heterogeneity, arising from both spatial and temporal variation, drives the emergence of drug-resistant subclones and treatment failure. Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics now allow precise tracking of these dynamics, revealing molecular mechanisms of resistance to targeted therapies. The authors argue that overcoming drug resistance requires shifting from static, single-target treatments to dynamic, biology-informed personalized strategies that integrate high-resolution monitoring with functional validation to identify subclonal vulnerabilities and enable adaptive therapy.

title: Inferred developmental origins of brain tumors from single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
authors: Wang S, Curry RN, McDonald MF, Koh HY, Erickson AW, Kleinman CL, Taylor MD, Rao G, Deneen B, Harmanci AO, Serin Harmanci A.
ai_summary: This study introduces COORS, a computational tool that uses single-cell RNA-sequencing data to infer the developmental origins of brain tumors by annotating "developmental-like" cell states. Applying COORS to medulloblastoma, glioma, and diffuse midline glioma datasets, the authors identified putative cells of origin, such as outer radial glia in IDH wild-type glioma and oligodendrocyte precursor cells and neuronal-like cells in IDH-mutant glioma, and provided novel developmental-state markers. The findings enhance understanding of brain tumor heterogeneity and may inform tailored treatment strategies.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals bromocriptine sensitivity genes and cellular targets in adenomyosis.
authors: Zhang Y, Luo D, Zhong Z, Chen J.
ai_summary:
Gene: ADAM12, HOXA11, SFRP1, SESN3
Finding: These genes are identified as bromocriptine sensitivity markers in adenomyosis, with distinct cell-type-specific expression (ADAM12 and HOXA11 in smooth muscle/epithelial cells; SFRP1 and SESN3 in fibroblasts) and increased expression in ectopic lesions.
Disease: Adenomyosis

title: Precision Nutrition in Type 2 Diabetes Prevention Through Molecular Nutrigenomic and Epigenetic Modulation of Insulin Signaling and Glucose Metabolism.
authors: Rumui D, Dama A, Gorica E, Halim VS, Setiawan AF, Tjia XC, Hadinata E, Harbuwono DS, Nurkolis F, Santini A.
ai_summary: Precision nutrition can help prevent type 2 diabetes by modulating gene expression and epigenetic mechanisms involved in insulin signaling and glucose metabolism. A review of 29 studies found that very-low-calorie diets shift metabolism toward fat oxidation and improve insulin sensitivity, while high-fat and fructose-rich diets promote inflammation and insulin resistance. Plant-based diets and targeted supplements (e.g., vitamin D with probiotics, fiber, nucleotides, copper) also showed favorable molecular effects, supporting nutrigenomics-guided dietary strategies for personalized diabetes prevention.

title: Genetic, Sociodemographic and Clinical Determinants of COVID-19 Severity in the Republic of Srpska: Exploring Potential Links with Neanderthal-Derived Variants.
authors: Dubravac Tanasković M, Mijović B, Kulić J, Joksimović B, Drašković-Mališ K, Mašić S, Vladičić-Mašić J, Krsmanović L, Radulović D, Elez-Burnjaković N.
ai_summary:
Gene: LZTFL1
Finding: The LZTFL1 rs35044562 AG genotype is associated with increased odds of hospitalization in COVID-19 patients compared to the AA genotype, with a potential synergistic effect when combined with the OAS3 rs1156361 CT genotype.
Disease: COVID-19 severity (hospitalization)

title: Integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to construct a risk model for histidine metabolism-related epithelial cell features in lung adenocarcinoma, predicting prognosis and immune landscape.
authors: Mao C, Zhou L.
ai_summary:
Gene: WIF1, GATA2, CD69, ID1, C4BPA, WFDC2, CCL20
Finding: A prognostic risk model based on seven histidine metabolism-related epithelial cell-specific genes predicts survival and immune infiltration in lung adenocarcinoma, with low-risk patients showing stronger immune activity and potential sensitivity to CTLA-4 and PD-L1 inhibitors.
Disease: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)

title: G protein‑coupled receptor kinase 4 governs early kidney development via STAT3 and Nhe3a.
authors: Vu LAT, Gerhards J, Maerz LD, Burkhalter MD, Philipp M.
ai_summary:
Gene: GRK4
Finding: Loss of GRK4 in zebrafish embryos causes pronephric dilatation, cilium elongation, glomerular cysts, and hydrocephalus via elevated Stat3 activity that upregulates Nhe3a transcription, and NHE3 inhibition with tenapanor rescues kidney development.
Disease: Renal developmental defects (pronephric dilatation, glomerular cysts) with associated hydrocephalus

title: A novel hsa_circ_0070963/miR-223-3p/ CCDC96-CCDC112 regulatory axis as a non-invasive biomarker for predicting sperm retrieval outcomes in non-obstructive azoospermia: A case-control study.
authors: Babakhanzadeh E, Khodadadian A, Nazari M, Mozhdeh M, Fazeli J, Vahidi S, Jafari MH, Dehghani M, Ghafouri-Fard S, Ghasemi N.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC96, CCDC112, hsa_circ_0070963, hsa-miR-223-3p
Finding: In non-obstructive azoospermia, plasma levels of CCDC96, CCDC112, and hsa_circ_0070963 are downregulated while hsa-miR-223-3p is upregulated, with the most pronounced dysregulation in individuals with failed sperm retrieval, and hsa_circ_0070963 and hsa-miR-223-3p show high predictive accuracy for micro-TESE outcomes.
Disease: Non-obstructive azoospermia (male infertility)

title: Enhanced endocrine-metabolic support and axonemal assembly in high-sperm-motility geese: insights from testicular cellular heterogeneity by scRNA-seq.
authors: Wang H, Cong K, Yin J, Jiang K, Liu Y, Ren X, Zhang Y, Liu S.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (no single gene link established)
Finding: High-sperm-motility geese show enhanced testicular endocrine-metabolic support (steroidogenesis, glycolysis, redox buffering) and axonemal assembly programs in round spermatids, while low-motility geese retain immature mitochondrial/cytoskeletal signatures in elongated spermatids.
Disease: Sperm motility variation (fertility phenotype) in geese

title: Molecular Pathways Driving Corneal Neovascularization in Herpes Simplex Keratitis.
authors: Akinsiku S, Shukla D.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: The JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis is identified as a key host-cell pathway driving corneal neovascularization in herpes simplex keratitis, alongside other molecular drivers such as growth factors, matrix metalloproteinases, heparanase, and Syndecan-1.
Disease: Herpes simplex keratitis-associated corneal neovascularization

title: Research advances in the role of circulating microorganisms in gastrointestinal tumors (Review).
authors: Yang Y, Ren Y, Ma T, An J, Jin S, Dong Y.
ai_summary: Circulating microorganisms (CM) in blood and other body fluids originate from microbial translocation through a compromised intestinal barrier and are closely associated with gastrointestinal tumor initiation and progression. Although not directly carcinogenic, their metabolites and exosomes may remodel the tumor microenvironment by activating inflammatory signaling pathways and facilitating immune evasion, potentially promoting the "inflammation-cancer" transition. CM show promise as liquid biopsy biomarkers for early diagnosis and as therapeutic targets, but face challenges including limited mechanistic validation and lack of standardized detection protocols.

title: The Barrier-Microbiota-Inflammation Axis in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms and Emerging Diagnostic & Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Dong X, Yang J, He L, Fang H, Wang L, Zhu J, Xu J, Song K, Xuan Z.
ai_summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is driven by a pathological axis linking intestinal barrier disruption, gut microbial dysbiosis, and chronic inflammation. Early lesions show reduced microbial diversity, enrichment of oral/pathobiont taxa, depletion of butyrate producers, impaired mucus and tight junction integrity, and altered chemical barriers (decreased short-chain fatty acids, increased secondary bile acids). This increased permeability allows microbial product translocation, triggering inflammation and tumorigenesis. The review highlights this cascade as a basis for early CRC detection and precision screening/intervention strategies.

title: Enhancement of Gastric Mucosal Defense by Phytomedicine in the Context of H. pylori-Associated Ulcer Disease.
authors: Paulraj RS, Perumal P, Ramachandran A, Sathiyaseelan A.
ai_summary: Phytomedicines enhance gastric mucosal defense against H. pylori-associated ulcer disease through multiple mechanisms, including antioxidant activity, anti-inflammatory modulation, inhibition of urease and bacterial adhesion, suppression of virulence factors, and restoration of epithelial barrier integrity. Plant-derived compounds exert multi-targeted gastroprotective effects by modulating oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, prostaglandin synthesis, and tight junction preservation. While preclinical and limited clinical evidence support their potential, further well-designed trials and standardized formulations are needed for clinical validation.

title: Exploring the Potential Roles of SLC39A8 and POC5 Missense Variants in the Association Between Body Composition, Beverage Consumption, and Chronic Lung Diseases: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Study.
authors: Apalowo OE, Walt HK, Alaba TE, Komakech JJ, Schilling MW.
ai_summary:
Gene: SLC39A8 (rs13107325) and POC5 (rs2307111)
Finding: Missense variants in SLC39A8 and POC5 are associated with body composition and alcohol intake-related genetic influences on increased risk of asthma and COPD.
Disease: Asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

title: Mechanistic Links Between the Gut Microbiome and Longevity Therapeutics.
authors: Garzon-Escamilla N, Medina-Cardena M, Roy P, Trent J, Jamous J, Somesan Y, Denslow SJ.
ai_summary: The gut microbiome is a key modulator of aging and may influence the efficacy of anti-aging therapeutics, but this review does not establish a link between a specific gene and a disease or phenotype. It synthesizes evidence that a balanced microbiome supports healthspan, while dysbiosis contributes to age-related diseases, and that interventions like metformin and rapamycin may act partly through microbiome-associated mechanisms.

title: Systemic inflammatory perturbations triggered by neuropathic pain in L5 compressed mouse and rat model.
authors: Chen S, Zheng Z, Ying H, Ye F, Liao P, Zhou J, Tong S, Gao J, Liu D, Zhong Z, Huang YG.
ai_summary: This study investigates whether neuropathic pain from L5 nerve compression triggers systemic inflammation beyond the local lesion site. Using mouse and rat models, the authors performed multi-omic analyses (bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq) on compressed nerves, brain, bone marrow, and major organs. They found that nerve compression induces systemic inflammatory perturbations, including upregulated pro-inflammatory genes (IL13, Csf3 in bone marrow/brain; TNF-α in compressed nerve), altered chromatin accessibility in bone marrow macrophages, metabolic dysfunction in liver and lungs, and renal lipid accumulation, with ligand-receptor networks facilitating cross-organ inflammation. The authors conclude that neuropathic pain should be redefined as a multi-organ disorder and propose myeloid-immune signaling pathways (e.g., Csf3, IL13, IL6/TNF-α) as potential therapeutic targets, though functional validation is still needed.

title: USP5 regulates purine metabolism and represents a therapeutic target in esophageal cancer.
authors: Zhao K, Zhang L, Yan M, Fang S, Wang Z, Song Y, Liu M, Zhang C, Shao Y, Jia X, Guo Q, Guo M, Yin J, Jin G, Dong Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: USP5
Finding: USP5 deubiquitinates and stabilizes IMPDH2 at lysine 489, promoting guanine nucleotide synthesis and esophageal cancer progression; mebendazole inhibits USP5 and enhances chemosensitivity when combined with oxaliplatin.
Disease: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC)

title: TLR4 maintains Treg-mediated protection against adverse outcomes in a model of hepatic surgical stress.
authors: Zhang H, Zhang Y, Ren T, Tsung C, Song P, Xu P, Wang G, Cao C, Wang C, Sun P, Zhang Q, Zhu Y, Zhong X, Guan Y, Zhang X, Wang H, Zhang J, Wang H.
ai_summary:
Gene: TLR4
Finding: TLR4 signaling in regulatory T cells maintains IL-10 production via the MyD88/ERK/CREB pathway, protecting against hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury.
Disease: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (liver surgical stress)

title: The Synthetic Extracellular Matrix as a Maestro of the In Vitro Stem Cell Niche: Orchestrating Fate and Function.
authors: Giri S, Rajesh P.
ai_summary: Synthetic extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds offer a fully defined, tunable alternative to Matrigel for culturing human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), enabling xenogen-free, chemically defined conditions for directed differentiation into specific cell types and organoids. This approach addresses the variability and poor definition of Matrigel, supporting clinical-grade applications in regenerative medicine.

title: Macrophage response to fibrin structure mediated by Tgm2-dependent mitochondrial mechanosensing.
authors: Gao B, Ni H, Lai J, Gao N, Luo X, Wang Y, Chen Y, Zhao J, Yu Z, Zhang J, Cai W, Yang G.
ai_summary:
Gene: TGM2
Finding: Fibrin architecture topography regulates macrophage polarization through integrin signaling that upregulates Tgm2, which augments PGC1α-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis and mechanosensing.
Disease: Foreign body response (FBR)

title: Genetics and Epigenetics of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
authors: Bernoni d'Aversa F, Gennarelli M.
ai_summary: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a highly heritable psychiatric condition, and recent large-scale genomic and epigenomic studies—including GWAS, whole exome/genome sequencing, and methylome-wide analyses—reveal a highly polygenic architecture with contributions from common variants, rare coding variants, and replicable methylation patterns. These signals converge on biological pathways related to synaptic organization, neurodevelopment, chromatin regulation, immune/stress responses, and cellular homeostasis, though single-gene convergence remains limited. The findings support an integrative model of OCD risk combining genetic load, rare variants, and epigenetic regulation affecting intermediate phenotypes, but they are not yet clinically applicable for individual diagnosis.

title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: Recent Updates in Its Prevalence and Diagnosis.
authors: Parker CP, Davis MD.
ai_summary: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder causing motile cilia dysfunction, leading to impaired mucociliary clearance and progressive respiratory disease. The review highlights that PCD is underdiagnosed and more prevalent than previously thought, with recent advances in molecular genetics and ciliary function testing reshaping diagnostic strategies, culminating in a new joint ATS/ERS guideline for diagnosis.

title: Clinical features, misdiagnosis, and treatment of clinically diagnosed complete Kartagener syndrome: A three-case series for primary care.
authors: Li D, Wang Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (clinical diagnosis only; no genetic testing performed)
Finding: In three adult patients, the clinical triad of situs inversus totalis, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis, combined with infertility, enabled diagnosis of complete Kartagener syndrome in primary care settings lacking genetic or ultrastructural confirmation; individualized antimicrobial and supportive treatment led to symptom resolution and stable disease over 6–12 months.
Disease: Kartagener syndrome (complete), a subtype of primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: BBS5 as a robust prognostic biomarker in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: validation in two independent cohorts.
authors: Aoki K, Yamagishi S, Sato Y, Shimizu D, Nakanishi K, Nakagawa N, Kurimoto K, Umeda S, Sato Y, Tanaka H, Takami H, Hattori N, Hayashi M, Tanaka C, Kanda M.
journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS5
Finding: BBS5 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and high expression independently predicts poor overall and disease-free survival in two independent patient cohorts.
Disease: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC)

title: Correction: Gad et al. Management of Childhood Obesity. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2026, 27, 3528.
authors: Gad H, Dauleh H, Mohammed I, Malik RA, Hussain K.
ai_summary: Plain-language summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on childhood obesity management. It does not present new research findings or establish a gene-disease link.

title: Evaluating the efficacy and safety of macrolide therapy in primary ciliary dyskinesia: A systematic review.
authors: Ghasempour Alamdari M, Pourpashang P, Khayatzadeh Kakhki S, Rahimi Azghadi MS, Ghanbari N, Ashournia P, Akhlaghi A, Shariatpanahi G.
ai_summary: Macrolide therapy, particularly azithromycin, may reduce respiratory exacerbations and improve selected clinical symptoms in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), with in vitro evidence suggesting anti-inflammatory and epithelial barrier repair effects. However, the evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and a scarcity of randomized controlled trials, so further large-scale, PCD-specific studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Editorial on: Respiratory bacterial epidemiology at three primary ciliary dyskinesia clinical centers.
authors: Fireizen Y.

title: Lung Adenocarcinoma in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: A Case Report of Metastatic Disease and Successful Multimodal Treatment.
authors: Kommineni V, Vegunta R, Rokkam V, Sridharan GK.
journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified
Finding: This case report describes the first known instance of lung adenocarcinoma in a patient with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), successfully treated with a combination of pembrolizumab, stereotactic radiation, and chemotherapy (carboplatin and pemetrexed), resulting in complete response.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma.

title: Can MQ232 guide to novel options for treatment of ADPKD?
authors: Klussmann E.
ai_summary: MQ232, a green mamba-derived compound, reduces cyst growth in a mouse model of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), with efficacy comparable to the approved drug tolvaptan. Its mechanism involves both cyclic AMP-dependent and -independent pathways, and it shows gender-specific effects, suggesting it could lead to new treatment options for ADPKD.

title: A Survey on the Current Status of Joubert Syndrome and Related Disorders Conducted Through a Patient and Family Group in Japan.
authors: Mano H.
ai_summary: This survey of Japanese patients and families affected by Joubert syndrome and related disorders (JSRD) found that most patients attended special needs schools or received individualized educational accommodations, and all had received rehabilitation therapy, with many continuing it. Families expressed a strong need for more information on medical care, social welfare, and education. The authors conclude that ongoing support in healthcare, research, and social systems remains a challenge for these rare diseases.

title: Sleep Disordered Breathing in Joubert Syndrome: Disease Spectrum in a Pediatric Cohort.
authors: Le Fevre E, Fitzgerald DA, Waters K, Seton C, Webster R, Pandit C.
ai_summary: Children with Joubert syndrome (JS) exhibit a spectrum of sleep disordered breathing (SDB), including obstructive sleep apnea that may respond to conventional treatment and central sleep apnea that can persist over time. In a cohort of 21 children followed over 16 years, not all were referred for sleep assessment, highlighting the need for ongoing screening and follow-up polysomnography in this population.

title: Global Perspectives in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Mexico.
authors: Zavala-Miranda MF, Ramírez-Sandoval JC.

ai_summary:

title: Prognostic Performance of Ellipsoid Kidney Volume Measurement in a Computed Tomography-Heavy ADPKD Cohort: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.

journal: Canadian journal of kidney health and disease
ai_summary:

Finding: The ellipsoid method for kidney volume measurement shows good concordance with manual segmentation (ICC 0.93) but systematically underestimates volume by 12.7%, leading to misclassification of Mayo Clinic Imaging Classification in 25.8% of cases, with high specificity (98.0%) but lower sensitivity (83.0%) for identifying high-risk disease.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Contribution of polycystic kidney disease to the development of chronic renal dysfunction in cats.
authors: Jamshidi A, Akhtardanesh B, Rasekh M, Vosough D, Behzadi MJ.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
ai_summary:

Finding: In PKD-affected cats, progressive increases in cyst volume and kidney length, along with elevated plasma creatinine, phosphorus, and blood urea nitrogen and progressive anemia, correlate with advancing chronic kidney disease stages.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease-associated chronic kidney disease in cats

title: Molecular characterization of FAM222B as a novel disease gene for dominant cardiovascular laterality defects.
authors: Reitz N, Lambertz J, Yilmaz Ö, Lindenberg TT, Channab K, Rau B, Ramrath S, Mingardo E, Schöpper H, Kirchmaier BC, Geyer M, Dworschak GC, Breuer J, Müller N, Schaidinger B, Hilger AC, Hoefele J, Riedhammer KM, Hitz MP, Dombrowsky G, Abdul-Khaliq H, Bauer UMM, Fester L, Reutter HM, Breuer K, Odermatt B.
ai_summary:

Finding: Rare variants in FAM222B, including a recurrent de novo c.899G>A (p.Arg300His) variant, cause perturbed cardiogenesis and aberrant cardiac looping in zebrafish models, implicating the gene in left-right axis determination.
Disease: Cardiovascular laterality defects (situs inversus totalis, heterotaxy, or isolated congenital heart defects)

title: Downstream-Aware Automated QC of Images and AI-Generated Segmentations.
authors: Green AE, Dhar MK, Gregory AV, Buchl SC, Holmes HL, Fati F, Bozkurt EG, Khalifa M, Klug JR, Dachowicz AP, Cook CJ, Conte GM, Shi T, Potretzke TA, Kline TL.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
ai_summary: Automated deep learning segmentation is increasingly used in medical imaging, but manual quality control (QC) remains standard. This study developed a 3D deep learning model (DenseNet121) to classify MR scans and their automated segmentations into Accept, Reject, or Rework categories for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), where accurate total kidney volume measurement is critical. Using 10,749 abdominal MR scans from 2,717 ADPKD patients, the model achieved macro F1-scores of 0.78–0.86 and accuracies of 79–86% across three reference standards, with combined false-Accept rates of 12.7–23.4%. The model's agreement approached observed variability among human readers, suggesting it could support clinical triage and expedite data curation by flagging problematic cases for radiologist review.

title: Stromme syndrome presenting with classic microcephaly and apple-peel intestinal atresia in a neonate: a genetically confirmed case report.
authors: Nawlakhe K, Bandiya P, Raghavendra P, Shivann N.
ai_summary:

Finding: A pathogenic homozygous CENPF variant (c.8692 C>T) was identified by whole-exome sequencing in a neonate presenting with microcephaly and apple-peel intestinal atresia, confirming Stromme syndrome.
Disease: Stromme syndrome (CENPF-related ciliopathy)

title: Protein Kinase D1 Inhibits AMP-Activated Protein Kinase Activity in the Rat Postural Muscle during the Initial Stage of Mechanical Unloading.
authors: Vilchinskaya NA, Mirzoev TM, Shenkman BS.
ai_summary:

Finding: Suppression of upregulated PKD1 activity with a specific inhibitor restores AMPK activity in rat soleus muscle during 24-hour hindlimb unloading, indicating that elevated PKD1 contributes to the unloading-induced decline in AMPK activity.
Disease: Mechanical unloading-induced muscle atrophy (postural muscle remodeling)

title: Cluster of Human Tanapox Cases in Wildlife Reserve, South Africa, 2024.
authors: Birkhead M, Grobbelaar AA, Morobadi D, Mpangani HD, Dabrowski J, Govender K, Blumberg LH, Zwane M, Moolla N, Tebeila ND, Govender N, Marshall T, Dermaux-Msimang V, Grayson W, Weyer J.
ai_summary: Tanapox, a rare mosquito-borne viral zoonosis, was identified in 11 human cases near Orpen in Kruger National Park, South Africa, during February–March 2024, with 2 additional suspected cases retrospectively identified from Pafuri in 2021. These findings indicate continued virus circulation in the region, highlighting the need for public awareness to ensure appropriate medical treatment.

title: Functional genomics in Xenopus identifies ARHGAP10 as a congenital heart disease and ciliopathy gene.
authors: Sochacka E, Hinson ST, Shook DR, DeSimone DW, Kulkarni SS.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARHGAP10 (GAP10)
Finding: Deletion of gap10 in Xenopus disrupts body axis extension, left-right organizer formation, and ciliogenesis, causing cardiac looping defects that mirror human congenital heart disease phenotypes, with Gap10 localizing to basal bodies of motile cilia and regulating basal body and apical F-actin organization via focal adhesion kinase recruitment.
Disease: Congenital heart disease (heterotaxy and atrial septal defects) and ciliopathy

title: Ciliogenic pancreatopathy reveals a link between ciliopathies and exocrine pancreatic disease.
authors: Rajput M, Flasse L, Porée E, Pointeau O, Serafin A, Papadopoulos N, Achouri Y, Moro J, Loriot A, Wilsch-Brauninger M, Gillion V, Godefroid N, Bodson C, Lopez Muneta L, Depestel C, Morel M, Cordi S, Garcia de Herreros A, Haumaitre C, Lemaigre F, Rovira M, Viau A, Grapin-Botton A, Saunier S, Jacquemin P, Scheers I.
ai_summary:

Finding: Mutations in HNF1B and NPHP3 are linked to a pancreatic phenotype characterized by acinar atrophy, adipopancreatosis (fat accumulation), and ductal cilia abnormalities, with increased pancreatic fat content confirmed in patients.
Disease: Ciliogenic pancreatopathy, associated with exocrine pancreatic dysfunction in ciliopathy patients.

title: Three-port laparoscopic cholecystectomy with common bile duct exploration in situs inverse totalis: a case report and literature review.
authors: Jiang C, Yang Y, Zhao K, Tang J, Gu H, Li Y.
ai_summary: This case report describes a 59-year-old woman with situs inversus totalis (SIT) who presented with cholelithiasis, obstructive jaundice, acute biliary pancreatitis, and atrial fibrillation. She successfully underwent a three-port laparoscopic cholecystectomy with common bile duct exploration (LC+LCBDE), using strategically placed trocar ports to accommodate the mirrored anatomy, with bile duct stones cleared via choledochoscopy and primary closure of the choledochotomy. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day two, demonstrating that tailored port placement and meticulous perioperative management can enable safe, enhanced recovery in complex SIT cases.

title: Editor's Note on 'Protein Syndesmos is a novel RNA-binding protein that regulates primary cilia formation'.
authors: Sale JE, Stoddard BL.

title: AI Structural Biology in Nephrology: Powerful Scaffolds, Fragile Certainties.
authors: Zoccali C, Petretto E, Capasso G, Gesualdo L, Mallamaci F, Cheungpasitporn W, Pesce F.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
ai_summary: AI-based protein structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold are increasingly used in nephrology to model renal proteins and interpret inherited kidney diseases, but their outputs can be misleading. Renal proteins often fall into underrepresented classes where confidence scores are unreliable, and the static predictions fail to capture dynamic, environment-dependent functions, leading to poor agreement with mutagenesis data for variant classification. The authors recommend an integrative, hypothesis-driven approach that cross-validates AI models with experimental methods like cryo-electron tomography and functional assays to ensure reliable mechanistic insights and clinical translation.

title: Integrating kidney imaging for risk prediction, therapeutic monitoring, and prognostication across the kidney disease spectrum: a review of emerging evidence.
authors: Guldan M, Gulmaliyev I, AlShiab R, Shah E, Ozbek L, Altindal M, Gurses B, Madero M, Ortiz A, Covic A, Kanbay M.
ai_summary: Imaging biomarkers such as cortical R2*, apparent diffusion coefficient, arterial spin labeling, and shear-wave elastography show predictive value for progression to kidney failure in chronic kidney disease, including diabetic kidney disease, independent of traditional measures like eGFR and albuminuria. Advanced imaging can detect CKD in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease decades earlier than laboratory tests, and may detect fibrotic remodeling and microvascular impairment in hypertensive and obese kidney phenotypes before laboratory indicators appear. However, most methods lack standardized protocols and comprehensive validation, and future work should focus on longitudinal studies, multi-omics integration, and machine learning-based models to enable personalized risk classification and therapy monitoring.

title: Deletion of ARPKD-associated Pkhd1 gene in mice results in decreased Tfap2b expression and eye abnormalities.
authors: Ishimoto Y, Menezes LF, Nakaya N, Barbosa-Sabanero K, Horie Y, Yoshida T, Reece JM, Zhou F, Tomarev S, Kerosuo L, Germino GG.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: Deletion of Pkhd1 in mice disrupts the genomic architecture of the Pkhd1-Tfap2b locus, leading to loss of Tfap2b/AP-2β expression in specific periocular mesenchymal cells and causing anterior segment dysgenesis and congenital glaucoma.
Disease: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), congenital glaucoma, anterior segment dysgenesis, autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD)

title: Postbiotic of Bifidobacterium breve i1088 alleviates type 2 diabetes by promoting GLP-1 secretion: identification of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid as a key active metabolite.
authors: Niu X, Zhao Y, Wang X, Feng L, Wang S, Guo H, Zhang D, Guo B, Wang R.
ai_summary: Postbiotic lysate from Bifidobacterium breve i1088 stimulates GLP-1 secretion in enteroendocrine cells and alleviates type 2 diabetes in a mouse model by upregulating the GCG/PC1 pathway. The key active metabolite is 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), which directly triggers GLP-1 release and enhances GLP-1 synthesis, highlighting the lysate's potential as a postbiotic therapy for T2DM.

title: Evaluation of the Antiviral Activity of Monomeric, Dimeric, and Oligomeric Flavonoids against Chikungunya and Mayaro Viruses.
authors: Gouvêa DM, Brand MCMS, Vaz MAM, Ferreira PG, Viana V, de Almeida KS, Coelho Ferraz A, Reis ACC, Brandão GC, Magalhães CLB, de Magalhães JC.
ai_summary: Procyanidin C1 (PC1), procyanidin A2 (PA2), and genistein (GNT) show antiviral activity against Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Mayaro (MAYV) viruses, with PC1 being the most promising candidate due to its high selectivity index (61 against MAYV) and strong virucidal effects, while GNT and PA2 are lead compounds for further optimization.

title: Recurrent transplant renal vein thrombosis caused by May-Thurner syndrome: a case report and review of literature.
authors: Kamali K, Saffari H, Zolfi E, Najafizadeh S, Abian N, Ahmadi F, Vahedisoraki V.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified
Finding: This case report describes a 62-year-old man with recurrent transplant renal vein thrombosis (TRVT) and deep vein thrombosis after left-sided kidney transplantation, where May-Thurner syndrome (MTS) was identified as the underlying mechanical cause; treatment with left common iliac vein stenting and long-term anticoagulation was implemented.
Disease: Transplant renal vein thrombosis (TRVT) associated with May-Thurner syndrome (MTS)

title: Nasal versus Buccal Breathing and Non-Invasive Indices of Vascular Function in Healthy Young Adults: An Observational Crossover Study.
authors: Snoeck T, Paillaugue F, Provyn S.
ai_summary: Nasal versus buccal breathing in healthy young adults produced distinct vascular responses: nasal breathing significantly increased pulse propagation time and reduced reflection index compared with buccal breathing, suggesting greater vascular relaxation. These findings indicate that the breathing route has physiological relevance for vascular function under resting conditions, though no specific gene or disease link was established.

title: Investigating the impact of poly(beta amino) ester-mediated FOXJ1 mRNA delivery on differentiation of primary human bronchial epithelial cells.
authors: Konstantinidi R, Subramanian M, Yates L, Lloyd CM, Saglani S, Patel AK.
ai_summary:
Gene: FOXJ1
Finding: PBAE-mediated delivery of FOXJ1 mRNA to primary human bronchial epithelial cells transiently upregulates ciliogenesis-related genes without impairing subsequent mucociliary differentiation or epithelial integrity.
Disease: Not applicable (model for airway differentiation; no disease link established)

title: Stereotypical interciliary contacts in a C. elegans sense organ.
authors: Krishnan N, Leslie S, Lawson H, Lu YM, Wexler L, Judge K, Heiman MG, Sengupta P.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (multiple genes implicated in ciliary trafficking, membrane phospholipid composition, and cilia-cell interactions)
Finding: Interciliary contacts in C. elegans amphid sensory neurons are stereotyped, form independently of neighboring cilia, and are disrupted by mutations affecting ciliary structure or trafficking, yet some altered cilia still establish correct contacts, suggesting instructive mechanisms.
Disease: C. elegans amphid sense organ phenotype (cilia structure and contact defects)

title: Refractory Ascites After Liver Transplantation due to Splenic Artery Steal Syndrome With Resolution After Splenectomy.
authors: Lowe D, Choi K, Shin JS, Pow R, Liu K.
ai_summary: Splenic artery steal syndrome is an under-recognized cause of refractory ascites after liver transplantation, characterized by reduced hepatic arterial perfusion due to excessive splenic blood flow. In this case, a 65-year-old man with pretransplant splenomegaly developed persistent ascites and ischemic biliopathy post-transplant; after failed splenic artery embolization, salvage splenectomy resolved the ascites, cholestasis, and biliopathy.

title: Coping with the challenges of caregiving: A qualitative exploration of the experiences of family caregivers of children with rare diseases in South Africa.
authors: van Niekerk J, Gush M, Moosa S, Pretorius C.
ai_summary: Family caregivers of children with rare diseases in South Africa face significant challenges, including uncertainty, difficult healthcare interactions, and the all-encompassing demands of caregiving. Their coping strategies involve acceptance, normalization, religious beliefs, and love for their children, but their experiences are shaped by structural inequities and limited support infrastructure. The study highlights the need for improved support and consideration for these caregivers in South Africa.

title: Driver or passenger? A new assessment of genes in the schizophrenia-associated 3q29 deletion locus for contribution to neurodevelopmental disorders.
authors: Herriges AR, Purcell RH.
ai_summary:
Gene: TFRC, UBXN7, FBXO45, PAK2, NCBP2, DLG1
Finding: Functional, expression, and gene constraint evidence identifies these six genes as the most likely phenotypic drivers in the 3q29 deletion locus, with compound haploinsufficiency of UBXN7, FBXO45, RNF168, and SENP5 potentially disrupting ubiquitination/SUMOylation processes.
Disease: 3q29 deletion syndrome, associated with schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders

title: Heme-binding protein CYB5D1 couples intraflagellar redox to calcium signaling for coordinated flagellar beating.
authors: Lin Y, Zhao L, Liu G, Deng X, King SM, Huang K.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
ai_summary:
Gene: CYB5D1
Finding: CYB5D1, a heme-binding axonemal protein, acts as a redox-sensitive switch that couples intraflagellar redox state to Ca2+ signaling, and its loss or heme-binding mutation disrupts coordinated flagellar beating and gliding motility.
Disease: Ciliopathies and respiratory diseases (implicated by conserved ciliary mechanism)

title: Inflammatory Factors and Chronic Rhinosinusitis: An Umbrella Review.
authors: Lialiaris ST, Chaidas K, Fyrmpas G, Deftereou TE, Spyroulia D, Prokopakis EP, Katotomichelakis M.
ai_summary: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease of the nasal passages and sinuses, broadly divided into phenotypes with or without nasal polyps. This umbrella review of 64 studies synthesizes evidence showing that CRS involves distinct but overlapping immune patterns driven by T helper cell types (Th1, Th2, Th17, Th22) and regulatory T cells. Type 1 inflammation is linked to CRS without polyps and neutrophilic infiltration, type 2 inflammation (with cytokines IL-4, IL-5, IL-13) is associated with nasal polyps and eosinophilic infiltration, and type 3 inflammation involves IL-17/IL-22 and relates to fungal infections. Comorbidities like aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease and cystic fibrosis shape disease endotypes, and biologic therapies such as dupilumab show promise for endotype-driven treatment, though further research is needed to refine classification and reduce surgery reliance.

title: PDGF-BB as a potential biomarker for early diagnosis of postpartum hemorrhage.
authors: Thirugnanam K, Polnaszek BE, Eng K, Pan AY, Ramchandran R.
ai_summary: PDGF-BB levels are inversely associated with postpartum hemorrhage risk, with lower levels indicating higher risk. The study evaluated ciliary-associated proteins and found PDGF-BB consistently differentially expressed across analytical platforms, with a threshold of 11.5 pg/mL showing high discriminatory performance for PPH. This suggests PDGF-BB may serve as an early biomarker for postpartum hemorrhage, though prospective validation is needed.

title: Enhancing Molecular Diagnostic Accuracy in Genetic Eye Disorders Through a Personalized Re-Evaluation Strategy.
authors: Martins PM, Figueiredo I, Cruz N, Gaspar BR, Silva R, Carvalho AL, Marques JP.
ai_summary: A personalized re-evaluation strategy—combining updated next-generation sequencing panels, exome sequencing reanalysis, assays for intronic/copy number/ORF15-RPGR variants, and evidence-based variant reclassification—increased the molecular diagnostic yield from 59.4% to 70.1% in 800 families with genetic eye disorders, providing definitive diagnoses for 86 additional families.

title: Single-cell RNA profiling of oligodendroglial lineage cells derived from iPSCs carrying Parkinson's disease-relevant LRRK2-G2019S mutation.
authors: Karmali N, Kessler W, Dehestani M, Sun W, Drwesh L, Volos P, Tsitkov S, Dhingra A, Thomas C, Rodriguez-Nieto S, Tietz J, Schafflick D, Fernandes N, Fitzgerald J, Fraenkel E, Gasser T, Rafiq NM, Kuhlmann T, Bansal V.
ai_summary:
Gene: LRRK2
Finding: iPSC-derived oligodendroglial lineage cells carrying the LRRK2 p.G2019S mutation show increased proportions of OPCs, proliferating OPCs, and ciliated ependymal cells, with transcriptomic changes including downregulation of myelin assembly, semaphorin-plexin, and cilium movement genes, and altered SHH expression along pseudotime.
Disease: Parkinson's disease

title: Use of Small-Molecule Inhibitors of CILK1 and AURKA as Cilia-Promoting Drugs to Decelerate Medulloblastoma Cell Replication.
authors: Fu SH, Park C, Shah NA, Limerick A, Powers EW, Mann CB, Hyun EM, Zhang Y, Brautigan DL, Hao S, Abounader R, Fu Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: CILK1, AURKA
Finding: Small-molecule inhibitors of CILK1 (Alvocidib) and AURKA (Alisertib) increase cilia frequency and significantly decrease replication of medulloblastoma cells.
Disease: Medulloblastoma

title: CDK1 and CEP97 cooperatively control centriole length to orchestrate ciliogenesis and developmental patterning.
authors: Liu Y, Wang Z, Sinha T, Li KH, Chalkley RJ, Herranz-Pérez V, Xie C, Yoder BK, Burlingame AL, Black BL, Reiter JF.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP97 (with CDK1 and Centrobin)
Finding: CEP97-CCP110 and CDK1 cooperatively restrict Centrobin's centriole-elongating function; loss of CEP97 causes centriole overelongation, impaired ciliogenesis, and attenuated Hedgehog signaling.
Disease: Disrupted heart development in mice (developmental patterning defects)

title: Nonsense Mutation in USH2A Exon-13 Activates the Innate Immune Response in Müller Glial Cells.
authors: Valenzano R, Lu X, McDonald A, Moustakas I, Menafra R, Mulder AA, Koning RI, Kloet SL, Yang J, Mei H, Wijnholds J.
ai_summary:
Gene: USH2A
Finding: A homozygous nonsense mutation in USH2A exon-13 disrupts ciliary localization of usherin long form B and its interacting proteins, and triggers major transcriptional changes in Müller glial cells indicative of innate immune response activation, despite normal photoreceptor development.
Disease: Usher syndrome type II (retinitis pigmentosa with hearing and balance impairment)

title: Air pollution-induced airway epithelial barrier dysfunction in COPD: a narrative review of mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
authors: He Z, Yang P, Shao L, Fang X, Zhao Z, Sun W, Song Y, Xu Y, Zhao X, Ma Z, Yue Y, Wang X, Zhang Q.
journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
ai_summary: Air pollution exposure, particularly from biomass burning, drives a COPD phenotype characterized by airway damage rather than emphysema. The review details how pollutants such as particulate matter, ozone, diesel exhaust, and microplastics disrupt the airway epithelial barrier through direct damage to junctional complexes, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative stress, epigenetic changes, and disturbed immune cell cross-talk, with exacerbation via the gut-lung axis. Emerging therapies aimed at restoring barrier integrity—including antioxidants, natural compounds, pathway-specific inhibitors, and probiotics—may reduce the onset and progression of pollution-related COPD.

title: Cytosolic heat shock protein 90 is required for photoreceptor outer segment development and vision.
authors: Aliff HL, Crockett AB, Munezero D, Reid C, Bockius HG, Kuzak SG, Rhodes S, Saravanan T, Ramamurthy V.
ai_summary:
Gene: HSP90 (HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1)
Finding: Cytosolic HSP90 paralogs are redundantly required for photoreceptor outer segment development and vision, with loss of both paralogs abolishing outer segment morphogenesis and visual responses, correlating with reduced peripherin levels.
Disease: Photoreceptor degeneration and visual dysfunction

title: Drugging Ras trafficking-are there new roads to travel?
authors: Schaffner-Reckinger E, Gómez-Mulas A, Abankwa DK.
ai_summary: Ras trafficking inhibition was the first clinical strategy to target Ras, but direct Ras inhibitors have made this approach seem outdated. However, targeting specific trafficking hubs may still offer unique therapeutic opportunities, particularly if we better understand how Ras functions in distinct organelles linked to processes like cell differentiation. The article discusses these future prospects.

title: Stepwise firing mechanism of an extracellular contractile injection system.
authors: Xu J, Ericson CF, Toenshoff ER, Pilhofer M.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no specific gene link reported)
Finding: This study describes the stepwise firing mechanism of the extracellular contractile injection system from Algoriphagus machipongonensis (AlgoCIS), revealing that signal propagation begins with tail-fiber binding, followed by cage opening, baseplate iris expansion, and ultimately sheath contraction and cap adaptor release.
Disease: Not applicable (no disease or phenotype link reported)

title: Nursing Management of Repeated Extubation Failure Following Colonic Volvulus Surgery in a Patient with Alstrom Syndrome: A Case Report.
authors: Shen Y, Chen Y, Fu X, Jiang W, Li J.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALMS1 (implied by Alström syndrome diagnosis)
Finding: A patient with Alström syndrome experienced repeated extubation failure after colonic volvulus surgery, successfully managed with multidisciplinary airway care and systematic weaning on the third attempt.
Disease: Alström syndrome with postoperative respiratory complications

title: Enhancing cancer classification accuracy with a self-attention network using panel capture sequencing data.
authors: Jia Y, Zhang C, Zhang H, Dong K, Hu Y, Wang Y, Zhao Z.
ai_summary: Short plain-language summary: This study presents a self-attention-based machine learning model that classifies cancer types from panel capture sequencing data with over 90% accuracy, identifying key genes and pathways that may improve precision oncology and cancer biology understanding.

title: A Comparative Study of Caerin 1.1/1.9 and Calcium Hydroxide in the Treatment of Apical Periodontitis in Rats.
authors: Qin L, You H, Zhang Z, Sun J, Fu Q, Rong M, Lin Z, Li H, Wang T, Ni G, Liu X, Yang W.
ai_summary: Caerin 1.1/1.9 hydrogel and calcium hydroxide paste both reduced inflammation and bone resorption in a rat model of apical periodontitis, but the peptide gel showed a more favorable trend in regulating key inflammatory cytokines (IL-17, TNF-α, IL-6) and bone-related markers (osteoclasts, OPG). This suggests caerin 1.1/1.9 may be a promising alternative therapy for refractory apical periodontitis.

title: A macrophage MHC-I axis links intratumoral heterogeneity to terminal CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell exhaustion in lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Yin S, Gao H, Li Q, Wang M, Zhang P, Guo Y, Nan P, Kong W, Shen H, Wang L, Lu J.
ai_summary:
Gene: CENPF
Finding: CENPF is part of a six-gene decision-tree classifier (with CDC45, PCLAF, SCGB3A1, CDCA8, and NDC80) that predicts intratumoral heterogeneity and CD8+ T-cell exhaustion phenotypes in lung adenocarcinoma.
Disease: Lung adenocarcinoma

title: Consequences of the Novel ALS-Associated KIF5A Variant c.2993-6C > A for Exon 27 Splicing and Axonal Transport of SFPQ.
authors: Rouleau GA, Yu Z, Ross JP, Rochefort D, Li B, Bornais K, Chum M, Farhan SMK, Dion PA.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF5A
Finding: The novel intronic variant c.2993-6C > A induces exon 27 skipping, abolishes axonal transport of the cargo SFPQ, and leads to TDP-43 proteinopathy in motor neurons under stress.
Disease: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)

title: Monitoring biological effects of somatic cell genome editing.
authors: Freedman BS, Bulte JWM, Conklin BR, Judge LM, Dwinell MR, Geurts AM, Sitton MJ, Mahajan V, Kiani S, Gersbach CA, Ebrahimkhani MR, Kelly JJ, Ronald JA, Morizane R, Gupta N, Shakeri-Zadeh A, Vo N, Saha K, Saxena S, Gamm DM, Sinha D, Tarantal AF, Vandsburger M, Matsubara A, Fu H, Tsai SQ, SCGE Dissemination and Coordinating Center Toolkit Team, SCGE Biological Effects Initiative.
ai_summary: This is a review article discussing technologies for monitoring the safety and efficacy of CRISPR-based genome editing therapeutics as they move from preclinical studies to clinical use. It covers methods ranging from direct measurement of editing outcomes in DNA, to organoids and organs-on-chips for phenotypic evaluation, and non-invasive imaging to track editors and edited cells in vivo. The authors conclude that these complementary technologies provide insights across biological scales, from single nucleotides to whole organisms, helping bridge preclinical development with clinical trials.

title: Ginsenoside Rb1 inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis to alleviate salpingitis infertility by down-regulating PTGS2 and up-regulating GPX4.
authors: Wang Y, Kuang J.
ai_summary:
Gene: GPX4
Finding: Ginsenoside Rb1 alleviates salpingitis infertility by down-regulating PTGS2 and up-regulating GPX4, which inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, improving pregnancy outcomes.
Disease: Salpingitis infertility

title: Genome-Wide Association Study for Glucocorticoid-Induced Ocular Hypertension.
authors: Lama J, Liu R, Huerta-Chagoya A, Li A, Huynh K, Stanwyck LK, Han S, Zhao Y, Chan W, Chen L, Mukundan A, Meng D, Yang JY, Susarla G, Sang D, Papaliodis GN, Shen LQ, Rossin E, Elkins C, Benavides I, Wafapoor H, Cutino A, Wiggs JL, Eaton AM, Segrè AV, Sobrin L.
ai_summary:
Gene: UBE2E3 (and MSTO1)
Finding: Common variants in the UBE2E3 locus are genome-wide significantly associated with maximal intraocular pressure change within 6 months after glucocorticoid exposure, with supporting expression regulation evidence; MSTO1 passed false discovery rate correction in rare variant burden analysis.
Disease: Glucocorticoid-induced ocular hypertension

title: Invoking ferroptosis and photon-controlled pyroptosis via an integrated therapeutic system for triple-pathway tumor therapy.
authors: Lou X, Liu W, Yang M, Zhang H, Fan J, Peng X.
ai_summary:
Gene: GPX4
Finding: A redox-responsive integrated therapeutic system (QSH) releases a dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibitor and a photosensitiser to trigger GPX4-mediated ferroptosis, DHODH-disrupted ferroptosis, and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, completely suppressing tumor growth in 4T1 breast cancer models.
Disease: Breast cancer (4T1 tumor model)

title: Astragalus polysaccharide mitigates the airway inflammation in bronchial asthma by regulating Hedgehog/NLRP3/GSDMD pathway.
authors: Yu L, Liu Z, Zhang R, Lai J.
journal: The Korean journal of physiology & pharmacology : official journal of the Korean Physiological Society and the Korean Society of Pharmacology
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI1
Finding: Astragalus polysaccharide reduces airway inflammation and remodeling in ovalbumin-induced asthma mice by downregulating the Hedgehog/NLRP3/GSDMD pathway, including decreased expression of GLI1.
Disease: Bronchial asthma

title: Fraxini cortex (Qinpi): reframing a traditional heat-clearing botanical drug as a systemic immune-metabolic regulator.
authors: Xin P, Fan YH, Xu JY, Mao SJ, Zhang JW, Luo ZL, Zhou X.
ai_summary: Fraxini Cortex (Qinpi), a traditional Chinese medicine, is reinterpreted as a systemic immune-metabolic regulator rather than merely an anti-inflammatory agent. Its constituents (coumarins, secoiridoids, phenylethanoid glycosides) are proposed to act on multiple targets—including GPI, Sortase A, urate transporters, and insulin signaling—while suppressing NF-κB/MAPK and activating Nrf2. Preliminary clinical evidence supports benefits in psoriasis and gouty arthritis, though low oral bioavailability of key coumarins remains a challenge.

title: Research on the Mechanism of Natural Products Acting on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
authors: Wei S, Liu X.
ai_summary: Natural products show promise for treating chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) by targeting multiple disease mechanisms, including oxidative stress, chronic airway inflammation, airway remodeling, and excessive mucus secretion. This review examines about 80 natural compounds from plants, microorganisms, animals, and marine organisms, summarizing over 350 references to analyze their potential therapeutic mechanisms and highlighting their multi-target effects and good biological safety as advantages over current clinical drugs.

title: Core conformation of arrestin coupling to parathyroid hormone type 1 receptor.
authors: Zhai X, Guo J, Shen Q, Chen LN, Wang G, Shen DD, Zhang C, Xu X, Mao C, Zhang Y, Liu Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: PTH1R
