Finding: Cryo-EM structures reveal a distinctive β-arrestin1 core coupling mode to PTH1R, involving TM6 kinking and TM5/ICL2 outward movement, which mediates receptor internalization and trafficking.
Disease: Parathyroid hormone receptor signaling (no specific disease named)

title: The Positive Roles for Reactive Oxygen Species in Human Reproduction; Implications for the Therapeutic Application of Antioxidants.
authors: Pyneandee EM, Bakos HW, De Iuliis GN, Aitken RJ.
ai_summary: Short plain-language summary: This review argues that reactive oxygen species (ROS) play essential positive roles in human reproduction, contrary to their usual portrayal as harmful. ROS are critical for processes such as sperm chromatin cross-linking, ovulation, implantation, and signal transduction, and they also help defend against infections and mediate cell death pathways. The authors caution that antioxidant therapy for infertility should be used carefully to avoid inducing reductive stress, which could impair reproductive success.

title: Parkinson's Disease: Conventional Pharmacotherapy, Drug Delivery Innovations, and Emerging Therapeutic Targets.
authors: Raina D, Marwah C, Singh S, Akhtar A.
ai_summary: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder marked by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra, leading to motor and non-motor symptoms. Current therapy is symptomatic, centered on levodopa and other dopaminergic drugs, but limited by motor fluctuations and adverse effects. This review covers conventional drug classes, formulation and delivery innovations (e.g., intestinal gel, continuous infusion) to stabilize drug exposure, and emerging therapeutic targets for future treatments.

title: The gut-liver-kidney-brain axis in Wilson disease: copper speciation-flux and barrier-mediated organ crosstalk.
authors: Qian N, Zhu S, Song Y, Yang Y, Wang H, Han H, Xu G, Hao W, Jiang H, Yang Y, Xi H, Ding Y, He W, Wei T, Yang W, Cheng T.
ai_summary:
Gene: ATP7B
Finding: Copper speciation and flux across gut, liver, kidney, and brain barriers—driven by ATP7B deficiency—disrupt barrier integrity, suppress autophagy, alter FXR signaling, and promote gut dysbiosis, cuproptosis, and multi-organ toxicity.
Disease: Wilson disease

title: Reactive Oxygen Species-Induced Damage in Cryopreserved Bovine Sperm: Mitigation Strategies.
authors: Akhtar MM, Hossain S, Meem AM, Lubaba AF, Kazal MKH.
ai_summary: Cryopreservation of bovine sperm induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction due to osmotic stress, ice crystal formation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative burst, leading to lipid peroxidation, protein oxidation, DNA fragmentation, and mitochondrial damage that reduce sperm motility, viability, and fertilization capacity. The review summarizes mitigation strategies, including enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidants, plant extracts, nanoparticles, mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, and non-antioxidant approaches, which can effectively curb oxidative damage and improve post-thaw sperm quality for artificial insemination and in vitro fertilization programs.

title: Adaptive restoration of T-cell motility by cold acclimation through metabolic and transcriptional remodeling.
authors: Hattori M, Onishi N, Sato T, Nakakura T, Suzuki T.
ai_summary: Cold temperatures suppress T-cell motility, but prior exposure to low temperatures induces cold acclimation that restores migratory activity. Acclimated T cells show enhanced motility at low temperatures, increased mitochondrial spare respiratory capacity, and extensive transcriptional reprogramming involving upregulation of ribosome biogenesis and protein quality control pathways alongside downregulation of DNA replication and cell cycle genes. This demonstrates that temperature actively regulates immune cell dynamics through metabolic and transcriptional remodeling rather than acting solely as an environmental constraint.

title: Interactions Between Plant-Derived Psychoactive Substances and Escherichia coli.
authors: Wróblewska J, Długosz A, Modrzejewska M, Wróblewski M, Czarnecki D, Woźniak A.
ai_summary: This is a review article examining how plant-derived psychoactive substances (opioids, cocaine, cannabinoids) affect Escherichia coli and the microbiota-gut-brain axis. The authors focus on how these substances may alter gut microbiota, modulate immune responses, and influence inflammatory processes that could contribute to addiction pathogenesis. No specific gene-disease link is established; the article is a literature review of interactions between psychoactive compounds, E. coli, and neuroimmunological mechanisms.

title: Giardia unveiled: a proteome view of the parasite in search of drug, vaccine and diagnostic targets.
authors: González-López L, Rodríguez-Lima O, Blancas-Luciano BE, Rosendo-Pineda MJ, Velázquez Zavala NG, Vaca L, Cabrera-Bravo M, Cruz-Reséndiz A.
ai_summary: Giardiasis remains a major global health problem due to limited diagnostics, drug resistance, and no licensed vaccine. This review comprehensively analyzes the Giardia proteome, detailing structural proteins (tubulin and giardins) essential for attachment, the secretome (cathepsin B-like proteases and variant-specific surface proteins) involved in immune evasion and host damage, and metabolic/encystation enzymes (carbamate kinase, fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase) with high therapeutic potential. The authors identify high-priority molecular targets for developing new drugs, vaccines, and diagnostics against this neglected disease.

title: Micro- and Nanoplastics as Emerging Drivers of Liver Injury: Exposure, Evidence, and Mechanisms.
authors: Badach M, Banaszek J, Barańska K, Kleinrok J, Flieger M, Flieger J, Teresiński G, Forma A, Sitarz R, Baj J.
ai_summary: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are emerging environmental contaminants that can reach the liver after ingestion or inhalation, where they accumulate due to portal blood flow and Kupffer cell activity. Experimental evidence indicates that MNPs may cause hepatic injury through oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and disrupted lipid metabolism, potentially contributing to steatosis, cholestasis, and fibrosis. While human biomonitoring has detected MNPs in blood and liver, current data remain limited and methodologically heterogeneous, so more comprehensive human studies are needed to confirm their role in liver pathology.

title: Advancements in Drug Delivery Systems in Glioblastoma Therapy.
authors: Mishra P, Gupta P, Markowska A, Ghavami S, Markowski J, Łos MJ.
ai_summary: Glioblastoma is a highly aggressive brain tumor whose treatment is limited by the blood-brain barrier and tumor heterogeneity. This review examines recent advances in drug delivery systems—including nanoparticles, hydrogels, extracellular vesicles, and microneedles—that improve blood-brain barrier penetration, tumor targeting, and controlled drug release in preclinical models. It also highlights key translational challenges such as large-scale production, off-target effects, and M2 macrophage induction, and discusses future strategies that integrate tumor stress responses into drug carrier design.

title: DYRK1A and Parkinson's disease, facts and hypotheses.
authors: Meijer L, Lindberg MF, Hogrel G, Khor B.
ai_summary:
Gene: DYRK1A
Finding: DYRK1A is a risk factor for Parkinson's disease, phosphorylates at least 20 PD-related proteins, and its inhibitors show protective effects in PD models.
Disease: Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

title: Liprin-α family proteins and their cellular functions.
authors: Mayer A, Zhang Y, Xia H.
ai_summary: Liprin-α proteins are scaffold proteins that organize subcellular compartments and regulate diverse functions, including presynaptic active zone formation, synaptic vesicle accumulation, neurotransmitter release, postsynaptic dendritic growth, spinogenesis, AMPA receptor trafficking, and cell adhesion/motility. They act through multivalent interactions and liquid-liquid phase separation to form membrane-less compartments, and their function is regulated by specific mechanisms.

title: Glycolipid MPIase, Essential for Membrane Protein Integration in the Cytoplasmic Membrane of Escherichia coli, Protects Membranes from Aggregation Induced by Chemicals.
authors: Sawasato K, Furuya S, Mori S, Osawa T, Fujikawa K, Nomura K, Fujimoto T, Shimamoto K, Nishiyama KI.
ai_summary:
Gene: MPIase (Membrane Protein Integrase)
Finding: The glycolipid MPIase, identified as a Biomembrane-Protecting Factor, prevents chemical-induced aggregation of biological membranes, with activity dependent on sugar chain length and pyrophosphate linker, while 6-O-acetylation reduces this protective function.
Disease: Not applicable (membrane protection for drug delivery and nucleic acid vaccines)

title: AtHSPR Plays a Positive Role in Arabidopsis Resistance Against Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 by Interacting with TOP1.
authors: Bian Z, Gao H, Wu H, Yang T.
ai_summary:
Gene: AtHSPR
Finding: AtHSPR interacts with TOP1 to positively regulate salicylic acid-mediated immune responses, enhancing Arabidopsis resistance against Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000.
Disease: Bacterial speck disease (Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 infection)

title: Multiple Roles of Protamine Kinase SRPK1 and Phosphatase PP1γ in Sperm Development.
authors: de la Iglesia A, Blanco M, Jodar M, Feudjio O, Leduc M, Castillo J, Cocquet J, Oliva R.
ai_summary:
Gene: SRPK1, PP1γ (PP1γ2)
Finding: Novel testicular protein interactomes of SRPK1 and PP1γ2 reveal interactions with splicing regulators (ASF/SF2), posttranscriptional regulators (PABP1, IGF2BP3), the R2TP chaperone component PIH1D1, and gene expression regulators (ILF2, TBLX1R1), suggesting additional roles in spermatogenesis beyond protamine phosphorylation.
Disease: Male infertility (defective chromatin structure)

title: A sequential MAP kinase cascade regulates mechanical signalling.
authors: Tran HC, Darwish E, Johansson V, Fernandez-Milmanda G, Zhu T, Fonseca de Lima CF, Van De Cotte B, Colcombet J, Vuylsteke M, De Smet I, Goossens A, Van Aken O.
ai_summary: This study identifies a MAP kinase cascade (MAPKKK3/4/5-MKK4/5-MPK3/6) that is activated within 60 seconds of mechanical stimulation in plants, leading to the induction of ~800 genes, most of which overlap with touch-responsive genes regulated by CAMTA transcription factors. Loss of MKK4/5 impairs touch-regulated protein phosphorylation and reduces thigmomorphogenesis, while the cascade does not clearly affect early jasmonic acid signaling. The findings establish this MAPK cascade as a key touch- and wounding signaling pathway in plants.

title: GALNT1 drives aggressive phenotypes of rheumatoid synoviocytes via NEK9 O-glycosylation.
authors: Zou Y, Lin H, Su J, Wang J, Zeng Q, Feng T, Lei Y, Ma J, Pan H, Xu H, Dai L, Li Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: GALNT1
Finding: GALNT1-mediated O-glycosylation of NEK9 drives aggressive phenotypes of rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes by promoting cytoskeleton reorganization and restraining ER stress, and its suppression reduces arthritis severity in a rat model.
Disease: Rheumatoid arthritis

title: Retinoic acid drives cell fate specification, maturation and retinal regionality in human retinal organoids.
authors: Lim BY, Chen C, Fredericks A, Nilli E, Mesa Mora S, Weatherstone M, Loi TH, Newman P, Aryamanesh N, Zreiqat H, Tam P, Yang P, Gonzalez-Cordero A.
ai_summary: Retinoic acid (RA) is a key morphogen in human retinal development, but its concentration-dependent effects on cell fate and regional identity were poorly understood. Using human retinal organoids, the authors show that temporal and dosage-dependent modulation of RA alters the abundance and maturation of photoreceptors and interneurons, as revealed by single-cell transcriptomics. Spatial transcriptomics further shows that low RA levels bias organoids toward a macular-like identity, while high RA levels promote peripheral-like development, highlighting RA's critical role in retinal maturation and regional specification with implications for disease modeling and photoreceptor transplantation.

title: Proteomic signatures of retinal pigment epithelium-derived exosomes in myopic and non-myopic tree shrew eyes.
authors: Sanchez NC, Roig-Lopez JL, Mobley JA, Khanal S.
ai_summary: This study compared the proteomic profiles of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)-derived exosomes from myopic versus non-myopic tree shrew eyes. Using mass spectrometry, the authors identified 506 exosomal proteins, with 286 differentially expressed between the groups, including upregulation of Histone H4, PTB 1, and Histone H3.1, and downregulation of RPS5, ACOT7, and CRYBB2, along with depletion of crystallin family proteins. Enrichment analyses highlighted extracellular matrix, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cell-matrix adhesion as key components. The findings provide the first demonstration of ex-vivo RPE exosome biogenesis in tree shrews and suggest that distinct exosomal protein signatures may mediate growth signal transmission in the emmetropization pathway, offering potential targets for understanding myopia mechanisms.

title: Ana1/Cep295 regulates centriole elongation via Cep135 and microtubules.
authors: Wang Z, Qian Y, Wang X, Ng Q, Zhang H, Wu Y, Liu Z, Feng Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP295 (Ana1)
Finding: Ana1/Cep295 promotes centriole elongation in fly spermatocytes through two distinct mechanisms: direct interaction with Cep135 to recruit it into the proximal centriole-like structure, and microtubule binding/bundling activity, both of which contribute to centriole overelongation.
Disease: Centriole elongation defects (relevant to centrosome and cilium formation)

title: The C9orf72/SMCR8 complex maintains microglial homeostasis via RAB8A-ESCRT-mediated lysosomal repair.
authors: Li S, Xu S, Li F, Zhao Q, Zhang P, Guan Q, Sun X, Bi J, Xiao H, Tang Y, Peng C, Chen Q, Wang Y, Yang M.
ai_summary:
Gene: C9orf72/SMCR8
Finding: The C9orf72/SMCR8 complex maintains microglial homeostasis by promoting RAB8A-ESCRT-mediated lysosomal membrane repair; its loss causes age-dependent neuroinflammation, microgliosis, and accumulation of damaged lysosomes.
Disease: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia (ALS/FTD)

title: Association of serum coiled-coil domain containing protein 11 levels with coronary artery disease.
authors: Gao J, Wang H, Wang W, Hu W, Yan P, Lu J, Liu Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC11
Finding: Elevated serum CCDC11 levels are independently associated with the presence and severity of coronary artery disease, with levels increasing across single-, double-, and triple-vessel disease subgroups.
Disease: Coronary artery disease

title: Pathogenesis of Neovascular Glaucoma in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Review.
authors: Wang X, Liu S, Wu Q, Lv Y, Yi S, Shi B, Wu Z, Yan J.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (pathway-level review; VEGF-A, PlGF, HIF-1α, PEDF, IL-6, TNF-α, TGF-β discussed)
Finding: Neovascular glaucoma in diabetic retinopathy arises from ischemia-induced upregulation of VEGF-A and PlGF, downregulation of PEDF, and inflammation/fibrosis leading to refractory intraocular pressure elevation and optic nerve damage.
Disease: Neovascular glaucoma secondary to diabetic retinopathy

title: Unveiling natural anti-inflammatory compounds for sinusitis treatments by modulating FOXP3, C5aR1, and LIF.
authors: Cao C, Hossen MA, Efti MS, Warda AA, AlJaouni SK, ElFar A, Lv C.
ai_summary:
Gene: FOXP3, C5aR1, LIF
Finding: Natural anti-inflammatory compounds (e.g., epigallocatechin-3-gallate, curcumin, rosmarinic acid, bromelain, cineole) can modulate the FOXP3-C5aR1-LIF regulatory axis to restore immune tolerance in chronic rhinosinusitis.
Disease: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS)

title: Exploring Biomarkers and Regulatory Mechanisms Associated with Lytic Cell Death in Allergic Rhinitis Based on Transcriptome Analysis.
authors: Dong R, Dong Z, Geng Z, Lu L, Ji Y, Xue J.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALOX15, TIMP1
Finding: ALOX15 and TIMP1 are significantly upregulated in allergic rhinitis patients and identified as exploratory biomarkers linked to lytic cell death, with roles in immune infiltration and regulatory networks.
Disease: Allergic rhinitis

title: The roles and functions of TMEM protein family members in cancers, cardiovascular and kidney diseases (Review).
authors: Xu H, Yang S, Liu P, Zhang Y, Zhang T, Lan J, Jiang H, Wu D, Li J, Bai X.
ai_summary:
This is a general review of the TMEM protein family across multiple diseases, without establishing a specific gene-disease link. 

TMEM proteins are membrane proteins involved in organelle formation, enzymatic activity, and signaling, and they regulate the development of various cancers, cardiovascular diseases, and kidney diseases. The review summarizes their roles and biological functions in these conditions, suggesting that better understanding of TMEM molecular mechanisms could aid disease prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

title: Development of Bispecific Antibody Targeting Human IL-17A and IL-6.
authors: Pamuła B, Banach M, Mikońska M, Korytkowska K, Lacek K, Śniadała O, Marczak M, Flis K, Sowińska A, Kołakowski D, Pieczykolan J, Zygmunt B, Wieczorek M, Abramczyk O.
ai_summary: This study describes the development of bispecific VHH-based antibodies that simultaneously target human IL-6 and IL-17A, two cytokines involved in autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases. Using phage display screening of llama-derived VHH libraries, the authors identified high-affinity binders for both cytokines and assembled them into bispecific antibody formats. The resulting constructs inhibited both cytokine signaling pathways in functional reporter assays and showed good stability and purity, suggesting their potential as therapeutic agents for inflammatory diseases.

title: Preclinical Models of Rare Corneal and Ocular Surface Diseases: a Comprehensive Narrative Review.
authors: Lecchi EAL, Dashti A, Frutos-Rincón L, Palombella S, Pederzolli M, Gallar J, Lagali N, Ferrari G.
ai_summary: This review summarizes the experimental platforms available for studying rare corneal and ocular surface diseases (REDs), including in vitro models (cell systems, cocultures, organoids), in vivo genetic and surgical models, and emerging technologies like organ-on-chip and AI-assisted analytics. It compares the strengths, limitations, and translational value of these approaches to optimize preclinical modeling of REDs pathophysiology and support therapeutic development.

title: JAK-STAT pathway-associated skin diseases: a refined functional framework for inflammatory skin diseases.
authors: Li B, Song X, Shan C, He J, Wang Z, Stevanovic K, Zuberbier T, Zhao Z, Zhang L.
ai_summary: This article reviews the role of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway in inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, alopecia areata, and vitiligo. It highlights the efficacy of JAK inhibitors (e.g., abrocitinib, upadacitinib, baricitinib) in treating these conditions and proposes a new functional classification framework that integrates JAK-dependent cytokine modules into the traditional T helper immune axis to better guide targeted therapy. The authors aim to improve mechanistic understanding and rational clinical use of JAK inhibitors.

title: Post-translational modification networks as master regulators of influenza virus replication, host adaptation, and immune evasion.
authors: Jin C, Zhang B, Gao Y.
ai_summary: Influenza viruses use coordinated post-translational modification (PTM) networks—including phosphorylation, ubiquitination, SUMOylation, glycosylation, acetylation, lipidation, and RNA methylation—to regulate viral replication, host adaptation, and immune evasion. These PTMs modulate polymerase activity, ribonucleoprotein trafficking, viral glycoprotein antigenic evolution, and host metabolic environments. The review highlights PTM-modulating enzymes as promising targets for host-directed antiviral and vaccine strategies, though the relevance of specific PTM events during human infection remains incompletely defined.

title: Postbiotics as Multifunctional Bioactives: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Applications in Host Physiology and Microbial Ecosystem Modulation.
authors: Babysulatha Sasidharan N, Hely S, John S, Arun K, Raveendran NJ, Rishitha G, Kumar SS, Nair KA, Pal S, Sunilkumar D, Nair BG, Prakash V.
ai_summary: Postbiotics are microbial-derived bioactive compounds that offer health benefits without the risks of live microbes. This review summarizes their mechanisms, including modulation of GPCRs, NF-κB, and epigenetic pathways, and their potential therapeutic applications in cancer, autoimmune, and metabolic diseases, as well as localized effects on tissue repair and collagen remodeling. The authors also highlight the expanding role of postbiotics in sustainable agriculture and environmental biotechnology, positioning them as a versatile tool bridging microbiome regulation, precision medicine, and sustainability.

title: Host-microbiome interactions in breast cancer progression and treatment response.
authors: Bautista J, Lara-Hernández ME, Hidalgo-De La Cruz M, Andino-Araque V, León-Rivera M, López-Cortés A.
ai_summary: Microbiome composition in breast tissue, the gut, and the oral cavity may influence breast cancer progression and treatment response through metabolic, inflammatory, and endocrine pathways, including microbial estrogen deconjugation and immune regulation, though methodological challenges remain.

title: Genotoxic Bacteria and Oncogenic Viruses in Colorectal Cancer: Evidence, Gaps, and a Proposed Interaction Model.
authors: Salazar-Ulbrich N, Haro-Solis D, Aguayo F, Quezada-Monrás C, Cárcamo L, Collado L, Carrillo-Beltrán D.
ai_summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis is increasingly linked to microbial contributions, with genotoxigenic bacteria (e.g., Escherichia coli, Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori) causing DNA damage and chronic inflammation, while oncogenic viruses (e.g., JC polyomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, human papillomavirus) are detected in colorectal tissues and affect cell cycle and DNA repair. The review proposes that bacterial genotoxins may reactivate persistent viruses via DNA damage-induced stress and NF-κB- or ATM-dependent signaling, suggesting a potential genotoxic collaboration between bacteria and viruses in colorectal tumorigenesis, though this interaction remains underexplored and could yield novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: From Leaky Gut to a Vulnerable Brain: Obesity-Associated Gut Barrier Failure in Colorectal Cancer and Cognitive Dysfunction.
authors: Lee SY, Cho SH, Song J.
ai_summary: Obesity promotes colorectal cancer (CRC) and cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) through a proposed "two-barrier failure" model: obesity-induced gut microbial dysbiosis and intestinal barrier disruption allow microbial products like lipopolysaccharide to enter circulation, driving chronic systemic inflammation that accelerates CRC progression and, via the gut-brain axis, disrupts the blood-brain barrier, activates microglia/astrocytes, and impairs synaptic plasticity—manifesting as cognitive deficits in attention, processing speed, and working memory. The review synthesizes in vivo, in vitro, and human evidence, and discusses barrier-targeted therapeutic strategies (probiotics, postbiotics, SCFAs, dietary/weight interventions, pharmacological approaches) and testable clinical trial designs, while noting that direct clinical causality remains unproven.

title: Deciphering the Role of Innate Lymphoid Cells Group 3 in the Gut Microenvironment: A Narrative Review of Their Novel Contributions to Autoimmune Disease Pathogenesis.
authors: Wang H, Wang T, He Z, Wen C, Huang L, Wang M.
ai_summary: Type 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) are key intestinal immune effectors that protect against pathogens and maintain mucosal barrier integrity, but their dysregulation is linked to autoimmune disease pathogenesis. This narrative review examines how gut microbes, metabolites, and diet interact with ILC3s in the gut microenvironment, and how these interactions may influence distant sites and autoimmune disease risk, highlighting a poorly understood but promising area of research.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Allergy: From Cellular Communication to Clinical Implications.
authors: Sysak A, Górska S.
ai_summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are lipid bilayer-enclosed particles that mediate intercellular communication by transferring bioactive cargo such as proteins, lipids, and microRNAs. In allergic diseases, EVs from epithelial, immune, and microbiota-associated cells regulate immune homeostasis and inflammatory responses, contributing to the initiation and persistence of allergic inflammation. The review highlights disease-specific EV cargo alterations as promising non-invasive biomarkers and discusses the therapeutic potential of EVs as cell-free immunomodulatory agents, synthesizing evidence across asthma, atopic dermatitis, and food allergy.

title: Germ cells are essential for testicular morphogenesis and functional reconstruction in a porcine xenograft model.
authors: Han MG, Jeon Y, Maeng H, Kim D, Do JT, Hong K, Choi Y, Song H.
ai_summary: Germ cells, specifically porcine spermatogonial stem cells, are indispensable for initiating and stabilizing testicular morphogenesis and functional spermatogenesis in a xenograft model, as tissues containing germ cells developed well-organized seminiferous tubules with multiple spermatogenic stages, whereas germ-cell-depleted tissues remained fragmented and poorly organized.

title: Across Kingdoms: The Bacteriome, Mycobiome, and Virome in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Therapeutic Perspectives, and the Emerging Role of COVID-19.
authors: Posta E, Gyarmati E, Majoros L, Fekete I, Varkonyi I, Zold E, Barta Z.
ai_summary: The gut ecosystem—comprising bacteria, fungi, and viruses—is increasingly recognized as a key interface in autoimmune and immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), where dysbiosis can influence immunity through barrier failure, altered metabolite signaling, molecular mimicry, and cross-kingdom interactions. Bacteriome data are most mature, while mycobiome and virome findings remain emerging and disease-specific. This narrative review integrates evidence across systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, Sjögren's syndrome, systemic sclerosis, spondyloarthritis, vasculitides, and myopathies), discusses COVID-19 as an environmental insult that can perturb microbiome-barrier-immune communication without proven causal autoimmunity, and highlights diet-based and microbiome-targeted therapies (probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, postbiotics) as adjunctive strategies to restore microbial resilience and immune balance.

title: Microglial PD-1/PD-L1 axis in CNS demyelinating diseases: a dual immunoregulatory perspective.
authors: Zhou M, Yao X, Liu L, Gao Y, Chen W, Zheng K, Li H, Meng Q.
ai_summary: Microglial PD-1/PD-L1 signaling acts as a dual immunomodulatory rheostat in CNS demyelinating diseases, capable of both exacerbating neuroinflammation and promoting tissue repair. This review examines how the PD-1/PD-L1 axis on microglia and T cells dampens immune activation and induces T cell exhaustion in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for modulating microglial polarization and developing precision immunotherapies.

title: Herbal Polyphenolic Mixtures as Antioxidant and Cytoprotective Agents in Respiratory Diseases: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
authors: Sergazy S, Shulgau Z, Nurgaziyev M, Nurgaziyeva A, Baurzhan M, Kairgeldina S, Gulyayev A.
ai_summary: Herbal polyphenolic mixtures show promise as antioxidant and cytoprotective agents for respiratory diseases by reducing oxidative stress through mechanisms such as Nrf2 activation and NF-κB suppression, but clinical use is limited by poor bioavailability and lack of standardization.

title: The Traditional Chinese Medicine Compound Hezi Qingyou Formula Controls the MAPK Signaling Pathway for Alleviating Gastric Ulcer Induced by Acetic Acid in Rats.
authors: Feng Z, Wei R, Tian J, Li H, Chen H, Hao Y, Chen M, Su B, Lai Y, Xun M, Zhang G, Yao M.
ai_summary: Hezi Qingyou Formula (HZQYF), a traditional Chinese medicine, was tested in a rat model of acetic acid-induced gastric ulcers. The treatment reduced ulcer area, promoted tissue repair, and suppressed inflammation by downregulating MAPK pathway phosphorylation (P-P38, P-JNK1/2, ERK1/2) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α), while increasing gastric repair factors (VEGF, EGF, TFF2, PGE2) and antioxidant activity (T-SOD), and decreasing MDA. Metabolomic analysis showed HZQYF normalized multiple metabolites in gastric tissue and feces, including taurine/hypotaurine and phenylalanine metabolism, suggesting its therapeutic potential for gastric ulcers via anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulation.

title: Potential role of the Trpv4 c.1491+1G>A mutation in pulmonary fibrosis in a gene-edited mouse model.
authors: Ruan H, Wang H, Zhu C, Li Z, ASu Y, Ji Z, Li Y, Gu L, Fu C, Yu H, Yue P.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: The Trpv4 c.1491+1G>A splice-site mutation reduces wild-type Trpv4 expression and exacerbates pulmonary fibrosis in a gene-edited mouse model, with altered lung cell composition and upregulation of ALCAM-CD6 and MIF-CD74 signaling.
Disease: Pulmonary fibrosis (associated with familial digital arthropathy-brachydactyly)

title: NF-κB-Dependent Transcriptional Regulation of Piezo1 Mediates Bacterial Clearance on Infected Lung Stiffness.
authors: Orsini EM, Boulton AM, Abraham S, Brown A, Ricci H, Ahuja A, Pant B, Snyder CM, Reinhardt A, Attaway AH, Musich R, Grove LM, Olman MA, Vachharajani V, Scheraga RG.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
ai_summary:
Gene: PIEZO1
Finding: NF-κB (p65) via MyD88 signaling upregulates Piezo1 transcription in macrophages during pneumonia, enhancing Ca2+ channel activity, Tfeb-mediated lysosome biogenesis, and stiffness-dependent phagolysosome maturation to promote bacterial clearance on infected stiffened lung matrix.
Disease: Pneumonia-induced lung injury

title: Mechanical regulation of microenvironment remodeling in brain tumors: from mechanism to therapy.
authors: Fan H, Xu C, He S, Wang J, Zhu H, Shu K.
ai_summary: Brain tumors develop in a uniquely soft mechanical microenvironment, where mechanical cues drive tumor progression and reshape the immune microenvironment to promote immunosuppression and treatment resistance. This review outlines how mechanical signaling regulates malignant behaviors and neuroinflammation, and summarizes mechano-targeting strategies as a promising approach to overcome immunotherapy resistance.

title: Cryogel-based therapeutic platforms for disease modification in osteoarthritis.
authors: Durant JA, Torres Gouveia ME, La Croix AE, Puninchittaya AR, Hixon KR.
ai_summary: Cryogels are porous, mechanically robust hydrogels being developed as therapeutic platforms for osteoarthritis (OA), a disease that currently lacks disease-modifying treatments. The review covers their use for stem cell delivery, release of bioactive molecules, localized gene activation, and immunomodulation, while highlighting key challenges for clinical translation.

title: Genetic and Clinical Spectrum of Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophies in Western Sicily.
authors: Rini N, Lupica A, Alonge P, Crescimanno G, Pignolo A, Messina C, Santa Paola S, Giuliano M, Borgione E, Lo Giudice M, Scuderi C, Di Stefano V, Brighina F.
ai_summary:
Gene: CAPN3
Finding: Pathogenic variants in CAPN3 were the most common cause of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy in a Western Sicilian cohort, associated with earlier onset and longer disease duration.
Disease: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy

title: Mesenchymal drift in ciliopathy iPSC-derived RPE reveals a convergent pathogenic cell state.
authors: Reichert D, Gul S, Ortolan D, McGaughey D, Montford J, Ryu J, Jeffrey AS, Lewallen CF, Veres K, Villasmil R, White Carreiro ND, Tsang SH, Huryn LA, Brooks BP, Zein W, May-Simera HL, Sharma R, Bharti K.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS1, BBS10, CEP290, LCA5
Finding: Ciliopathy iPSC-derived RPE from multiple gene mutations converge on a shared pathogenic cell state characterized by abnormal epithelial polarization and impaired mitochondrial health, driven by TGF-β signaling-mediated mesenchymal drift.
Disease: Ciliopathy-associated retinal degeneration

title: A Novel Homozygous Mutation in ARL2BP Causes Multiple Morphological Abnormalities of the Flagella and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Li M, Tao W, Ji Q, Yan D, Zhang C, Zhang Q, Jiang P, Qiu J, Wen J, Xu B, Bai S, Jiang X.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL2BP
Finding: A novel homozygous splice-site mutation (c.294-2A>G) causes aberrant splicing and nonsense-mediated decay, leading to complete loss of ARL2BP protein, flagellar axonemal disorganization with central pair microtubule depletion, and SPAG6 deficiency.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF)

title: Skeletal involvement in Joubert syndrome: From low bone mineral density to severe secondary osteoporosis.
authors: Babina T, Górczewska BA, Jakubowska-Pietkiewicz E.
ai_summary:
Gene: TMEM67, OFD1
Finding: TMEM67 and OFD1 mutations in Joubert syndrome are associated with a spectrum of skeletal involvement, ranging from low bone mineral density to severe secondary osteoporosis with fractures, likely exacerbated by hypotonia and immobility.
Disease: Joubert syndrome with skeletal complications (low bone mineral density and secondary osteoporosis)

title: Modeling Complex Developmental Disease: The Case of Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: DeLoriea J, Casey C, Shearer L, Chen V, Bryant A, Gamberi C.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2, PKHD1, NPHP (multiple genes)
Finding: Polycystic kidney diseases (ADPKD, ARPKD, NPH) share networked genes, modifiers, and developmental pathways, with partial phenotypic overlap, and Drosophila melanogaster is proposed as a reliable model for mechanistic and precision medicine studies.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD, ARPKD, nephronophthisis)

title: Prenatal molecularly supported diagnosis of a fetus with urinary malformation caused by novel compound heterozygous variants in the FAM149B1 gene.
authors: Liu J, Wu Y, Xu S, Qin Y, Li G, Chen Y, Li L, Liu F, Li S, Li N, Wang J.
ai_summary:
Gene: FAM149B1
Finding: Novel compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants (p.Tyr93* and p.Ser192Phefs*7) cause isolated prenatal urinary tract malformation without cerebellar or neuroimaging abnormalities.
Disease: Joubert syndrome-related ciliopathy with isolated urinary tract malformation

title: Hepatocyte Growth Factor in Children of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia and Its Relation to Disease Severity. A case-control study.
authors: Fouda EM, Barakat MMK, Kamel TB, Nabih ES, Barakat MMK, Ali HA, Hussein MM.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (HGF is a biomarker, not a disease-causing gene in this study)
Finding: Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage hepatocyte growth factor levels are significantly associated with disease severity in children with primary ciliary dyskinesia, with the modified Bhalla score independently predicting both serum and BAL HGF levels, and higher HGF correlating with lower lung function (FVC and FEV₁).
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: A Case of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia Caused by CFTR Gene and SFTPC Gene Variants.
authors: Yuan X, Shao D, Li Y, Ling J, Gong Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: CFTR; SFTPC
Finding: Heterozygous variants in CFTR (c.374T>C, p.Ile125Thr) and SFTPC (c.115G>T, p.Val39Leu) were identified in a child with recurrent respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, and abnormal ciliary ultrastructure, and are considered potentially associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Combined Liver-Kidney Transplantation in Pediatric Patients From Colombia: A Case Series.
authors: Padilla-Guzmán A, Ortega-Gamboa SA, Forero-Delgadillo JM, Ochoa-Jiménez VA, Portilla-Buenaventura AM, Mateus CJC, Botero-Osorio V, Pachajoa H, Restrepo JM.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHP3 (nephronophthisis type 3)
Finding: Combined liver-kidney transplantation was successfully performed in two pediatric patients with nephronophthisis type 3, achieving favorable long-term graft function and patient survival.
Disease: Nephronophthisis type 3

title: Evaluation of Pulmonary and Otological Manifestations in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia and Their Effect on Quality of Life.
authors: Yanaz M, Eralp EE, Yegit CY, Gulieva A, Kalyoncu M, Balci MS, Karabulut S, Aliyev N, Ozturk N, Ergenekon AP, Gokdemir Y, Yumusakhuylu AC, Ciprut A, Karadag B.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified
Finding: Sinopulmonary involvement and hearing manifestations, including impaired speech understanding in noise, are very common in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia and significantly impact health-related quality of life, particularly in adults.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)

title: Diagnosing the canvas: challenging the diagnosis of Prader-Willi syndrome in Eugenia Martínez Vallejo (1674-1699).
authors: Hamiel U, Pinhas-Hamiel O.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
ai_summary:
Gene: MC4R
Finding: Historical and auxological reanalysis of Eugenia Martínez Vallejo, including early hyperphagia and accelerated growth, challenges the Prader-Willi syndrome diagnosis and suggests melanocortin receptor 4 deficiency as a more compatible cause of isolated severe early-onset obesity.
Disease: Severe early-onset obesity (melanocortin receptor 4 deficiency)

title: A Rare Presentation of X-Linked Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia Due to Xq22.3 Deletion .
authors: Yan L, Su Y, Li H.
ai_summary:
Gene: Xq22.3 deletion (hemizygous)
Finding: A male pediatric patient with recurrent pulmonary infections, chronic sinusitis, and situs inversus carries an approximately 720.3 kb hemizygous deletion in the Xq22.3 region, consistent with a rare X-linked recessive form of primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Disease: X-linked primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Renal rupture associated with electrocution in a man with polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Rouah R, Matheux A, Cavard S, Loiseau M, Orillus E.
ai_summary: This case report describes a 43-year-old man with polycystic kidney disease (PKD) who died after electrocution from a high-voltage current. The autopsy revealed severe burns, blunt trauma from falling, and rupture of the right renal hilum causing massive blood loss. The authors discuss the potential role of the electric current in causing the renal rupture, suggesting that further investigation is needed in cases of electrocution involving patients with PKD.

title: An integrin beta-1-anchored bicaudal C1-polycystin-1 module essential for tubular morphogenesis in polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Streets AJ, Valluru MK, Smith D, Chang L, Ben-Dov IZ, Wilson SA, Toseland CP, Ong ACM.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: BICC1 and polycystin-1 form an integrin-beta1-anchored complex that regulates F-actin organization, cell adhesion, and migration via FBLIM1, with disruption of this module causing cytoskeletal abnormalities and cyst formation.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: Pregnancy and Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A GENKYST Study.
authors: Vigneau C, Morice S, Lemeur Y, Bayat S.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Comment on Yamazaki et al. Long-Term Effects of Tolvaptan in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: Predictors of Treatment Response and Safety over 6 Years of Continuous Therapy. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2024, 25, 2088.
authors: De Rosa LI, Catania M, Kola K, Vezzoli G, Brambilla Pisoni M, Farinone S, Manunta P, Sciarrone Alibrandi MT.
ai_summary: This is a comment/correspondence piece responding to a previously published study on tolvaptan treatment in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). It does not present new experimental findings or establish a gene-disease link. The comment likely discusses methodological or interpretive issues regarding the original study's conclusions on long-term tolvaptan efficacy and safety predictors, but the abstract provides no specific details.

title: Targeting Runx1 Slows Cyst Growth in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Zhang Y, Liu C, Liu J, Li LX, Torres V, Li X, Zhou JX.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
ai_summary:
Gene: RUNX1
Finding: Runx1 is upregulated in Pkd1 mutant renal epithelial cells via cAMP signaling, and its pharmacological inhibition with Ro5-3335 slows cyst growth by reducing proliferation, inflammation, and fibrosis while enhancing apoptosis.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Ciliary ARL13B Drives Cystogenesis in the Kidney via Its GEF Activity.
authors: Van Sciver RE, Forster A, Lewis LM, Caspary T.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL13B
Finding: Ciliary ARL13B drives Pkd1-dependent cystogenesis in the kidney via its ARL3 GEF activity, as loss of ciliary ARL13B or mutation of a critical GEF residue suppresses cyst formation, fibrosis, injury, and Wnt signaling.
Disease: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD)

title: The fibrocystin C-terminal domain inhibits Src/STAT3 signal induced cystogenesis of kidney epithelial cells.
authors: Hassan F, Hahnenstein ST, Kraus A, Buchholz B, Mukenhirn M, Honigmann A, Dafinger C, Liebau MC, Pokrant T, Faix J, Grund A, Haffner D, Ziegler WH.
journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: The fibrocystin C-terminal domain (FPCct) inhibits Src-mediated STAT3 phosphorylation and STAT3-dependent transcription, thereby suppressing the secretory phenotype and cystogenesis in kidney epithelial cells.
Disease: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD)

title: The autosomal road.
authors: Zieneldien T.

title: Association of semaglutide use with kidney outcomes in adults with ADPKD: A propensity score-matched real-world study.
authors: Chen TP, Tsai SF.
ai_summary: Semaglutide use in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) was associated with a higher follow-up creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and a lower risk of progression to stage 5 chronic kidney disease, but not with differences in end-stage kidney disease, acute kidney injury, or urinary tract infection. The authors caution that semaglutide-induced weight loss and muscle mass reduction may lower serum creatinine independently of true glomerular filtration, and that the observational design and potential confounding mean the findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

title: Role of the primary cilium in muscle tissue.
authors: Quezada ER, Morselli E, Buvinic S, Criollo A.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
ai_summary: Primary cilia act as sensory organelles that regulate signaling pathways (e.g., Hedgehog and Wnt) in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle, influencing satellite cell activation and regeneration, cardiac fibroblast fibrogenic responses, and vascular smooth muscle mechanosensation. Disruptions in ciliary structure or signaling are linked to impaired muscle regeneration, increased adipogenesis, and maladaptive tissue remodeling, highlighting their potential role in muscle disease.

title: Application of clinical exome sequencing in sperm donor screening in China.
authors: Huang J, Yu M, Yang J, Xue W, Zhang Z, Shi J, Shi W.
journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
ai_summary:
Gene: UGT1A, FLG, GJB2, SMN1
Finding: Clinical exome sequencing of 391 sperm donors identified that 95.14% carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant, with an average of 3.53 recessive genetic defects per donor, leading to rejection of 11.51% of donors.
Disease: Recessive, digenic recessive, complex inheritance, autosomal dominant, and X-linked genetic disorders

title: Dysfunction of Primary Cilium in Huntington's Disease: How Mutant Huntingtin Disrupts This Cellular Signaling Hub.
authors: Churkina AS, Shakhov AS, Alieva IB.
ai_summary:
Gene: HTT (huntingtin)
Finding: Mutant huntingtin disrupts PCM1 trafficking, causing primary cilium elongation and altered signaling pathways in neurons.
Disease: Huntington's disease

title: The primary cilium-autophagy axis in vascular homeostasis and cardiovascular disease: mechanistic crosstalk and evidence boundaries.
authors: Fu X, Zhou W, Zhang C, Bai Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: OFD1
Finding: Autophagy reciprocally regulates ciliary homeostasis through cilia-related proteins such as OFD1, contributing to the proposed primary cilium-autophagy axis in vascular pathophysiology.
Disease: Hypertension, atherosclerosis, and aortic aneurysm

title: Nationwide attribute-based cross-classification reveals distinct risk patterns of major complications in ADPKD.
authors: Kataoka H, Nishio S, Hoshino J, Hiromura K, Isaka Y, Muto S.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (ADPKD, not a single gene)
Finding: Attribute-based cross-classification of 12,466 ADPKD patients identified distinct risk patterns for major complications, such as intracranial aneurysms being more frequent in women and older individuals, and intracranial hemorrhage strongly associated with hypertension, supporting risk-stratified screening.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Targeted analysis of salicylate binding partners in renal epithelial cells reveals major AMPK dependency.
authors: Kanhai AA, Lodder K, Wisse LE, Louzao-Martinez L, Bange H, Price LS, Leonhard WN, Peters DJM.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular cell research
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Salicylate's beneficial effects on metabolism, proliferation, and inflammation in Pkd1-/- renal epithelial cells are largely AMPK-dependent, but it also exerts AMPK-independent effects including mitochondrial uncoupling and heme synthesis inhibition.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Biliary atresia-related liver fibrosis.
authors: Zhou T, Wang F, Sun P, Kong M.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1L1
Finding: Ciliopathy-related PKD1L1 is identified as a genetic susceptibility locus contributing to the pathogenesis of biliary atresia-associated liver fibrosis.
Disease: Biliary atresia

title: The dynamics of ciliogenesis in prepubertal mouse meiosis reveals new clues about testis maturation.
authors: Pérez-Moreno I, López-Jiménez P, Zapata-Polo H, Pérez-Martín S, López-Panadés M, Urtasun-Elizari J, Barbeito P, Roig I, Garcia-Gonzalo FR, Page J, Gómez R.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: Primary cilia in mouse spermatocytes are not present during the first wave of meiosis but appear only from day 20 postpartum, with cilia disassembly in late diplotene linked to Aurora kinase A and required for bipolar spindle assembly. Proteomic analysis identifies days 19–21 as a key developmental window for ciliogenesis and flagellogenesis, and ciliated spermatocytes are also found in human testes, indicating that ciliogenesis is developmentally regulated during testicular maturation.

title: Glucose Transporter Deficiency Syndrome Type 1 (Glut1-DS): New Insights From a Brazilian Cohort of Patients.
authors: Sobrinho LMF, Fontana JC, Lorea CF, van der Linden Júnior H, Leite ACS, Maia RE, Farret L, Moura de Souza CF, Poloni S, Poswar FO, Schwartz IVD, Sperb-Ludwig F.
ai_summary:
Gene: SLC2A1
Finding: A Brazilian cohort of 40 Glut1-DS patients harboring 31 distinct SLC2A1 variants (15 novel) shows that missense variants generally cause milder phenotypes than truncating variants, with intrafamilial variability and reduced penetrance observed.
Disease: Glucose transporter deficiency syndrome type 1 (Glut1-DS)

title: Diffusion MRI Radiomics Predict Renal Function Decline in ADPKD.
authors: Bargagli M, Altabella L, Fedon Vocaturo M, Negrelli R, Ambrosetti MC, Puppini G, Cavedon C, Scoglio M, Fuster DG, Ferraro PM.
ai_summary: Diffusion MRI radiomics, using apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, improved prediction of rapid renal function decline in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) beyond standard clinical and conventional MRI measures. In 112 patients, ADC-based radiomics achieved an AUC of 0.82, and combining ADC, T1/T2-weighted imaging, and clinical data reached an AUC of 0.85, with improved risk reclassification. This approach captures both cystic and noncystic tissue alterations and may enhance early risk stratification and treatment decisions in ADPKD.

title: Genetic Traces in Autism Spectrum Disorders: A Whole Exome Sequencing Study from Türkiye.
authors: Kayhan G, Ozaslan A, Işeri E, Guney E, Kazan HH, Buyuktaskin D, Mulayim MF, Ergun MA, Percin FE.
ai_summary:
Gene: MECP2 (also EP300, PTEN, KMT2C, TRRAP)
Finding: Whole exome sequencing in 75 Turkish ASD patients identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 24% of cases, with MECP2 most frequently affected, and four novel de novo missense variants in KMT2C, MECP2, PTEN, and TRRAP.
Disease: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs)

title: The JAK1 Inhibitor Upadacitinib Curbs Acute Liver Failure via Suppressing IFN-γ/JAK1/STAT1 and TNF-α/NF-κB/MAPK Pathways and Modulating Bax/Bcl-2 Ratio.
authors: Alhussaini AF, Hazem SH, Saad EA, Elshal M.
ai_summary: Upadacitinib (UPA), a selective JAK1 inhibitor, was tested in a mouse model of acute liver failure (ALF) induced by LPS/D-galactosamine. UPA pretreatment significantly reduced liver injury, oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and improved survival-related histopathology. Mechanistically, UPA suppressed IFN-γ/JAK1/STAT1 and TNF-α/NF-κB/MAPK signaling and modulated the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, suggesting it is a promising therapeutic candidate for ALF.

title: GRAF1-dependent endocytotic processes and the Golgi apparatus contribute to previously unrecognized intermediate stages of early ciliogenesis.
authors: Schmidt KN, Buerger K, Maier O, Zügner A, Osten L, Hofstetter P, Othmen H, Zaytseva Y, Hecht A, Read C, Rachel R, Witzgall R.
ai_summary:
Gene: GRAF1
Finding: GRAF1 is essential for early ciliogenesis, mediating endocytotic delivery of plasma membrane-derived material to the developing ciliary membrane during previously unrecognized intermediate stages.
Disease: Primary cilia formation (ciliogenesis)

title: Ancestral pattern of the Xenopus germ cell cyst: From the germ stem cells to the oocytes and nurse cells.
authors: Kloc M.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Systematic identification of microtubule lumen proteins reveals a taxane-sensitive luminal resident JPT2 regulating MEC17 accessibility.
authors: Shao J, Zhang R, Wu P, Xu H, Zhou Z, Chen W, Gu L, Wang L, Luo S, Ren J, Huan Q, Huang X, Xie Q, Wang Y, Ji W, Feng W, Liang X, Meng W.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
ai_summary:
Gene: JPT2
Finding: JPT2 is a conserved microtubule-binding protein that localizes to the singlet microtubule lumen in a C-terminal-dependent manner, modulates the distribution of the α-tubulin acetyltransferase MEC17, and its luminal accessibility is markedly reduced by Paclitaxel treatment.
Disease: No specific disease or phenotype is established; the finding relates to microtubule lumen biology and drug-induced structural changes.

title: Selected Abstracts from The Royal College of Ophthalmologists Annual Congress 2025 ACC, Liverpool, UK.
High-resolution optical genome mapping unveils gene disruptions in a reciprocal chromosomal translocation and severe male infertility: a case report.
authors: Montjean D, Darwiche W, Fotopoulos N, Pagé MG, Fetni R, Petrella F, Bélanger MC, Jedraszak G, Benkhalifa M, Miron P.
journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI3
Finding: Optical genome mapping identified a reciprocal translocation with breakpoints in ASB17 and INHBA-AS1, potentially disrupting regulatory effects on GLI3, a gene involved in reproductive development, in a man with severe male infertility.
Disease: Primary male infertility associated with a balanced reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 1 and 7.

title: Metabolomics and Lipidomics in the Study of Reproductive Performance in Livestock.
authors: Sheng Z, Gao Y, Chong Y, Lu Y, Shi J, Liu H, Li K, Deng W, Wu J.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
ai_summary: This is a review article summarizing the use of metabolomics and lipidomics to study reproductive performance in livestock. It discusses methodological advances and how metabolic and lipid pathways affect gametogenesis, embryo development, and pregnancy, highlighting potential biomarkers for fertility assessment. No specific gene-disease link is established.

title: 2'-Fucosyllactose and its metabolites propionate/butyrate suppress inflammation through a shared TLR4/p38 MAPK-dependent pathway in vitro and in vivo.
authors: Na K, Chao C, Yu T, Wang L, Liu X, Zhang L, Feng K, Lei J, Xiong Y, Guo X.
ai_summary: 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL), a human milk oligosaccharide, suppresses intestinal inflammation through a shared TLR4/p38 MAPK-dependent pathway. In vitro fermentation showed 2'-FL boosts production of the short-chain fatty acids propionate and butyrate while enriching SCFA-producing bacteria. In ETEC-infected Caco-2 cells and DSS-induced mouse colitis, 2'-FL and its metabolites inhibited TLR4/p38 MAPK signaling and reduced inflammation, with molecular docking suggesting binding to the TLR4-MD2 complex. The findings support a dual mechanism where 2'-FL acts both directly and via microbiota-derived SCFAs to modulate this signaling axis, positioning it as a precision prebiotic for gut inflammation.

title: Research Advances in Glanimal Models of Glaucoma: Exploring Multidimensional Mechanisms and Novel Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Liu J, Zhang H, Chen J, Zhou J, Yu Y, Cheng F, Bao J, Feng C, Yu X, Xia Z, Ding R, Li Z, Li X.
ai_summary: This review summarizes the establishment methods, applications, and future directions of animal models for glaucoma, a condition marked by progressive retinal ganglion cell loss. The authors systematically searched literature from 2015–2025 and describe how diverse models replicate glaucoma’s multifaceted pathogenesis—including mechanical stress, immune inflammation, excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, and fibrosis—and are used to screen neuroprotective and anti-fibrotic therapies. The review concludes that future work should focus on standardizing models to better mimic clinical disease and integrating multimodal assessments with targeted therapies to advance personalized glaucoma treatment.

title: Traffic Jams in the Brain: How Kinesin Dysfunction Shapes Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
authors: Shams Nosrati MS, Doustmohammadi M, Dostmohammadi A, Kakavand Hamidi A, Boogari M, Hoseini Tavassol Z, Khosravinejat S, Asgari M, Shafiei M, Nemati AH, Romano F, Capra V, Sterlini B, Darbalaei M, Salehi M, Omrani MD, Zara F, Kibar Z, Miyamoto T, Scala M.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF14, KIF7
Finding: Kinesin dysfunction, including in KIF7 and emerging member KIF14, disrupts microtubule-based neuronal transport and ciliary signaling, contributing to a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders.
Disease: Neurodevelopmental disorders (intellectual disability, epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, microcephaly, malformations of cortical development, spasticity, axonal neuropathy)

title: Overexpression of the NEK8 kinase inhibits homologous recombination.
authors: Turner JL, Moore G, McCraw TJ, Mason JM.
ai_summary:
Gene: NEK8
Finding: Overexpression of NEK8 inhibits homologous recombination by suppressing RAD51 focus formation, causing replication fork degradation and sensitizing cells to the PARP inhibitor Olaparib.
Disease: Breast cancer (NEK8-overexpressing tumors may be recombination-deficient and responsive to PARP inhibitor therapy)

title: Prefrontal cortical microglial transcriptome relates to mouse offspring executive function deficits after perinatal opioid exposure in a sex-dependent manner.
authors: Smith BL, Brooks-Patton B, Bollinger JL, Guzman TA, Brendle AH, Woodburn SC, Makela AG, Wohleb ES, Reyes TM.
ai_summary: Perinatal morphine exposure in mice causes sex-dependent executive function deficits in adult offspring, with males showing reduced accuracy and females showing increased inattentive behavior in the 5-choice serial reaction time task. Transcriptomic analysis of prefrontal cortical microglia revealed largely sex-divergent gene expression changes, with only three differentially expressed genes shared between sexes, and identified sex-specific genes and pathways potentially linked to the behavioral deficits.

title: Translational Potential: Kidney Tubuloids in Precision Medicine and Regenerative Nephrology.
authors: Hossain MK, Lee HY, Kim HR.
ai_summary: Kidney tubuloids, derived from adult kidney epithelium, offer a more mature and reproducible alternative to pluripotent stem cell-derived organoids for modeling tubular disorders, nephrotoxicity, and inherited tubulopathies. Their patient-specific phenotypes enable drug screening and personalized disease modeling, with integration of microfluidics, biomaterials, and gene editing promising enhanced physiological realism. Persistent barriers to broader adoption and clinical translation remain, but a roadmap is proposed for advancing tubuloids toward precision nephrology and regenerative applications.

title: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) channels mediate pulmonary surfactant protein A and D secretion.
authors: Alt P, Müller I, Kiefmann M, Gudermann T, Kuebler WM, Griese M, Staab-Weijnitz CA, Dietrich A.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: TRPV4 channels are required for the secretion (but not production) of surfactant proteins A and D from alveolar epithelial type 2 and tracheal/bronchial epithelial cells, as shown by reduced secreted SP-A/SP-D levels in TRPV4-deficient mice and human airway epithelial cells with TRPV4 knockdown.
Disease: Pulmonary host defense impairment; relevance to lung diseases such as asthma and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Club Cells in Nasal Epithelial Repair: Insights From an IL-13-Induced Inflammatory Model.
authors: Huang ZQ, Liu J, Ye J, Sun LY, Ong HH, Peng Y, Lin BQ, Tu JH, Wang KS, Xiong YS, Luo Q, Thong M, Xu Y, Wang DY.
ai_summary:
Gene: SCGB1A1
Finding: Club cells (SCGB1A1+) are significantly decreased in all four endotypes of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and IL-13 drives their differentiation toward goblet cells (MUC5AC+) at the expense of ciliated cells, a process reversed by Dupilumab and STAT6 inhibition.
Disease: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP)

title: Activation of toll-like receptor 2 promotes the expression of inflammatory mediators and cell proliferation of human polycystic kidney disease cells.
authors: Zhang Y, Plansinis M, Peak S, Weber E, Wei A, Xu Y, Ross M, Leagjeld A, Wallace DP, Zhang Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: TLR2
Finding: Activation of TLR2 promotes NF-κB-mediated inflammatory mediator expression and ERK-dependent cell proliferation via TAK1 in ADPKD cells, with no such effect in normal kidney cells.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: The Oral Microbiome and Systemic Health: Current Insights into the Mouth-Body Connection.
authors: Glavina A, Martić D, Perko MA, Mešin Delić D, Tadin A, Lešić S, Šupe-Domić D.
ai_summary: The oral microbiome plays a central role in maintaining local and systemic homeostasis, and disturbances in oral microbial communities (oral dysbiosis) are associated with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic respiratory infections, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, with emerging links to neurodegenerative disorders, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune diseases, and cancer. Proposed mechanisms include bacteraemia, systemic inflammation from microbial metabolites and endotoxins, immune disruption, molecular mimicry, and modulation of host metabolic pathways. However, most evidence is observational, and causal relationships remain to be established through longitudinal and interventional research.

title: Targeting the microbiota-miRNA-protease axis: A new therapeutic avenue in melanoma.
authors: Katsoulieris EN, Ioannou P, Afratis NA.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (review article; discusses multiple miRNAs and matrix metalloproteinases without a single gene focus)
Finding: This review synthesizes evidence that gut microbiota dysbiosis alters miRNA profiles targeting ECM proteases, influencing melanoma progression and immunotherapy resistance, and proposes combined microbiota modification and miRNA-based therapies as a novel adjuvant strategy.
Disease: Melanoma

title: Binding of CEP152 to PLK4 stimulates kinase activity to promote centriole assembly.
authors: Gürkaşlar HK, Hoffmann I.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP152
Finding: CEP152 binds to PLK4 via its N-terminal region, stimulating PLK4 phosphorylation and kinase activation, which promotes centriole assembly.
Disease: Centriole duplication defects (associated with ciliopathy-related phenotypes)

title: Delta tubulin stabilizes male meiotic kinetochores and aids microtubule remodeling and fertility.
authors: Stathatos GG, Merriner DJ, O'Connor AE, Zenker J, Dunleavy JEM, O'Bryan MK.
ai_summary:
Gene: TUBD1
Finding: TUBD1 stabilizes kinetochores during male meiosis, supports spindle polarity and cytokinesis, and partners with KATNAL2 and KATNB1 to regulate manchette remodeling and sperm head shaping; its loss causes sterility in mice.
Disease: Male infertility (sterility due to defective spermatogenesis)

title: The Dynamic Gut Microbiota: Monitoring Alterations During Lung Cancer Progression for Diagnosis and Precision Medicine.
authors: Xiao X, Wang Y, Yin T, Wang Q, Feng Y, Ren H, Li J, Cheng L.
ai_summary: The gut microbiota and its metabolites change dynamically during lung cancer progression and in response to treatment, reflecting a bidirectional gut-lung axis that influences disease. This review suggests that longitudinal monitoring of gut microbiota composition could aid in early diagnosis, precision therapy, and prognosis of lung cancer.

title: Increased Risk of Incident Uveitis Among Patients with Psoriasis: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
authors: Ehrenberg S, Elizur Y, Ben-Shabat N, David P, Sharif K, Bernstein YS, Abu Hilwe I, Cohen AD, Watad A, Amital H, Patt YS.
ai_summary: Psoriasis is associated with a significantly higher risk of incident uveitis (adjusted hazard ratio 1.80), but this risk is driven primarily by disease severity and systemic inflammatory burden: mild psoriasis shows no increased risk, while severe disease and concomitant spondyloarthritis (SpA) show markedly elevated risks. Independent predictors of uveitis within the psoriasis cohort include SpA, diabetes mellitus, systemic lupus erythematosus, and sarcoidosis, and biologic exposure (especially etanercept) is associated with higher odds of uveitis, likely reflecting greater disease severity. Clinicians should maintain heightened vigilance for ocular symptoms in psoriasis patients with severe disease or concomitant SpA.

title: Complexity of Inheritance of Pathogenic Mutations Associated with Epilepsy in Consanguine Families from Pakistan.
authors: Tahira K, Ullah A, Ullah F, Aziz J, Javed MI, Kiyani A, Khanum A, Hallmann K, Baumgartner T, Surges R, Shaiq PA, Kunz WS.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRAF3IP1
Finding: A homozygous pathogenic TRAF3IP1 p.Gly387* nonsense mutation was identified in one consanguine family with epilepsy, but likely did not contribute to the phenotype due to stop-codon read-through.
Disease: Epilepsy

title: Ion channels as therapeutic targets in osteoarthritis.
authors: Zhou R, Hu W, Waxman SG, Liu CJ.
ai_summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of disability, and this review highlights ion channels—including sodium, potassium, TRP, Piezo, acid-sensing, and chloride channels—as key regulators of cartilage loss, inflammation, and pain. The authors discuss preclinical and clinical advances in ion channel-targeted therapies, such as small-molecule inhibitors, biologics, gene therapies, and drug repurposing, while addressing challenges in selective targeting, drug delivery, and patient stratification. Continued research on ion channel biology is essential for developing targeted OA therapies and enabling precision medicine with site-specific strategies that minimize systemic side effects.

title: Genetics of Idiopathic Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism
authors: Topaloğlu AK, Kotan LD.
journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
ai_summary: Idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (IHH) is a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders caused by deficient GnRH secretion or action, leading to impaired puberty and infertility. Next-generation sequencing has identified pathogenic variants in over 60 genes, accounting for up to 50% of cases, with oligogenic inheritance seen in 10-20% of individuals. Genetic studies have revealed the Kisspeptin, Neurokinin B, Dynorphin neurons as the GnRH pulse generator, informing targeted therapies such as the FDA-approved neurokinin B receptor antagonist fezolinetant.

title: Proteomic Investigation of Neurotrophic trans-Banglene Reveals Potential Link to Iron Homeostasis.
authors: Gunawardana PBW, Gohil K, Moon KM, Foster LJ, Williams FJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified
Finding: Neurotrophic trans-banglene (t-BG) treatment alters iron-binding and iron-regulating proteins and reduces intracellular and mitochondrial ferrous (Fe2+) ion levels without changing total iron, unlike nerve growth factor, suggesting a novel link between iron homeostasis and neurotrophic activity.
Disease: Neurodegenerative disease (contextual, via iron dysregulation)

title: Gene-Disease Relationships in Kidney Genetics.
authors: Gitau V, Ratliff J, Webb R, Mallett AJ, Ajuyah P.
ai_summary: Plain-language summary: This review describes how gene curation—the systematic evaluation of evidence linking genes to diseases—is used to determine which genes are included in diagnostic genetic testing for kidney diseases. The ClinGen Kidney Disease Clinical Domain Working Group oversees expert panels that curate genes across five areas, including renal ciliopathies, and their publicly available results help nephrologists interpret whether genetic findings are clinically relevant for patient care.

title: Rod-cone dystrophy with myriad systemic manifestations.
authors: Patil G, Pandarasamy P, Reddy NVSK, Ganne P.
ai_summary:
Gene: ABCA4
Finding: A heterozygous ABCA4 c.3113C>T (p.Ala1038Val) mutation was identified in a patient with rod-cone dystrophy and multiple systemic abnormalities, suggesting a blended phenotype of ABCA4-related retinal disease and an unidentified systemic syndrome.
Disease: Rod-cone dystrophy with systemic manifestations (atrial septal defect, hypogonadism, liver disease, hypothyroidism, adrenal insufficiency, and delayed epiphyseal closure)

title: Integrated Oral Microbiome and Metabolome Profiling Identifies Disease-Associated Multi-Omics Signatures in Alström and Bardet-Biedl Syndromes.
authors: Mojsak P, Zmyslowska-Polakowska E, Chmielewska S, Sołowiej K, Ploszaj T, Skoczylas S, Grzybowska-Adamowicz J, Pienkowski T, Kretowski A, Zmyslowska A, Ciborowski M.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (multi-omics study of ALMS and BBS without a single gene focus)
Finding: Integrated oral microbiome and metabolome profiling reveals disease-associated multi-omics signatures, including enrichment of Prevotella, Enterococcus, and Eikenella with reduced Lactobacillus, and coordinated shifts in amino acid, lipid, and carbohydrate metabolism in Alström and Bardet-Biedl syndromes.
Disease: Alström syndrome (ALMS) and Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS)

title: Prenatal imaging of upper urinary tract abnormalities: when is MRI useful?
authors: Mallin SM, Forbes-Amrhein MM, Marine MB.
ai_summary: Fetal MRI serves as a complementary tool to ultrasound for evaluating prenatal upper urinary tract abnormalities, helping clarify diagnoses such as urinary tract dilatation, renal agenesis, renal ectopia, multicystic dysplastic kidney, and other cystic renal diseases. The paper reviews these common conditions and discusses specific scenarios where MRI adds diagnostic value.

title: Trifid epiglottis in a neonate with choanal atresia and hydrometrocolpos: the third reported case and the first symptomatic neonatal presentation.
authors: Khorashadizadeh M, Doostparast A, Sabahi MA, Ghahramani S.
ai_summary: Trifid epiglottis is an extremely rare congenital laryngeal anomaly, and this report describes the third known case and the first symptomatic neonatal presentation. The two-day-old female presented with abdominal distension, oliguria, poor feeding, stridor, polydactyly, syndactyly, and an anteriorly displaced anus; imaging revealed hydrometrocolpos with bilateral hydronephrosis, and airway evaluation confirmed right choanal atresia and trifid epiglottis. The case highlights the importance of early diagnosis and multidisciplinary evaluation of rare congenital laryngeal anomalies in neonates.

title: Monogenic and syndromic obesity in children: Clinical recognition, genetics, and precision management.
authors: Khalil H, Feigin E, Zaitoon H.
ai_summary:
Gene: MC4R (also LEP, LEPR, POMC, PCSK1, SH2B1, SIM1, BDNF)
Finding: Mutations in these genes disrupt the leptin-melanocortin pathway or hypothalamic development, causing hyperphagia, early-onset severe obesity, and metabolic dysregulation, with MC4R mutations being the most common cause of monogenic obesity.
Disease: Monogenic and syndromic obesity (including Bardet-Biedl and Alström syndromes) in children

title: Diagnostic yield and variant spectrum of whole-exome sequencing in Iranian probands with congenital and early-onset ocular disorders.
authors: Asadi A, Sadat Shandiz SA, Ebrahimi A, Hosseini ZS, Shirsalimi N, Neamatzadeh H, Ebrahimi A.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP290, CRB1, GUCY2D
Finding: Whole-exome sequencing identified pathogenic or likely-pathogenic variants in these and other established genes (ABCA4, USH2A, RP1, CYP1B1, TYR) in 21 of 30 Iranian probands with congenital or early-onset ocular disorders, yielding a diagnostic rate of 70%.
Disease: Congenital and early-onset ocular disorders (inherited retinal and anterior segment diseases)

title: Bronchiectasis in renal transplant patients: a narrative review.
authors: Dury S, Ancel J, Mulette P, Malet J, Vivien A, Dormoy V, Guillard T, Muggeo A, Vuiblet V, Colosio C, Launois C, Perotin JM, Deslee G.
ai_summary: Bronchiectasis can occur in renal transplant patients, with pathogenesis likely involving underlying renal disease, immunodeficiency, immunosuppressive drug toxicity, and lower respiratory tract infections. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge on epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical impact, and offers management proposals for this condition.

title: Genetic determinants of obesity: mechanisms, clinical implications, and targeted therapies.
authors: Serbis A, Kantza E, Garoufou M, Christou M, Siomou E, Tigas S.
ai_summary: Obesity arises from a spectrum of genetic causes, ranging from common polygenic forms influenced by gene-environment interactions to rare syndromic and monogenic forms. Monogenic obesity, caused by single-gene mutations in hypothalamic appetite-regulating pathways, leads to severe early-onset obesity and has been key to understanding hunger and satiety mechanisms. Advances in GWAS and sequencing have improved diagnosis and enabled personalized treatment approaches for this multifaceted disease.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Chronic Airway Infection in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
authors: Saba TG, Zimbric M, McCaffery H, Caverly LJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no single gene link established)
Finding: In a retrospective cohort of 32 PCD patients, chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection was associated with a 5-fold higher pulmonary exacerbation rate, while chronic Aspergillus fumigatus infection was associated with lower lung function (ppFEV1); chronic Haemophilus influenzae, MSSA, and AF infections did not significantly affect exacerbation rates.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) with chronic airway infection

title: Potentially Deleterious Nonsynonymous Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (nsSNPs) in the Human MCPH1 Gene: Systematic In Silico Predictions and Implications for Structure and Function.
authors: Kousar R, Latif S, Alharthi MTH, Tabassum S, Khan MA, Alayoubi AM, Qarmali M, Latif M.
ai_summary:
Gene: MCPH1
Finding: In silico analysis identified 23 potentially deleterious nonsynonymous SNPs, of which 16 reduce protein stability and 8 (p.A11D, p.H49D, p.T59I, p.W60S, p.W60C, p.L74P, p.C79G, p.L781P) cause structural loss, mostly in the N-terminal BRCT domain implicated in neurodevelopment.
Disease: Primary microcephaly (MCPH)

title: Filippi syndrome-associated CKAP2L modulates microtubule dynamics essential for mitosis and ciliary length regulation.
authors: Lyu Q, Wang Y, Zhou J, Zhao H, Zhong T, Li Q.
ai_summary:
Gene: CKAP2L
Finding: CKAP2L regulates microtubule dynamics, and its loss causes shortened mitotic spindles, cytokinesis failure with multinucleation, and abnormally elongated primary cilia and sperm flagella.
Disease: Filippi syndrome

title: Hyperglycemic stress aggravates diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy by promoting cilium disassembly via a deacetylation- and methylation-mediated regulatory mechanism.
authors: Ran J, Wei C, Yang Y, Zhang Y, Guo G, Ma N, Yin L, Fan H, Li J, Guo H, Zhang R, Wang R, Li D, Liu M.
ai_summary:
Gene: PRMT1, HDAC6
Finding: Hyperglycemic stress upregulates PRMT1 and HDAC6, which reciprocally stabilize each other via arginine methylation (HDAC6 at R16) and deacetylation (PRMT1 at K128), forming a positive feedback loop that promotes cilium disassembly and aggravates diabetic complications.
Disease: Diabetic retinopathy and diabetic nephropathy

title: A role for EHMT2 in a novel autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental syndrome? A case report.
authors: Rots D, de Oliveira BC, Carvalho LML, Zhao X, Sadikovic B, Sim T, Rigobello R, Tedder M, Donoghue S, Maripuri DP, Hnizda A, Barr E, Fletcher R, Noskova L, Li D, Kleefstra T, Zackai EH, Barrero MJ, Krepischi ACV, Strong A.
ai_summary:
Gene: EHMT2
Finding: Compound heterozygous loss-of-function and splice variants in EHMT2 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with a phenotype and DNA methylation episignature overlapping Kleefstra syndrome type 1.
Disease: Autosomal recessive EHMT2-related neurodevelopmental disorder

title: Biallelic nonsense variants in GAS8 associated with asthenoteratozoospermia and PCD-like symptoms.
authors: Zhao M, Guo S, Ran L, Meng Y, Zhao Y, Wang J, Wang B.
ai_summary:
Gene: GAS8
Finding: Biallelic nonsense variants (p.Glu94Ter and p.Gln128Ter) cause asthenoteratozoospermia with PCD-like symptoms, and TESA-ICSI achieved a biochemical pregnancy.
Disease: Asthenoteratozoospermia with primary ciliary dyskinesia-like symptoms

title: What does a negative genetic test mean?
authors: Schwartz S, Capasso J, Levin AV.

title: Smoking-Related Clinical and Molecular Abnormalities in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
authors: Zhyvylo I, Sood N, Pugashetti JV, Linderholm AL, Hsu SW, Oldham J, Chen CH, Goncharova EA.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS1
Finding: In smokers with IPF-PH, whole-blood expression of BBS1 (along with BARD1 and SMURF1) negatively correlates with mean pulmonary arterial pressure, suggesting a potential biomarker role for PH severity.
Disease: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis-associated pulmonary hypertension (IPF-PH)

title: Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Rotigotine Safety in PKD.
authors: Dumont A, Cour A, Quillard-Murraine M, Van Wynsberghe M, Ruault S, Prod'Homme S, Houivet E, Choukroun G, Renard C, Béchade C, Claudinot A, Glowacki F, Puech P, Marty N, Buchbach V, Donnadieu N, Duhamel E, Dacher JN, Guerrot D, Bellien J.

title: Obesity-Related Functional Hypogonadism Requires Therapeutic Recalibration: Implications for GLP-1-Based Therapies.
authors: Jensterle M, Janez A.

title: Neuroendocrinology and the Genetics of Obesity.
authors: Ruggiero-Ruff RE, Coss D.
ai_summary: Obesity has a strong genetic component, with heritability estimated at 45% to 70%, yet known single-gene mutations account for only 5% to 10% of cases, typically causing early-onset severe obesity. Genome-wide studies have identified over 250 genes with small effect sizes, and several genetic syndromes include obesity alongside neurodevelopmental disabilities. This review summarizes genetic causes of obesity in relation to brain circuitry regulating food intake and energy homeostasis, emphasizing the need for further studies on gene-environment and sex-dependent interactions, as genetics alone cannot explain the recent dramatic rise in obesity prevalence.

title: Weight Loss Following Liraglutide Therapy in a Patient With Smith-Magenis Syndrome: A Case Report.
authors: Garg DK, Wei J.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (GLP1RA/liraglutide therapy, not a specific gene)
Finding: A young man with Smith-Magenis syndrome and obesity achieved significant weight loss (22.2 kg over 11 months) with daily liraglutide, titrated to maximum dose, alongside lifestyle modifications, without severe gastrointestinal side effects.
Disease: Smith-Magenis syndrome with obesity and metabolic comorbidities (prediabetes, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease)

title: Base editing-derived models of human WDR34 and WDR60 disease alleles replicate retrograde intraflagellar transport (IFT) and hedgehog signaling defects.
authors: Antony D, Güleç EY, Klawonn A, Bakey Z, Schüle I, Kim GJ, Cathomen T, Skatulla I, Brunner HG, Arnold SJ, Schmidts M.
ai_summary:
Gene: WDR34, WDR60
Finding: CRISPR base editing recreating human disease missense alleles (including novel WDR60 p.Ala968Val) causes hedgehog signaling defects and disturbed retrograde intraflagellar transport, plus transcriptomic changes in actin cytoskeleton and Golgi transport genes, suggesting non-ciliary functions.
Disease: Short Rib Thoracic Dystrophy (SRTD)

title: Obstetric outcomes in pregnancies complicated by polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Chappus-McCendie H, Bendayan E, Spence AR, Abenhaim HA.
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
ai_summary: Pregnant patients with polycystic kidney disease (PKD) face significantly higher risks of maternal complications—including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, cesarean delivery, hemorrhage, sepsis, acute renal failure, and death—as well as adverse neonatal outcomes such as preterm birth, intrauterine growth restriction, and congenital anomalies. The authors conclude that PKD pregnancies should be managed as high-risk by a multidisciplinary team.

title: Increased risk of incident and recurrent urinary tract infection in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a contemporary propensity score-matched cohort study.
authors: Wang J, Lee SY, Chao CT, Chien KL, Hung KY.
ai_summary:
