Gene: Not applicable (ADPKD is polygenic/cystic kidney disease, not a single gene finding here)
Finding: In a contemporary propensity-matched cohort, ADPKD is independently associated with a modestly increased risk of incident UTI (aHR 1.20) and recurrent UTI (IRR 1.32), with higher risk in males and advanced CKD stages.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with urinary tract infection (UTI)

title: The Importance of Familial Co-segregation in the Classification of a Novel PKD1 Variant Associated With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Vasconcelos AP, Rocha L, Fernandes S, Oliveira JP.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Familial co-segregation analysis using the full likelihood Bayes factor (FLB=96.8) reclassified the novel PKD1 missense variant c.8999G>C p.(Arg3000Pro) from a variant of uncertain significance to likely pathogenic.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Factors associated with cerebrovascular complications in a cohort of patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in South Africa.
authors: Kapche CXM, Assounga A.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1/PKD2 (implied by ADPKD diagnosis, not explicitly genotyped)
Finding: In a South African ADPKD cohort, cerebrovascular complications occurred in 4.7% of patients, with intracranial aneurysms in 3% (half ruptured); Black African patients had a reduced risk of intracranial aneurysms but predominantly presented with spontaneous subdural haematomas, and intracranial bleeding was significantly associated with higher systolic blood pressure.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with cerebrovascular complications (intracranial aneurysms, intracerebral/subarachnoid haemorrhage, spontaneous subdural haematoma)

title: Genetic Testing in the Management of Adult CKD.
authors: Chebib FT, Wang X, Udani SM, Westemeyer M, Clark D, Zhang Z, Bloom MS, Milo Rasouly H, Kolupaeva V, Mizani MR, Dossabhoy NR, Faravardeh A, Demko ZP, Kotte S, Punj S, Chapman SL, Rabinowitz M, Schneider R, Tabriziani H, Bhorade S, Gharavi AG, Dahl NK.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
ai_summary: Genetic testing with a 385-gene panel in adult chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients showed diagnostic and clinical utility at 1 year post-testing: 24% had a positive finding, and testing was helpful for or changed management in 86% of positive and 42% of negative cases, with prognostic estimates altered in 55% and 18% respectively, across diverse CKD etiologies.

title: Efficacy and safety of reduced-dose valganciclovir prophylaxis for cytomegalovirus infection after pediatric kidney transplantation.
authors: Nakatani R, Shirai Y, Ando T, Yamasaki Y, Kume Y, Tsugawa K, Unagami K, Shimizu T, Ishida H, Miura K.
ai_summary: Reduced-dose valganciclovir prophylaxis after pediatric kidney transplantation was evaluated in nine patients. In high-risk (donor-positive/recipient-negative) patients, the regimen led to a high incidence of CMV infection (four cases) and adverse events including neutropenia and febrile neutropenia, indicating a suboptimal efficacy-safety balance. In intermediate-risk (recipient-positive) patients, the regimen appeared effective and tolerable, but further optimization is needed for high-risk recipients.

title: Is Peritoneal Dialysis a Better Modality than Hemodialysis for Incident Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Patients?
authors: Ghamrawi R, Dahl NK.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

title: Scoping Review on Polycystic Liver Disease in PKD1/PKD2 Gene Carriers: Genetic Aspects, Pathophysiology, and Therapeutic Approaches.
authors: Muñoz-Delgado DY, Zuñiga-Hernández LF, Barrios-Bermúdez H, Velasco-Erira S, Diaz-Brochero C, Suarez-Quintero CY.
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2
Finding: Mutations in PKD1 and PKD2 are associated with differences in polycystic liver disease severity and hepatic cyst burden, confirming their central role in PLD pathogenesis.
Disease: Polycystic liver disease (PLD), including ADPLD and ADPKD-associated liver cysts

title: Case Report: Severe bronchiectasis in three kittens with detection of Mycoplasma felis: radiographic and computed tomography findings.
authors: François C, Billen F, Van Renterghem E, Jauniaux T, Bolen G.
ai_summary: Plain-language summary: This case series describes three kittens under 6 months old with severe bronchiectasis and concurrent Mycoplasma felis infection. Imaging (radiography and CT) revealed varicose bronchiectasis in all kittens, primarily affecting the caudal lung lobes of one hemithorax, with moderate to severe atelectasis and compensatory hyperinflation of the contralateral lung. CT provided additional detail over radiography, and Mycoplasma felis was detected in all cases, suggesting a possible association between this infection and severe bronchiectasis in young kittens.

title: Design of Nanocarriers for Kidney Targeted Delivery of Nucleic Acid Therapeutics.
authors: Lee JH, Han J, Park S, Mok H.
ai_summary: This review discusses the design of nanocarriers for delivering nucleic acid therapeutics (siRNAs, CRISPR systems, mRNA) specifically to the kidneys, covering renal microenvironment considerations, treatment approaches for renal genetic disorders, and recent kidney-targeted delivery strategies along with their challenges and limitations.

title: Monogenic kidney disease and monogenic diabetes are present in renal clinic patients with non-genetic diagnoses.
authors: Huang M, Pianta T, Barit D, Mahmood K, Colville D, Mack H, Savige J.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in PKHD1 and other kidney disease genes (COL4A3, CFH, CHD7, SEC63, LRP5) were identified in 11% of renal clinic patients with non-genetic diagnoses, despite no recorded family history of genetic disease.
Disease: Monogenic kidney disease (including cystic kidney disease)

title: Wnt and Nodal asymmetries stratify mouse laterality phenotypes in the absence of node flow.
authors: Ochandorena-Saa A, Perthame E, Oulerich Z, Chamolly A, Blisnick T, Lokmer J, Rouillon C, Bastin P, Meilhac SM.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC40
Finding: In CCDC40 mutants with abrogated node flow, 70% of mice still develop normal situs, and transcriptomic analyses reveal WNT and NODAL pathway asymmetries that stratify laterality phenotypes, implicating WNT signaling in symmetry breaking independent of node flow.
Disease: Laterality defects (situs inversus totalis and heterotaxy with left isomerism)

title: A novel XPNPEP3 gene variant manifesting as rhabdomyolysis and exercise intolerance.
authors: Staedler K, Nectoux J, Metay C, Lermine A, Villar-Quiles RN, Evangelista T, Labasse C, Lacène E, Stojkovic T.
ai_summary:
Gene: XPNPEP3
Finding: A homozygous frameshift variant in XPNPEP3 is associated with a metabolic myopathy manifesting as exercise intolerance and recurrent rhabdomyolysis, with additional subclinical nervous system involvement.
Disease: Metabolic myopathy with rhabdomyolysis and exercise intolerance (expanding the phenotype beyond nephronophthisis)

title: Th2 cytokine-induced mucociliary remodeling in chronic rhinosinusitis: implications for antiviral defense and epithelial function.
authors: Theorell J, Drnevich J, Jovanovic Gasovic S, Lawate B, Lee VS, Veiga-Lopez A.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (Th2 cytokines IL-4, IL-13)
Finding: Chronic Th2 cytokine exposure during epithelial differentiation downregulates cilia-related pathways and impairs antiviral responses to rhinovirus, reducing viral reads and shifting cytokine release toward an anti-inflammatory profile in both CRS and non-CRS nasal epithelial cultures.
Disease: Chronic rhinosinusitis

title: Primary Cilia of Astrocytes in the Retina in Development and Disease.
authors: Ning K, Tran M, Xia X, Kowal TJ, Wang Q, Lo CH, Chen S, Liu Z, Li T, Zhang F, Wang W, Sun Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL13B
Finding: Primary cilia are present on retinal astrocytes in mice, macaque, and humans, and their ciliation is reduced in the peripheral retina of aged mice and altered in glaucoma models (ocular hypertension and optic nerve crush).
Disease: Age-associated retinal disease and glaucoma

title: Prenatal exome sequencing of fetuses with central nervous system anomalies based on prenatal ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging diagnosis: A retrospective cohort study with a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Yao J, Wang Y, Li G, Zhang Z, Lv Y, Chen L.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multiple genes implicated)
Finding: Prenatal exome sequencing provides a significantly higher diagnostic yield than chromosomal microarray analysis for fetal central nervous system anomalies, with the highest yields in complex phenotypes such as corpus callosum anomalies with facial abnormalities (75%) and neural tube defects with urogenital malformations (80%), and yields increasing with the number of CNS abnormalities.
Disease: Fetal central nervous system anomalies detected by prenatal imaging

title: Primary cilia connect epithelial mesenchymal plasticity with anoikis resistance and cancer stemness.
authors: Chen Q, Yang J, Yu J, Jiang S, Zhang J.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLIS2
Finding: Cilium-dependent GLIS2 signaling, linked to selected epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity states in mammary epithelial and breast cancer models, may support stem-like properties and treatment resistance.
Disease: Breast cancer

title: A global survey of systems biology-based predictions of gene-rare disease associations to enhance new diagnoses.
authors: Benítez Y, Uría-Regojo G, Mínguez P.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multi-gene, systems-level study)
Finding: A network-based algorithm predicted novel gene-disease associations for over 200 rare and Mendelian diseases, and a global analysis across predictions identified 192 genes linked to a single disease and 251 genes functionally associated with specific disease classes, integrated into a gene-disease specificity score to improve variant prioritization.
Disease: Rare and other Mendelian diseases

title: Carrier frequency of autosomal recessive monogenic disorders in the peruvian population.
authors: Abarca Barriga HH, Vásquez-Sotomayor FDM, Punil Luciano R.
ai_summary:
Gene: GJB2, PAH, ABCA4
Finding: Carrier frequencies for these genes were slightly lower than previously reported, with at least 63.5% of the Peruvian cohort carrying at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant for an autosomal recessive disorder.
Disease: Autosomal recessive monogenic disorders

title: Non-Linear Dysanaptic Lung Growth in Patients With Post-Infectious Bronchiolitis Obliterans.
authors: Clegg JM, Cacho F, McGraw MD, O'Connor MG.
ai_summary: Patients with post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans (PIBO) show non-linear dysanaptic lung growth, characterized by stagnant FEV1 z-scores over time while FVC z-scores improve, leading to a declining FEV1/FVC ratio. In a retrospective study of 15 patients, adenovirus was the most common pathogen; those infected with adenovirus had lower initial FVC but faster FVC growth compared to those with other pathogens. The findings suggest that severe respiratory infections in childhood may drive abnormal, non-parallel lung growth patterns in susceptible children.

title: CHEST Pulmonary Journal in 2026.
authors: Miles MC.

title: GSK3β functions as a mechanosensitive regulator that links flow stress to Shh signaling.
authors: Dai Y, Liu Y, Xu H, Chi Y, Chen J, Li V, Jiang Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: GSK3β
Finding: Flow-induced ciliary bending promotes ciliary accumulation of GSK3β, which phosphorylates Smoothened (Smo) at two C-terminal sites to repress Sonic Hedgehog signaling, whereas Shh stimulation relieves this inhibition via GSK3β phosphorylation at T390.
Disease: Primary cilia-related hedgehog signaling disorders

title: Nephron-Segment Composition and Apparent Fatty Acid Oxidation Suppression in Pkd1KO+Glis3KO Kidneys.
authors: Chen P, Zhang Z, Yan S, Zhang F.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Tubulin hyperglutamylation induces retinal degeneration by disrupting ciliary architecture and protein trafficking.
authors: Wang HL, Wang T, Zhen FY, Lin YQ, Tong YJ, Wu JH, Guo JX, Wang JJ, Dong SQ, Janke C, Magiera MM, Zhang HB, Zou TD.
ai_summary:
Gene: AGBL5
Finding: Loss of AGBL5 causes tubulin hyperglutamylation in photoreceptors, disrupting connecting cilium architecture and intraflagellar transport, leading to mislocalization of phototransduction proteins and progressive retinal degeneration.
Disease: Retinitis pigmentosa

title: Anisometropia and Its Related Traits: Ocular, Systemic, and Genetic Characteristics-Results From the Gutenberg Health Study.
authors: Welzel AM, Böhm EW, Wolfrum P, Schulze A, Wild PS, Lackner KJ, Lurz P, Ghaemi Kerahrodi J, Schmidtmann I, Tüscher O, Weinmann-Menke J, Konstantinides SV, Fieß A, Pfeiffer N, Schuster AK.
ai_summary:
Gene: DNAH5
Finding: A single genomic locus at the intron of DNAH5 is associated with intereye differences in axial length.
Disease: Anisometropia (intereye difference in axial length)

title: Progress in the diagnosis and treatment of post-traumatic hydrocephalus.
authors: Yang T, Zhang S, Bai L, Xie Y, Liu S.
ai_summary: Post-traumatic hydrocephalus (PTH) is a common complication after traumatic brain injury that impedes neurological recovery. This review summarizes its epidemiology, mechanisms (including CSF circulation disturbance, impaired absorption, and neuroinflammation), risk factors (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage, decompressive craniectomy, infection, advanced age), and advances in diagnosis and treatment. While diagnostic accuracy has improved with neuroimaging and dynamic CSF assessment, and therapy has evolved toward individualized shunting strategies, PTH remains underdiagnosed; future work should focus on standardized criteria, early risk stratification, and integrating glymphatic/AQP4 pathways and AI-guided diagnostics.

title: Roles of primary cilia in cardiovascular diseases: mechanisms and therapeutic prospects.
authors: Yang Z, Tang Y, Guan B, Zhao C, Shang Y, Xiong M, Xu M, Liu Y, Qin Z, Yang Z, Ren Z.
ai_summary: Primary cilia dysfunction contributes to cardiovascular diseases through multiple mechanisms, including impaired fluid shear stress sensing (reducing calcium influx and nitric oxide, promoting hypertension and atherosclerosis), disrupted PKC-Akt-NF-κB signaling and connexin downregulation (driving aneurysm), and decreased ciliary palmitoylation (causing atherosclerosis). Ciliary loss also induces congenital heart diseases via signaling pathways like Wnt, while cilia accumulation at myocardial injury sites mediates TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to cause cardiac fibrosis. Maintaining ciliary homeostasis—via strategies such as stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 inhibitors or opto-bio-hydrodynamic platforms—shows therapeutic promise, though detailed mechanisms remain unclear.

title: Imaging features of TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion syndrome in adults.
authors: Bitton J, Boudhabhay I, Dariane C, Essig M, Tourret J, Audrezet MP, Hummel A, Knebelmann B, Correas JM, Hélénon O, Bodard S.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1 (TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion)
Finding: Adult patients with TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion syndrome show a distinct imaging phenotype combining enlarged polycystic kidneys with high cyst burden (Mayo class 1E in 88%), angiomyolipomas in 78%, and extrarenal TSC features (cortical tubers, subependymal nodules, hepatic cysts/AMLs, lymphangioleiomyomatosis, cardiac rhabdomyomas); end-stage renal disease occurred in 67% at median age 25 years.
Disease: TSC2/PKD1 contiguous gene deletion syndrome

title: Multifaceted roles of sonic hedgehog signaling in mammalian inner ear development.
authors: Qin T, Bronner ME.
ai_summary: Shh signaling plays multiple roles in mammalian inner ear development, including patterning of the otic vesicle and differentiation of specific cochlear cell types, integrating with other pathways and transcription factors to ensure proper hearing and balance structure formation.

title: 'Fly'ing Toward New Drugs to Treat Podocytopathies.
authors: Little MH, Dorison A.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Transient Nephrotic Syndrome in an Infant With Heterozygous Variants of Uncertain Significance in LMX1B and TTC21B.
authors: Greisch A, Hennaut E, Ismaili K.
ai_summary:
Gene: TTC21B (with LMX1B)
Finding: Two heterozygous variants of uncertain significance in LMX1B and TTC21B were identified in an infant with transient nephrotic syndrome, but no causal oligogenic mechanism could be established.
Disease: Infantile nephrotic syndrome

title: A novel homozygous frameshift mutation in CFAP65 is associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of sperm flagella in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
authors: Abbas M, Hussain A, Hui M, Ali H, Lateef M, Hussain M, Mustafa G, Shi B, Zhang H, Lin T, Yin H, Shi Q.
ai_summary:
Gene: CFAP65
Finding: A novel homozygous frameshift mutation (c.582_587delinsCG; p.Q194Hfs*4) in CFAP65 causes severe axonemal disorganization and classic MMAF sperm flagellar defects in over 97% of sperm, with an isolated sperm-specific phenotype and no respiratory or situs inversus involvement.
Disease: Multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) / male infertility

title: Genetic kidney disease in adults-the pathologists' perspective.
authors: Paterson AL, Chan MMY, Roufosse C.
journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
ai_summary: Plain-language summary: This review discusses the role of pathologists in identifying genetic kidney disease in adults, which accounts for 10%-20% of chronic kidney disease cases. It highlights how histology from kidney biopsies can either support a suspected genetic cause or be the first clue to an underlying monogenic disease, and provides a practical framework for pathologists and nephrologists to recognize these cases and decide when genetic testing is appropriate.

title: Long-term HLA-incompatible kidney transplant outcomes.
authors: Kahanpää M, Lauronen J, Lempinen M, Ahopelto K, Sallinen V, Helanterä I.
journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
ai_summary:
Gene: HLA (donor-specific antibodies)
Finding: Pre-transplant donor-specific HLA antibodies, especially class II and higher cumulative MFI, are associated with worse graft survival and higher risk of acute rejection and antibody-mediated rejection, though long-term graft survival remains acceptable.
Disease: HLA-incompatible kidney transplantation outcomes

title: ADPKD Progression by Variant Type and Molecular Domain Among Participants in the HALT PKD Trial.
authors: Sucholeiki RL, Jochum E, Chen P, Wessely O, Galasinski S, Chapman AB.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

title: Evaluation and Management of Genetic Respiratory Disorders Presenting as Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure in the Newborn Infant.
authors: Wambach JA, Cole FS, Nogee LM.
ai_summary: This article reviews genetic causes of hypoxemic respiratory failure in newborns, including surfactant dysfunction disorders, alveolar capillary dysplasia with misalignment of the pulmonary veins, and other developmental lung disorders. It summarizes clinical features to help clinicians distinguish these rare, often severe or fatal conditions from more common causes of neonatal respiratory failure, and provides guidance on when to pursue genetic testing.

title: Global Group Testing and Screening With Dynamic Effects.
authors: Cui Y, Peng L.
ai_summary: This paper proposes a new statistical framework for identifying outcome-related variables in biomedical research, particularly when the effects of variables change dynamically. The method uses a model-free approach based on interval quantile independence, allowing for robust identification of variables and group testing of multiple covariates. The authors demonstrate that their approach can be extended to screening procedures for ultra-high dimensional data and show its practical utility through simulations and a real microarray data application.

title: Developmental Progress and Future Potential for Inhaled Biologics in the Treatment of Respiratory Diseases.
authors: Giri BR, Spahn JE, Alsaidalani R, Behrend-Keim B, Bhia M, Doyle JH, Herpin MJ, Moore RC, Murali NS, Safak A, Smyth HDC.
ai_summary: Inhaled biologics for treating respiratory diseases have a long history, but few products have reached commercialization despite many potential targets. This review examines past and current clinical and preclinical programs—both successful and discontinued—to identify key lessons, and discusses the physical, biological, and technical barriers to delivering fragile protein, peptide, or nucleic acid therapeutics to the lung. The authors conclude that, as the field advances, the inhaled route is expected to expand rapidly due to its pharmacokinetic advantages for local lung diseases.

title: TAK1 operates at the primary cilium in non-canonical TGFB/BMP signaling to control heart development.
authors: Doganli C, Thomsen OK, Baird DA, Ali Y, Sarusie MVK, Audain E, Jessen LJ, Truelsen PM, Mogensen JB, Holm MS, Apolínová K, Buttò L, Diamanti M, Fialová JL, Wade EM, Robertson SP, Pedersen LB, Argiro L, Lescroart F, Hitz MP, Christensen ST, Larsen LA.
ai_summary:
Gene: TAK1 (MAP3K7)
Finding: TAK1, acting with TAB2 and PKA-Cα at the primary cilium in non-canonical TGFB/BMP signaling, is required for cardiomyocyte differentiation and heart development, and patient-derived TAK1 variants impair its ciliary localization.
Disease: Syndromic congenital heart disease (CHD) with extracardiac abnormalities

title: A comprehensive approach to users from a Brazilian clinical genetics service: an observational study.
authors: de Francisco DD, Silva IMW, Steiner CE, Gil-da-Silva-Lopes VL.
ai_summary: This observational study describes access to health care and social integration among 200 patients at a Brazilian clinical genetics service. Key findings include that 18.5% reported difficulty seeing a geneticist, half of the patients did not understand the cause of their condition, and many faced barriers in education and employment, with 48.7% needing a tutor and only 37.4% of adults participating in the job market. The authors conclude that these regional data highlight universal challenges in access and social integration for this population, which can inform public policy design.

title: Prevalence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms according to comorbidities, risk factors, country, and time period: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Dremel J, Rücker V, Badel C, Ziebart A, Vlak M, Hetjens S, Abdulazim A, Jírů-Hillmann S, Heuschmann P, Rinkel GJE, Etminan N.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no single gene is the focus; ADPKD and connective-tissue disorders are mentioned as risk groups)
Finding: The prevalence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs) is increasing over the past two decades, with higher prevalence in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (12.8%), connective-tissue disorders (10.3%), and a positive family history of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage or UIA (7.9%), compared with a reference population prevalence of 3.9%.
Disease: Unruptured intracranial aneurysms

title: Evolving Understanding of RNA Biology in Kidney Disease.
authors: Piret SE, Aboudehen K, Aboudehen K, Agrawal S.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Case Report: Diagnosis and treatment report and literature review of 2 cases of VHL-deficient renal cell carcinoma.
authors: Wang Y, Gao T, Ren N, Liu Y, Li Q, Guo X.
ai_summary:
Gene: VHL
Finding: Mutations or inactivation of the VHL tumor suppressor gene cause VHL-deficient renal cell carcinoma, and treatment combining surgery, radiofrequency ablation, and targeted therapy yielded highly favorable outcomes in two cases.
Disease: Von Hippel-Lindau disease-associated renal cell carcinoma

title: Gastrointestinal Mucormycosis Masquerading as an Abdominal Mass in an Immunocompetent Child.
authors: Dey R, Gupta P, Sinha SK.
journal: Journal of Indian Association of Pediatric Surgeons
ai_summary: Gastrointestinal mucormycosis is a rare fungal infection that typically affects immunocompromised patients. This case report describes a 5-year-old immunocompetent child who presented with an abdominal mass that was initially mistaken for a tumor but was correctly diagnosed as mucormycosis after surgical removal. The child recovered with antifungal treatment, highlighting that this infection can occur in healthy children and may mimic other conditions.

title: Toward a Peritoneal Dialysis-First Policy in the United Kingdom and Europe: A Phenotype-Based Analysis of Survival and System-Level Implications.
authors: Ali H, Fülöp T, Casula AM, Ortega Alban AP, ElHafeez SA, Hamer R.
journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no specific gene studied)
Finding: In a UK cohort of 96,809 incident dialysis patients, hemodialysis was associated with higher mortality before transplantation than peritoneal dialysis across all three data-driven phenotypes, with the effect strongest in younger patients and attenuating with age.
Disease: End-stage kidney disease requiring dialysis

title: Peroxiredoxins in the kidney: a Jekyll and Hyde existence in disease pathogenesis.
authors: Jia LH, Song YX, Bai QX, Li YR, Jia J, Tan RZ, Wang L.
ai_summary: Peroxiredoxins (PRDXs) are redox-sensitive antioxidant enzymes that play dual, context-dependent roles in kidney disease: they protect against renal injury by preserving mitochondrial integrity and reducing inflammation and fibrosis, but certain members can paradoxically aggravate injury through post-translational modifications, chaperone switching, or extracellular release as damage signals. This functional duality complicates their use as therapeutic targets and biomarkers, requiring spatiotemporally precise regulation for future drug development.

title: Prenatal Etiology Diagnosis of Rare Compound Heterozygous PROC Gene Variants in a Fetus With Ocular Ultrasonic Anomaly Using Whole Exome Sequencing.
authors: Zhuang J, Huang N, Gu L, Fu W.
ai_summary:
Gene: PROC
Finding: Two rare compound heterozygous PROC variants (p.W126* and p.R220W) were identified in a fetus with prenatal ocular ultrasound anomalies, expanding the mutational spectrum of protein C deficiency-associated thrombophilia.
Disease: Protein C deficiency-associated thrombophilia with prenatal ocular anomalies

title: Cross Sectional Study of Prenatal Diagnosis Uptake Among Individuals With Genetic Conditions.
authors: Ojo E, Zemet R, Nevins A, Abraham K, Adams AD.
ai_summary: This is a cross-sectional study examining prenatal diagnostic testing uptake among 283 individuals with genetic conditions who delivered between 2011 and 2024. Only 8.8% underwent prenatal diagnostic testing, with 96% of those testing specifically for the maternal genetic condition. Offspring of those who underwent prenatal testing had a higher inheritance rate of the maternal condition (48% vs. 18.6% for post-natal testing), and this group had fewer autosomal recessive conditions (8% vs. 38%). The authors conclude that prenatal diagnostic testing rates are notably low despite elevated transmission risk, and call for further research into barriers and attitudes toward testing.

title: Rhabdomyolysis After COVID-19.
authors: Kataria N, Devadass A, Sundac L, De Souza L, Sheikh N, Ng S, Campbell S, Wang Y, Francis RS.
ai_summary: Rhabdomyolysis and severe acute kidney injury developed in a kidney transplant recipient with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with muscle pain, weakness, and brown urine. A muscle biopsy revealed immune-mediated necrotising myositis. Treatment with intravenous fluids, remdesivir, and haemodialysis led to resolution of muscle injury and recovery of kidney function, highlighting the potential for severe myositis and rhabdomyolysis in COVID-19.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of infratentorial anomalies: ultrasound, fetal MRI, and implications for counseling.
authors: Chapman T, Mirsky DM, Iruretagoyena JI, Guimaraes CV.
ai_summary: Prenatal ultrasound and fetal MRI can identify infratentorial (posterior fossa) brain malformations, which may be isolated or part of broader syndromes. This review categorizes these anomalies by their dominant morphological feature—cystic lesions, cerebellar dysgenesis, or brainstem malformations—and describes their imaging characteristics to guide diagnosis and prenatal counseling, including genetic implications.

title: Cone-Rod Dystrophy PCARE-Associated Retinopathy.
authors: Sopena-Pinilla M, Arruebo-Muñio M, Arias-Alvarez M, Arcas-Carbonell M, Tejada-González P, Lahuerta-Pueyo C, Pérez García D, Pinilla I.
ai_summary:
Gene: PCARE
Finding: A homozygous pathogenic nonsense variant in PCARE (c.3289C>T; p.(Gln1097*)) causes late-onset severe retinal dystrophy with predominant macular atrophy, cone-rod dysfunction, and central scotoma.
Disease: Cone-rod dystrophy (CORD23) / retinitis pigmentosa type 54 (RP54)

title: Soft matrix promotes ciliogenesis in human retinal pigment epithelial cells.
authors: Zahra R, Munding N, Domsch K, Braun-Lee H, García-Navarrete C, Tanaka M, Pereira G.
ai_summary: Soft extracellular matrix (1 kPa) promotes primary cilium formation and elongation in human retinal pigment epithelial (RPE1) cells, independent of serum starvation. These mechanically induced cilia are functional, as they transduce Sonic hedgehog signaling normally. Transcriptome analysis shows that soft matrix triggers cell cycle exit and changes in ECM and cytoskeletal gene expression favoring ciliogenesis, with distinct gene expression profiles compared to serum starvation (e.g., less autophagy enrichment but more ECM upregulation and actin downregulation).

title: Comparative Proteomics of Plasma and Flagellar Membranes in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
authors: Lin Y, Yao S, Long H, Huang K.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multi-protein comparative study)
Finding: Comparative proteomics of plasma and flagellar membranes in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii identified 2779 proteins with distinct compartment-specific enrichment, revealing that flagellar membranes are specialized for cilium movement, axoneme assembly, and intraflagellar transport, while plasma membranes are enriched in proton transport and ATP synthesis.
Disease: Not applicable (basic ciliary biology study)

title: Nek1 defines a branch of centriolar microtubule length control parallel to CP110-Cep97.
authors: Streubel JMS, Karasu OR, Munoz IM, Neuner A, Numanoglu EN, Macartney TJ, Schiebel E, Rouse J, Pereira G.
ai_summary:
Gene: NEK1
Finding: NEK1 acts in parallel with the CP110-Cep97 complex to restrict centriolar microtubule length, and its removal from the basal body during ciliogenesis is dependent on Cep78.
Disease: Centriole length control defects (relevant to ciliopathy-associated structural abnormalities)

title: Alström syndrome in a Chinese girl: a case report and literature review.
authors: Bao J, Kou S, Liu X, Zhang Y, Li Y, Zhang M, Zhang Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALMS1
Finding: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ALMS1, including a novel likely pathogenic variant, were identified by whole-exome sequencing in a Chinese girl presenting with nystagmus, visual impairment, diabetes mellitus, hepatosplenomegaly, mixed hearing loss, ovarian pedicle torsion, and acanthosis nigricans.
Disease: Alström syndrome

title: Genes Related to Sperm Motility Are Under Recent Ongoing Selection in Two Shorebird Species With a Polygynous Mating System and Frequent Multiple Paternity.
authors: Mueller JC, Kempenaers B.
ai_summary:
Gene: Axonemal constituent genes (e.g., sperm motility-related genes)
Finding: Genes coding for axonemal constituents, mostly expressed in the testis and influencing energy-driven sperm motility, show recent ongoing selection signals in two polygynous shorebird species (pectoral sandpiper and ruff) and historical selection across six Calidris species.
Disease: Not applicable (phenotype: sperm motility and sperm competition in a polygynous mating system)

title: The genetic insights of sporadic male infertility: a systematic review of WES and WGS studies (2014-2024).
authors: Zahi H, Sfifou F, Slaoui M, Chentoufi L, Abouqal R, Hardizi H.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multiple genes; review-level synthesis)
Finding: A systematic review of 23 WES/WGS studies (2014-2024) identified 143 unique candidate genes for male infertility; only 5 genes were replicated with functional validation, and most (116) were reported in single studies with only in silico support, with diagnostic yields of 48% for MMAF and 12-23% for NOA.
Disease: Male infertility (including multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella and non-obstructive azoospermia)

title: Screening the composition of tubulin isotypes reveals the most abundant TUBB4B for ciliary polarity in ependymal cells.
authors: Liu Y, Liu M, Xue H, Chang B, Shao F, Cao S, Li J, Zhang X, Diao L, Bao L.
ai_summary:
Gene: TUBB4B
Finding: TUBB4B is the most abundant β-tubulin isotype in ependymal cilia, is specifically upregulated by the ciliogenesis factor FOXJ1, and its deficiency disrupts ciliary planar polarity and impairs cerebrospinal fluid flow.
Disease: Hydrocephalus

title: Mapping the chaperonin TRiC/CCT interactome in mouse photoreceptors reveals functional significance for energy metabolism.
authors: Brooks C, Salcedo-Tacuma D, Mascari I, Eminhizer M, Ngo T, Kolson D, Sechrest E, Guan T, Billington N, Deng WT, Smith D, Du J, Skiba N, Sokolov M.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRiC/CCT (Tcp-1α subunit)
Finding: TRiC/CCT deficiency in rod photoreceptors disrupts folding of canonical substrates and induces an "energy crisis" via impaired glucose metabolism and mitochondrial bioenergetics, with defective Rab10-dependent GLUT4 trafficking as a likely mechanism.
Disease: Photoreceptor neurodegeneration (rod photoreceptor dysfunction)

title: Mechanistic insights into transcriptional regulation of ARHGAP36 expression identify a factor predictive of neuroblastoma survival.
authors: Havrylov S, Gamper AM, Lehmann OJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARHGAP36
Finding: FOXC1 binds a closed chromatin locus to induce ARHGAP36 expression, which inhibits protein kinase A and thereby increases Hedgehog pathway activity; high ARHGAP36 levels predict improved 5-year survival in neuroblastoma.
Disease: Neuroblastoma

title: Genetics versus environment in the pathophysiology of sagittal synostosis.
authors: De Gregorio V, Tosi DD, Vita A, Salvati M, Massimi L, Tamburrini G, Tiberio F, Lattanzi W.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
ai_summary: Sagittal craniosynostosis (sCS) is a multifactorial condition rather than one with a single dominant cause. In a systematic review of 97 studies covering 25,877 patients (11,086 with sCS), germline genetic variants were found in only 12.6% of genetically tested individuals, distributed across 125 genes with recurrent findings in 25. Environmental and perinatal factors—including male sex, advanced maternal age, maternal smoking, thyroid dysfunction, fertility treatments, fetal constraint, prematurity, and abnormal birth weight—were more consistently reported in large population-based studies. The evidence suggests that rare genetic susceptibility and non-genetic influences likely interact in sCS pathogenesis, though study heterogeneity and methodological limitations prevent definitive conclusions about the relative contribution of each factor.

title: A biomimetic tubuloid-on-a-chip for human renal fibrosis research and anti-fibrotic drug development.
authors: Zhang X, Yang F, Han C, Wang Y, Liu X, Wang Z, Suo J, Long H, Zhou L, Zhang Z, Song B, Zhang J, Li Q, Gu Z, Chen Z, Shen Z.
ai_summary: This study describes the development of a human tubuloid-on-a-chip model that integrates tubuloids, endothelial cells, and immune cells in a microfluidic system to mimic renal fibrosis. The model recapitulated key pathological features of fibrosis after TGF-β1 induction, including extracellular matrix deposition, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, loss of epithelial polarity, impaired tubular reabsorption, and elevated oxidative stress. The anti-fibrotic drug nintedanib attenuated these phenotypes, demonstrating the platform's potential for chronic kidney disease research and anti-fibrotic drug development.

title: Establishment of insulin resistance-related ten-gene signature in endometrial cancer and identification of ACTL8 as a prognostic and immunological biomarker.
authors: Lu S, Xu J, Sun X, Yuan J, Cheng J, Qin J.
journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
ai_summary:
Gene: ACTL8
Finding: Upregulation of ACTL8 is associated with poor prognosis in endometrial cancer and exerts a carcinogenic effect through its regulation of cilium movement.
Disease: Endometrial cancer (associated with insulin resistance)

title: Whole genome resequencing reveals the genetic basis of stature in short-statured Indian cattle.
authors: Ahmad SF, Aarif O, Hassan MM, Chand R, Gangwar M, T SK, Kumar A.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL13B
Finding: Unique non-overlapping copy number regions present in 100% of short-statured (dwarf) Indian cattle harbor ARL13B, a gene implicated in osteogenesis, alongside other stature-related genes.
Disease: Short stature (height at withers) in Indian cattle breeds.

title: Systematic mapping and in silico reevaluation of genomic copy number variations in primary ovarian insufficiency.
authors: Hossein Garakani M, Kakavand K, Hajiesmaeili Y, Haratian K, Z Moradi M, Zarei Moradi S, Mohseni Meybodi A.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
ai_summary:
Gene: ATF3, GAS5, PPP4R1, PRKAA1
Finding: Systematic re-analysis of 382 CNVs from 25 studies identified 42 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants and 25 large CNVs, with the X chromosome showing the highest burden, and highlighted four ovary-expressed candidate genes (ATF3, GAS5, PPP4R1, PRKAA1) within disrupted loci that are absent from most commercial diagnostic panels.
Disease: Primary ovarian insufficiency (POI)

title: Comprehensive analysis of small GTPases in Microsporidia reveals new extremes in eukaryotic cell biology.
authors: Vargová R, Majnušová V, Eliáš M.
ai_summary: Plain-language summary: This study analyzes the Ras GTPase superfamily in Microsporidia, a group of obligate intracellular parasites, revealing extreme gene loss across their evolution. Notably, some species have lost nearly all such genes, including the ubiquitous Rab5 and its regulators, and even the beta subunit of the signal recognition particle receptor—a loss unseen in other eukaryotes—which may be compensated by a unique transmembrane domain in the alpha subunit. These findings highlight how reductive evolution can drastically reshape fundamental eukaryotic cellular processes.

title: Keratin 1 and keratin 18 as immunohistochemical markers for distinguishing pulmonary metastases of oral squamous cell carcinoma from primary lung squamous cell carcinoma.
authors: Watanabe Y, Kato H, Ishikawa R, Yoshimura K, Yamada H, Miyazaki R, Takeuchi S, Haque SMJ, Yoshimura K, Sakai Y, Sugita M, Inoue Y, Takanashi Y, Sekihara K, Funai K, Masumoto K, Shinmura K.
ai_summary:
Gene: KRT1, KRT18
Finding: Keratin 1 (K1) and keratin 18 (K18) show opposite, highly specific expression patterns that reliably distinguish pulmonary metastases of oral squamous cell carcinoma from primary lung squamous cell carcinoma, with concordant staining between primary oral tumors and lung metastases.
Disease: Pulmonary metastases of oral squamous cell carcinoma versus primary lung squamous cell carcinoma

title: MicroRNAs Play Key Roles in Progenitor Maintenance, Proliferation, and Osteogenic Differentiation of Osteogenic Progenitor Cells in Syndromic and Nonsyndromic Craniosynostosis.
authors: Suzuki A, Iwaya C, Rahimi K, Iwata J.
ai_summary: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short noncoding RNAs that may contribute to craniosynostosis (CS), a birth defect involving premature cranial suture closure. Through a systematic review and bioinformatic analysis, the authors identified 165 CS-associated genes and nine candidate miRNAs that regulate them, with some specific to syndromic CS (miR-377, miR-335-3p), nonsyndromic CS (miR-371-5p, miR-329, miR-204-5p), or both (miR-651-3p, miR-362-3p, miR-425). These miRNAs' targets were enriched in the TGF-beta signaling pathway, and experimentally modulating them altered the undifferentiated state, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation of suture progenitor cells, suggesting these miRNAs drive CS by changing progenitor cell behavior.

title: Diarylpropionitrile, a selective agonist of estrogen receptor β, protects the kidney against ischemia-reperfusion injury and enhances the repair of tubular epithelial cells.
authors: Han YK, Jang G, Park YR, Lim HJ, Park KM.
ai_summary: Diarylpropionitrile (DPN), a selective ERβ agonist, protects mouse kidneys from ischemia-reperfusion injury by reducing plasma creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, tubular damage, and oxidative stress, while enhancing tubular epithelial cell proliferation and inhibiting fibrosis. These findings suggest ERβ is a potential therapeutic target for acute and chronic kidney disease.

title: L-DOPA Promotes Post-Treatment Neurovascular and Synaptic Homeostasis in Early Diabetic Retinopathy.
authors: Chlan E, Li C, Bales KL, Wood LB, Pardue MT.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (L-DOPA/levodopa treatment, no single gene implicated)
Finding: L-DOPA treatment in diabetic mice protects retinal function (ERG oscillatory potentials, optomotor response, and flicker-induced vasodilation) for at least two weeks after treatment cessation, with transcriptional changes linked to synaptic function and cytoskeletal organization.
Disease: Early diabetic retinopathy

title: Distinctive hydrocephalus-like phenotype in NOTCH2NLC-related neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease: clinicopathological features and therapeutic implications.
authors: Zhong S, Lian Y, Zhou B, Liang J, Li Y, Huang L, Chen X, Yan Y, Sun W, Luo R, Lu H, Liu J, Hu F, Wang X, Ding J.
ai_summary:
Gene: NOTCH2NLC
Finding: A hydrocephalus-like phenotype with ventriculomegaly, distinctive radiological features (smaller callosal angle, less frequent DWI hyperintensities, periventricular-dominant white matter lesions), and ependymal/choroid plexus/astrocytic intranuclear inclusions with loss of aquaporin-4 polarization is common in NIID, and some patients improve after cerebrospinal fluid drainage or shunt surgery.
Disease: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) with hydrocephalus-like phenotype, often misdiagnosed as idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus

title: Post‑translational modifications in atherosclerosis: Roles, mechanisms and therapeutic potential (Review).
authors: Xu X, Ma F, Yu W.
ai_summary: Atherosclerosis (AS) is the main pathological basis of cardiovascular disease, driven by endothelial dysfunction, lipid accumulation, foam-cell formation, smooth muscle cell remodeling, inflammation, and plaque destabilization. This review summarizes how post-translational modifications (PTMs)—including lysine and cysteine modifications, phosphorylation, glycosylation, nitration, and ADP-ribosylation—regulate these processes, with emphasis on lysine lactylation as a metabolic-epigenetic link between lactate and vascular pathology, and on PTM crosstalk (e.g., SUMOylation-ubiquitination) coordinating inflammation and cell phenotype switching. The authors also evaluate the therapeutic potential of targeting PTM-related enzymes (e.g., histone deacetylases, PARPs, kinases) while noting challenges such as context-dependent effects and limited human plaque evidence.

title: Using Large Genomic Biobanks to Generate Insights into Genetic Kidney Disease.
authors: Chang AR, Wongboonsin J, Mallett AJ, Morales A, Retterer K, Mirshahi T, Sayer JA.
ai_summary: Large genomic biobanks are essential tools for uncovering the genetic basis of chronic kidney disease (CKD), which affects ~9% of the global population. By analyzing DNA from large populations, these biobanks have identified genes with major effects on CKD risk, enabled the construction of polygenic risk scores to flag high-risk individuals, and improved detection of monogenic disorders like autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and Alport syndrome, especially in milder or asymptomatic cases. Expanding biobanks to diverse populations and integrating multi-omics data will further advance personalized prevention and treatment of kidney disease.

title: Resident mesenchymal progenitor cells require autocrine IGF-I in homeostatic and regenerating skeletal muscle.
authors: Luo YE, Abe-Teh Z, Alsaghir TY, Kuo LY, Yu F, Stoker BE, Zhou Y, Appu AB, Dy EM, Yue F, Kopinke D, Barton ER.
ai_summary:
Gene: IGF1 (Igf1)
Finding: Fibro-adipogenic progenitor (FAP)-derived IGF-I is required for FAP proliferation and function, and its loss impairs muscle regeneration, reduces fibrosis and fat accumulation, and increases senescence markers.
Disease: Skeletal muscle regeneration impairment (following injury)

title: An integrated roadmap of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) spermatogenesis across the annual reproductive cycle.
authors: Sanchis N, Díaz N, Blázquez M.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This study provides a stage-resolved RNA sequencing atlas of European sea bass spermatogenesis across the annual reproductive cycle, anchored to six histological testicular stages. It details the molecular programs driving early spermatogonial maintenance and meiotic preparation, a major transcriptional shift during spermiogenesis involving axonemal motors, intraflagellar transport, BBSome components, and chromatin remodeling, followed by spermiation-related signaling and regression-stage immune and clearance pathways. The authors identified 132 temporal expression patterns from 9,327 differentially expressed genes and curated stage markers, fertility gene sets, and chromatin-associated resources, offering biomarkers for broodstock management and aquaculture applications.

title: Increased Prevalence of Rare Copy Number Variants in Australian Children With Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder: Experience in a State-Wide Diagnostic Service.
authors: Byrnes S, Collins F, Elliott E.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multiple CNVs and genes implicated, including CACNB2, CACNA1A, CACNA2D3)
Finding: Approximately 24.2% of children diagnosed with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) harbor rare copy number variants, with most being of uncertain clinical significance and some involving genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders.
Disease: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

title: Pan-cancer investigation identifies ARL4A as a prospective therapeutic indicator for thyroid cancer.
authors: Men Y, Zhao J, Feng R, Wang Z, Ye B, Zheng Y, Yang Z, Chen X, Zhang L, Wang N, Chen Y, Shao Y, Wang H, Song Y, Ding C.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL4A
Finding: ARL4A is downregulated in thyroid carcinoma tumors yet its overexpression in THCA cell lines promotes proliferation, migration, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and its expression correlates with poor survival and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.
Disease: Thyroid carcinoma (THCA)

title: Multi-Layer Omics Analysis Identifies Anxa3 and Coro1a as Candidate Targets of Pien Tze Huang in a Mouse Model of Liver Fibrosis.
authors: Wu H, Gao L, Zhao X, Li X, Lin Y, Chen L, Li L, Shen L, Bao W, Zhu J, Huai C, Chen Z, Zhuang Y, Qin S.
ai_summary:
Gene: ANXA3, CORO1A
Finding: Multi-layer omics analysis in a CCl4-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis identifies Anxa3 and Coro1a as candidate therapeutic targets of Pien Tze Huang, with significant inverse methylation-expression correlations validated at transcriptomic and proteomic levels.
Disease: Liver fibrosis

title: Astrocytic ankyrin-2 enables memory persistence in the mouse hippocampus.
authors: Kim H, Lim J, Kim J, Ozkan E, Kim GH, Park H, Park MG, Joo B, Lee S, Lee KJ, Kaang BK, Lee CJ, Koh W.
ai_summary:
Gene: ANK2
Finding: Astrocyte-specific deletion of Ank2 impairs remote memory persistence and long-term potentiation maintenance by reducing astrocyte–engram neuron contacts and disrupting BDNF/TrkB.T1/IP3R2-mediated astrocyte morphogenesis in the mouse hippocampus.
Disease: Long-term memory persistence (hippocampal-dependent memory)

title: Histone deacetylases and their inhibitors in kidney diseases.
authors: Zheng Y, Zhang TN, Hao PH, Yang N, Du Y.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
ai_summary: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are key regulators in the pathogenesis of kidney diseases, including chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, and diabetic kidney disease. HDAC inhibitors show therapeutic promise by modulating apoptosis, autophagy, inflammation, and fibrosis, though further research is needed to improve their selectivity, reduce toxicity, and overcome drug resistance.

title: The roles of cytoplasmic dynein complex in various ocular disorders.
authors: Zhou X, Xie J, Tong W, Fu J.
ai_summary: The cytoplasmic dynein complex, which mediates retrograde intracellular transport, is increasingly linked to ocular degenerative diseases. Mutations in dynein subunits and regulators cause ocular pathologies through mechanisms involving endoplasmic reticulum stress, impaired Notch signaling, and disrupted Sonic Hedgehog pathways, as shown in Drosophila, mouse, and zebrafish models. Integrating gene functional data across these models may refine gene-phenotype-mechanism correlations and advance precision diagnosis and targeted therapy for dynein-related ocular disorders.

title: Identification of a Duplication in the RP17 Locus in an Individual With Pathogenic CEP290 Variants: Implications for RP17 Variant Classification.
authors: Holtes LK, Chen D, Guilfoyle S, O'Leary H, Corral-Serrano JC, Boonen EGM, Haer-Wigman L, Nieuwenhuis SE, Guarascio R, Toulis V, Andrade de Jesus D, Cremers FPM, Thiadens AAHJ, Cheetham ME, de Bruijn SE, Hardcastle AJ, Roosing S.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP290
Finding: A novel 324-kb duplication in the RP17 locus is classified as likely benign because it does not disrupt chromatin looping or upregulate GDPD1 expression, whereas the proband's cone dystrophy is caused by biallelic CEP290 variants that induce pseudoexon inclusion and exon 36 skipping.
Disease: Cone dystrophy

title: RGS22 is a metazoa-specific radial spoke component required for coordinated ciliary beating.
authors: Fang A, Luo J, Xu H, Peng YJ, Xu W, Cao H, Li W, Dai J, Shi Z, Wang Y, Li XM, Zhao H, Gui M, Yu C, Zhu X, Zhang Q.
ai_summary:
Gene: RGS22
Finding: RGS22 is a metazoa-specific radial spoke component of RS1/2 complexes; its deficiency in mice causes RS1 deformation, outer dynein arm disorganization, impaired planar polarity with unsynchronized ciliary beating, and progressive ciliary loss.
Disease: Postnatal hydrocephalus

title: Structure of the ciliary tip central pair reveals the unique role of the microtubule-seam binding protein SPEF1.
authors: Legal T, Joachimiak E, Parra M, Peng W, Tam A, Black C, Guha M, Nguyen CA, Ghanaeian A, Valente-Paterno M, Brouhard G, Gaertig J, Wloga D, Bui KH.
ai_summary:
Gene: SPEF1
Finding: SPEF1 binds to microtubule seams and crosslinks the two central pair microtubules at the ciliary tip, stabilizing microtubules in vitro and maintaining axoneme integrity.
Disease: Ciliary tip structural integrity (motile cilia function)

title: Transcriptomics Reveals L-Carnitine to Enhance Semen Quality in Malabari Bucks via Nutrigenomic Regulation of Key Biological Processes Associated With Male Fertility.
authors: Shashikiran D, Asaf M, Abraham BL, Anand LF, Murugan S, Naheef K, Surendra GT, Madhuri J, Vigneshwaran B, Nisha TS, Promod K.
ai_summary:
Gene: PMS1, ZFAND4, MYSM1, EEFSEC, CEP126
Finding: L-carnitine supplementation in Malabari bucks improves semen quality (acrosomal and plasma membrane integrity, oxidative stress markers) via transcriptomic changes, including upregulation of spermatogenesis-related processes and identification of hub genes associated with male fertility.
Disease: Male infertility (in Malabari bucks)

title: Transcriptomic and functional responses of human airway cells to vaped ∆8-THC and its oxidation product ∆8-THCQ.
authors: Love CA, Kim HH, Rager JE, Tallman KA, Schichlein KD, Porter NA, Jaspers I.
ai_summary: Vaping Δ8-THC generates substantial amounts of the reactive electrophile Δ8-THCQ (HU-336), which rises an average of 3.67-fold in high-potency products to millimolar levels. In bronchial epithelial cells, Δ8-THCQ—but not Δ8-THC alone—induced marked gene-expression changes activating cilia-related, stress-response, xenobiotic-metabolism, and inflammatory pathways. Aerosols from commercial Δ8-THC mixtures rapidly induced immediate-early stress genes, suppressed ribosomal and mitochondrial programs, activated fibrosis-linked signaling, and impaired motile-cilia activity, whereas milder "juice" products mainly upregulated cell-cycle pathways. These findings suggest that repeated inhalation of vaped Δ8-THC may disrupt mucociliary defense and raise concern for chronic airway injury.

title: Associations between READ1 deletion, reading proficiency, and white matter network organisation in children with and without developmental dyslexia.
authors: Di Stefano M, Mascheretti S, Lampis V, Di Segni M, Mauri C, Maccarone F, Arrigoni F, Peruzzo D.
ai_summary:
Gene: DCDC2
Finding: The READ1 deletion within intron 2 of DCDC2 is associated with subtle but widespread reductions in white matter network integration (lower global efficiency, local efficiency, and clustering coefficient) and altered nodal connectivity across lateral, occipital, and frontal cortex, independent of reading performance.
Disease: Developmental dyslexia

title: Genome-Wide Association and Meta-Analysis Identify Candidate Genes for Sperm Freezability in Duroc and Yorkshire Boars.
authors: Wu S, He J, Liang Q, Li X, Lu Z, Li Z, Ji H, Feng Y, Zhuang Z, Zhao Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC181, PARN, SOX9, NCKAP5L
Finding: Genome-wide association and meta-analysis in Duroc and Yorkshire boars identified significant SNPs and candidate genes associated with sperm freezability, with variants in PARN and MAP2K6 showing strong additive effects on sperm recovery rate.
Disease: Boar sperm freezability (a reproductive trait in pigs)

title: TACC3, correlated with immune cell infiltrates, is a novel prognostic biomarker in BRCA.
authors: Li Z, Zhou X, Wu X, Li H, Zhou C.
ai_summary:
Gene: TACC3
Finding: High TACC3 expression in breast cancer tissues is associated with poor overall and disease-free survival and positively correlates with tumor-infiltrating immune cells, indicating its potential as a prognostic biomarker.
Disease: Breast cancer (BRCA)

title: Alliin Regulates Intracellular Cholesterol Metabolism Through the PCSK9/LDLR Axis in Ox-LDL-Induced HepG2 Cells: A Proteomics Study.
authors: Tang Y, Liu X.
ai_summary:
Gene: PCSK9/LDLR
Finding: Alliin reduces intracellular cholesterol and triglyceride levels in ox-LDL-induced HepG2 cells by upregulating LDLR and downregulating PCSK9, thereby modulating the PCSK9/LDLR pathway.
Disease: Lipid metabolism-related disorders (hypercholesterolemia context)

title: Gene expression adaptation of metastases to their host tissue.
authors: Nagel L, Wenzel M, Hoppe S, Karimpour M, Plum PS, Hamoudi A, Jahan I, Schmitt S, Franitza M, Wahba R, Bludau M, Bruns CJ, Quaas A, Beyer A, Hillmer AM.
ai_summary:
Gene: PPAR-α
Finding: Metastatic colorectal cancer cells adapt to their host liver tissue by shifting gene expression toward benign liver epithelial programs, including PPAR-α-regulated lipid metabolism.
Disease: Colorectal adenocarcinoma with liver metastasis

title: Increased PRSS56 expression is a causal factor and therapeutic target for human axial high myopia.
authors: Wu B, Zeng W, Tang K, Xiong J, Mo X, Fu Q, Fu D, Chu R, Zhao G, Lu L, Wang Z, Wu L, Yu Z, Zhou X, Wang H.
ai_summary:
Gene: PRSS56
Finding: Noncoding promoter variants (c.-187G>T and c.-187G>C) increase PRSS56 expression via enhanced EGR1 binding, and higher PRSS56 levels causally drive ocular axial elongation in a dose- and activity-dependent manner.
Disease: High myopia (MYP12)

title: Optics-free spatial genomics for mapping mammalian brain aging by IRISeq.
authors: Abdulraouf A, Jiang W, Zhang Z, Xu Z, Lu Z, Merlinsky T, Liao A, Doymaz A, Isakov S, Raihan T, Zhou W, Cao J.
ai_summary:
Gene: Rag1, Prkdc
Finding: Lymphocyte deficiency (Rag1 and Prkdc mutants) alters brain aging by downregulating interferon signaling and inflammation in ventricular regions, upregulating senescence pathways, and preserving ependymal cell abundance and distinct microglial state dynamics.
Disease: Brain aging

title: Longitudinal Behavior of the Hyper-Reflective Ganglion Cell Layer Band and Its Association With Ellipsoid Zone Constriction Rate in RP.
authors: Antropoli A, Toscani R, Scalabrin G, Forte G, Bianco L, Del Fabbro S, Caliandro E, Pina A, Arrigo A, Bandello F, Battaglia Parodi M.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not specified (photoreceptor-associated genes)
Finding: The hyper-reflective ganglion cell layer band (HGB) is a stable OCT finding in retinitis pigmentosa, associated with increased ganglion cell layer thickness and a slower rate of ellipsoid zone constriction.
Disease: Retinitis pigmentosa

title: Phosphatase and tensin homolog: A potential target for therapeutic intervention in optic nerve regeneration.
authors: Tong B, Song Y, Li Z, Cai M, Qi H, Su K, Xu HA.
ai_summary:
Gene: PTEN (phosphatase and tensin homolog)
Finding: Suppression of PTEN promotes optic nerve regeneration through activation of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway, enhancing retinal ganglion cell survival, mitochondrial transport, mitophagy, synaptic reconstruction, and remyelination across five regeneration phases.
Disease: Optic nerve injury/regeneration (central nervous system regeneration context)

title: In vivo delivery strategies for therapeutic CRISPR genome editing.
authors: Martin L, Bohinc J, Recchia A, Gritti S, Santilli G, Zeyland J, Vidaković M, Grdović N, Benabdellah K, Ortiz-Bueno M, Butuner BD, Pisaniello L, Stilhano R, Benati D, Hapil FZ, Khawaja S, Nair RR, Giacomelli C, Atilla E, Zinghirino F, Ferrari T, Corradi F, Laufer TJ, Khnykin D, Aseguinolaza GG, Skrbinek M, Mlakar T, Lapanja T, Lainšček D.
ai_summary:
This is a review article on delivery strategies for in vivo CRISPR-based genome editing, covering various delivery modalities and their organ-specific constraints. It does not establish a link between a specific gene, a finding, and a disease phenotype, so a plain-language summary is appropriate.

In vivo delivery of CRISPR therapeutics is a critical barrier to their clinical translation, with anatomical, cellular, and immunological factors shaping organ-specific editing strategies. The review outlines recent advances in delivery chemistry and vector engineering that enable direct in vivo editing, highlighting key preclinical and clinical milestones and remaining challenges for durable, tissue-selective therapies.

title: Signaling pathways regulating cardiac regeneration.
authors: Li J, Hu M, Ding L, Wang Y.
ai_summary: This review summarizes current knowledge of molecular mechanisms driving cardiac regeneration, focusing on signaling pathways (Hippo/YAP, Wnt/β-catenin, NRG1-ErbB, MAPK, Notch), transcriptional regulators, and extracellular matrix components that control cardiomyocyte proliferation and repair. It highlights remaining challenges such as spatiotemporal control of proliferation and therapeutic delivery, and discusses emerging translational technologies including engineered myocardial grafts and modified mRNA systems.

title: Protein persulfidation: a ubiquitous modification regulating a broad spectrum of biological processes.
authors: Romero LC, Carrillo R, Montesinos-Pereira D, Luque C, Aroca A, Gotor C.
ai_summary: Protein persulfidation is a widespread post-translational modification in plants, driven by hydrogen sulfide signaling and reversed by the thioredoxin system. Proteomic studies in Arabidopsis and crops identify over 11,700 persulfidated proteins, many involved in primary and secondary metabolism, as well as processes such as proteolysis, defense, embryo development, protein transport, and responses to cold, abscisic acid, oxidative stress, and water deprivation. This review highlights the broad regulatory role of persulfidation in plant biology and suggests future research directions.

title: Langer mesomelic dysplasia as a rare manifestation of SHOX deficiency: a narrative review.
authors: Piwar H, Pawlasek J, Sielaff P, Sztachelska M, Ordak M.
ai_summary:
Gene: SHOX
Finding: Complete or functionally complete deficiency of SHOX causes severe disproportionate short stature with marked mesomelic limb shortening, including hypoplasia/aplasia of the ulna and fibula.
Disease: Langer mesomelic dysplasia

title: Argonaute proteins orchestrate Meiotic Sex Chromosome Inactivation and timing of the spermatogenic transcriptional program.
authors: Carro MLM, Dziubek A, Touey-May A, Popkowski EA, Abdelmassih M, Simon LE, Tanis SL, Ahmed F, Grenier JK, Grimson A, Cohen PE.
ai_summary:
Gene: AGO3, AGO4
Finding: AGO3 and AGO4 localize to sex chromatin in pachytene spermatocytes and are required for Meiotic Sex Chromosome Inactivation and timely repression of spermiogenesis genes during prophase I; their combined loss disrupts gene regulation and chromatin accessibility, causing reduced fertility.
Disease: Male infertility (reduced sperm production, abnormal sperm morphology, impaired fertilization)

title: GLI3 in cancer: a context-dependent regulator with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic potential.
authors: Wang Y, Wu J, Zhong D, Jun X.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI3
Finding: GLI3 acts as a context-dependent regulator in cancer, with oncogenic or tumor-suppressive effects governed by the balance between its activator (GLI3A) and repressor (GLI3R) isoforms, influencing epithelial-mesenchymal transition, cancer stem cell maintenance, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance.
Disease: Malignant tumors (cancer)

title: Anesthetic Management of Cesarean Delivery in a Patient With Ellis-van Creveld Syndrome.
authors: Kalvapudi D, Shah SA, Singh H.
ai_summary:
Gene: EVC2
Finding: A heterozygous EVC2 gene variant was identified in a 23-year-old pregnant patient with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome, who was successfully managed with neuraxial spinal anesthesia for repeat cesarean section without perioperative complications.
Disease: Ellis-van Creveld syndrome

title: Tendon stem/progenitor cells in heterotopic ossification: functional regulation, molecular mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies.
authors: Zhu X, Gao Y, Cai M, Jiang H, Gao R, Tang H, Liu T, Zhou X, Lai B.
ai_summary: Tendon stem/progenitor cells (TSPCs) are a key cellular source of heterotopic ossification (HO), a pathological process where ectopic bone forms in soft tissues like tendons. Under trauma or inflammation, TSPCs undergo abnormally activated chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation—regulated by BMP and NF-κB signaling pathways—shifting their fate from tendon repair to ectopic bone formation. This review highlights that drugs and biomaterials targeting TSPC function show potential for HO prevention and treatment, with future research needed on TSPC heterogeneity and regulatory network dynamics.

title: Regulatory Signaling Pathways in Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells: Their Role in Tumor Progression and Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Amalia D, Febriani F, Arfianti A.
ai_summary: Ovarian cancer stem cells (OCSCs) drive tumor formation, progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance in ovarian cancer. Their key properties are sustained by the Wnt/β-catenin, Notch, and Hedgehog signaling pathways, which act synergistically rather than independently. Although targeted agents against these pathways (e.g., γ-secretase inhibitors, smoothened inhibitors, and Wnt/β-catenin inhibitors) show antitumor activity in preclinical and early clinical studies, their efficacy is limited by compensatory cross-talk between pathways, highlighting the need for combination and personalized therapeutic strategies.

title: Integration of transcriptome and DNA methylation reveals the mechanism of cilia-related genes in recurrent miscarriage.
authors: Li J, Jing J, Liu J, Zhang D, Zhang L, Xie G.
ai_summary:
Gene: SLC1A2
Finding: Methylation-regulated cilia-related gene SLC1A2 is overexpressed in recurrent miscarriage chorionic tissue, correlates with reduced CD4+ T cell, effector memory CD4+ T cell, and Th2 cell infiltration, and is linked to spliceosome, cell cycle, and proteasome pathways.
Disease: Recurrent miscarriage

title: KIF7 promotes the proliferation of clear cell renal cell carcinoma by activating the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway.
authors: Wang Y, Wang XM, Huo D, Wang SB, Liu QY, Pang J, Shen T, Cui D, Zhao WJ, Luo QF, Li N, Chen AQ, Cui J.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF7
Finding: KIF7 is overexpressed in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and promotes tumor cell proliferation by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, correlating with poor survival and altered immune infiltration.
Disease: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC)

title: Mechanotransduction in intervertebral disc degeneration: from compartment-specific sensors to translational frontiers.
authors: Li H, Han C, Yang G, Zheng J, Peng B, Chen J, Liu H, Zhu L, Feng M.
ai_summary: Intervertebral disc degeneration is increasingly understood as a disorder of mechanobiological dysregulation, where disc cells sense mechanical cues through diverse sensors (e.g., Piezo1, TRP channels, integrins, primary cilia) that converge on downstream hubs like YAP/TAZ and MAPK/NF-κB to drive cell-fate programs. The extracellular matrix both transmits and is remodeled by these signals, creating a self-reinforcing degenerative loop. Mechanistic research is concentrated in nucleus pulposus models, with limited cross-compartment data, and while biomaterial-based injectable hydrogels show early translational promise, most progress remains preclinical.

title: L-type voltage-gated Ca<sup>2+</sup> channels control T cell killing via non-canonical Hedgehog signalling.
authors: Beke F, Hanna J, Kapeni C, Carbonaro V, Mueller N, Trotter S, Chilamakuri C, O'Brien LM, de la Roche M.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI1
Finding: TCR-induced extracellular calcium influx through L-type voltage-gated Ca2+ (Cav1) channels drives non-canonical, Hedgehog-ligand-independent induction of the transcription factor Gli1, which is required for cytotoxic T lymphocyte killing in vitro and in vivo.
Disease: Not applicable (immune effector function relevant to cancer immunotherapy and CAR T cell therapy)

title: Identification of N4-Acetylcytidine-Related Biomarkers in Adult Asthma: An Integrative Multi-Omics Study.
authors: Zhang M, Lin H, Huang Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: MCM5, PUM1, TRIP6, PALM, NPEPL1
Finding: These five N4-acetylcytidine-related genes were identified as biomarkers for adult asthma, with MCM5, TRIP6, and PALM acting as protective factors and the others as risk factors, validated through multi-omics and in vitro expression analyses.
Disease: Adult asthma

title: HNF1B-related disease: developmental origins, molecular mechanisms, and multisystem clinical challenges.
authors: Heneberg P.
ai_summary:
Gene: HNF1B
Finding: Variants or deletions in HNF1B cause a multisystem developmental disorder affecting the kidney, pancreas, liver, genitourinary tract, and nervous system, with large 17q12 deletions correlating with neuropsychiatric features.
Disease: HNF1B-MODY (HNF1B-related disease)

title: Evaluation of Itraconazole as a repurposed small molecule inhibitor of EMT in breast cancer: a molecular docking and dynamics study.
authors: Gayam PKR, Kulkarni AM, Aranjani JM.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI1
Finding: Itraconazole does not directly inhibit GLI1, as molecular dynamics simulations show significant structural instability in the GLI1-itraconazole complex, whereas SMO is identified as the primary high-affinity target.
Disease: Breast cancer

title: Signal-driven interplay between lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis orchestrates osteoarthritis degeneration.
authors: Kulyar MF, Pachaleva J, Brazaite S, Akhtar M, Hasan MM, Kaboli S, Lebedis I, Bernotiene E.
ai_summary:
Gene: GPX4
Finding: Impaired GPX4 activity drives ferroptosis in chondrocytes, contributing to osteoarthritis degeneration through lipid peroxide accumulation and inflammatory signaling.
Disease: Osteoarthritis

title: Glutathione metabolism-linked ferroptosis in human seminoma: a spatial multi-omics mapping study.
authors: Deng C, Li J, Guo Z, Zhu J, Zhao Q, Fang Z, Zheng J, Ran L, Li R, Li X, Gong K, Peng J, Wang A, Guo J, Yang Y, Jiang H, Jin Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: SLC7A11 (xCT)
Finding: Glutathione metabolism-linked ferroptosis is a convergent regulatory pathway in seminoma, and inhibiting glutathione synthesis or xCT induces ferroptosis and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.
Disease: Seminoma (testicular cancer)

title: Vismodegib Improved Therapy of Medulloblastoma by Targeting Sonic Hedgehog Signaling Pathway on DAOY Medulloblastoma Cell Line.
authors: Behruzi M, Ghorbanlou M, Shabani R, Rustamzadeh A, Gorgich EA, Seidkhani E, Usefi F, Mehdizadeh M, Moradi F.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI1
Finding: Vismodegib treatment of DAOY medulloblastoma cells significantly reduced expression of SMO, GLI1, and MYCN, key components of the sonic hedgehog signaling pathway, while increasing pro-apoptotic Bax and p53 and decreasing anti-apoptotic Bcl2 activity.
Disease: Medulloblastoma

title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
authors: Li Y, Ning J, Wang A, Shi M, Chen Y, Liu G, Sun S.
ai_summary: CAPER is a matrix factorization tool for multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing data that separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation while preserving the biological signal of interest. It outputs an interpretable, batch-corrected expression matrix and was validated through simulations and three real-world datasets (immune-stimulated PBMCs, lung adenocarcinoma tumor microenvironment, and type 1 diabetes), where it accurately recovered differentially expressed genes and identified the most responsive cell populations. CAPER provides a robust method for extracting meaningful biological signals from complex multi-condition scRNA-seq data in disease research.

title: Expanded Hepatic Progenitor Cells Featured with Aggregation of α-Synuclein Contribute to Pathologic Bile Duct Regeneration in Biliary Atresia.
authors: Xie H, Zhu M, Zhu Z, Tang J, Zhang R, Ding Z, Li J, Wu Z, Tam PKH, Wang Q, Lui VCH, Xia Y, Tang W.
ai_summary:
Gene: SNCA (α-synuclein)
Finding: Expanded NCAM1+EpCAM+ hepatic progenitor cells accumulate α-synuclein, which impairs biliary differentiation, reduces glutathione content, and increases mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, driving aberrant bile duct regeneration.
Disease: Biliary atresia

title: The Therapeutic Use of Natural Products in Myopia Prevention: Recent Applications.
authors: Wang G, Ren C, Dong X, Zhao L, Guo B.
ai_summary: This review discusses natural products as a potential strategy for myopia prevention, given the limitations of current behavioral, optical, and pharmacological interventions. It highlights the advantages of natural products—diverse structures, availability, biological activity, and low toxicity—and summarizes recent findings on their application, aiming to support the development of new preventive approaches.

title: Signalling through RXRβ and its agonist, bexarotene, promotes neuron formation in Xenopus laevis embryos.
authors: Lopes Cardoso D, Loizou M, Fourla DD, Woodman C, Guille MJ, Sharpe C.
ai_summary:
Gene: RXRβ
Finding: Signalling through RXRβ and its agonist bexarotene promotes neuronal differentiation in Xenopus laevis embryos and ectodermal explants, activating genes for neuronal fate and posterior character including canonical Wnt pathway genes.
Disease: Not specified (neurogenesis-related, relevant to Alzheimer's disease models)

title: GHRHR Deficiency Enhances Retinal Ganglion Cell Survival and Visual Functions in Experimental Glaucoma by Inhibiting Ferroptosis.
authors: Tong Y, Yam MH, Zhang J, Du L, Zhou L, Yip YWY, Ho BM, Bisnauthsing H, Li J, Kong I, Xu S, Fu C, So KKH, Vong JSL, Cen LP, Yang MM, Yousaf K, Sham MH, Chan SO, Chan PP, Pang CP, Tham CC, He JN, Li J, Chu WK.
ai_summary:
Gene: GPX4
Finding: GHRHR deficiency preserves retinal ganglion cell survival and visual function in glaucoma models by preventing the pathological downregulation of anti-ferroptotic mediators GPX4 and FTH1 and suppressing pro-ferroptotic ACSL4, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis.
Disease: Glaucoma

title: From mechanotransduction to manual therapy: advances in piezo/TRP channels and lumbar degeneration.
authors: Liu Z, Peng T, Li W, Zhu M.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: TRPV4 shows context-dependent effects in lumbar degeneration shaped by loading pattern, osmotic milieu, and tissue state, contributing to disturbed mechanotransduction alongside Piezo1 and Piezo2.
Disease: Degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis and related lumbar instability

title: Changes in Melanopsin expression in the iris after corneal abrasion in an experimental rat model.
authors: Jenike A, Zeimantz S, Gunter C, Jiang CL, Hegarty DM, Hilton TN, Matynia A, Largent-Milnes TM, Morgans CW, Aicher SA.
ai_summary: Melanopsin expression in the iris, but not the retina, increases transiently at 24 hours after corneal abrasion in rats, correlating with peak pain behavior and morphological changes in the pupillary ruff, before returning to baseline at 1 week. This suggests that dynamic molecular and structural changes in the iris may contribute to ocular pain and photoallodynia following corneal injury.

title: The emerging roles of ITM2A: At the molecular crossroads of development and pathogenesis.
authors: Deng X, Wang Y, Yang L, Wu K, Qin W, Ali DW, Michalak M, Tang J, Zhou C, Chen XZ.
ai_summary: ITM2A is a type II transmembrane glycoprotein of the BRICHOS superfamily that regulates development and homeostasis by modulating multiple signaling pathways (BMP, JAK/STAT, ERK, Hedgehog, PKA-CREB) and is essential for differentiation of cartilage, bone, and muscle. Dysregulation of ITM2A is linked to malignancies, thyroid disorders, and acute transplant rejection, and this review highlights its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target, particularly in skeletal development and tumorigenesis.

title: Leveraging mechanobiology: Identifying mechanotransducers with potential applications for tendon repair.
authors: Stephenson TR, Wong MY, Schiele NR.
ai_summary: Tendons are collagen-rich tissues exposed to mechanical forces that affect their formation, maintenance, and injury response. This review summarizes recent discoveries in tendon mechanobiology, focusing on cell-level mechanotransduction mechanisms such as calcium signaling, activation of specific receptors and ion channels, and the role of primary cilia and downstream signaling pathways. These newly identified mechanotransducers show promise as therapeutic targets for improving tendon repair and preventing degeneration from aberrant mechanical loading.

title: Molecular and Cellular Hallmarks of Age-Related Vestibular Hair Cell Degeneration.
authors: Kulasooriya S, Liu H, Vijayakumar S, Bloom C, Xu Z, Tu S, Borgmeier BJ, Zhou M, Tao L, Kachar B, He DZ.
ai_summary: Age-related vestibular dysfunction (ARVD) is common in the elderly but poorly understood. Using single-cell RNA-seq on young and old mice, the authors show that old vestibular hair cells display aging hallmarks such as cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired proteostasis, along with cell type-specific changes in hair bundle architecture and mechanotransduction machinery. Imaging and electrophysiology confirm hair bundle degeneration and reduced mechanotransduction that precede hair cell loss, indicating impaired bundle function is a key driver of ARVD. Comparative analysis reveals shared and distinct aging signatures between vestibular and cochlear hair cells, offering insight into their differing rates of degeneration.

title: How to recognize if a cell dies from pyroptosis?
authors: Gebuza M, Bihl W, Brawańska-Maśluch K, Tomecka P, Kulbacki M, Kulbacka J.
ai_summary: Pyroptosis is a form of programmed cell death mediated by the inflammasome pathway, characterized by the release of proinflammatory cytokines, and distinct from apoptosis and necroptosis. This review discusses methods and key factors for detecting pyroptosis in cells, highlighting its dual role in cancer (promoting or suppressing tumors depending on context) and the potential of pyroptosis-related molecules as prognostic indicators and therapeutic targets.

title: Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies.
authors: Xu X, Chen J, Feng Y, Zou C, Peng X, Wang Z, Ma Y, Xie Y, Li H, Zhang D.
ai_summary: Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a complex clinical challenge involving progressive failure of two or more organ systems after severe insults. Its pathogenesis involves dynamic interactions across inflammatory responses, microcirculatory disruption, coagulation abnormalities, cell death, DNA damage, and reactive oxygen species production. Despite comprehensive therapeutic strategies, mortality remains high, highlighting the urgent need for research into pathogenesis, early biomarkers, and novel treatments.

title: The Dual Role of the Gut Microbiota in Cancer Chemoresistance.
authors: Tahmasebi H, Bahar A, Khazaei M, Arabestani MR.
ai_summary: The gut microbiota plays a dual role in cancer chemoresistance: certain "bad bacteria" contribute to treatment failure, while beneficial microbes such as Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia, and Lactobacillus can enhance treatment success. This review examines the molecular mechanisms involved—including microbial drug metabolism, immune modulation, regulation of cellular apoptosis, and metabolic crosstalk between tumors and the microbiome—and discusses emerging microbiome-centered therapies (fecal microbiota transplantation, probiotics, prebiotics, and dietary changes) that aim to overcome chemoresistance and personalize cancer treatment.

title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in ulcerative colitis: mucosal immune mechanisms and precision microbiota therapy.
authors: Lu E, Zhang M, Zhao Y, Meng H, Xu Z.
ai_summary: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is an investigational therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC) that aims to restore gut microbial balance.
