Mechanistic studies suggest FMT reshapes the microbiome, boosts short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, remodels bile acid and tryptophan signaling, strengthens the epithelial barrier, and modulates mucosal immunity (e.g., Th17/Treg balance, IgA responses, macrophage reprogramming, IL-10/IL-22 signaling). Randomized trials show FMT can induce clinical and endoscopic remission in selected UC patients, especially via lower gastrointestinal delivery with multi-donor or optimized regimens, but efficacy is limited in moderate-to-severe or biologic-refractory disease, and current guidelines do not recommend routine use outside trials. Personalized approaches—such as donor-recipient matching, dietary modulation, and next-generation microbiota therapeutics—may improve outcomes but need prospective validation.

title: Deconstruction of Human Age-Related Cataract Capsules Defines Aging.
authors: Tang Q, Tong Z, Fan C, Chen S, Guo J, Hu J, Yao K, Yin Z, Chen X, Yu Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: NRG1 (ligand) and ERBB3 (receptor)
Finding: In age-related cataract lens epithelial cells, cluster 0 highly expresses NRG1, which forms a stable ligand-receptor axis with ERBB3 on sympathetic neurons, and neuronal axon-like ingrowth with SLIT-ROBO signaling enrichment is associated with cataractogenesis and progression.
Disease: Age-related cataract (ARC)

title: An update in the MRI features, classification, and associated brain abnormalities in hypothalamic hamartomas.
authors: Rahimian E, Tahsini MR, Azin N, Ghafouri-Fard S, Habibabadi JM, Fesharaki SSH, Farahvash MA, Farahvash S, Morovvati M, Bisdas S.
ai_summary: Hypothalamic hamartomas (HHs) are rare, non-neoplastic brain malformations often linked to gelastic seizures and precocious puberty. In this retrospective MRI/MRS study of 18 patients, most HHs were isointense on T1 and T2-weighted imaging, and half had concurrent brain abnormalities such as focal cortical dysplasia, amygdala enlargement, and corpus callosum hypoplasia. Elevated choline-to-N-acetylaspartate (Cho/NAA) ratios were observed in some cases, suggesting metabolic alterations, particularly in seizure-related HHs, and the authors propose this ratio as a potential biomarker for better understanding HH pathophysiology and diagnosis.

title: Reactive Oxygen and Nitrogen Species in Male Reproductive Health: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Consequences.
authors: Wang S, Chung JPW, Chan DYL.
ai_summary: Reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) play a dual role in male reproductive health: physiological levels are required for sperm function, but overproduction causes oxidative/nitrosative stress that damages sperm DNA, proteins, and lipids, impairs motility and fertility, and disrupts hormonal regulation. This stress is implicated in disorders such as varicocele, genital tract infections, obesity, diabetes, and toxicant-related dysfunction. The review highlights the clinical value of integrating oxidative stress assessment with semen analysis and notes that antioxidant supplementation shows promise but requires standardized protocols.

title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Pleiotropic Effects of Scandium Chloride on C2C12 Myoblasts.
authors: Zhao J, An Y, Shi J, Ma L, He X, Liu Y, Liu C.
ai_summary: Scandium chloride (ScCl3) promotes proliferation of C2C12 myoblasts by inducing the G1/S phase transition, but only at a high concentration (1 mM), not at a low concentration (0.01 mM). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that scandium coordinates distinct functional modules involving mitosis, myogenesis, and metabolism, with key regulators including Foxo1, Rela, and myogenic transcription factors, suggesting regulatory effects on myoblast proliferation, differentiation, and metabolism.

title: Deciphering the role of tubulin's C-terminal tail in kinesin binding using computational and clustering approaches.
authors: Shen T, Li Y, Li Y, Zhao J, Ma J, Cheng H, Zhang J, Zhou M, Zheng W, Hu D, Li L, Liu K, Sun S.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF7
Finding: Computational simulations show that tubulin C-terminal tails extend outward to capture KIF7, then transition into α-helical conformations that enhance kinesin-microtubule binding affinity, with key hydrogen bonds (e.g., arginine 308 in kinesin, glutamine 410 in β-tubulin) stabilizing the interaction.
Disease: Not specified (microtubule-kinesin binding mechanism)

title: The Multifaceted Role of Pyroptosis: Molecular Mechanisms, Crosstalk with Other Cell Death Pathways, and Therapeutic Implications.
authors: Boaru DL, De Castro-Martinez P, Garcia-Montero C, Fraile-Martinez O, Alhaddadin MNM, Barrena-Blázquez S, Lopez-Gonzalez L, Fernández CT, Alvarado-Hurtado R, Giménez TR, Lasa-Unzúe I, Alonso MD, Gutiérrez-Calvo A, Saez MA, Cobo-Prieto D, Saz JV, Alvarez-Mon M, Diaz-Pedrero R, Ortega MA.
ai_summary: Pyroptosis is a proinflammatory form of programmed cell death mediated by gasdermin pore formation, activated through multiple pathways including canonical/noncanonical inflammasomes, caspase-3/8-gasdermin axes, and granzyme mechanisms. It engages in extensive crosstalk with other cell death modalities (apoptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, NETosis, PANoptosis) via shared regulators. The review systematically dissects pyroptosis molecular mechanisms, its interplay with other death programs, and its contributions to cancer, infectious, autoimmune, metabolic, and cardiovascular diseases, while evaluating therapeutic strategies to inhibit or exploit pyroptosis.

title: Genetic screens of imaging-derived kidney volumes identify genes linked to kidney function.
authors: Monteiro-Martins S, Li Y, Borisov O, Khan A, Reichardt W, Haug S, Kellner E, Buechert M, Ott E, Russe MF, Bamberg F, Kiryluk K, Sekula P, Reisert M, Köttgen A.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: Genome-wide association studies of MRI-derived kidney sub-volumes identified PKHD1 as a locus strongly associated with kidney volumes but not with eGFR, complementing kidney function studies.
Disease: Chronic kidney disease (CKD)

title: Effects of early life adversity on acute metabolic outcomes during neonatal development.
authors: Lapp HE, Salazar MG, Deveraux E, Misztal PK, Champagne FA.
ai_summary: Early life adversity, modeled in rats using limited bedding and nesting material (LBN), alters maternal behavior, milk composition (increasing corticosterone and triglycerides), and acute metabolic outcomes in pups, including serum hormones, estimated energy expenditure, and gene expression in the liver and hypothalamus. These effects are timing- and sex-specific and linked to individual milk components and pup weight, suggesting that early adversity shapes metabolic programming through interacting pathways that may increase later vulnerability to metabolic and endocrine dysfunction.

title: Cell-Free Fat Extract (CEFFE) as a Versatile Cell-Free Biologic for Multitissue Regeneration: From Skin and Bone to Nerve, Reproductive, and Systemic Applications-A Comprehensive Review.
authors: Karimi Rouzbahani A, Aliakbari M, Amiri B, Fereydoonnezhad T, Behzadi A, Delfani S, Sharafi Z, Miran S, Marzban A.
ai_summary: CEFFE is an adipose-derived, cell-free biologic containing growth factors and regulatory proteins that promotes regeneration across multiple tissue types. Through a review of over 55 preclinical and clinical studies, the authors find that CEFFE accelerates tissue repair via three conserved mechanisms: antiapoptotic survival signaling, context-specific immunomodulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling with angiogenesis. Emerging evidence supports its efficacy in intervertebral disc degeneration, corneal neurodegeneration, sepsis, and as an IVF culture supplement, while clinical trials confirm safety and efficacy in dermatological applications and superiority over hyaluronic acid for early-to-mid-stage osteoarthritis, though standardized dosing and batch consistency remain challenges.

title: A narrative review on the role of autophagy in male infertility-associated sperm abnormalities.
authors: Jin YH, Gao DW, Li CY, Sun DL, Mo H, Jin BF.
ai_summary: Autophagy dysfunction is linked to sperm abnormalities that cause male infertility, including oligozoospermia, asthenozoospermia, teratozoospermia, and azoospermia. This narrative review synthesizes clinical and basic research on how aberrant autophagic activity disrupts spermatogenesis and sperm function, highlighting autophagy regulation as a potential therapeutic target for managing male infertility.

title: Gasdermin-Mediated Pyroptosis: Novel Strategies Against Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Guo K, Feng Y, Lu J, Abudurexiti N, Zhou X, Wei M, Zheng S.
ai_summary:
Gene: GSDMD, GSDME, GSDMC
Finding: Gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis has a dual role in colorectal cancer, where acute induction of pyroptosis in tumor cells (via GSDMD/GSDME) enhances antitumor immunity and therapy sensitivity, while chronic pyroptosis-driven inflammation and GSDMC activation can promote tumor progression.
Disease: Colorectal cancer

title: Use of Hedgehog Pathway Inhibitors in Combination Therapy for Basal Cell Carcinoma: A Review and Narrative Synthesis.
authors: Jeon H, Berman S, Zeitouni N.
journal: The Journal of clinical and aesthetic dermatology
ai_summary: Combination therapies pairing Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (vismodegib or sonidegib) with agents such as radiation, photodynamic therapy, itraconazole, or intratumoral immunotherapy generally improved tumor response rates and tolerability compared to monotherapy in basal cell carcinoma, though vismodegib plus pembrolizumab performed worse than monotherapy. The review highlights these combinations as a promising strategy to overcome the adverse events and resistance that limit single-agent HHI use.

title: Migration of immune cells in tumors and inflammation: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targets.
authors: Lu Y, Shao D, Xiao Y, Jiang YZ, Shao ZM.
ai_summary: Immune cell migration into tumors and inflamed tissues is orchestrated by chemokine/cytokine networks, adhesion molecules, extracellular vesicle signaling, metabolic reprogramming, and microbiota, with immune reservoirs such as tertiary lymphoid structures and bone marrow serving as mobilization hubs. This trafficking shapes the local immune landscape, driving either protective immunity or disease progression. Therapeutic strategies targeting migration—including chemokine modulation, lymphatic/extracellular matrix reprogramming, diet, and microbiome manipulation—face hurdles from microenvironmental heterogeneity, poor migratory efficiency, and limitations in tracking cell dynamics, but integrating insights from oncology and inflammation may enable precision immunomodulation.

title: Unveiling Gut Homeostasis Disruption in Sepsis: Towards an Integrated Mechanistic and Translational Roadmap.
authors: Bao Y, Qi L, Zou G, Yang X, Ma Y, Li Z, Du X, Zhao P.
ai_summary: Sepsis disrupts gut homeostasis through oxidative stress and inflammatory cascades that compromise intestinal barrier integrity and local immunity, leading to increased permeability, bacterial translocation, and systemic inflammation via gut-liver and gut-brain crosstalk. This review synthesizes recent advances in the pathophysiology of sepsis-induced intestinal injury, highlighting key signaling networks, candidate biomarkers for early diagnosis, and the therapeutic potential of intestinal-protective agents, including insights from traditional Chinese medicine, to propose a translational framework for clinical management.

title: Dynamic Landscape of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 Modification During Postnatal Leydig Cell Fate Determination.
authors: Sun J, Lian X, Luo S, Lin Z, Luo L, Zheng M, Zhang D, Lin Z, Wang X, Wang S.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no single gene-disease link established; study focuses on epigenetic marks H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 in Leydig cells)

Finding: This study maps the dynamic, stage-specific changes of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 during postnatal mouse Leydig cell differentiation, revealing that steroidogenic genes (e.g., Star, Cyp17a1, Hsd17b3) are regulated solely by H3K4me3, while H3K27me3 permanently silences proliferation genes (e.g., Ccna2, Mki67, Ccnd1) in adult cells. The authors propose an H3K4me3/H3K27me3-transcription factor-target gene axis that balances steroidogenic potential with loss of stemness.

Disease: Not applicable (basic developmental biology study, no disease phenotype specified)

title: Targeting Macrophage-Mediated Mechanisms in Sepsis-Induced Cardiomyopathy: From Pathophysiology to Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Wang J, Zhang J, Luo N, Zhou Z, Zhang Y, Guo K, Li R, Li C.
ai_summary: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a life-threatening complication of sepsis driven by dysregulated inflammation and complex cellular interactions. This review examines the dual role of macrophages in SICM, highlighting three key mechanisms: inflammatory activation via M1/M2 polarization, TLR4/NF-κB signaling, and inflammasome pathways; myocardial injury through oxidative stress, suppressed mitophagy, and MMP-9-mediated endothelial disruption; and regulatory layers involving immunometabolic reprogramming and intercellular communication with neutrophils, T cells, and complement signaling. The authors propose therapeutic strategies targeting macrophage polarization, metabolism, specific subsets like TREM2hi macrophages, and intercellular communication as a framework for precision immunotherapies in SICM.

title: Integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing with GWAS reveals regulatory networks underpinning complex traits in beef cattle.
authors: Zhang B, Qiu S, Du Z, Xiao H, Su Y, Tang A, Bao B, Zhu B, Chen Y, Gao X, Xu L, Wang Z, Zhang L, Gao H, Li J, Zheng C.
journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (multi-trait, multi-tissue study; no single gene-disease link)
Finding: This study integrates multi-trait GWAS with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to map tissue- and cell-type-specific regulatory networks for 20 beef cattle traits, identifying myofibers as key for carcass traits, hepatocytes for fatty acid and meat-quality traits, and cell-type-specific transcription factors (e.g., TBX15, SOX6, FOXA2) as regulators.
Disease: Not applicable (livestock complex traits, not a disease)

title: Mechanistic Links Underlying the Comorbidity of Osteoporosis and Osteoarthritis: Cell Fate Plasticity Driven by the Subchondral Bone Microenvironment.
authors: Zhang J, Chen B, Yang Q, Yan H, Xiao N, Xu Y, Zeng S, Zhao S, Wang R, Qian H, Xie Z, Xie J, Li Z.
ai_summary: This review examines the comorbidity of osteoporosis (OP) and osteoarthritis (OA), proposing that it is driven by disruption of the subchondral bone microenvironment rather than being a simple combination of bone loss and cartilage degeneration. The authors argue that microenvironmental changes—including mechanical imbalance, aberrant bone remodeling, inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and cellular senescence—induce phenotypic remodeling and fate deviation in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, bone remodeling cells, osteoimmune cells, and chondrocytes. They propose that microenvironment-driven cell fate plasticity serves as a key mechanistic hub linking OP and OA, offering a theoretical framework for early identification and combined targeted interventions.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of the host-tumor metabolic interface: Implications for precision nutritional oncology.
authors: Li M, Huang C, Yu S.
ai_summary: This is a review article, not a study linking a specific gene to a disease. It discusses the systemic metabolic interactions between host and tumor, proposing a framework for precision nutritional oncology that integrates diet, microbiome, and multi-omic biomarkers to improve cancer therapy outcomes. No specific gene-disease link is established.

title: PANoptosis in diabetic retinopathy: immunological insights into mechanisms and translational therapies.
authors: Ma L, Hou N, Zhao X, Li Z, Liu Q, Zhao J, Wang Q.
ai_summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness driven by hyperglycemia-induced neurovascular damage. This review examines the emerging role of PANoptosis—an integrated inflammatory cell death pathway combining apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis—in DR progression, noting that supporting evidence varies across clinical specimens, animal models, and cell cultures. The authors summarize PANoptosome signaling networks, non-coding RNA regulation, and immune-metabolic crosstalk, and discuss candidate biomarkers and therapeutic strategies including small-molecule inhibitors, gene intervention, and nanomedicine. They caution that PANoptosis has context-dependent dual roles, and that non-selective blockade carries safety risks, so they advocate for biomarker-guided, locally delivered, stage-specific, and cell-type-targeted interventions rather than systemic suppression. The review concludes that PANoptosis is a dynamic conceptual framework for understanding inflammatory neurovascular degeneration in DR, but not yet a fully confirmed clinical target, emphasizing the need for DR-specific mechanistic studies, longitudinal biomarker cohorts, and multicenter trials.

title: Comparative Impact of Selenium Selenite and Nano-Selenium on Physiological Functions in Male Goat Kids.
authors: Dhruw K, Garg AK, Chaturvedani AK, Singh AK.
journal: Journal of animal physiology and animal nutrition
ai_summary: Nano-selenium supplementation in male goat kids improved antioxidant status (increased glutathione peroxidase activity), enhanced humoral and cell-mediated immune responses, and boosted sperm quality parameters, without affecting growth, nutrient digestibility, or metabolic health. Higher supplementation levels (0.30 ppm) produced the greatest benefits, suggesting nano-selenium may serve as a functional micronutrient to support reproductive and immunological resilience in goats.

title: The Concise Guide to PHARMACOLOGY 2025/26: Catalytic receptors.
authors: Alexander SPH, Fabbro D, Peach CJ, Gibb AJ, Kelly E, Mathie AA, Veale EL, Armstrong JF, Faccenda E, Harding SD, Southan C, Davies JA, Beuve A, Brouckaert P, Bryant C, Burnett JC, Farndale RW, Friebe A, Garthwaite J, Hobbs AJ, Jarvis GE, Kilpatrick L, Koesling D, Kuhn M, Leitinger B, MacEwan D, Monie TP, Potter LR, Russwurm M, Schmidt HHHW, Stasch JP, Waldman SA.
ai_summary: This article is a reference guide describing the seventh edition of the Concise Guide to Pharmacology, which catalogs drug targets and ligands. It does not report a specific experimental finding linking a gene to a disease. The guide provides a comparative overview of approximately 1900 human drug targets and nearly 7000 interactions, including a section on catalytic receptors, and serves as a citable, point-in-time record of pharmacological data curated with IUPHAR.

title: Regulation of mitochondrial function during spermatogenesis and sperm maturation.
authors: Meng K, Zhu Z, Jia H, Feng Y, Feng J, Shen Y, Jiang W, Liu C, Qin Q, Gao F, Yuan J.
ai_summary: Mitochondria are essential for male fertility, undergoing dynamic changes and mitophagy during spermatogenesis, sperm maturation, and fertilization to meet energy demands and clear damaged mitochondrial DNA. Mitochondrial dysfunction—caused by external factors—disrupts energy supply, induces oxidative stress and apoptosis, and leads to abnormal sperm structure and male infertility. The review discusses these mechanisms chronologically from spermatogonial stem cell division to fertilization and highlights mitochondrial function as a potential therapeutic target for improving male fertility.

title: Integrated Engineering of CAR-T Cells for Solid Tumours.
authors: Yang C, Li T, He P, Zhao Z, Li S, Wang L.
ai_summary:
This is a review article on CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumours, not a ciliopathy or gene-disease study. It discusses integrated engineering strategies—logic-gated receptors, metabolic/epigenetic reprogramming, and tumour microenvironment modulation—to overcome barriers like antigen heterogeneity and T-cell exhaustion, with emphasis on managing toxicities like cytokine release syndrome.

CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumours remains limited by antigen heterogeneity, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and T-cell dysfunction. This review highlights a shift toward integrated engineering that combines controllable activation (logic-gated, regulatable receptors), intrinsic resilience (metabolic/epigenetic reprogramming), and extrinsic microenvironment modulation (depleting regulatory cells, blocking 'don't eat me' signals, biomaterial scaffolds). The authors conclude that rational, multi-axis combinations—rather than isolated optimizations—are needed to close the efficacy gap with haematologic cancers, while carefully managing toxicities such as cytokine release syndrome.

title: Supplementation of the freezing extender with glutathione peroxidase improves the post-thaw quality of ram semen by enhancing antioxidant capacity, regulating metabolic enzyme activity, and modulating proteome expression.
authors: Wang K, Zhou Q, Wang Y, Shen Z, Li J, Li X, Shi S, Yan Y, Zhang C, Lei S, Ren Y.
ai_summary: Supplementation of ram semen freezing extender with 1.6 U/L glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) improves post-thaw sperm quality by enhancing motility, viability, and structural integrity (acrosome, plasma membrane, DNA), increasing antioxidant capacity (T-AOC, superoxide dismutase, catalase), reducing oxidative stress (lower malondialdehyde), and altering metabolic enzyme activity and proteome expression (e.g., upregulation of G1 to S Phase Transition 1 and ribosomal protein L11, downregulation of annexin A2).

title: The current landscape of indole hybrids with in vivo antitumor potential.
authors: Ling H, Congcong Z.
ai_summary: Indole hybrids are multi-target anticancer compounds that can modulate multiple cancer cell pathways, potentially overcoming drug resistance and side effects of single-agent therapies. This review summarizes indole hybrids developed since 2021—including indole-azoles, indole-chalcones, indole-sulfonamides, indole-sulfones, indole-ureas, and indole-hydrazides—that have been evaluated for in vivo antitumor activity, metabolic stability, pharmacokinetics, toxicity, and mechanisms of action, providing a foundation for future rational drug design.

title: Oxidative Stress and its Implications for Male Reproductive Dysfunction: Mechanistic Insights, Clinical Impacts, and Advances in Therapeutic Interventions.
authors: Yu X, Jin M, Zhang Y, Lu Y, Zhu R, Liu YF, Jie Ma Y, Song J, Sun J.
ai_summary: Oxidative stress impairs male fertility through reactive oxygen species that cause sperm membrane lipid peroxidation, DNA damage, and apoptosis. Lifestyle and environmental factors worsen this oxidative imbalance, and antioxidant therapies plus novel ROS-detection diagnostics are emerging as key strategies to mitigate damage and restore reproductive function.

title: Exosome Nanotherapy Rescues Male Fertility by Delivering Integrin β1 to Repair Environmental Stress-Damaged Testes.
authors: Meng J, Wang J, Li Z, Li F, Yun X, Jin Y, Zhang L.
ai_summary:
Gene: ITGB1
Finding: Macrophage-derived exosomes delivering Integrin β1 repair stress-damaged spermatogenic cytoskeletons, restoring sperm motility and reducing abnormalities in thermal-mechanical stress models.
Disease: Environmental stress-induced male infertility

title: Prevalence of bovine endometritis, virulence mechanisms of Escherichia coli, and current therapeutic strategies: A review.
authors: Wang M, Wen X, Li X, Li H, Cheng J, Liu M.
ai_summary: This review examines the prevalence of bovine endometritis and the role of Escherichia coli as a key pathogen, detailing its virulence factors (adhesins, toxins, lipopolysaccharides, capsule antigens, siderophores, and biofilm formation) that promote colonization, immune activation, and tissue damage. Combining systematic review and meta-analysis, it links epidemiological patterns with pathogenic mechanisms and evaluates current and novel therapeutic strategies, though it notes high heterogeneity and limited clinical validation of treatments. The goal is to inform precise prevention and control of this common postpartum disease in dairy cows.

title: Spatial architecture of autism pathogenesis reveals mosaic structural disarray during early development.
authors: Lin L, Saw TY, Chou N, Goh JLJ, Kwa JE, Chock WK, Singhal V, Li Z, Huang MJ, Ng HH, Khor CC, Kuan HL, Chen KH, Prabhakar S, Liu J.
ai_summary: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics of patient-derived prenatal cortex organoids reveal that autism spectrum disorder pathogenesis involves abnormal partitioning of progenitor and neuron zones, with local patches of disorganized neurons that vary among patients. This mosaic structural disarray persists into neuronal maturation, is linked to impaired progenitor adhesion, and may contribute to the clinical and structural heterogeneity of ASD.

title: Potassium Channels of the Airway Epithelium.
authors: Villanueva S, Vera E, Apablaza T, Catalán MA, Flores CA.
ai_summary: This review discusses the role of potassium (K+) channels in the airway epithelium, focusing on their regulation of transepithelial ion transport, ciliary beating, and mucus secretion—key components of mucociliary clearance (MCC). The authors compile evidence on targeting K+ channels as a therapeutic strategy for muco-obstructive diseases such as cystic fibrosis, COPD, and asthma, noting renewed interest after findings that CFTR-targeting drugs also modulate airway K+ channels. They highlight emerging functions of these channels and outline future research priorities.

title: Correction: A rare missense variant impacting NEK1 kinase function is associated with ALS.
authors: Brenner D, Ponomarenko A, Petrut I, Beyrle S, Contardo M, Loss I, Radke C, Frank J, Zimmer E, Schlesner M, Achenbach P, Scheveneels W, Aly A, Nazlican H, Hesebeck-Brinkmann J, Oeckl P, Müller K, Siebert R, Böckers T, van Eijk K, Veldink J, Kleger A, Mulaw M, Andersen PM, Forsberg K, Weishaupt JH, Loghmani SB, Grehl T, van Damme P, Weis J, Catanese A.

title: Application of autoantibody markers based on phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing technology in the diagnosis of periprosthetic joint infections.
authors: Chang G, Ma Y, Xu J.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
ai_summary:
Gene: IFT80
Finding: Anti-IFT80 autoantibody levels are significantly elevated in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) patients compared to aseptic loosening or post-primary arthroplasty controls, showing diagnostic potential.
Disease: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI)

title: Decoding MAPK cascades in plant immunity: Activation, regulation, integration, and pathogen manipulation.
authors: Zhong G, Wang Z, Tang D, Wang W.
ai_summary: This is a review article summarizing recent advances in understanding MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase) cascades in plant immunity. It covers the composition and activation of these signaling modules, how plants regulate their activation, their crosstalk with other immune signaling events, and how pathogen effectors manipulate MAPK signaling to suppress immunity. The review concludes that MAPK cascades serve as an essential signaling hub in activating plant immunity.

title: A Pentaradial and Bilateral Combined Photoreception System in the Sea Cucumber is Mediated by a Blue Light-Sensitive R-Opsin.
authors: Huang J, Ren C, Qin Z, Cui Y, Zhang B, Luo P, Wang X, Xie Y, Zhang X, Yan A, Zhang Y, Fan D, Liu Y, Pan W, Jiang X, Yuan L, Qin H, Irwin DM, Hu C, Liu Y, Chen T.
ai_summary:
Gene: r-opsin (rhabdomeric opsin)
Finding: A blue light-sensitive r-opsin (peak absorption 459 nm) expressed in oral tentacles, dorsal papillae, and ventral tube feet mediates negative phototaxis and forms an interconnected photoreception system in the sea cucumber.
Disease: Not applicable (wild-type photoreception phenotype in Holothuria leucospilota)

title: Sense, plug, and seal: proteins as both rapid responders and constitutive barriers supporting organelle compartmentalization.
authors: King MC, Lusk CP, Ader NR.
ai_summary: This is a review article discussing the role of proteins as diffusion barriers that support organelle compartmentalization, particularly in contexts of membrane damage. The authors synthesize evidence for a conserved two-step "sense, plug, and seal" paradigm where repair proteins rapidly respond to membranous organelle damage—first sensing and plugging the rupture, then sealing the membrane—as exemplified at the nuclear envelope, lysosomes, and plasma membrane. The review highlights how constitutive and induced proteinaceous barriers complement lipid bilayers in defining organelle boundaries, with future work needed to understand their biophysical nature and sensing mechanisms.

title: Induction of Oxidative Stress on Retinal Pigment Epithelial Cells Triggered a Proangiogenic Environment.
authors: Abdouh M, Goyeneche A, Yurchuk M, Burnier MN.
ai_summary: Oxidative stress induced by hydrogen peroxide in retinal pigment epithelial cells reduces their metabolic activity, increases reactive oxygen species, and upregulates proangiogenic factors such as VEGF and FGF. Conditioned medium from these stressed cells promotes tube formation in endothelial cells, suggesting that oxidative stress may drive the progression of dry age-related macular degeneration toward the exudative (wet) form.

title: Moderately severe osteogenesis imperfecta-like osteochondrodysplasia associated with heterozygous variants in both COL1A2 and TRPV4.
authors: Evans EF, Chung WY, Barnes AM, Makareeva E, Talvacchio S, Abtahi AM, Jenkins LM, Leikin S, Muallem S, Marini JC.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: A heterozygous TRPV4 p.G370S variant reduces mutant protein at the plasma membrane and impairs calcium influx in response to agonist, likely contributing to rhizomelia in a patient who also carries a COL1A2 splice variant causing osteogenesis imperfecta type III.
Disease: Moderately severe osteogenesis imperfecta-like osteochondrodysplasia with rhizomelia

title: A modular chromosomal passenger complex rewires chromosome segregation in Plasmodium berghei.
authors: Roques M, Niu C, Brochet M, Brusini L.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARK1 (Aurora-related kinase 1)
Finding: ARK1 regulates chromosome segregation by forming stage-specific modular chromosomal passenger complexes (with INCENP-A during male gametogenesis and additional components during meiosis), and its depletion causes spindle defects, kinetochore misalignment, and failed chromosome partitioning.
Disease: Plasmodium berghei malaria parasite transmission (sexual development)

title: Single-cell transcriptome defines cell-type repertoire of adult Daphnia magna.
authors: Krishnan I, Yampolsky LY, Petrova K, Peshkin L.
ai_summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of adult Daphnia magna females and males identified over 25 distinct cell types, about half functionally annotated, including ovaries, testes, striated myocytes, enterocytes, cuticular cells, and 9 neuron types (including photoreceptors). Comparisons with Drosophila cell atlases and bulk RNAseq data suggest the existence of noncirculating, fat body-, ovary-, or neuron-associated hemocyte populations, and indicate that circulating hemocytes express cuticular proteins, implying roles in wound repair beyond macrophagy. This provides a baseline single-cell resource for eco-physiology, toxicology, and evolutionary genomics studies in Daphnia.

title: Bi-allelic deleterious variants in SNAPIN, which encodes a retrograde dynein adaptor, cause a prenatal-onset neurodevelopmental disorder.
authors: Yousaf H, de Koning MA, Khan K, Gilmore KL, Hoffer MJV, Kellaris G, Lanone S, Dagouassat M, Ullah F, Adama van Scheltema PN, Heron D, Capri Y, Kuechler A, Schweiger B, Haak MC, Keren B, Tran Mau Them F, Peeters-Scholte CMPCD, Kaiser FJ, Koopmann TT, Mei H, Yalcin B, Depienne C, Vora NL, Santen GWE, Davis EE.
ai_summary:
Gene: SNAPIN
Finding: Bi-allelic deleterious variants in SNAPIN cause a severe prenatal-onset neurodevelopmental disorder, as shown by patient phenotypes and zebrafish models exhibiting reduced head size, altered brain morphology, and autophagy-lysosomal pathway defects with retrograde vesicle transport impairment.
Disease: Prenatal-onset neurodevelopmental disorder with neuroanatomical, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies

title: Low-Coverage Whole-Genome Sequencing Identifies Loci Associated with Birth Weight in East Friesian × Hu Crossbred Sheep.
authors: Bai Y, Jiao S, Yang J, Liu J, Sun B, Cao C, Gao H, Wang R, Wang M, Qin J, Li Y, Wang H, Jiang Y, Li R.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
ai_summary:
Gene: SPATA7
Finding: Variants in a ~6 kb interval within the SPATA7 region on chromosome 7, including the lead SNP Chr7:98,178,889 A > G, are associated with birth weight in East Friesian × Hu crossbred sheep, with AG genotype lambs showing significantly higher birth weight than AA lambs.
Disease: Birth weight variation (quantitative trait in sheep)

title: Telomere dysfunction and mucociliary impairment drive idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis susceptibility: insights from a Sardinian whole-exome study.
authors: Mocci S, Littera R, Deidda S, Cannas F, Cocco C, Lorrai M, Mereu C, Murgia M, Nutile G, Lai F, Sanna C, Serventi L, Tosone G, Zedda E, Giuressi E, Lai S, Perra A, Floris M, Giglio S.
ai_summary:
Gene: MUC5B
Finding: Rare loss-of-function variants in MUC5B, along with other genes related to cilium organization and motility (including dynein-related genes), are significantly enriched in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients, supporting a role for mucociliary impairment in disease susceptibility.
Disease: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)

title: Recurrent Fever and Biliary Ectasia Leading to the Diagnosis of Caroli Syndrome: A Diagnostic Challenge.
authors: Usman M, Basit A, Buttar BA, Ahmad MA, Murtaza L.
ai_summary: Caroli syndrome is a rare congenital liver disorder characterized by non-obstructive dilatation of the intrahepatic bile ducts and congenital hepatic fibrosis. This case report describes a 38-year-old man presenting with recurrent fevers and right upper quadrant pain; despite normal liver enzymes, imaging revealed intrahepatic cystic dilatations with biliary ectasia, and liver biopsy confirmed congenital hepatic fibrosis, leading to the diagnosis. The patient improved with antibiotics, highlighting that Caroli syndrome should be considered in unexplained recurrent fevers with biliary abnormalities even when liver enzymes are normal.

title: Empagliflozin mitigates lipopolysaccharide-induced tracheal injury in rats via downregulation of IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway and stem cell preservation: histological and molecular study.
authors: Sarhan NR, Elekhtiar SA, Elmowafy R, Shrief AI.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: Empagliflozin alleviates lipopolysaccharide-induced tracheal injury in rats by downregulating the IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway, reducing inflammation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and preserving tracheal basal stem cells.
Disease: Lipopolysaccharide-induced tracheal injury

title: New insights into the physiological, pathological and pharmacological roles of voltage‑gated potassium channel Kv10.1 in cancer (Review).
authors: Zhen Y, Hu W, Dong S, Wang B, Shen J, Ding L, Li L, An H, Wang X, Chen Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: KCNH1 (Kv10.1/Eag1)
Finding: Kv10.1 is essential for the occurrence, growth, metastasis, proliferation and death of various malignant tumors, with its regulatory signaling pathways differing across cancer types.
Disease: Cancer (multiple malignant tumors and precancerous lesions)

title: Tubal Patency Decoction and Its Ingredient β-Sitosterol Alleviate Tubal Infertility by Inhibiting Inflammation and Promoting Cilia Formation Through PGR.
authors: Shao L, Wang N, Yan Y, Tan Q, Huang Y, Wu Q, Tan Y, Zhu Y, Xia Y, Liu L.
ai_summary:
Gene: PGR
Finding: β-Sitosterol, an active ingredient of Tubal Patency Decoction, binds to PGR to inhibit inflammation and promote cilia formation, thereby improving tubal infertility.
Disease: Tubal infertility

title: Sexually distinct multi-omic responses to progressive endurance exercise training in the rat lung.
authors: Many GM, Sagendorf TJ, Mitchell H, Sanford JA, Cohen SE, Misra RS, Estevao I, Ludovico ID, Gaul DA, Lindholm ME, Ushakumary MG, Pino JC, Musi N, Nie J, Fernández FM, Ortlund EA, Esser KA, Bodine SC, Schenk S, Clair G, Adkins JN, MoTrPAC Study Group.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
ai_summary: This study used a multi-omics approach in rats to examine how progressive endurance exercise training affects the lung at the molecular level, revealing sex-specific differences. Female rats showed enrichment in immune-related features that were largely maintained with training, while both sexes showed decreased immune pathway activity after 8 weeks, more pronounced in males. Shared training responses included increased cilia-related proteomic pathways and decreased acetylation of mitochondrial pathways, with lung disease-associated features attenuated in both sexes.

title: Methylphenidate exposure alters brain gene expression and induces transgenerational DNA methylation changes in Poecilia reticulata guppies.
authors: Jolicoeur Alfaro RM, De Serrano AR, Sokolowski D, Hughes KA, Rodd FH, Anreiter I.
ai_summary:
Gene: LOC103476631
Finding: Chronic methylphenidate exposure in male guppies alters brain gene expression (including this lncRNA) and induces transgenerational DNA methylation changes in unexposed descendants, associated with a male-lineage-dependent increase in swimming behavior.
Disease: Transgenerational behavioral phenotype (increased swimming) in Poecilia reticulata guppies

title: Deciphering the tubulin code: roles and mechanisms of microtubule post-translational modifications in gastrointestinal tumors: a narrative review.
authors: Zhou C, Li D, Wang Z, Xie M, Ding X, Li D.
ai_summary: Microtubule post-translational modifications (PTMs), including acetylation, detyrosination, methylation, and polyglutamylation, are dysregulated in gastrointestinal tumors and contribute to tumor progression by affecting microtubule stability, mitosis, migration, invasion, and the tumor microenvironment. Key regulatory enzymes such as HDAC6, αTAT1, TTL, TTLLs, and VASH1/2 are highlighted as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets, though clinical translation is limited by insufficient tumor-specific validation and incomplete understanding of PTM crosstalk. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the roles and mechanisms of the "tubulin code" in gastrointestinal malignancies, emphasizing its promise for biomarker development and targeted therapy.

title: Cell-specific MicroRNA networks orchestrate the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Donepudi K, Eadha S, Rodarte D, Sharma B, Kumar S.
ai_summary: This review examines how microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate cell-type-specific pathological processes in Alzheimer's disease (AD), including amyloid and tau biology, synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, myelin maintenance, neurogenesis, and blood-brain barrier integrity across neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, neural stem cells, ependymal cells, and endothelial cells. The authors highlight that dysregulated miRNAs act both within and across cell types via extracellular vesicle transfer, and discuss the potential of circulating and cerebrospinal fluid miRNAs as biomarkers and of miRNA-based therapeutic strategies. The review emphasizes the central role of cell-specific miRNA networks in AD pathogenesis and the promise of targeted miRNA modulation.

title: CLCF1-ZIC5-CNTFR feedback loop drives cisplatin resistance in cervical squamous cell carcinoma.
authors: Jia Q, Li M, Liu J, Xu T, Xu J, Yuan Y, Sui F, Yang X.
ai_summary:
Gene: ZIC5
Finding: ZIC5 promotes cisplatin resistance in cervical squamous cell carcinoma by transcriptionally activating CNTFR and sustaining cancer stem cell properties, forming a CLCF1-ZIC5-CNTFR positive feedback loop via STAT3 signaling.
Disease: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (cisplatin-resistant)

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Opportunities and Obstacles for Therapeutic Advancement.
authors: Hu R, Ataullev Z, Lou L.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
ai_summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells help the tumor microenvironment promote leukemia progression and survival, contributing to treatment failure and relapse. EVs also show therapeutic promise as carriers that can induce apoptosis in cancer cells or suppress oncogene expression via their RNA cargo. This review synthesizes recent findings on the dual roles of EVs in AML—both as drivers of disease and as potential targeted treatment tools.

title: The Respiratory Epithelial Barrier as an Immunopharmacological Rheostat: From Homeostatic Sentinel to Therapeutic Target in Chronic Lung Disease.
authors: Ni FX, Hu J, Chen HH, Huang DH, Jiang ZB.
ai_summary: The respiratory epithelium is presented as a dynamic "immunopharmacological rheostat" that calibrates pulmonary immune activation through four interacting axes (barrier integrity, alarmin/type 2, senescence/repair, and tolerogenic programming). The review examines how dysregulation of these axes drives chronic lung diseases such as asthma, COPD, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and evaluates emerging therapeutic strategies—including alarmin-targeted biologics, barrier-restorative agents, kinase inhibitors, and senotherapeutics—along with the pharmacokinetic and biomarker challenges to their clinical translation.

title: EDNRB-dependent endothelin signaling reduces proliferation and promotes proneural-to-mesenchymal transition in gliomas.
authors: Pineau D, Garcia L, Arnold H, Hanžek A, Arrieta M, Gauthier LR, Granotier-Beckers C, Boussin FD, Herbet A, Hautière M, Asei-Ceschino V, Jacques C, Brard L, Harnois T, Coronas V, Constantin B, Chatelier A, Chemin J, Urbach S, Seveno M, Hideg S, Ripoll C, Aguilar-Cázarez K, Zheng M, Huang GH, Lv SQ, Zhang L, Rondard P, Prezeau L, Pin JP, Duffau H, Bauchet L, Rigau V, Denat F, Truillet C, Boquet D, Hugnot JP.
ai_summary:
Gene: EDNRB
Finding: EDNRB-dependent endothelin signaling reduces glioma proliferation and promotes proneural-to-mesenchymal transition via Ca2+ signaling, ERK/STAT3 activation, and SK2/SK3 potassium channel activity.
Disease: Gliomas (including glioblastomas, astrocytomas, and oligodendrogliomas)

title: Genomic Prediction and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Egg Fertility and Hatchability Traits in Thai Native Grandparent Stock.
authors: Tantiyasawasdikul V, Juiputta J, Lomngam R, Chankitisakul V, Kenchaiwong W, Boonkum W.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
ai_summary: This study evaluated genetic parameters and prediction models for fertility and hatchability traits in Thai native chickens, analyzing 7075 egg records from 1558 animals with pedigree and genomic data. Weighted single-step genomic BLUP (WssGBLUP) achieved the highest prediction accuracy (0.647-0.648), improving accuracy by 30-39% over pedigree-based methods, while genome-wide association analysis identified 65 candidate genes with strong enrichment on the Z chromosome, confirming the polygenic nature of these low-to-moderately heritable traits. The findings support implementing genomic selection to improve reproductive performance in Thai native chickens.

title: Flavonoids in Nasal Therapeutics: Biological Activities, Delivery Challenges, and Formulation Strategies-A Systematic Review.
authors: Hernández JVR, Bianchi SE, Fachel FNS, Braganhol E, de Matos SP, Bassani VL.
ai_summary: Flavonoids are plant-derived compounds with diverse biological activities that can be delivered through the nasal route. This systematic review (covering 1997–2024, 40 included studies) examines three levels of nasal flavonoid administration: topical effects on the nasal mucosal epithelium, treatment of naso-respiratory and other diseases, and nose-to-brain delivery to prevent or treat central nervous system diseases. The review highlights the therapeutic potential of nasal flavonoid delivery, particularly in the free (aglycone) form, while noting formulation challenges for this route.

title: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition in atherosclerosis: mechanisms, therapeutic targets, and future perspectives.
authors: Cui X, Chen Y, Luo H, Li H, Yu Z, Guo H.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a heterogeneous, partially reversible endothelial plasticity program that contributes to atherosclerosis progression and plaque instability through vascular remodeling, inflammation, and matrix degradation. Recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies reveal a spectrum of EndMT states with stage- and region-specific effects, regulated by interconnected signaling, metabolic, and epigenetic pathways. Therapeutic strategies aim to prevent early maladaptive EndMT while selectively restraining pathogenic states, though clinical translation is limited by marker nonspecificity and lack of validated biomarkers.

title: The gut microbiota in colorectal cancer: role in cytokine regulation, intestinal immune barrier dysfunction.
authors: Zhou P, He Y, Qu H, Zhou Y, Pan H.
ai_summary: The gut microbiota plays a critical role in colorectal cancer (CRC) by promoting dysbiosis that disrupts the intestinal immune barrier and drives aberrant cytokine production and chronic inflammation. These microbiota-driven changes contribute to tumor initiation and progression through pathways such as NF-κB and STAT3, though causal links between specific microbial signatures and CRC remain unproven. This review highlights emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the microbiota-immune axis for CRC diagnosis and treatment.

title: The oral microbiota in oral squamous cell carcinoma: unravelling mechanisms and clinical potential.
authors: Kamel AHM, El-Tantawy N, Ahmed S, Wadan AS, AbuBakr N.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: Oral microbial dysbiosis, particularly involving periodontal bacteria such as Porphyromonas gingivalis, Treponema denticola, and Fusobacterium nucleatum, promotes oral squamous cell carcinoma progression by activating oncogenic signaling pathways including STAT3.
Disease: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)

title: Network Biology of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Neurodegenerative Disorders: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Strategies.
authors: Wali Z, Neha, Shahwan M, Dinislam K, Shamsi A, Anwar S.
ai_summary: Neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, are redefined as system-level failures driven by a self-reinforcing network of pathogenic processes such as oxidative stress, protein misfolding, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. The review highlights the convergence of JAK/STAT, HIF-1α, and Notch signaling pathways under metabolic stress as a key mechanism, and discusses advances in biomarkers and therapeutic strategies including antisense oligonucleotides, gene therapies, and AI-driven drug discovery.

title: LAG3 Gene Therapy Attenuates Autoimmune Uveitis by Regulating the PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway.
authors: Zheng L, Jiang J, Zhang Q, Su X, Yang B, Li J, Huang J, Du J, Ding Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: LAG3
Finding: AAV2-mediated LAG3 gene therapy attenuates experimental autoimmune uveitis by modulating the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, restoring Th17/Treg balance, and preserving blood-retinal barrier integrity.
Disease: Autoimmune uveitis

title: Advances in Helicobacter pylori-mediated oncogenic signaling pathways in gastric cancer: From pathological evolution to clinical application prospects (Review).
authors: Ding T, Hu W, Qi X, Zhang Y, Wang H.
ai_summary: Helicobacter pylori infection is a major risk factor for gastric cancer, but the molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This review synthesizes the oncogenic signaling pathways involved (NF-κB, MAPK, JAK/STAT, PI3K/AKT), epigenetic changes, virulence factors (CagA and VacA), and interactions with the gut microbiota and gastric stem cells. It highlights how these mechanistic insights are informing the development of molecular diagnostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and immunotherapies for early diagnosis and precision treatment of gastric cancer.

title: Role of gut microbiota in cancer modulation: molecular mechanisms and emerging therapeutic strategies.
authors: Preetam S, Bora J, Porna Dutta S, Talukdar N, Rustagi S, Thapliyal S, Malik S, Choudhary N, Kumar D, Kondaveeti SB.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: Gut microbiota dysbiosis and microbial-derived metabolites modulate oncogenesis and tumour biology through pathways including NF-κB, STAT3, Wnt/β-catenin, and inflammasome activation, affecting cancer initiation, progression, and therapy response.
Disease: Cancer (colorectal, gastric, liver, breast, gynaecological, and pulmonary cancers)

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Therapy.
authors: Zhang X, Zhang Z, Jin L, Huang Y.
ai_summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale messengers implicated in the pathogenesis of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), the most common metabolic complication of pregnancy. This review synthesizes findings on EVs from various sources—placenta, adipose tissue, blood, breast milk, and urine—to construct an EV-mediated multi-organ crosstalk network and evaluates their dual potential as liquid biopsy biomarkers for diagnosis and as drug delivery vehicles for therapy. The authors discuss current challenges and future directions for translating EV-based strategies into clinical practice for GDM.

title: Gut Microbiota in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis, Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
authors: Cristinescu BA, Dura H, Fleaca SR, Onisor DM, Brusnic O, Porr C, Birsan S, Boicean A.
ai_summary: Gut microbiota plays a key role in colorectal cancer (CRC) development, with specific bacterial species and metabolites under investigation as non-invasive biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Fusobacterium nucleatum is the most promising candidate for stool-based CRC detection, while Streptococcus gallolyticus subsp. gallolyticus and Clostridium septicum serve as clinical warning markers for occult malignancy; other species like pks+Escherichia coli, enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis, Enterococcus faecalis, and Peptostreptococcus anaerobius remain investigational, and Helicobacter pylori has limited diagnostic value. The review emphasizes underlying pathogenic mechanisms and highlights emerging bacterial taxa linked to early tumorigenesis, though most biomarkers require further clinical validation.

title: The sensory gene repertoire of deep-sea hydrothermal shrimp.
authors: Chertemps T, Montagné N, Mathou A, Léger N, Zbinden M, Ravaux J.
ai_summary:
Gene: IR40a (variant Ionotropic Receptor family)
Finding: Deep-sea hydrothermal vent shrimp show a massive expansion of variant Ionotropic Receptors, particularly the IR40a clade, alongside diverse TRP channels, enabling chemical and thermal detection in extreme vent environments.
Disease: Not applicable (ecological adaptation in deep-sea shrimp, no human disease link)

title: Nasal immunity in respiratory viral infection, transmission, and protection.
authors: Kazer SW, Walsh JML, Juttukonda LJ, Ordovas-Montanes J.
ai_summary: The nasal mucosa is the primary barrier against airborne respiratory viruses, and recent work—accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic—has clarified how epithelial and immune cells cooperate to fight infection, limit spread to the lower airways, and reduce onward transmission. Using technologies like single-cell RNA sequencing and air-liquid interface models, researchers have mapped cell states and responses during and after viral infection in mice and humans, identifying correlates of protection that differ between natural infection and intramuscular vaccination. The review highlights emerging intranasal vaccination strategies aimed at programming tissue-scale immune memory in the nose to prevent both disease and viral transmission.

title: Research progress on the chemical and pharmacological effects of Semen Strychni (Review).
authors: Mao J, Du X, Zeng D, Luo X, Li Y.
ai_summary: Semen Strychni, a traditional South Asian medicinal plant, shows potential efficacy in treating nervous system diseases, arrhythmia, pain, inflammation, and tumors, but its pharmacological research is mostly limited to in vitro studies. The review highlights gaps in systematic exploration of its extracts and compounds, as well as significant safety risks before and after processing that require further investigation into its toxicity mechanisms. It provides a comprehensive overview of the plant's medicinal history, chemical composition, and pharmacological activity to support future basic research and pharmaceutical applications.

title: A Plant Photoregulator-Inspired S-Type Heterojunction System for Diabetic Keratopathy via Tri-Modal Light-Driven Immunometabolic Reprogramming, Tissue Repair, and Antibacterial Activity.
authors: Zhao M, Zhou Z, Wei Y, Huang X, Zhou Z, Chen J, Cheng H, Hu X, Wang X.
ai_summary: This study describes a light-activated biomimetic platform (WCNx-Rh2) designed to treat diabetic keratopathy (DK), a corneal complication of diabetes. The platform combines an S-scheme heterojunction (WCNx) for visible-light-driven glucose degradation, dark-state glucose monitoring, and near-infrared photothermal antibacterial activity, with ginsenoside Rh2, which inhibits NOD-like receptor signaling. In diabetic mouse models, the system reduced advanced glycation end products, reactive oxygen species, and inflammation, reprogrammed dendritic cells to restore corneal epithelial-neural-immune homeostasis, and accelerated epithelial and nerve repair; in a diabetic keratitis model, it achieved effective bacterial eradication and tissue repair. The findings propose an integrated light-driven strategy for managing the metabolic-immune-infection imbalance in DK.

title: Context-dependent regulation of IL-6 in exercise and colorectal cancer cachexia.
authors: Xiong J, Liu S, Xu J, Zhang J, Peng Y, Xia Y, Qian J.
ai_summary: This is a review article, not a study establishing a gene-disease link. It discusses the context-dependent role of IL-6 in colorectal cancer and cancer cachexia, particularly in relation to exercise. The authors conclude that while IL-6 dynamics offer a framework for understanding exercise responses in CRC-related cachexia, current evidence is insufficient to guide clinical exercise prescription or therapy based on IL-6 levels.

title: Beta-caryophyllene mitigates high fat diet-induced testicular dysfunctions by targeting JNK/ERK-1 and JAK-1/STAT-3 pathways in rats.
authors: Muqbil Alsirhani A, Alzahrani OR, Abu-Almakarem AS, Al-Sowayan NS, Shakoori AM, AlRashidi AA, Aljohani S, Aljarari RM, Alowaidi SA, Mobasher MA, El-Said KS.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: Beta-caryophyllene treatment dose-dependently mitigates high-fat diet-induced testicular dysfunction in rats by downregulating the overexpression of JNK/ERK-1 and JAK-1/STAT-3 signaling pathways, reducing oxidative stress and inflammation, and restoring sperm parameters and testosterone levels.
Disease: Obesity-associated male reproductive dysfunction

title: Major bioactive metabolites derived from Tripterygium wilfordii: structures, mechanisms, and therapeutic potentials.
authors: Jin Y, Xu J, Yan X, Tong R, Zhang Z, Ling Y, Ma Y, Huang C, Zhan Q, Leng X, He J, Wang L, Gao J.
ai_summary: Tripterygium wilfordii produces bioactive diterpenoids and triterpenoids (triptolide, triptonide, celastrol) with immunosuppressive, anti-inflammatory, and anti-tumor effects via pathways such as NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and TGF-β/Smad. This review covers their chemical classification, mechanisms, and clinical potential in autoimmune diseases, cancer, fibrosis, and metabolic disorders, while noting challenges in safety, solubility, and bioavailability and discussing drug delivery and structural modification advances.

title: Mechanopriming by vascular stiffness and phenotypic reprogramming by disturbed flow: mechanobiology and clinical translation in atherosclerosis.
authors: He J, Meng J.
ai_summary:
Gene: PIEZO1
Finding: Piezo1 and the 5-HT1B receptor act as "coincidence detectors" that integrate fluid shear stress and matrix stiffness signals to activate YAP and c-REL, driving pathological endothelial reprogramming in atherosclerosis.
Disease: Atherosclerosis

title: A Multimodal Biomedical Transformer Fusion Network for Disease-Level Rare-Disease-Inheritance Classification Using Ontology-Enriched Text, Metadata, and Gene Associations.
authors: Mahmood MA, Alsalem K.
ai_summary: RareFusion-Net is a multimodal benchmark framework that classifies inheritance patterns in rare diseases at the disease level, combining ontology-enriched disease text, structured epidemiological metadata, and gene-association information. The gated fusion model (RareFusionBalanced) achieved 0.7382 test accuracy and 0.9183 macro-AUC, with ontology-enriched text as the strongest predictive modality and gene associations providing complementary value. However, the multimodal approach only slightly outperformed text-only models, with no statistically significant improvement over the best TF-IDF baseline, highlighting challenges with minority classes and the need for external validation. The framework is intended for knowledge organization and hypothesis generation in curated rare-disease resources, not for individual patient diagnosis.

title: Colorectal cancer landscape from gut microbiota: Insights into mutations, epigenetic dysregulation, and immune microenvironment alterations.
authors: Li Y, Yang Y, Zhang X, Huang Z, Zhang X, Wen J.
ai_summary: Gut microbiota and their metabolites drive colorectal cancer (CRC) initiation and progression by inducing driver mutations (via DNA damage and signaling interference), altering epigenetic regulation (DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs), and reshaping the tumor immune microenvironment to promote immune evasion. Distinct microbial species act at different tumor stages, and these causal changes support microbiota-based strategies for CRC prevention, early diagnosis, and treatment, including targeting microbes, metabolites, or signaling pathways.

title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for dry eye disease: principles, progress, and challenges.
authors: Feng Y, Zhang M.
journal: Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids
ai_summary: This review discusses the use of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) as a potential therapy for dry eye disease (DED), a multifactorial ocular surface disorder driven largely by inflammation. The authors summarize the anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and regenerative properties of MSC-EVs, along with strategies to enhance their delivery and efficacy, such as cargo engineering and biomaterial-assisted approaches. While MSC-EVs, particularly from umbilical cord sources, show promise for treating refractory DED, most evidence is preclinical, and challenges remain in standardization, safety evaluation, and regulatory approval before clinical translation.

title: Neonatal genetic sequencing as a first-tier option: a real-world clinical implementation study in Northern China.
authors: Mu J, Sun M, Li Y, Li P, Zou H.
ai_summary: Newborn genetic screening using a targeted 465-gene panel in 1,590 newborns in Northern China showed a high positive predictive value (80%) for inherited metabolic disorders compared to biochemical screening (5.71%), with a carrier frequency of 70.94%. Regional hotspot variants (e.g., MMACHC c.609G>A, MUT c.1286A>G) and allele frequency differences from gnomAD_EAS highlight the need for a local genetic database. Despite high diagnostic accuracy, low uptake (10.41%) and barriers like cost and provider awareness limit broader implementation.

title: Immune-inflammatory endotypes of chronic rhinosinusitis: from epithelial alarmins to personalized therapy.
authors: Li H, Wang L, Li D.
ai_summary: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease traditionally classified by the presence or absence of nasal polyps, but this phenotypic classification fails to capture its underlying pathophysiology. This review highlights immune-inflammatory endotyping as a more precise approach, categorizing CRS into type 1, type 2, and type 3 immune responses driven by distinct cytokines and immune cells, including epithelial alarmins (TSLP, IL-33, IL-25), ILC2s, Th2, and Th17 cells. The authors emphasize that variations in immune responses across populations underscore disease heterogeneity and argue that integrating these endotypes provides a theoretical foundation for developing personalized therapeutic strategies tailored to individual immune-inflammatory profiles.

title: Beyond mass effect: An age-stratified analysis of CSF circulation disturbance in symptomatic intracranial arachnoid cysts.
authors: Middelkamp M, Asey B, Sauvigny T, Dührsen L, Duda S.
ai_summary: Pediatric intracranial arachnoid cysts are associated with disturbed cerebrospinal fluid circulation, including hydrocephalus and aqueductal stenosis, rather than purely mass effect. In a retrospective cohort of 30 symptomatic patients, postoperative hydrocephalus strongly predicted reoperation and worse functional outcomes, while cyst volume reduction did not consistently correlate with clinical improvement. Younger age, increased head circumference, and neurenteric histology predicted the need for salvage CSF diversion, supporting an age-dependent view of pediatric AC as CSF circulation disorders.

title: Molecular insights and therapeutic implications for the tumor suppressor role of LKB1 in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Yan P, Jiang W, Xue X, Hou T, Wang J, Huang D, Chen L, Inuzuka H, Dai X, Wei W.
ai_summary:
Gene: LKB1
Finding: Loss of LKB1 kinase activity in NSCLC impairs energy/metabolic stress sensing via AMPK and related networks, deregulates mTOR signaling, promotes metabolic reprogramming, oxidative stress, disrupted polarity, invasion/metastasis, altered tumor microenvironment, and resistance to radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Disease: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

title: Current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting adherent-invasive Escherichia coli in Crohn's disease: a review.
authors: Mohammed Abdelhadi LA, Liang Y, Liao Y, Zhu G.
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (AIEC is a bacterial pathotype, not a human gene)
Finding: This review categorizes emerging therapies against adherent-invasive E. coli in Crohn's disease into four pillars—direct pathogen targeting, blockade of virulence factors, host-mediated clearance, and ecological restoration—and highlights novel modalities like predatory bacteria and siderophore immunization.
Disease: Crohn's disease

title: Upper and Lower Respiratory Tract Compartmentalization in Pediatric Stem Cell Transplantation.
authors: Evans EM, Mayday MY, Pearce EM, Iwanaga K, Ly NP, Church GD, Reyes G, Simon MR, Blum J, Kim H, Mu J, Baez-Maidana J, Auletta JJ, Shaw PJ, Kreml EM, Martin PL, Duncan CN, Rowan CM, Godder K, Hurley C, Cuvelier GDE, Qayed M, Abdel-Azim H, Keating AK, Fitzgerald JC, Hanna R, Killinger JS, Hume JR, Quigg TC, Castillo P, Satwani P, Moore TB, Dvorak CC, Zinter MS, Pediatric Transplantation And Cell Therapy Consortium.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
ai_summary:
Gene: Not applicable (no single gene link established)
Finding: Not applicable
Disease: Not applicable
Plain-language summary: This study compared nasal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples from pediatric stem cell transplant patients with lung injury, finding that gene expression, immune cell composition, and microbiomes are largely compartmentalized—alveolar (BAL) signatures reflect injury and predict poor outcomes, while nasal samples provide minimal prognostic information. The results highlight the need for minimally invasive diagnostics that can capture alveolar-specific changes.

title: KIF15 (Kinesin-12): molecular biology, physiological functions, and roles in disease.
authors: Xiang S, Li Y, Zhuang H, Lu Y.
journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF15
Finding: KIF15 is recurrently upregulated across multiple solid tumors, where it drives oncogenic signaling (MEK-ERK, PI3K-AKT, EGFR), metabolic reprogramming, cancer stem cell maintenance, and resistance to Eg5 inhibitors and enzalutamide, with germline variants also linked to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis susceptibility.
Disease: Multiple cancers (lung, breast, prostate, pancreatic, gastric, colorectal, hepatocellular) and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

title: Branched-chain amino acids and gut microbiota: coregulation and impact on neurological function via the gut-brain axis.
authors: Li Q, Fan B, Xiao Y, Zhang Z, Zhao S, Liao B, Zeng J, Shan X, Ye H, Wen Y, Zhang L, Guo H, Xiao F, Zhu H.
ai_summary: This review examines the role of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), which are regulated by the gut microbiota, in neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and maple syrup urine disease. The authors summarize BCAA biochemistry and metabolism, discuss how gut microbiota regulate BCAA metabolism, and present evidence linking this pathway to brain function via the gut-brain axis. They conclude by highlighting future research directions for targeting gut BCAA metabolism as a potential treatment for brain and gastrointestinal dysfunction.

title: Host-Pathogen Interaction as a Driver of Cellular Senescence: Microbial Triggers and Host Response.
authors: Iordache F, Zaharie AA, Rosu PM, Holban AM, Curutiu C.
ai_summary: Cellular senescence, aging, and host-pathogen interactions are interconnected, and this review examines how bacterial infections drive immunosenescence. Bacterial pathogens induce senescence through genotoxic effects, oxidative stress, and disruption of host signaling pathways, with virulence factors modulating key pathways such as p53-p21, p16INK4a-Rb, NF-κB, mTOR, and cGAS-STING. This promotes a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), facilitating chronic infection and tissue damage, and offering a perspective on infections contributing to premature aging and age-related diseases, with potential therapeutic targets for modulating senescence.

title: Neutrophilic asthma: advances in experimental models from pathogenesis to therapeutic translation.
authors: Yao J, Lu J, Gao J, Liao X, Wu D, Wang M, Li Q, Gao W.
ai_summary: Neutrophilic asthma is a severe, steroid-resistant asthma endotype characterized by persistent airway inflammation and neutrophil infiltration. This review synthesizes current in vivo models (murine, rat, equine) and in vitro approaches (air-liquid interface cultures, organoids, lung-on-a-chip) for studying its pathogenesis, highlighting their strengths and limitations in modeling steroid resistance and epithelial dysfunction. The authors conclude that standardizing these experimental tools is essential for advancing mechanistic understanding and developing targeted therapies for precision medicine.

title: Beyond receptor activation: biased toll-like receptor signaling in periodontal inflammation and regeneration.
authors: Mekhemar M, Hassanein FEA, Abou-Bakr A.
ai_summary: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of tooth-supporting tissues, and this review argues that its persistence and variable outcomes stem not from uniform Toll-like receptor (TLR) overactivation but from biased downstream signaling—specifically, dominance of pro-inflammatory MyD88-dependent pathways over regulatory and resolution programs. This imbalance promotes inflammation, osteoimmune disruption, and dysfunction of periodontal stromal and stem cells, contributing to disease heterogeneity and poor regenerative outcomes. The authors propose that regenerative failure reflects an unfavorable inflammatory signaling milieu rather than loss of regenerative cells, and they discuss emerging experimental tools for modulating TLR networks as research strategies rather than immediate therapies.

title: The long reach of influenza and other respiratory viruses: from acute epithelial injury to post-viral lung disease.
authors: Janas PP, Rozario C, Lucas CD, Hiemstra PS, Schwarze J, Chauché C.
ai_summary: Respiratory viral infections, including influenza, RSV, rhinovirus, and SARS-CoV-2, cause extensive lung epithelial cell death and trigger repair programs involving progenitor cells. These infections and the associated inflammation can induce long-term changes in epithelial progenitor cells that persist after recovery, potentially driving post-viral lung disease (PVLD). This review examines how such infections alter gene expression and function of epithelial progeny, highlighting lung epithelial memory and discussing therapeutic strategies to preserve long-term lung health.

title: Gut microbiota-immune crosstalk in osteoarthritis: pathogenic mechanisms and emerging therapeutic opportunities.
authors: Zhang T, Tang B, Yu Z, Zhang C, Pan Z, Liang C, Zheng H, Wang Q.
ai_summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as involving immune imbalance and low-grade inflammation, not just mechanical joint damage. This review describes a "gut microbiota-immune-joint axis" in which gut microbial disruption impairs intestinal barrier function, allowing microbial signals to enter circulation and activate inflammatory pathways (e.g., TLR4/NF-κB, JAK/STAT), leading to immune cell reprogramming and altered macrophage/T-cell responses that drive pathological changes in synovium, cartilage, and bone. The authors summarize microbiota-targeted therapies (probiotics, prebiotics) and call for multi-omics and longitudinal studies to advance targeted OA interventions.

title: TRPM2 Deficiency Attenuates Allergic Rhinitis-Like Inflammation With Altered Ca<sup>2+</sup>-NFAT Signaling, Treg Responses, and sIgE Production.
authors: Huang Z, Fan J, Shan X, Su J, Zhu L, Peng L.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPM2
Finding: TRPM2 deficiency attenuates ovalbumin-induced allergic rhinitis-like inflammation by reducing clinical symptoms, nasal inflammation, serum OVA-specific IgE, and Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-33), while expanding Treg cells and suppressing Ca2+ influx, NFATc1 nuclear translocation, and IL-2 production.
Disease: Allergic rhinitis

title: Interleukin-8 in health and disease.
authors: Bazzichetto C, Dell'Aquila E, Veroli M, Belluomini L, Bonato A, Bernardini G, Bevilacqua M, Cattazzo F, Dalbeni A, Tampu TM, Salari V, Fabene PF, Luchini C, Milella M, Conciatori F.
ai_summary: Interleukin-8 (IL-8) is a pleiotropic cytokine involved in cell-to-cell communication, serving as a detectable biomarker and drug target across various diseases. It plays a central role in the pathogenesis of autoimmune disorders, sepsis, neurological, liver, and cardiovascular diseases, and acts as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in solid cancers, including for immunotherapy patient stratification. The review highlights IL-8's pro-tumorigenic roles and immunosuppressive microenvironment effects, but notes that lack of standardization in detection methods and unclear sources of IL-8 production hinder its clinical utility.

title: From Modic changes to the disc-endplate-bone marrow complex: imaging stratification, immune remodeling, and translational implications in intervertebral disc degeneration.
authors: Liu Y, Huang H, Lin M, Yang C, Shen T, Zhou H.
ai_summary: This is a review article, not a study linking a specific gene to a disease. It discusses imaging classification frameworks for intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) and low back pain, focusing on the disc-endplate-bone marrow complex (DEBC) as a complement to Modic changes. The authors argue that DEBC is a hypothesis-generating tool for lesion-level stratification, not a standalone diagnostic or treatment guide, and call for longitudinal and molecular studies to validate its clinical relevance.

title: Exploring macrophage polarization: biological insights, key laboratory techniques and research perspectives.
authors: Battumur E, Clegg JR, Acar H.
ai_summary: Macrophages are innate immune cells that maintain tissue homeostasis and coordinate immune responses, exhibiting remarkable phenotypic plasticity in response to microenvironmental signals. This review discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization into pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory states, while highlighting persistent experimental challenges such as variability in isolation procedures, overlapping activation states, and lack of reliable phenotypic markers. The authors emphasize that standardized protocols for cell isolation, culture, stimulation, and multiparametric phenotyping are essential for improving reproducibility and translational relevance in studying macrophage biology for therapeutic applications in autoimmune diseases, infections, cancer, and chronic inflammation.

title: Gut microbiota in health and disease.
authors: Li Y, Xiao X, Jiang X, Li X, Wang W, Lin R.
ai_summary: The gut microbiota supports host physiology through metabolic, barrier, immune, and gut-organ axis functions; its disruption (dysbiosis) contributes to gastrointestinal and extra-intestinal diseases via interconnected mechanisms such as barrier failure, altered microbial metabolism, and inflammatory signaling. The review highlights challenges in establishing causality and translating microbiome data clinically, and discusses therapeutic strategies including dietary modulation, biotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and precision therapies.

title: Precision identification and targeted therapy for neutrophilic asthma: from molecular mechanisms to clinical translation.
authors: Sun M, Xu Y, Song G, Zhang B, Peng M, Yu S, Zhang G.
ai_summary: Neutrophilic asthma is a distinct asthma phenotype marked by high sputum neutrophils (≥61%), glucocorticoid resistance, and more severe disease than eosinophilic asthma. This review details its molecular drivers—the Th17/IL-17 axis, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), and NLRP3 inflammasome activation—and proposes a precision framework linking molecular endotypes, clinical phenotypes, and biomarkers to guide therapy. Emerging treatments targeting IL-17, NETs, and inflammasome components, along with the microbiome-neutrophil axis, are highlighted as promising avenues for this difficult-to-treat phenotype.

title: Decoding the microbiome-immune crosstalk in cancer: from mechanisms to therapeutic translation.
authors: Zhao N, Wu L, Peng S, Yang H, Song Y, Zhang Y, Ding L.
ai_summary: The gut microbiome shapes host immunity and influences the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. This review summarizes mechanisms by which gut microbiota affect antitumor immunity and highlights clinical studies of interventions like fecal microbiota transplantation, probiotics, and engineered bacteria. It also discusses challenges such as inter-individual variability, colonization stability, delivery barriers, and safety concerns, and outlines future directions for translating microbiome-targeted therapies into oncology.

title: Eosinophil IL-5Rα/JAK2/STAT5 Signaling Contributes to Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition in Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps.
authors: Choi H, Choi H, Oh JM, Lee HS, Kim SW, Kim BG, Lee DC.
ai_summary:
Gene: IL5RA (IL-5Rα), JAK2, STAT5
Finding: IL-5-activated IL-5Rα/JAK2/STAT5 signaling in eosinophils induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition in human nasal epithelial cells, and silencing IL5RA, JAK2, or STAT5 attenuates this effect.
Disease: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (ECRSwNP)

title: Decoding Cardiac Development and Maturation at Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Resolution.
authors: Li B, Liu X, Murphy S, Tampakakis E, Kwon C.
ai_summary: Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have transformed our understanding of cardiac development and maturation by resolving cellular heterogeneity, lineage trajectories, and gene regulatory networks. Spatial transcriptomics complements single-cell profiling by preserving tissue architecture, revealing how gene expression is organized in anatomic context. Emerging developmental datasets now enable reconstruction of spatially resolved trajectories of heart formation, and integrative approaches are redefining the molecular and spatial logic of cardiogenesis, with implications for regenerative and translational research.

title: IL-5Rα-Mediated Signaling in Eosinophils May Contribute to the Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition in Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps.
authors: Choi H, Choi H, Oh JM, Kim SW, Kim SW, Kim BG, Cho JH, Lee DC.
journal: Journal of rhinology : official journal of the Korean Rhinologic Society
ai_summary:
Gene: IL5RA (IL-5Rα)
Finding: IL-5Rα-mediated JAK2/STAT5 signaling is upregulated in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and IL-5-activated eosinophils promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition in human nasal epithelial cells.
Disease: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (ECRSwNP)

title: Polymorphism in Ontogenetic Duration in Dendrolimus (Lepidoptera: Lasiocampidae): Diapause, Developmental Variability, and the Role of Facultative Summer Diapause in the Siberian Moth.
authors: Zhevnova NA, Dubatolov VV.
ai_summary: This review examines developmental duration polymorphism in Dendrolimus moths, a major conifer pest group. The authors distinguish biological generation time from calendar span and identify diapause as the main mechanism generating alternative developmental trajectories. Evidence for natural intrapopulation splitting is strongest in the Siberian moth, where fast and delayed trajectories appear linked to facultative summer diapause. The authors recommend incorporating delayed fractions and cohort ratios into models to improve pest forecasting and control.

title: Decoding the CSF Proteomic Signature of Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus: A Systematic Review.
authors: Kwiecień A, Dudzic M, Lemański A, Kalka JM, Drużdż A, Hojan K, Palandri G, Sokół B.
ai_summary: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a potentially reversible neurological disorder, but diagnosis and prediction of shunt responsiveness remain difficult. This systematic review of 14 studies (1171 patients) found that CSF proteomic analyses consistently show upregulation of inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related proteins and downregulation of synaptic and neuronal markers in iNPH. Neurodegenerative proteins (amyloid-β, tau, neurofilament light chain) help differentiate iNPH from comorbid neurodegenerative diseases and predict response to ventriculoperitoneal shunting, but the authors emphasize that multidimensional biomarker profiles, rather than single proteins, offer the greatest clinical utility. They propose a hypothetical conceptual "Vulnerability Model" integrating CSF biomarkers to reflect reversible versus irreversible pathology, but stress that current proteins are only candidate biomarkers requiring validation in standardized prospective cohorts.

title: Integrated post-GWAS, single-cell, and functional analyses prioritize TCTN2 at an osteoarthritis locus associated with innate immunity-related cartilage remodeling.
