authors: Lu C, Wang L, Cao X, Zhao K, Yin N, Zhang D.
ai_summary:
Gene: TCTN2
Finding: Integrated post-GWAS, single-cell, and functional analyses prioritize TCTN2 at an osteoarthritis locus, where TCTN2 knockdown in ATDC5 cells increases hypertrophic markers (Col10a1, Mmp13, Runx2) and overexpression reverses them.
Disease: Osteoarthritis

title: Cerebrospinal fluid mechanics across CNS barriers: from production, circulation, and clearance to mechanomedicine.
authors: Cheng X, Deng B, Zhao Y, Li H, Zhan T, Peng D.
ai_summary: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) motion and pressure exert mechanical forces on CNS barriers, and abnormal CSF mechanics can drive barrier dysfunction and disease. This review synthesizes evidence that specialized mechanotransduction modules in the choroid plexus, ependyma, neurovascular unit, and meningeal outflow pathways sense shear, pulsatility, and pressure changes, regulating permeability and immune states. The authors propose a "mechanomedicine" framework linking measurable mechanical exposures to barrier-specific mechanosensors and clinical endpoints, potentially guiding therapies that modulate CSF dynamics or target mechanotransduction in conditions like hydrocephalus, neurodegeneration, and trauma.

title: Brainstem Disconnection Syndrome in a Patient With Respiratory Failure and Failed Weaning From Oxygen: A Case Report.
authors: Alshehri A, Ashi M, Sulaiman S, Alzahrani A.
ai_summary:
Gene: TMEM67
Finding: A carrier-status frameshift variant in TMEM67, a gene implicated in ciliary hindbrain morphogenesis, was identified in a patient with brainstem disconnection syndrome, suggesting ciliary gene mutations may be genetic factors or modifiers in this condition.
Disease: Brainstem disconnection syndrome with respiratory failure, seizures, hypotonia, and multisystem vascular and skeletal malformations

title: Compressive stress-driven mechanosignaling in chondrocytes: From molecular mechanism to scaffold engineering and translational opportunities.
authors: Mou Y, Tian T, Wang P, Wang X, Li W, Tang W, Wang Y, Zhu D, Huang Y, Huang X.
ai_summary: Compressive stress is the most prominent mechanical signal regulating chondrocyte behavior in articular cartilage. This review dissects the multi-layered mechanisms of compressive stress-mediated chondrocyte regulation—from integrin-mediated mechanosensing and downstream signaling (calcium, MAPK, SOX9, Runx2, Sp1) to cellular responses and translational applications—highlighting that moderate dynamic compression promotes cartilage repair while aberrant loading exacerbates osteoarthritis. It emphasizes the need for cell-type-specific mechanical intervention strategies and optimization of scaffold materials and culture systems, while noting current limitations in physiological models, standardized loading parameters, and clinical translation.

title: Exploring and translating novel approaches targeting the choroid plexus for the treatment of hydrocephalus: a literature review.
authors: Sluijters OJJ, Pooley JR, Singleton WGB.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
ai_summary: Hydrocephalus is primarily treated by surgical CSF diversion, which does not address the underlying disease mechanism. Recent rodent models of post-haemorrhagic hydrocephalus show that the choroid plexus exhibits a hypersecretory response that may contribute to the condition, making the choroid plexus a promising novel therapeutic target. However, translating these pre-clinical findings into clinical practice is limited by the lack of large animal hydrocephalus models.

title: Exercise-primed Trpv4+ progenitors sense mechanical to regulate graded transition in enthesis regeneration.
authors: Xu S, Lin Y, Yu Y, Zhu Z, Huang P, Xie Q, Chen Y, Tao X, Zhou M, Liu Z, Bian X, Guo L.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: Exercise-induced mechanical stimulation activates Trpv4+ progenitors via calcium-calcineurin-NFATc1 signaling to enhance chondrogenic differentiation and improve enthesis regeneration.
Disease: Tendon-bone interface (enthesis) injury

title: Unravelling the Impact of Microgravity on Calcium Ion Signaling and Sensorium in Spaceflight.
authors: Marza L, Mohammed R, Abdelrahman Y, Hajjiri A, Abuhjar M, Deen GR.
ai_summary: Microgravity may alter calcium ion (Ca2+) signaling and Ca2+-dependent processes across the five senses, potentially contributing to sensory disturbances such as altered taste and smell, visual issues, reduced touch sensitivity, and vestibular imbalance in astronauts. The review synthesizes evidence from spaceflight and ground-based analogs, but notes that direct proof of microgravity-induced Ca2+ signaling disruption is limited for several sensory modalities. It proposes Ca2+ signaling as a unifying mechanism for sensory adaptation to microgravity and identifies knowledge gaps for developing countermeasures.

title: Recent Advances in Mechanobiology-Mediated In Situ Tissue Engineering.
authors: Agbe H, Jaato BN, Dadzie DA, Frimpong BM, Mensah PM, Appiah MK, Dodoo-Arhin D, Kabla A.
ai_summary: This review discusses the shift from traditional ex vivo tissue engineering to in situ approaches that recruit the body's own stem cells for repair. It emphasizes the importance of biomimetic scaffolds that deliver biochemical cues and highlights the central role of mechanobiology—how physical forces regulate cell behavior through mechanotransduction—in guiding successful tissue regeneration. The article covers scaffold designs, applications for hard and soft tissue repair, and future challenges in the field.

title: Single-cell analysis of the epigenome and 3D chromatin architecture in the human retina.
authors: Yuan Y, Biswas P, Zemke NR, Dang K, Wu Y, D'Antonio M, Xie Y, Yang Q, Dong K, Lau PK, Li D, Seng C, Bartosik W, Buchanan J, Lin L, Lancione R, Wang K, Lee S, Gibbs Z, Yang B, Ecker JR, Frazer K, Wang T, Preissl S, Wang A, Ayyagari R, Ren B.
ai_summary: Single-cell multiomics profiling of the human retina, macula, and retinal pigment epithelium/choroid generated atlases of gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and 3D chromatin architecture across 23 retinal cell types, identifying 420,824 candidate regulatory elements. Comparative analysis with mouse retina revealed conserved and divergent gene-regulatory programs, and deep-learning models were developed to interpret noncoding risk variants for retinal diseases. This resource advances understanding of retinal gene regulation and the mechanisms underlying ocular disease risk variants.

title: The Mammalian Ocular Lens in Focus: Development, Anatomy, Physiology, Transparency, Biomechanics, and Age-related Challenges.
authors: Cheng C, Vu MP.
ai_summary:
This is a general review of the mammalian ocular lens, covering its development, anatomy, physiology, transparency, biomechanics, and age-related changes such as cataracts and presbyopia. It does not focus on a specific gene or establish a gene-disease link, so a plain-language summary is appropriate.

The lens is a transparent, ellipsoid organ that focuses light onto the retina, relying on highly organized epithelial and fiber cells, crystallins, cytoskeletal proteins, and cell-cell communication to maintain transparency and refractive index. Its elastic properties enable accommodation, but age-related stiffening contributes to presbyopia, while any opacity—cataract—remains a leading cause of blindness. This review synthesizes knowledge on lens development, lifelong growth, biomechanics, and emerging methods for studying this unique tissue.

title: Research Progress on Upper Airway Cough Syndrome.
authors: Huang WT, Chen J.
journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
ai_summary: Upper airway cough syndrome (UACS) is a major cause of chronic cough, but its diagnosis and treatment are challenging due to complex pathogenesis, unclear diagnostic criteria, and overlap with other cough causes. Nasal and laryngeal endoscopy is essential for diagnosis, and a multidisciplinary approach improves accuracy and outcomes. This review summarizes UACS clinical features, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and underlying mechanisms to help clinicians manage the condition better.

title: Mechanobiology of hippocampal neurogenesis: directing neural stem cell fate through physical cues.
authors: Akyel I, Moeendarbary E, Sheridan GK.
ai_summary: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis is essential for memory and emotion, and this perspective article discusses how mechanical forces—such as extracellular matrix stiffness and tissue viscoelasticity—influence neural stem cell fate. It reviews the cellular machinery (integrins, mechanosensitive ion channels, cytoskeleton) and signaling pathways (Rho GTPases, YAP/TAZ) that convert physical cues into cellular responses, and considers how changes in tissue mechanics affect neurogenesis in health and disease. The authors propose that integrating mechanobiology could open new therapeutic avenues for neurological disorders through biomaterials or drugs that modulate cell–microenvironment interactions.

title: Neuromodulation Techniques Alleviating Neuropathic Pain by Targeting Microglia: A Narrative Review.
authors: Mu Q, Li X, Li L, Sun S, Xu J, Song G, Chen Y, Lv Y, Gan Z, Yang D.
ai_summary: Neuromodulation techniques show promise for treating neuropathic pain by regulating microglial activation, which plays a key role in pain development and maintenance. The review synthesizes evidence on both indirect mechanisms (modulating neuronal activity to influence microglial phenotypes) and direct mechanisms (acting on microglia-specific properties) but notes that therapeutic parameters remain unstandardized.

title: Distribution of transgene in the rodent choroid plexus after intracerebroventricular injection of adeno-associated virus.
authors: Pooley JR, Bienemann AS, Young A, Hollings O, Wu J, Mayo E, Chu CJ, Singleton WGB.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
ai_summary:
Gene: AQP1
Finding: AAV serotype ShH10Y445F transduces choroid plexus epithelium in mouse, rat, and pig, and when delivering CRISPR/Cas9 can permanently reduce aquaporin-1 expression, though transduction is unevenly distributed with bias toward the injected lateral ventricle.
Disease: Choroid plexus-related brain conditions (gene therapy target)

title: Effect of Solute Molecular Weights on Mass Transfer within the Rat Lacunar-Canalicular System under Gravity.
authors: Xiong B, Liu T, Zhao Y, Gao L, Li X, Zhang C.
ai_summary: This study investigated how solute molecular weight affects mass transfer in the rat lacunar-canalicular system (LCS) under normal and hypergravity conditions. Using fluorescent tracers of varying molecular weights injected into rats, the authors found that tracer concentration in lacunae decreased with distance from the Haversian canal and with increasing solute molecular weight. Hypergravity (5 g) enhanced solute transfer to lacunae, with larger molecules showing greater gravity-driven augmentation, suggesting that hypergravity could improve bone mass transfer and potentially serve as a therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis.

title: Standardized Effect Measures Informing Next-Generation Strategies for Mechanical Stimulation in Cartilage Tissue Engineering.
authors: Shen JK, Huang TB, Davey CE, Salzer E, Van Osch GJVM, Shefelbine SJ, Pandy MG, Stok KS.
ai_summary: Standardized effect measures were applied to compare mechanical stimulation protocols across 95 in vitro cartilage tissue engineering studies. Combined compression and shear was the most effective modality for chondrogenic outcomes, while higher intensities of fluid-induced shear reduced efficacy. The review highlights the need for standardized, controlled comparisons to optimize mechanical stimulation for cartilage tissue engineering.

title: Primary Bronchiectasis and Chronic Sinus Disease in Retinitis Pigmentosa.
authors: Kluanwan Y, Koo CW, Moua T.

title: Structure Makes a Difference: IFT Complex in Ciliary Function and Ciliopathy.
authors: Liu Y, Zhang Y, Ni H, Liu P.
ai_summary: This review describes how the intraflagellar transport (IFT) system builds and maintains cilia. IFT complexes form anterograde trains at the ciliary base, are remodeled at the tip into retrograde trains, and move bidirectionally along microtubules, with the BBSome acting as an adaptor that links membrane cargoes to the trains, mainly for exit from the cilium. The authors synthesize the molecular architecture, transport mechanisms, and regulatory networks of the IFT complexes and connect their dysfunction to human ciliopathy phenotypes.

title: Preimplantation genetic testing for concurrent Meckel Syndrome and hereditary breast cancer in a Chinese family harboring a novel NPHP3 pathogenic variant and a canonical BRCA2 frameshift variant.
authors: Zhang Y, Huang X, Qiu P, Ji H, Ding L, He X, Shi Y, Huang Y, Li P, Mei L.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHP3
Finding: Two compound heterozygous NPHP3 variants (a novel c.950T>C, p.Phe317Ser and c.2694-2_2694-1delAG) were identified in a proband with occipital encephalocele and polycystic kidneys, and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders successfully prevented transmission of both the NPHP3 and co-inherited BRCA2 variants.
Disease: Meckel syndrome type 7 (with concurrent hereditary breast cancer predisposition)

title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Zhou H, Terbeck L, Berical A, Brunet M, Lange SM, Anderson JR, Olbrich H, Bracht DC, Wohlgemuth K, Rieck C, Raidt J, Klingauf J, Sutharsan S, Mussaffi H, Prais D, Dunphy V, Homma ST, Guichard P, Hamel V, Hawkins FJ, Omran H, Brown A.
ai_summary:
Gene: ECT2L and DZANK1
Finding: In situ cryo-electron tomography of human multiciliated epithelial cells showed that ECT2L and DZANK1 form the major linker complexes between adjacent transition zone doublet microtubules, and biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene disrupt transition zone architecture, cause microtubular abnormalities and bulbous ciliary tips, and impair mucociliary clearance.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Atypical Prenatal Phenotypic Spectrum: A Case Series of Four Unique Presentations With Genetic and Diagnostic Insights.
authors: Rathod RS, Kolar G, Vavilala S, Redishetty S, Pawar S, Reddy P, Shah A, Nerakh G.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS1
Finding: In a fetus with an atypical prenatal presentation (heterotaxy with complex heart disease), a pathogenic variant was identified by exome/genome sequencing, illustrating the variability of prenatal phenotypes in monogenic disorders.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS1-related ciliopathy)

title: IMPROVE 2025: The 3rd International Meeting on Pathway-Related Obesity: Vision & Evidence.
authors: Argente J, van den Akker ELT, Cetiner M, Clément K, Forsythe E, Garfield A, Kühnen P, Martos-Moreno GÁ, Meeker D, Müller HL, van Santen HM, von Schnurbein J, Segrestin B, Tanaka T, Tena-Sempere M, Wabitsch M, Zorn S, Farooqi IS.
ai_summary: The third International Meeting on Pathway-Related Obesity (IMPROVE 2025) brought together 161 clinicians and researchers from 19 countries to discuss hyperphagia and obesity caused by defects in the melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) pathway. Sessions covered hyperphagia, monogenic MC4R pathway diseases, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity, with a focus on defining and measuring hyperphagia, genetic diagnostics and natural history, real-world and trial data on targeted therapies, multidisciplinary care models favoring earlier intervention, and patient/caregiver quality of life. The proceedings summarize key updates, discussions, and initiatives from the meeting.

title: A Rare PKHD1 Frameshift Variant Identified in a Prenatally Diagnosed ARPKD Case From a Consanguineous Jordanian Family.
authors: Al-Kuran O, Albadaineh R, Almallah A, Al-Atrash D, Dahbour D, Al-Mehaisen L.
journal: Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: Postnatal exome sequencing in a deceased twin infant with prenatally detected features of ARPKD identified a pathogenic homozygous frameshift variant in PKHD1, confirming the genetic diagnosis.
Disease: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD)

title: The N-terminal, WD40, and C-terminal domains of WDR-31 control ciliary localization and cooperate with ELMOD/RP2 gaps to maintain membrane compartmentalization.
authors: Çevik S, Güzel F.
journal: Turkish journal of biology = Turk biyoloji dergisi
ai_summary:
Gene: WDR-31
Finding: In-frame deletions of the N-terminal, WD40, or C-terminal domains of WDR-31 in C. elegans each disrupted its dynamic localization at the ciliary base (altered mobility, transition zone mislocalization, loss of basal body confinement, or distal axoneme spreading) and caused TRAM-1 leakage into the cilium in a sensitized background, with WDR-31 localization depending on IFT, the BBSome, and transition zone components.
Disease: Ciliary gate/periciliary membrane compartmentalization defects (ciliopathy-related ciliary trafficking phenotype)

title: Whole-exome sequencing-centered genetic evaluation for early-onset obesity in Chinese children: a retrospective single-center cohort.
authors: Chen S, Zhang J, Ge L, Li Z, Wang L, Cheng X.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS1
Finding: A phenotype-correlated variant of uncertain significance (p.T374S), relatively enriched in East Asian reference data, was identified among four VUS findings in a WES-centered workflow, contributing to a 26.1% overall clinically relevant genetic yield (8.7% definitive/likely diagnostic) in children with early-onset obesity.
Disease: Early-onset obesity (onset before 5 years)

title: Tmem216 deficiency induces hydrocephalus via impaired ciliogenesis and disrupted ependymal planar polarity in mice.
authors: Gong Q, Lv Z, Dou Z, Wang S, Zhang K, Guo Y, Wang Y, Shao M, Su L, Liu X, Sun X.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
ai_summary:
Gene: TMEM216
Finding: CNS-specific inactivation of Tmem216 in mice disrupts transition zone structure and ciliogenesis in ependymal cells and their radial glia precursors, impairs translational and rotational planar polarity, and produces immotile or dyskinetic cilia with reduced cerebrospinal fluid flow, causing severe postnatal hydrocephalus.
Disease: Hydrocephalus (Joubert, Meckel, and related ciliopathy syndromes)

title: Pulmonary exacerbations in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Gatt D, Golan-Tripto I, Goldbart A, Hazan G.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on pulmonary exacerbations (PEx) in primary ciliary dyskinesia, covering their definition, epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical impact, and management. Although recent international consensus efforts have proposed standardized PEx definitions, heterogeneity persists across studies. Prospective cohort data show PEx occur frequently across all ages, including infancy, at roughly 3.1 events per person-year, with higher risk in adult females and Pseudomonas aeruginosa-colonized patients; exacerbations cause substantial acute FEV1 loss, and about 20-25% of events fail to recover baseline lung function. Emerging biomarkers such as lung clearance index and exhaled volatile organic compounds may improve prediction and monitoring. Management still relies largely on extrapolation from cystic fibrosis and non-CF bronchiectasis, but the BESTCILIA trial provides the first high-quality evidence that maintenance azithromycin reduces PEx frequency by 55%, and CLEAN-PCD supports airway rehydration (ENaC blockade plus hypertonic saline) as a PCD-specific strategy. Anti-inflammatory agents, inhaled biologics, and gene-directed therapies are entering the pipeline, though gaps remain in optimal definitions, treatment duration, and predictors of incomplete recovery.

title: The Role of Microfilaments in Cilia Formation and Function.
authors: Lyu Q, Ma M, Song T.
ai_summary: This review discusses how the actin cytoskeleton contributes to cilia biology. Actin polymerization regulates basal-body migration and docking at the plasma membrane, interacts with motor proteins involved in vesicular trafficking, and, through remodeling of the actin lattice, modulates microtubule growth and organization. The authors summarize recent findings on the regulatory mechanisms by which actin dynamics influence ciliogenesis, ciliary elongation, and ciliary stability, noting that defects in ciliogenesis underlie ciliopathies.

title: Structural insights into predicted protein-protein interactions and protein complexes in the human proteome.
authors: Pei J, Zhang J, Cong Q.
ai_summary: This computational study extends a prior large-scale effort to predict human protein-protein interactions at near-atomic resolution, presenting new case studies of biological and biomedical interest. The authors highlight novel predicted interactions in DNA repair, mitochondrial function, and the biogenesis of cilia and other organelles, using predicted interfaces to generate mechanistic hypotheses about protein function and pathway crosstalk. They further show how binary interaction predictions can be assembled into models of higher-order multi-protein complexes, revealing candidate subunits and organizational principles. Notably, they map disease-associated mutations onto predicted interaction interfaces, many of which fall directly within these interfaces, offering explanations for how genetic variation may disrupt protein networks and contribute to pathology. Overall, the work illustrates how large-scale computational predictions can be distilled into mechanistic insights and hypotheses for functional study, expanding structural and functional annotation of the human interactome.

title: Response: Commentary: "Clinical evaluation of pediatric olfactory disorders: a review from etiology to management".
authors: Trecca EMC, Marra M, Reale M, Leone L, Cassano M, Della Volpe A, La Mantia I, Pagella F, Cantone E.

title: Self-reported perspective in rare genetic diseases: a systematic review of patient-reported outcome measures classified using the international classification of functioning, disability and health framework.
authors: Simeon R, Usai M, Tramonti A, Canova R, Frigerio D, Berardi A, Pelosin E, Cosentino C.
ai_summary: This systematic review identified 45 patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) developed or validated to assess health-related quality of life across 29 rare and ultra-rare genetic diseases, based on 59 included studies. Mapping content to the ICF framework showed that instruments predominantly captured body functions and activities/participation, while environmental factors, social participation, stigma, and access-to-care domains were consistently underrepresented. Internal consistency and construct validity were the most frequently evaluated measurement properties, whereas responsiveness, measurement error, and cross-cultural validity were rarely assessed. Only three PROMs (HAE-QoL, NF1-AdQoL, EPP-QoL) met COSMIN criteria for category A recommendation; most were category B and five were category C. The authors conclude that the evidence base is limited and methodologically weak, and call for more rigorous, patient-centered, disease-specific PROM development and validation across age groups, languages, and disease contexts.

title: Sporadic cone-rod dystrophy caused by a heterozygous RAB28 p.Ser23Phe pathogenic variant and a de novo 4p16.1p15.33 deletion.
authors: Park J, Jang W, Ahn Y, Lee HJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: RAB28
Finding: A heterozygous RAB28 c.68C>T/p.(Ser23Phe) pathogenic variant inherited from the father combined with a de novo 4p16.1p15.33 deletion encompassing RAB28 on the maternal allele caused severe cone-rod dystrophy with markedly reduced visual acuity, color vision impairment, macular atrophy, and severely diminished cone responses on ERG.
Disease: Autosomal recessive cone-rod dystrophy

title: Current and forthcoming pharmacotherapies for adolescent obesity: Evidence-based review.
authors: Fuentes-Mendoza JM, Concepción-Zavaleta MJ, Dongo-Dueñas LG, Jara-Pianto JMJ, Sierra-Martel JA, Medina-Angulo CA, Virú-Flores HM, Mendoza-Godoy JJ, Zavaleta-Gutiérrez FE, Paz-Ibarra J.
ai_summary: This review compared pharmacotherapies for adolescent obesity (ages 12-18) using randomized trials and meta-analyses lasting over 12 weeks. Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, produced substantial benefit, reducing BMI by 16.1% and improving insulin sensitivity more than liraglutide. However, cost and social inequalities limit access, and data remain scarce for newer agents such as tirzepatide and CagriSema in adolescents. The authors conclude that semaglutide is the current gold standard but call for longer-term, comparative, and safety trials in pediatric cohorts.

title: Validation of Prognostic Tools for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease Progression in a Multiethnic South African Cohort ​.
authors: Kapche CXM, Assounga A.
ai_summary: This retrospective study of 276 South African adults with ADPKD tested pragmatic prognostic tools that avoid MRI and genotyping, which are often unavailable in resource-limited settings and unvalidated in African populations. A Modified PROPKD score (0–5, based only on age, sex, hypertension, and urological events) independently predicted progression to end-stage kidney disease, with the high-risk category showing a hazard ratio of 4.34 (95% CI 2.88–6.71). Ultrasound-measured kidney length above 16.5 cm was also predictive (HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.32–2.64). The score performed especially well in Black African patients, suggesting that clinical phenotypes such as early-onset hypertension are strong markers of disease severity in this group.

title: Giant Hydronephrosis Secondary to Ureteral Obstruction Imposed by Massive Hepatomegaly in a Patient with Polycystic Liver Disease: A Case Report.
authors: Tzelepis K, Vartzelis G, Stamatiou K, Manolakos E, Giannakodimos I, Langouretos V, Kotoulas C, Venieris P, Ziogou A, Stylianidis N, Tsakali K, Stamouli D, Sotiriou S, Meimaris G.
ai_summary: This case report describes a patient with isolated polycystic liver disease (without bilateral polycystic kidney disease) in whom massive hepatomegaly compressed and displaced the kidney, obstructing the ureter at the pyeloureteral junction and causing giant hydronephrosis. Imaging (ultrasound and CT) confirmed the cystic liver involvement and resulting mass effect, which produced abdominal distension, dysphagia, reflux, early satiety, reduced mobility, and abdominal/lumbar pain. The authors emphasize that clinicians should consider mass-effect complications in isolated polycystic liver disease, since early recognition and intervention may prevent severe secondary organ dysfunction.

title: Global research trends in heterotaxy syndrome with congenital heart defects: a 20-year bibliometric analysis (2006-2025).
authors: Zhao M, Cong X, Liu X, Pan J, Hou Z, Wang F, Wang L.
ai_summary: This bibliometric analysis of 493 publications (2006–2025) found that heterotaxy syndrome research output has grown steadily, peaking in 2022, with the United States, Harvard Medical School, and Boston Children's Hospital as leading contributors. Keyword and co-citation analyses showed a shift in research focus away from anatomical classification and staged surgical palliation toward genetic mechanisms, prognostic assessment, and long-term outcomes.

title: ERS Congress 2025: highlights from the Paediatrics Assembly.
authors: Patel D, Shahbazi Khamas S, Maier P, Ersu R, Moeller A, Vijverberg SJH.
ai_summary: This conference highlights summary reports on a surge in youth vaping, new evidence on exposome-driven respiratory risks, and advances in rare paediatric lung diseases, emphasizing that global collaboration is needed to support low-resource settings and reduce growing respiratory health inequities.

title: Pontine Tegmental Cap Dysplasia Presenting With Global Developmental Delay and Vestibulocochlear Nerve Aplasia: A Case Report.
authors: Bilal K, Rao MO, Hassan SMS, Tagani AH, Nadeem N, Shahab SH, Habib F.
ai_summary: Pontine tegmental cap dysplasia (PTCD) should be suspected in children presenting with global developmental delay and sensorineural hearing loss. MRI is essential for detecting the hallmark dorsal "tegmental cap" and associated hindbrain malformations, and vestibulocochlear nerve aplasia can account for the severe hearing impairment seen in these patients. Early recognition allows timely multidisciplinary rehabilitation and audiological intervention.

title: Centrosome Protein CCDC81 Promotes Ciliogenesis.
authors: Liu X, Liu F, Nai S.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC81
Finding: CCDC81 localizes to the centrosome via its 301-505 aa region, is highly conserved in mammals, and its silencing reduces the frequency and length of primary cilia without affecting centriole number; Ccdc81 is enriched in mouse tissues bearing motile cilia (testis, lung, trachea, fallopian tubes), and knockout mice show no overt body weight abnormalities over six weeks.
Disease: Primary cilia formation and motile cilia function (ciliogenesis)

title: Correction: Clinical, genetic and bioinformatic analysis of Saudi families with Joubert syndrome and related disorders.
authors: Alafghani R, Aljeaid D, Shaik NA, Banaganapalli B, Elango R, Khard G, Habhab W, Jadkarim G, Alshaer DS, Almutadares M, Alrayes NM, Issa NM.

title: Precision diagnostics in bronchiectasis: current advances in imaging, microbiology, biomarkers, and digital health.
authors: Wu B, Lu S, Liu H.
ai_summary: This review examines emerging precision-diagnostic approaches for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, arguing that static anatomical classification via HRCT, standard sputum cultures, and subjective symptom tracking fail to capture the disease's clinical heterogeneity and underlying drivers. It evaluates AI-driven quantitative imaging, molecular microbiology, high-throughput biomarker profiling, and digital remote monitoring, concluding that these tools can clarify obscure phenotypes, reveal actionable treatable traits, and support earlier preemptive care, though they cannot replace bedside clinical judgment. Because current evidence remains fragmented, the authors call for standardized imaging protocols, transparent algorithmic pipelines, clinically actionable metagenomic reporting, validation in underrepresented Asian and Chinese cohorts, and integration of high-dimensional data into pragmatic point-of-care pathways that improve outcomes without widening healthcare disparities.

title: A Case of Progressively Worsening Dyspnea and Chronic Cough in a Patient With Known Bronchiectasis.
authors: Eldeiry D, Geyer A, Machnicki S.
ai_summary: A 53-year-old woman with a 10-year history of bronchiectasis, childhood asthma, and chronic cough presented with three years of progressively worsening exertional dyspnea despite adherence to airway clearance therapy. Her history also included fatigue, seasonal allergies, heartburn, and occasional small-joint stiffness of the hands, with a family history notable for sarcoidosis in her father. The abstract presents only the case presentation, without diagnostic findings or conclusions.

title: In Reply: Pseudo-Index Events cannot be Configured on the TriNetX Platform.
authors: Wu TK.
journal: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes

title: Advances in organoids for personalized medicine: from technological development to clinical application.
authors: Zhou X, Yan X, Zhang Z, Zhang Z, Que Y, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Lu K, Wang L.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review surveys the technological evolution and construction methods of organoids—three-dimensional cultures derived from patient tissues or stem cells that mimic in vivo tissue architecture and function. It highlights their applications in oncology, genetic disorders, infectious diseases, and drug screening, emphasizing how they support precision medicine through preservation of genomic fidelity, prediction of drug sensitivity, and gene-editing-based disease modeling. The authors note that technical challenges still limit full clinical translation, and that overcoming these obstacles is essential for realizing organoids' potential in individualized therapy.

title: Structured Application of Genetic Testing in a Pediatric Kidney Clinic.
authors: Salcedo-Giraldo J, Wink KR, Dadzie N, Freiman A, Pyle T, Gordish-Dressman H, Moxey-Mims M, Dahl NK, Guay-Woodford LM, Gulati A, Inherited and Polycystic Kidney Disease (IPKD) Program at Children's National Hospital, Washington, DC.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Pseudo-Index Events Cannot be Configured on the TriNetX Platform.
authors: Wang J.
journal: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes

title: Response to "Beyond Pain: Sarcopenia, Malnutrition, and Sex-Specific Body Image Distortion as Potential Additional Mediators of HRQOL Impairment in ADPKD".
authors: Fadlallah J, Ho M, Hassan MT, Dehkharghanian T, Cam MM, Lee SH, Khowaja S, Bichet DG, Brown PA, Lanktree MB, Moist L, Wang B, Khalili K, Mucsi I, Pei Y.

title: Centrosome-Signaling Pathway Crosstalk: A Core Hub From Cellular Homeostasis to Disease.
authors: Pan M, Li J, Fu J.
ai_summary: This review describes how the centrosome acts as a signaling hub, integrating multiple pathways—including Hedgehog, Wnt, and Notch—that control cell growth, division, differentiation, and tissue homeostasis. It highlights bidirectional crosstalk in which these pathways both depend on and shape centrosomal behavior, positioning the centrosome as a central node linking cellular homeostasis to disease.

title: Lipid-Retinoid Metabolic Network Links Genetic Variation to Molecular Heterogeneity in Inherited Retinal Degeneration.
authors: Sołek P, Cholewińska E, Rejdak R, Nowomiejska K, Ognik K.
ai_summary: This study combined whole-exome sequencing with profiling of lipid-related proteins (ApoA1, ApoE, LPL) and systemic lipid measures in 203 patients with inherited retinal degeneration to explore how lipid and retinoid metabolism contributes to disease heterogeneity. The authors identified a coordinated lipid-retinoid-photoreceptor metabolic network connecting systemic lipid metabolism to photoreceptor processes. Although standard lipid values mostly fell within clinical reference ranges, their distributions showed considerable biological variability, and network architecture differed by sex, with denser, more interconnected networks in female patients. Integrating genetic and protein data indicated that variant pathogenicity is associated with coordinated remodeling of lipid-related molecular states, supporting lipid and retinoid metabolism as integral to the molecular heterogeneity of IRD.

title: Bovine Pericardium Patch Application in Living Donor Kidney Transplantation With Multiple Renal Arteries: A Case Series.
authors: Dahiya R, Garner S, Sorrentino M, Burns J, Croome KP.

title: Social Reintegration and Associated Factors Among Patients Receiving Peritoneal Dialysis: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Lin QQ, Wang YC, Zhang XM, Zhang YB, Luo GZ, Tian N, Wang Y.
ai_summary: Among 202 adults on maintenance peritoneal dialysis in China, 81.7% had high social reintegration. Dialysis duration over 10 years and dependence in activities of daily living were each independently associated with lower odds of high social reintegration, suggesting that functional assessment and social reintegration should be incorporated into routine follow-up, with extra support for patients on prolonged dialysis or with reduced functional independence.

title: A Clinical Genetics-Driven Dual Diagnosis of Prader-Willi Syndrome Due to Mosaic Maternal UPD(15) and NOTCH3-Related CADASIL.
authors: Bogliardi FM, D'Ambrosio P, Quattromini G, Di Mario G, Pomponi MG, Miele L, Vergani E, Zampino G, Liguori A, Zollino M, Crinò A.
ai_summary:
Gene: NOTCH3
Finding: Exome sequencing identified a paternally inherited pathogenic NOTCH3 variant (c.3016C>T, p.Arg1006Cys), with brain MRI showing chronic vascular-type leukoencephalopathy consistent with CADASIL despite no overt ischemic events.
Disease: CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy)

title: Chronic Kidney Disease in Lithuanian Children: Single Center Experience.
authors: Rukšėnaitė U, Ažukaitis K, Čerkauskienė R, Ruzgienė D, Vitkevič R, Litvinenko D, Jankauskienė A.
ai_summary: This single-center cross-sectional study of 65 Lithuanian children with chronic kidney disease (mean age 11.1 years) found that CAKUT was the predominant etiology (61.5%), with renal hypoplasia the most common variant, followed by cystic kidney diseases (13.9%) and glomerulopathies (9.2%). Most children (66.2%) were in CKD stage 2 (mean eGFR 60.5 mL/min/1.73 m²), and age, sex, eGFR, and CKD stage did not differ significantly across etiology groups. Normal weight predominated at every CKD stage (60.0–66.7%), and nearly half of patients had CKD-related complications—most commonly CKD-mineral and bone disorder, proteinuria, and arterial hypertension—even in early stages. While management generally aligned with KDIGO guidelines, gaps remained in treating proteinuria, anemia, and growth impairment.

title: Prevalence and Pattern of Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Pruritus in a Nigerian Teaching Hospital.
authors: Edeki IR, Madubuko RC.
journal: Nigerian medical journal : journal of the Nigeria Medical Association
ai_summary: This cross-sectional study of 171 pre-dialysis Nigerian patients with stage 3-5 CKD found a CKD-associated pruritus prevalence of 26.9%, with most cases of moderate severity and generalized distribution. CKD stage independently predicted pruritus (adjusted OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.24-5.19, p=0.011), while gender and CKD aetiology showed no significant association with pruritus or its severity. The authors recommend routine periodic assessment and management of pruritus in all CKD patients to improve quality of life and reduce morbidity and mortality.

title: Opportunities for renal genetic evaluation among pregnant patients with kidney disease.
authors: Nandigam L, Parobek CM, Moseley T, Davis AE, Denning SG, Reza M, Saridey SK, Lombaard HA.
ai_summary: This retrospective cohort study of 103 pregnant patients with CKD or ESRD found that although 64% were referred for genetic counseling for any reason, only 27% of referrals cited a renal indication and just 8% underwent genetic testing to determine the etiology of their renal disease. Renal transplant and family history of renal disease were associated with a recommendation for renal genetic workup, while commercial insurance coverage was the only factor significantly associated with completion of a renal genetic workup. The authors conclude that renal genetic evaluation is underutilized across all demographic and socioeconomic groups and should be considered for pregnant patients with renal disease.

title: CRISPR and Gene Augmentation Rescue Trabecular Meshwork Dysfunction in iPSC Models of Lowe Syndrome.
authors: Chen S, Liu Z, Wang W, Wang Q, Kowal TJ, Zhang F, Walkiewicz G, Hossen F, Lachman HM, Zhou J, Wang Y, Sun Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: OCRL
Finding: In patient iPSC-derived trabecular meshwork models, AAV2-OCRL showed the highest transduction efficiency among three AAV-OCRL vectors, and CRISPR-mediated gene correction restored OCRL enzyme activity and corrected cellular defects, while RNA sequencing implicated dysregulated extracellular matrix organization, cell adhesion, focal adhesion, and cytoskeletal pathways in trabecular meshwork dysfunction.
Disease: Lowe syndrome (including associated glaucoma)

title: Cerebrospinal fluid-driven ependymal motile cilia defects are implicated in multiple sclerosis.
authors: Bigotte M, Groh AMR, Afanasiev E, Wong V, Lancon K, Yaqubi M, Creeggan F, Sinott A, Pei J, Moore CS, Harroud A, Schneider R, Séguéla P, Charabati M, Tea F, Fournier AP, Wang YC, Ragoussis J, Prat A, Thebault S, Zandee S, Stratton JA.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC39
Finding: Single-cell RNA sequencing and in situ staining showed loss of ependymal motile cilia in MS brain tissue, MS CSF reduced ciliary beating frequency and altered ciliary gene/protein expression (partly via IFNγ), and conditional knockout of Ccdc39 in adult mouse ependymal cells caused transient ventricular enlargement, increased periventricular microglial density, and altered nesting behaviour.
Disease: Multiple sclerosis (periventricular pathology and non-motor behavioural deficits)

title: From Guidelines to Clinical Practice: Expert Perspectives on Long-Term Management of Obesity.
authors: Chen H, Li L, Zhang J, Zhu S, Cornier MA, Purnell JQ.
ai_summary: An international expert panel discussed the 2026 TOS-OMA-OAC guidance on pharmacological obesity management, agreeing that obesity is a chronic, progressive disease requiring lifelong pharmacotherapy once started, since discontinuation leads to weight regain and lost metabolic benefit. They emphasized treating obesity as an upstream intervention for related complications, with greater weight loss yielding greater benefit, and highlighted visceral adipose tissue as a key target—especially in Asian populations, where metabolic risk can occur at lower BMI. The panel noted variable treatment response and that weight-loss plateaus reflect maximal effectiveness rather than failure, endorsed individualized stepwise care combining pharmacotherapy and metabolic surgery, and stressed that policy, access, affordability, and stigma barriers must be addressed for real-world benefit.

title: Genome-Wide and Rare Variant Association Studies of Amblyopia in Admixed American and African Ancestry Groups.
authors: Lee KAV, Whitman MC.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF7
Finding: In a gene-level rare variant association study of admixed American ancestry participants, KIF7 was among 15 genes identified, alongside other axonal transport genes (KIF1B) and growth factor signaling genes (EGF, ERBIN, AKAP17A).
Disease: Amblyopia

title: Novel MORC2 variants in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z: genetic and functional insights.
authors: Tao R, Zhang T, Luo F, Liu Y, Fan L, Wu X, Liu Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: MORC2
Finding: Two heterozygous MORC2 variants were identified in CMT families: the previously unreported c.34G>C (p.A12P), which reduced protein half-life and stability without affecting transcription, and the rare c.848G>A (p.R283H), which reduced MORC2 transcription.
Disease: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z (CMT2Z)

title: Beyond Pain: Sarcopenia, Malnutrition, and Sex-Specific Body Image Distortion as Potential Additional Mediators of HRQOL Impairment in ADPKD.
authors: Farinone S, Brambilla Pisoni M, Paolisi M, Bianca P, Kola K, Petrone M, Maiucchi P, Vezzoli G, Alibrandi MTS.

title: Beyond the salt barrier: CRISPR-mediated DNA reprogramming to uncouple yield from tolerance in Rice: A review.
authors: Bulle M, Kondi RKR, Rahman MM, Sharma M, Rana P, Chaudhary C, Subudhi PK.
ai_summary: This review argues that the decades-long focus on Na+ exclusion via Saltol and OsHKT1;5 has hit a physiological ceiling: excluder rice survives salt stress but fails to fill grain because continuous ion extrusion drains ATP from reproductive sinks and ABA-driven stomatal closure limits carbon supply, producing a "survival-yield gap." The authors propose a five-tier systems-level strategy combining CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of negative regulators (OsRR22, RST1, PC1), cytoskeletal reinforcement of transporter delivery, import of halophyte traits from Oryza coarctata, recalibration of the ROS-photosynthesis axis via DHHC09-STRK1-CatC and stomatal density engineering, and pyramiding all modules into a "Salt-Shield Rice" via multiplex editing, introgression, speed breeding, and genomic selection. They outline a ten-year roadmap targeting >70% yield stability at 8-10 dS m-1, while explicitly noting this is aspirational: three of the five tiers remain unvalidated in rice.

title: AI-driven CT quantification of mucus plugs to evaluate the effect of inhaled hypertonic saline in children aged 3-6 years with cystic fibrosis: a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Chen Y, Latisenko R, Davis SD, Rosenfeld M, Ratjen F, Hinckley Stukovsky KD, Stick S, Tiddens HAWM, on behalf the SHIP-CT study group.

title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage in a pediatric patient with cri du chat syndrome: a case report.
authors: Sharma R, Adhikari D, Shrestha B, Kc S, Gupta P, Aryal S.
ai_summary: A pediatric patient with cri du chat syndrome developed diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, a life-threatening pulmonary complication not previously reported in this condition. The case highlights the need to consider DAH in children with genetic disorders who present with recurrent hemoptysis and anemia, and underscores the importance of early recognition and multidisciplinary management.

title: Combining Cystatin C and Creatinine Increases eGFR Slope Accuracy in ADPKD.
authors: Bais T, Mohamed AAA, Noruzi A, Umar M, Binoy BA, Salih M, Meijer E, Gansevoort RT.
ai_summary:
Gene: CST3
Finding: In 260 patients with ADPKD, eGFR based on combined creatinine and cystatin C (eGFRcr-cys) correlated more strongly with iothalamate-measured GFR decline than creatinine-based eGFR (CCC 0.68 vs. 0.58), and its lower slope variability reduced hypothetical trial sample size requirements by 37% to 38%.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Lung ultrasound versus chest X-ray in pediatric lower respiratory tract infections at a tertiary center: a prospective observational study.
authors: Elmeazawy R, Aborady AA, Abd-Razik AM, Erfan AA, Eltomey MA, Hamza MB.
ai_summary: Lung ultrasound showed high sensitivity (95.6% at admission, 96.7% at follow-up) but initially low specificity (29.4%, rising to 62.9%) compared with chest X-ray in 338 children with suspected lower respiratory tract infections. Agreement between the two modalities improved from fair at admission (κ = 0.311) to substantial at follow-up (κ = 0.607), and varied by diagnosis: best in pneumonia (moderate agreement), lower in recurrent wheezing, and poor to negligible in acute bronchiolitis and the heterogeneous "others" group. The authors conclude that LUS is a promising radiation-free tool for diagnosis and serial monitoring, especially in pneumonia, but its reduced specificity and weaker performance in airway-predominant conditions require cautious interpretation alongside clinical findings.

title: The New Nexin-Dynein Regulatory Complex Component CCDC153 Is Dispensable for Ciliary Motility and Fertility in Mice.
authors: Nai S, Zheng Y, Liu X, Zhao H.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC153
Finding: Ccdc153 knockout mice are viable with normal brain ventricles and fertility, and CCDC153 localizes to the axonemal lumen of motile cilia but is dispensable for ciliary motility in brain ventricles and sperm.
Disease: Ciliopathies (not a causative gene)

title: Characterization of Ocular Developmental Disorders in the Israeli Population: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations and Novel Candidate Genes.
authors: Rabinovich Y, Vardizer Y, Pincovich S, Wolowelsky M, Kulyamzin S, Ehrenberg M, Zayit-Soudry S, Man Peles I, Leibu R, Goldenberg-Cohen N, Ben-Yosef T.
ai_summary:
Gene: MFRP, SMO, GJA8, SOX2, RARB, TSPAN12, SHH, PTPN11, BEST1, TP63
Finding: Whole exome sequencing of 47 Israeli individuals with microphthalmia, anophthalmia, and ocular coloboma yielded definite or possible molecular diagnoses in 30% of probands (13/43 families) across 10 genes, with microphthalmia the most common phenotype (64%), and identified 226 rare possibly pathogenic variants in 218 genes not previously linked to these disorders.
Disease: Microphthalmia, anophthalmia, and ocular coloboma (MAC)

title: "The feasibility of free septal mucosal grafts in preventing postoperative middle meatus synechia after endoscopic sinus surgery".
authors: Elgendy A, Elzayat S, El-Ouny AG, Morshedy A, Khaled S, Gehad I.
ai_summary: This prospective study of 116 adults with chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps found that placing a free septal mucosal graft over exposed bone in the middle meatus after unilateral endoscopic sinus surgery was feasible, biocompatible, and technically straightforward. Patients showed significant improvement in symptom scores (SNOT-22) and endoscopic findings (LKES) at 6 months, and stable middle turbinate position without lateralization was achieved in 78% of cases, suggesting the graft helps reduce postoperative middle meatal synechiae.

title: Correlation Between Body Mass Index (BMI) and Severity of Bronchial Asthma in Children: A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Satija P.
ai_summary: This cross-sectional study of 42 children aged 5–18 with physician-diagnosed asthma examined whether nutritional status, measured by BMI-for-age on WHO growth charts, correlates with asthma severity graded by GINA criteria. Increasing BMI was significantly associated with greater asthma severity overall (p=0.007), with overweight/obese children most often having moderate persistent asthma. On subgroup analysis, the association held in boys (p=0.012) but not girls (p=0.30). The authors conclude that higher BMI correlates with greater asthma severity, driven largely by boys, but caution that the findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and that prospective studies are needed to determine whether weight optimization improves asthma outcomes.

title: Assessing Surgical Extent Before Biologic Therapy for CRSwNP.
authors: Yu AJ, LaPointe KA, Roberts KA, Yu M, Palmer JN, Workman AD, Mattos JL, Schlosser RJ, Soler ZM.
ai_summary: Nearly two-thirds of patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) received biologics without prior surgery or with incomplete sinus surgery, and the frontal sinus was the least frequently addressed sinus before biologic therapy. These findings suggest that surgical extent is often limited before patients are started on biologics.

title: Baseline hematuria in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Serra A, Serra JH, Severin M, Russmann S.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Baseline hematuria (macroscopic or non-infection-associated microscopic) independently predicts faster eGFR decline and worse renal survival but not total kidney volume growth in ADPKD.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

title: Unmasking a Deeper Cause of Persistent Lung Disease: More Than Just Pneumonia.
authors: Tekin MN, Gürler E, Polat ZB, Yörük B, Ülgen Ö, Girit S.

title: Non-transport functions of motor proteins in corticogenesis.
authors: Mitina N, Medyanik A, Tarabykin V, Kondakova E.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review argues that dyneins, kinesins, and myosins contribute to cerebral cortex development through functions beyond their canonical role in intracellular transport. It synthesizes current evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which these motor proteins act as regulators at key stages of corticogenesis—proliferation of neural progenitors, neuronal migration, neurite differentiation, axonal pathfinding, and synaptogenesis—and examines how disruption of these non-transport functions is causally linked to cortical developmental disorders such as microcephaly, lissencephaly, and agenesis of the corpus callosum.

title: Human airway organoids for bacterial-host interaction studies: methods, insights and translational promise.
authors: Huang Y, Liao S, Chua D, Shi Y, Tan Y, Mac Aogáin M, Liu Y, Xu Z, Li L.
ai_summary: This review argues that human airway organoids (HAOs) bridge the gap between animal models and conventional cell cultures for studying bacterial respiratory infections, combining biological relevance with experimental versatility. It surveys advances in HAO technology over the past decade, highlighting how these models have transformed understanding of infection pathogenesis and expanded the scope of infection biology, and concludes that HAOs hold promise for improving healthcare management of bacterial respiratory infections amid rising antimicrobial resistance.

title: Tuberculosis in the Context of Idiopathic CD4 Lymphocytopenia: A Case Report and Literature Review.
authors: Alwarthan SM, Alsaid AH, Attia AEA, Alsahlawi A, AlZahrani SA, Alotaibi KG, Al Dhneem HN, Alwazzeh MJ.
journal: The American journal of case reports
ai_summary: This case report describes a 42-year-old man with no HIV infection who presented with active pulmonary tuberculosis alongside persistent, unexplained CD4 lymphocytopenia (103.8 cells/µL, remaining below 200 cells/µL even after successful anti-tuberculosis therapy). The authors emphasize that idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia should be suspected in patients with lymphocytopenia and negative HIV status, as it can predispose to opportunistic infections such as tuberculosis, and note that formal management guidelines for this rare immunodeficiency are still lacking.

title: Automated reanalysis of genomic data for rare disease diagnostics at scale.
authors: Welland MJ, Ahlquist KD, De Fazio P, Austin-Tse C, Pais L, Wedd L, Bryen S, Rius R, Franklin M, Morrison C, Hall G, Gauthier L, Bloemendal A, Francis DI, Mallett AJ, Mallawaarachchi A, Lockhart PJ, Leventer R, Scheffer IE, Howell KB, Kassahn KS, Scott HS, McGaughran J, Christodoulou J, Thorburn DR, Thompson BA, Patel CV, Smith G, O'Donnell-Luria A, Sadedin S, Rehm HL, Lunke S, Wander J, Samocha KE, Simons C, MacArthur DG, Stark Z.
ai_summary: Talos, an open-source tool, automates variant prioritization by combining dynamically updated gene-disease and variant-level evidence with inheritance-aware filtering, enabling iterative genomic reanalysis without manual effort. Validated on 1,089 individuals with rare disease, trio-based analysis recovered 90% of known diagnoses while returning only 1.3 variants per case on average, and variant burden fell to one variant per 200 cases with monthly reanalysis. Applied to 4,735 undiagnosed individuals, it yielded 241 diagnoses (5.1%), of which 32% stemmed from new gene-disease relationships, 22% from new variant-level evidence, and 45% from improved analysis strategies. The results demonstrate that frequent, systematic reanalysis can be delivered at scale.

title: Patterns of dialysis-related complications and their association with baseline characteristics in outpatient hemodialysis: a retrospective analysis of nursing documentation.
authors: Zhang J, Chen LS, Yang XL, Yang W, Wu Y.
ai_summary: This retrospective single-center study analyzed routine electronic nursing records from outpatients with end-stage kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis to describe documented complication patterns and their links to baseline characteristics. At the patient level, older age showed a marginal inverse association with intradialytic hypotension (IDH), and diabetic nephropathy was associated with lower recorded odds of IDH relative to the uremia reference group; other complication associations were not statistically significant and are considered exploratory. Because dialysis prescription variables were unavailable and chart abstraction is inherently limited, the authors frame these findings as hypothesis-generating and call for prospective studies with real-time hemodynamic monitoring and structured nursing assessments to validate the patterns.

title: To face overwhelming odds - multiple vascular complications in a woman with bicuspid aortic valve: multivessel spontaneous coronary artery dissection, bilateral cerebral aneurysms and multi-site fibromuscular dysplasia.
authors: Kądziela J, Michałowska I, Soćko G, Rutka B, Sadowski K, Kądziela J.
journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology

title: Case Report: Severe asthma following earthquake-related inhalational exposure in a child.
authors: Al-Zoubi G, Nofal M, El Wahab K, Alkhlaifat N.
ai_summary: This case report describes a 5-year-old girl who developed severe, recurrent hypoxemic respiratory failure (oxygen saturations as low as 70%, five hospitalizations over five months) after being trapped under earthquake rubble for three days two years earlier. Her workup showed diffuse bronchial wall thickening and air trapping on CT, markedly elevated total IgE with a negative allergen panel, and peripheral eosinophilia, while infectious and alternative causes were excluded. She failed GINA Step 4-5 triple controller therapy, with two admissions triggered by medication access lapses after immigration, and was lost to follow-up. The authors conclude that prolonged early-childhood rubble entrapment may contribute to severe asthma with non-allergen-specific IgE elevation and eosinophilia, compounded by viral triggers, immigration-related medication access barriers, and psychological trauma, and suggest biologic therapy and systematic respiratory surveillance for pediatric earthquake survivors.

title: Abdominopelvic Preoperative Imaging in Adult Candidates for Kidney Transplant: A Systematic Review of Its Impact on Surgical Decision-making.
authors: Costa Silva A, Di Bello F, Lopez-Abdad A, Haberal HB, Piana A, Pecoraro A, Dönmez Mİ, Bañuelos Marco B, Prudhomme T, Alturas Silva J, Breda A, Territo A, EAU Young Academic Urologists (YAU) Kidney Transplantation Working Group.
ai_summary: This systematic review of 13 studies found that preoperative abdominopelvic imaging in adult kidney transplant candidates frequently alters clinical management: imaging findings changed surgical strategy in up to 24% of cases and led to exclusion from transplantation in 2.0-29%. Vascular calcifications were detected in 14-20% of patients by Doppler ultrasound and up to 90% by noncontrast CT, with age, diabetes, and dialysis duration commonly used as criteria for imaging. However, heterogeneous data and small sample sizes (20-470 patients) prevented firm conclusions, leading the authors to recommend structured expert consensus as an interim step toward more consistent imaging practices and future multicenter research.

title: A comparative analysis of fetal mirror-image dextrocardia in China pre- and post-COVID-19 lockdown lifting.
authors: Xu W, Wei Y, Gao X, Yang X, Gao J, He S, Huo H, Qiao M, Dong X, Chen W, Zhao E, Liu B.
ai_summary: This retrospective study found that the incidence of fetal mirror-image dextrocardia in Xi'an, China rose sharply after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted on December 7, 2022: from 0.9 per 10,000 pregnancies during the control period (January–April 2022) to 18.2 per 10,000 after lifting (January–April 2023), an 8–20-fold increase over both the control period and the pre-pandemic period (January–April 2019). An online survey identified 111 additional cases across 22 other provinces after restrictions were lifted. All affected pregnant women had a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection, with timing coinciding with early embryonic development (approximately 4–6 weeks after the last menstrual period). The authors conclude that the temporal overlap between the rise in fetal dextrocardia cases and the COVID-19 outbreak in China may suggest a potential association between the two, though the study design cannot establish causation.

title: Rapid molecular detection of respiratory pathogens in patients with bronchiectasis.
authors: Alferes de Lima Headley D, Young M, Hull RC, Bell AJ, Hennayake C, Galloway R, McIntosh E, Eke Z, Richardson H, Long MB, Williams-Macdonald S, Mountjoy E, Kempen MHC, Fawcett-Gibson D, De Vega D, Long JA, Buchanan H, Sibila O, Aliberti S, Dakin R, Holmes R, Clarke C, Chalmers JD.
ai_summary: Bacterial rRNA-targeted quantification assays for H. influenzae, S. aureus, S. pneumoniae and M. catarrhalis detected these respiratory pathogens in bronchiectasis samples with over 90% sensitivity and identified additional positive cases that conventional methods missed.

title: Roxadustat-Associated Cholestatic Jaundice in Haemodialysis Patients with Positive Rechallenge.
authors: Ke X, Liu C.
journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine
ai_summary: This case series describes four haemodialysis patients who developed cholestatic jaundice after starting roxadustat, marked by elevated direct bilirubin and bile acids with normal transaminases; two had positive rechallenge, other causes of cholestasis were excluded, and biochemistry recovered after drug withdrawal. The findings support a causal link between roxadustat and cholestatic jaundice and argue for monitoring cholestatic parameters during therapy.

title: Correction to "A Quarter Century of EHD Protein Research: From Endosomal Recycling to Ciliopathies".
Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal mesenchymal tissues: implications for bone, tendon, and cartilage regenerative engineering-a narrative review.
authors: Rosenberg N.
ai_summary: This narrative review integrates evidence on how mechanical signals regulate musculoskeletal connective-tissue biology, emphasizing that mechanotransduction operates as a coupled extracellular matrix–integrin–cytoskeleton–nucleus continuum rather than through isolated cytoskeletal or nuclear drivers. Responses are shaped by lineage stage, anatomic niche, inflammation, cellular subpopulation, and prior loading, with mechanical memory potentially encoded via persistent YAP/TAZ activity, microRNA programs, DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin architecture, and metabolic remodeling. Evidence is strongest for bone (Piezo-dependent osteogenesis, TRPV4-mediated shear sensing, viscoelastic compression, osteocyte–stromal extracellular-vesicle signaling, and osteogenesis–angiogenesis coupling); tendon and ligament depend on anisotropic architecture and strain-window control, while cartilage shows a narrow boundary between physiologic TRPV4-associated anabolism and high-strain or inflammation-sensitized Piezo/YAP-mediated maladaptation. Translational implications include mechanically defined cell expansion, biomaterial preconditioning, stage-specific rehabilitation, and potency assays incorporating loading history, though direct clinical validation of stable perioperative cellular mechanical memory remains limited.

title: The Trajectory of Gene Discovery in Retinitis Pigmentosa.
authors: Wong AXJ, Chua Z, Guo J, Tay HG, Wang ZX, Quinodoz M, Tan TE, Rivolta C, Fenner BJ.
ai_summary: This hypothesis-generating analysis of RetiGene data examined how the year a retinitis pigmentosa (RP) gene was discovered relates to its inheritance pattern, functional category, and phenotypic onset. Across 83 genes with at least 5 extractable onset cases (and a secondary set of 66), later gene discovery was associated with later mean age of symptom onset, and discovery year also differed significantly by functional category. The authors conclude these patterns likely reflect biological detectability, study design, and publication dynamics rather than intrinsic gene-phenotype relationships, and suggest that future RP gene discovery should focus on less obvious pathways (ciliary, transport, metabolic) and later-presenting or subtler phenotypes.

title: Multiomics studies reveal how ambient temperature changes govern cellular responses of Chlamydomonas.
authors: Shetty P, Vuong T, Li C, Wagner V, Myrzakhmetova D, Peng CC, Li W, Ching J, Zander A, Weiser S, Rosenbaum MA, Allen RJ, Lakemeyer M, Mittag M.
ai_summary: This study profiled the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii grown mixotrophically across ambient temperatures from 18 °C to 33 °C, using transcriptomics plus proteomics of isolated cilia and secreted proteins. Over 5,000 transcripts changed significantly, spanning photosynthesis, lipid metabolism, photoreception, cilia formation, the secretome, and algal-bacterial interactions. CO2 transfer and acetate measurements at 18 °C versus 28 °C indicated reduced photoautotrophic growth at the higher temperature, and antagonistic bacterial activity persisted longer at lower temperatures. Proteomic analysis corroborated abundance shifts in ciliary intraflagellar transport complexes and mating-related secreted proteins. These molecular changes translated into altered growth, cell and cilium length, swimming behavior, mating ability, and bacterial antagonism, showing that even short-term ambient temperature shifts drive major cellular reorganization in this microalga.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Active and Latent Phases of Inherited Retinal Dystrophies Using Synthetic Proteomic Data: A Pathway-Based Application Exercise.
authors: Macchia A, Medori MC, Abidin AJ, Bonetti G, Dhuli K, Ferrari L, Feizyab S, Miertuš J, Falsini B, Placidi G, Chiurazzi P, Gordani O, Dhamo X, Kalluci E, Vešelényiová D, Miertuš S, Luptáková ID, Pospíchal J, Gregorini M, Bertelli M.
ai_summary: This methodological simulation exercise generated an artificial dataset of 500 samples with arbitrary plasma proteomic profiles, classified by a pathway activation score, to test four machine learning models (support vector machine, random forest, logistic regression, and extreme gradient boosting) for distinguishing active from latent phases of inherited retinal dystrophies. Logistic regression performed best, achieving accuracy, precision, and F1-score of 0.73. The authors conclude that synthetic proteomic data can serve as a substitute for evaluating ML approaches when real datasets are scarce, and can help build targeted datasets for retinal dystrophy-associated proteins.

title: Receptor allostery promotes context-specific Sonic Hedgehog signaling during embryonic development.
authors: Dillard ME, Daly CA, Pradhan R, Ansari SS, Hack SJ, Wright WC, Stewart DP, Ghonim MA, Zhang Y, Canac R, Moskowitz IP, Pruett-Miller SM, Steinberg J, Wang YD, Sykes AD, Mori M, Hom CC, Chen T, Thomas PG, Bridges JP, Ogden SK.
ai_summary:
Gene: SMO
Finding: Disruption of an arachidonic acid-binding pocket at the top of the SMO 7TM bundle attenuates SHH- and sterol-stimulated SMO induction, and knock-in mice with compromised AA binding show cyanosis, perinatal lethality, congenital heart disease, and pulmonary maldevelopment while neurodevelopment remains unaltered.
Disease: Congenital heart disease and pulmonary maldevelopment

title: The Cilia-Associated Protein CCDC89 Is Dispensable for Male Fertility in Mice.
authors: Song D, Li Q, Sun Y, Zhao H, Song T.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCDC89
Finding: CCDC89 is a new axonemal-lumen ciliary protein, but Ccdc89 knockout mice show no morphological abnormalities in lung or brain and normal male fertility despite high testicular abundance.
Disease: Male fertility (no phenotype observed)

title: Single-cell transcriptomics and functional validation reveal a TUBB4B-associated malignant epithelial state in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
authors: Chen X, Liao W, Xu M, Peng B, Pan F, Xiao Y, Chen D, Wu Y, Hu R, Qin H, Feng G, Zheng Y, Du H, Zhang Q, Chen G, Song L, Zhang X, Lu Y, Xie J.
ai_summary:
Gene: TUBB4B
Finding: scRNA-seq of normal nasopharynx, primary NPC, and nodal metastases identified an early-trajectory malignant epithelial state with high inferred CNV burden, increased cell-cycle engagement, and microtubule/cilium-associated programs enriched for TUBB4B; TUBB4B localized to mitotic structures, its knockdown reduced G2/M cells while overexpression increased PCNA, clonogenic growth, and xenograft tumor growth, and high cytoplasmic TUBB4B was associated with worse overall and progression-free survival.
Disease: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma

title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in retinitis pigmentosa: structural and vascular insights using OCT and OCTA.
authors: Balikoglu-Yilmaz M, Kocar A, Subasioglu A, Gasimli R, Elmali F.
journal: International journal of retina and vitreous
ai_summary:
Gene: USH2A
Finding: RP patients with multiple-gene variants showed reduced preserved ellipsoid zone, lower subfoveal choroidal thickness, and lower inferior-quadrant choriocapillaris vascular density compared with single-variant groups, while USH2A cases formed a distinct subgroup with no significant differences in most structural or vascular parameters.
Disease: Retinitis pigmentosa

title: Comprehensive bioinformatics analysis identifies candidate ciliogenesis-related genes preferentially associated with N0-stage lung squamous cell carcinoma.
authors: Alipour M, Moghanibashi M, Naeimi S, Mohamadynejad P.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS7, TTC30A
Finding: A bioinformatics analysis of TCGA data identified 1103 candidate N0-stage-associated differentially expressed genes in lung squamous cell carcinoma, with a ciliogenesis-related PPI cluster containing TTC30A, TTC30B, BBS7, and KIF3B, plus seven consensus hub genes (ERBB2, CHUK, CASP8, NOTCH1, HNF4A, CREBBP, IRS1); upregulated genes were enriched in immune-related processes and downregulated genes in lysosomal/trans-Golgi pathways.
Disease: N0-stage lung squamous cell carcinoma

title: A Novel Reporter Mouse for Astrocyte-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Reveals Enrichment of Cargo at Neuronal Mitochondria.
authors: Ren X, Quadri Z, Zhu Z, Fu X, Zhang L, Bieberich E.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
ai_summary:
Gene: CD9
Finding: An astrocyte-specific CD9-tGFP reporter mouse shows that astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles are taken up by neurons and their cargo preferentially enriches at synaptic mitochondria (3-fold higher puncta density) in vivo.
Disease: Astrocyte-neuron extracellular vesicle transfer / neuronal mitochondrial function (not a specific disease)

title: ARL13B is regulated by the ERK/P90 pathway and mediates TMZ resistance in glioblastoma via microvesicles.
authors: Xing H, Chen Y, Li H, Wang M, Cao Y, Liu X.
ai_summary:
Gene: ARL13B
Finding: ARL13B is transcriptionally regulated by the ERK/P90 pathway (with C/EBPβ as a transcription factor) and mediates temozolomide resistance by increasing drug efflux through ectosomes/microvesicles, thereby lowering intracellular drug concentration; inhibiting the ERK/P90 pathway enhances TMZ efficacy.
Disease: Glioblastoma/glioma (temozolomide resistance)

title: Adaptable centriole biogenesis via the intrinsically disordered protein ALMS1.
authors: Ozaki K, Chang TB, Yang WQ, Shulman A, Izquierdo D, Jane WN, Wang WJ, Stearns T, Lüders J, Yang TT, Tsou MB.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALMS1
Finding: The intrinsically disordered protein ALMS1 acts as an extrinsic cofactor that seeds cartwheel formation without incorporating into the seed, and its depletion aborts cartwheel seed assembly while reintroduction restarts biogenesis, with hypomorphic mutations causing aberrant cartwheel expansion-shedding and ectopic centriole formation.
Disease: Centriole biogenesis defects (ALMS1-related, as in Alström syndrome)

title: Did axons evolve by activating cytokinesis during interphase? A hypothesis on the origin of neurons.
authors: Miller KE, Oprea F, Alam S, Grodsky A, Craig EM.
ai_summary: The abstract reviews the evolutionary histories, biophysics, and cell biology of cytokinesis, cell crawling, and ciliogenesis to investigate how axons first arose. Although cilia and axons are outwardly similar and growth cones resemble the leading edge of crawling cells, the authors find that the biophysical processes and critical proteins driving these structures are only weakly linked to axons. In contrast, the traction force machinery that pulls daughter cells apart during cytokinesis and the cytoskeletal organization of cytokinetic bridges show a one-to-one correspondence to neuronal growth cones and axons. The authors therefore hypothesize that axons evolved through mutations that partially activated cytokinesis in an interphase cell, and propose testing this via systematic phylogenetic analysis of genes essential to each process combined with molecular genetic disruption studies, with potential implications for cancer treatment and neuronal regeneration.

title: Overactivation of SHH signaling induces a cascade of dedifferentiation and oncogenesis in a new mouse model for choroid plexus carcinoma.
authors: Peter LS, Altendorf L, Hack K, Thaden V, Göbel C, Mahnke B, Krebs C, Jauch-Speer SL, Kordes UR, Obrecht-Sturm D, Thomas C, Schüller U, Schoof M.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI2
Finding: Constitutive SHH/GLI2 activation combined with MYCN overexpression and Tp53 loss drives choroid plexus epithelial cells to dedifferentiate from mature secretory multiciliated cells into proliferative SOX2-positive monociliated progenitors, producing tumors vulnerable to ATR and CDK inhibition.
Disease: Choroid plexus carcinoma

title: Photostimulation improves maturation of human photoreceptors.
authors: Celiker C, Hruba E, Kyriakou K, Dorgau B, Gambin FM, Weissova K, van Oosten E, Englmaier L, Vaskovicova N, Savage MA, Hilgen G, Sernagor E, Garanto A, Lako M, Barta T.
ai_summary: Rhythmic light flickering at a specific frequency was used to stimulate stem-cell-derived human retinal organoids, a non-invasive and scalable approach. Stimulated organoids showed improved formation of presumptive outer segments, transcriptional shifts from precursor toward mature photoreceptor states, and enhanced responsiveness of downstream retinal neurons. The findings identify patterned light as a physiologically relevant developmental signal for driving retinal differentiation in vitro, with implications for disease modelling, drug discovery, and preparing photoreceptors for cell-based therapies.

title: The Odf2 status contributes to asymmetric inheritance of CD133-positive recycling endosomes during cytokinesis in SK-N-DZ human neuroblastoma cells.
authors: Izumi H, Mae T, Tsukita S, Nakagawara A.
ai_summary:
Gene: Odf2
Finding: Depletion of Odf2/cenexin, which localizes to centrosomal distal and subdistal appendages, strongly promoted recycling endosome localization at both centrosomes and abolished the asymmetric inheritance of CD133-positive recycling endosomes normally seen in daughter cells inheriting daughter versus mother centrosomes.
Disease: Neuroblastoma (SK-N-DZ cells)

title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analyses Identify Candidate Genes for Convergent Reproductive Shifts in a Bimodal Viviparous Amphibian.
authors: Mulder KP, Lourenço A, Gomez-Mestre I, Carneiro M, Buckley D, Martínez-Solano I, Fleischer RC, Bell RC, Velo-Antón G.
ai_summary: Comparative transcriptomic analysis of the uterus and oviduct of pregnant female fire salamanders compared two independent evolutionary transitions from larviparity to pueriparity (in S. s. bernardezi and island S. s. gallaica). Pueriparous females of both lineages shared changes in maternal gene expression relative to larviparous counterparts, alongside lineage-specific differences. Differentially expressed genes were enriched for functions related to reproductive timing, angiogenesis, and maternal signalling, matching phenotypic differences in the uterine environment and embryonic development between reproductive modes. The study provides candidate genes and transcriptomic resources for understanding the genomic basis of pueriparity.

title: Testicular toll with viral intrusion: Molecular insights into the impact of chronic HIV infection on male fertility.
authors: Hediyal TA, Stone EM, Shukri O, Schaal VL, Foroughi-Nezhad A, Devanaboyina M, Crenshaw JS, Elrefaie A, Kolli S, Davis CN, Pradhan D, Yelamanchili SV, Pendyala G.
ai_summary: This preclinical study used an HIV-1 transgenic rat model to investigate how chronic HIV infection impairs male fertility. Testes of transgenic animals showed marked downregulation of sperm cation channels CatSper1-4 at both mRNA and protein levels, together with dysregulation of mitochondrial and inflammatory gene networks and structural disruption of the seminiferous tubules. Functional assays confirmed reduced sperm motility and abnormal nuclear morphology, while transcriptomic sequencing revealed novel gene signatures and disrupted pathways linked to testicular dysfunction. The authors conclude that HIV-1 transgene expression impairs spermatogenesis and sperm function through ion channel dysregulation and broader molecular pathway perturbation, offering clinically relevant insight into HIV-associated male infertility.

title: The genetic architecture of epilepsy across molecular mechanisms and clinical heterogeneity.
authors: Seyedtaghia MR, Babanzadeh J, Scala M, Perilli L, Striano P.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes the multilayered genetic architecture of epilepsy, which spans rare high-penetrance monogenic variants, common polygenic risk, brain-restricted somatic mosaicism, and gene-environment interactions. These diverse genetic substrates converge on shared biological pathways—ion channel function, synaptic vesicle cycling, mTOR signaling, glial and metabolic homeostasis, neuroinflammation, and circuit development—that destabilize excitation-inhibition balance, promote epileptogenesis, and drive pharmacoresistance. The authors connect these mechanisms to clinical heterogeneity (age of onset, seizure type, penetrance, pleiotropy, treatment response) and discuss translational implications for precision medicine, pharmacogenomics, and emerging therapies such as antisense oligonucleotides, gene regulation, and cell-based interventions.

title: Toward Next-Generation Teratology: Understanding Developmental Vulnerability Through Evolutionary and Comparative Genomics.
authors: Kon T.
ai_summary: This review argues that understanding why developmental systems are vulnerable to disruption requires an evolutionary perspective alongside mechanistic teratology, drawing on concepts such as evolutionary trade-offs, environmental mismatch, and developmental constraints. The authors examine three research areas across different evolutionary timescales—vertebrate appendage patterning and its origins, whole-genome duplication and ohnolog evolution as sources of developmental complexity and dosage sensitivity, and conserved chromosomal organization and transposable-element dynamics—and propose a "next-generation teratology" that integrates evolutionary and comparative genomics with conventional teratology to better understand, diagnose, and prevent congenital anomalies.

title: Organoids - the future of pre-clinical development of AAV gene therapy for CNS disorders.
authors: Kaiser VM, Gonzalez-Cordero A.
ai_summary: This review argues that human stem cell-derived brain and retinal organoids can improve pre-clinical development of AAV gene therapy for CNS disorders, including retinal diseases. Because species differences between humans and animal models limit accurate disease modelling and the prediction of vector safety and delivery efficacy, organoids offer a more faithful representation of human cellular microenvironments and niches, a point reinforced by the FDA's push for non-animal alternatives. The authors survey the advantages and limitations of these organoid models, focusing on their use in identifying novel AAV capsids and cell-specific promoters and on their role in recent pre-clinical AAV gene therapy studies.

title: Selective Brain-Penetrant TTBK1 Inhibitors Modulate TDP-43 Pathology and Rescue Cognitive Deficits in a Mouse Model of TDP-43 Proteinopathy.
authors: Sanchez-Santos C, Jimenez-Amor A, Martinez-Gonzalez L, Nozal V, Martin-Morales R, Aledavood E, Bausela D, Merrigan K, Diaz-Palacios K, Zhubi R, Knapp S, Garcia-Gonzalo FR, Rodriguez-Cueto C, Gil C, de Lago E, Martinez A.
ai_summary:
Gene: TTBK1
