Finding: Structure-guided optimization yielded selective, brain-penetrant TTBK1 inhibitors that spare TTBK2 and ciliogenesis, reduce TDP-43 phosphorylation in cells and FTD patient-derived models, and in an FTD-TDP mouse model restore cognitive deficits, provide frontal cortex neuroprotection, and reduce microglial activation.
Disease: TDP-43 proteinopathy (frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis)

title: Unveiling a small new glassfrog of the genus Vitreorana (Anura, Centrolenidae) from Cerrado, central Brazil.
authors: Vaz-Silva W, Pereira de Andrade S, Filho Rocha C, Victor EP, Brandão RA, Maciel NM.
ai_summary: A new glassfrog species, Vitreorana micaelae, is described from the Cerrado of central Brazil using morphological, molecular, and bioacoustic data. It is a small frog (21.7–26.1 mm) distinguished by white iridophores on the parietal and visceral peritonea, a rounded snout in dorsal view, cloacal ornamentation, and an advertisement call comprising two call types. It is only the second glassfrog known to be endemic to the Cerrado, where it inhabits humid gallery forests. Genetic divergence (16S rRNA) among sampled Vitreorana species ranged from 3.5% to 9.6%, with the new species showing the least divergence from V. parvula.

title: Hexatoma (Eriocera) guangxiensis sp. nov., a new crane fly in the plumbicincta species group (Diptera, Limoniidae) from China.
authors: Zhang B, Yan J, Ning Y, Liu P, Yan M, Liu Q, Yang D.
ai_summary: This taxonomic study treats the crane fly species group Hexatoma (Eriocera) plumbicincta, a small lineage previously represented in China by only two species. The authors redescribe H. (E.) chrysomela and report it as a new record for Guizhou, Hunan, and Guangxi in China, and describe and illustrate a new species, H. (E.) guangxiensis sp. nov., from Guangxi and Yunnan. A key to the Chinese species of the plumbicincta group is provided.

title: Non-Random Association of Ultraconserved Genomic Elements (UCE) with Human Genes.
authors: Fedorova L, Orlov YL, Mulyar OA, Fedorov A.
ai_summary: Ultraconserved elements (UCEs) are non-randomly distributed across the human genome: about 40% cluster within 20 kb intervals, and they are strongly enriched near non-KRAB transcription factor genes (sevenfold) while depleted near KRAB zinc-finger genes (tenfold). UCE-rich genes are mainly master developmental regulators involved in chromatin remodeling, RNA processing, and embryonic neurogenesis, whereas UCE-poor genes encode membrane proteins, ion channels, and synaptic components of mature neurons. UCEs also show roughly fourfold positional enrichment near the 3' ends of protein-coding genes, a pattern absent in lncRNAs, which are only modestly enriched overall except for a small subset carrying many UCEs. The authors conclude that UCEs preferentially associate with developmental regulators rather than downstream neuronal effector genes.

title: Critical ischemia duration thresholds in the rat middle cerebral artery occlusion model: Implications for drug screening.
authors: Puente-Sanz A, Herrero-González A, Pérez-Rodríguez D, Gonzalo-Orden JM, Letek M, Anuncibay-Soto B, Fernández-López A.

title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
authors: Zhang B, Zheng S, Guo L, Zhao H.
ai_summary: This review examines how bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have been used to dissect the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder, perinatal depression, perimenopausal depression, and post-stroke depression. Across subtypes, immune-inflammatory activation, impaired synaptic plasticity, and mitochondrial energy metabolism dysfunction emerge as shared core mechanisms, while each subtype also shows distinct transcriptomic features—MDD displays sexual dimorphism and immunophenotypic characteristics, PND and PMD involve neuroendocrine-immune network imbalances driven by hormonal fluctuations, and PSD is marked by innate immune responses interacting with impaired autophagy flux. The authors note persistent challenges including limited sample sources, high data heterogeneity, and poor clinical translation, and recommend single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics integration, and cross-species comparisons to advance precision diagnosis and personalized treatment.

title: Inflammation in atherosclerosis: Drivers, mechanisms and therapies.
authors: Su Z, Xu S.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence repositioning atherosclerosis as an inflammation-driven disease rather than purely lipid-driven. Multiple cell types (endothelial cells, macrophages, other immune cells) form a chronic inflammatory microenvironment within lesions, driven by lifestyle factors, smoking, and metabolic disorders such as hyperlipidemia and hyperglycemia. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein outperforms LDL-cholesterol in predicting future cardiovascular risk, and combining lipid-lowering with anti-inflammatory therapy reduces event recurrence, though cholesterol-independent immunosuppressive strategies carry infection risks. The authors highlight emerging tools and targets—high-throughput screening, iPSC-derived vascular organoids, organ interaction networks, trained immunity, and enhancement of intrinsic resilience mechanisms—as promising avenues for reducing residual cardiovascular risk in the post-statin era.

title: Retinal proteomics in neurodegeneration: Insights into ocular and brain disorders.
authors: Mirshahvaladi S, Gaire BP, Kashani SA, Guha A, Koronyo Y, Fuchs DT, You Y, Black KL, Paulo JA, Graham SL, Gupta V, Mirzaei M, Koronyo-Hamaoui M.
ai_summary: This review discusses how mass spectrometry-based retinal proteomics can reveal therapeutic targets and noninvasive biomarkers for neurodegenerative and ocular diseases, including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, retinitis pigmentosa, Alzheimer's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Parkinson's disease. Recent innovations—particularly AI-driven computational pipelines such as GPU-accelerated deep learning—are overcoming prior limitations of small sample size and limited protein coverage, enabling high-resolution identification of protein signatures in large multi-omics datasets and supporting earlier, more sensitive and specific biomarker discovery. Complementary and alternative technologies further expand this potential.

title: The cost of persistent alarm: temporal transcriptional reprogramming of macrophages from acute activation to chronic immune suppression by day 11.
authors: Mazzio EA, Barnes AS, Badisa RB, Darling-Reed SF, Soliman KFA.
ai_summary: This study developed an in vitro model of sustained TLR4 activation in macrophages, tracking the transition from resting baseline through acute activation (24 h) to a chronic tolerant state (days 7–11) under continuous media exchange that eliminated autocrine and toxic interference. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, validated by RT-PCR and immunoblots, showed that the chronic state is not passive exhaustion or simple tolerance but an active, coordinated negative-feedback program across an eight-phase trajectory. By days 7–11, macrophages adopted a TAM-like signature with upregulated immune checkpoints (PD-L1/MSN, TIM-3, SPP1, CD73, CD44, LILRs) and suppressive networks (SOCS/JAK/STAT, IL-10, CCL2/7/12, CXCL2), downregulated MHC-I antigen-presentation genes, and profound loss of interferon-stimulated genes (IFIT family, Ly6e, Irf7, Rsad2/Viperin, Oas family), crippling antiviral and antitumor surveillance. The chronic stage also featured degradative proteases, adhesion molecules, iron-storage and lipid-handling transcripts, Nos2/Cox2 upregulation with mitochondrial OXPHOS collapse, and a striking sustained surge in small proline-rich proteins (Sprr2b–2k). The authors propose this as a reproducible model for studying how chronic inflammation drives immune suppression and impairs host defense against viral and tumor cells.

title: Exploring the Role of Long Non-Coding RNAs in Mediating Cisplatin Resistance in Glioma/Glioblastoma Cells.
authors: Sahrai H, Mosaddeghi-Heris R, Forghani N, Norouzi A, Zare S, Aghazadeh H, Bagheri K, Kocsis R, Ahmed F, Taheri N, Uddin S, Farzaneh M.
ai_summary: This review examines how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) contribute to cisplatin resistance in malignant glioma/glioblastoma. It highlights several implicated lncRNAs—DANCR, HOXD-AS1, MEG3, MALAT1, and HOTAIR—with DANCR specifically reported to promote resistance by suppressing apoptosis and activating pro-survival signaling. The authors describe resistance mechanisms including altered drug transport, DNA damage repair, apoptosis evasion, cancer stem-cell maintenance, and adaptive signaling, while noting limitations, clinical translation challenges, and evidence gaps. They conclude that clarifying lncRNA-mediated resistance could reveal new therapeutic targets for overcoming cisplatin resistance in these tumors.

title: Interdependent roles of PKM2 in photoreceptors and RPE: implications for retinal degeneration.
authors: Rajala A, Rajala R, Trevino LJ, Black TM, Moiseyev G, Kinter M, Rajala RVS.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKM2
Finding: PKM2 is enriched in photoreceptors and required in both photoreceptors and the RPE to sustain glycolysis, ATP production, and metabolic balance; its loss causes cellular disorganization and degeneration, reduces RPE65 and 11-cis-retinal regeneration, disrupts the cone opsin gradient, and accelerates retinal degeneration in Abca4 mutant mice.
Disease: Retinal degeneration (including age-related macular degeneration)

title: Plasmodium falciparum PfMyoF contains a Rab-like tail domain and associates with perinuclear membrane trafficking proteins.
authors: Holmes AJ, Ilani P, Batters C, Kemp A, Aniweh Y, Amenga-Etego LN, Awandare GA, Rayner JC, Buss F.
ai_summary:
Gene: PfMyoF
Finding: PfMyoF is a plus-end-directed, processive class XXII myosin with a unique tail containing predicted WD40 and Rab-like domains, interacts with trafficking proteins including PfRab18, localizes to a perinuclear membrane compartment, and is required for normal asexual growth.
Disease: Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum blood-stage infection)

title: Fetal Interrupted Aortic Arch and Unilateral Duplex Kidney Identified by Second Trimester Ultrasound Prompting Genetic Diagnosis of Neonatal Sclerosing Cholangitis.
authors: Huang DP, Gu CM, Yu QX, Jiang F, Li DZ.

title: Full-Field Stimulus Threshold: A Key Functional Outcome Measure in Retinal Diseases and Clinical Trials.
authors: Macha N, Yu M.
ai_summary: Full-field stimulus threshold (FST) testing is a psychophysical method for assessing global retinal function that is especially useful in severe visual impairment, where conventional perimetry is unreliable. This review covers its development, protocols, and applications in retinal disease, focusing on inherited retinal dystrophies such as Leber congenital amaurosis and retinitis pigmentosa. Because it is fixation-independent and can detect residual visual function, FST has become a key functional outcome measure in clinical trials, particularly for novel gene therapies, aiding assessment of disease progression and treatment efficacy. Standardization and test variability remain challenges, and ongoing efforts aim to optimize FST protocols and establish it as a standardized clinical and research metric.

title: Long-read sequencing reveals a hidden Alu-mediated splice defect in CPLANE1, causing orofaciodigital syndrome type VI.
authors: Pozojevic J, Sczakiel HL, Balachandran S, Kruse N, Mensah MA, Hülsemann W, Händler K, Spielmann M.
journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
ai_summary:
Gene: CPLANE1
Finding: Long-read sequencing uncovered two biallelic splice-site variants — c.8633-4_8633-3del and an Alu element insertion near an exon-intron boundary — each causing exon skipping and reduced total CPLANE1 mRNA in patient fibroblasts, allowing reclassification of the deletion variant from VUS to likely pathogenic.
Disease: Orofaciodigital syndrome type VI (OFD VI)

title: Inherited Retinal Dystrophies in the Differential Diagnosis of Uveitis: Clinical Clues from a Case.
authors: Yabanoğlu D, Özyol P, Şahlı E, Yalçındağ N.

title: A Case of Short-Rib Thoracic Dysplasia: Diagnostic Clues in Early Pregnancy and Genetic Analysis.
authors: Li C, Kang X, Tao J, Yang X, Liu C, Song X, Lin X.
ai_summary:
Gene: DYNC2H1
Finding: In a fetus with ultrasound findings suggestive of short-rib thoracic dysplasia at 13 weeks of gestation, prenatal genetic testing identified a pathogenic DYNC2H1 variant, and post-abortion examination with X-ray confirmed the diagnosis.
Disease: Short-rib thoracic dysplasia 3 (SRTD3; OMIM #613091)

title: Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Hippocampal Neuroplasticity as an Indicator of Stress Responsiveness in Laying Hens (Gallus gallus domesticus).
authors: Neuert L, Osborne V, Armstrong EA, Pértille F, Bosagna CG, Boswell T, Smulders TV, Baes CF, Makanjuola BO.
ai_summary: This genome-wide association study investigated the genetic basis of hippocampal neuroplasticity, measured as doublecortin-positive (DCX+) neuron density, as a biomarker of stress responsiveness in laying hens. Genotyping by sequencing of 42 hens yielded over 200,000 SNPs, and immunostaining quantified plastic neuron density in hippocampal tissue. The analysis identified 19 genomic regions across eight chromosomes in the top 1% of windows explaining the greatest genetic variance, containing 39 annotated genes within ±100 kb, several involved in cellular regulation and genetic information processing. The authors highlight PIK3R6, VPS37D, STX1A, BAZ1B, HGH1, MAF1, MAPK15, and PIT54 as positional candidate genes potentially underlying individual variation in stress responsiveness, offering preliminary insight into the genetic architecture of this trait with possible implications for breeding strategies to improve poultry welfare.

title: Defining a Novel RPGR Phenotype of Sector Retinitis Pigmentosa With Cone Dystrophy.
authors: Abdalla Elsayed MEA, Mahroo OA, Webster A, Tsang SH, Marques JP, Traboulsi E, Tan TE, Boon CJF, de la Camara CM, Fenner BJ, Barone V, Dollfus H, MacLaren RE.
ai_summary:
Gene: RPGR
Finding: Fourteen patients with ORF15 mutations in a defined transitional zone showed a mixed phenotype of cone dystrophy plus bilateral, symmetrical sectoral rod-cone atrophy along the inferior vascular arcades; all mutations were predicted to cause truncated, loss-of-function proteins, some also disrupting splicing regulatory elements.
Disease: Sector retinitis pigmentosa with cone dystrophy

title: Genetic Ablation and Multi-Omics Profiling Reveal CEP55 as a Key Driver of Tumorigenesis in Diverse Cancer Models.
authors: Rashidieh B, Yang Y, Bain AL, Theron P, Vosloo C, Keshvari S, Ahangar P, Bowden B, Tria SM, Wang BB, Isenmann S, van Holthe NJW, Xiong Z, Vu H, Sharma S, Sengal A, Lopez JA, Finnie J, Papa A, Duijf PHG, Nguyen Q, Apaja PM, Khanna KK.
ai_summary:
Gene: CEP55
Finding: Inducible Cep55 knockout is tolerated in adult tissues but delays tumor onset and progression in E1A/Ras-driven and PTEN-deficient cancer models, with multi-omics revealing that CEP55 coordinates ECM remodeling, integrin/adhesion signaling, AKT/ERK pathways, stress responses, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (reduced tumor-supportive macrophage polarization, enhanced antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses).
Disease: Cancer (E1A/Ras-driven and PTEN-deficient tumor models)

title: A role for the Stentor syntaxin protein in post-wound cell survival.
authors: Nadkarni AV, Diaz U, Rodriguez R, Zhang KS, Tang SKY, Marshall WF.
ai_summary:
Gene: syntaxin
Finding: RNAi knockdown of a Stentor syntaxin gene reduced post-bisection survival to ~37% versus ~98% in controls, with knockdown cells showing increased vacuolation, hypersensitivity to hypoosmotic shock, and partial rescue of survival when wounded in 75 mM sorbitol, indicating a defect in membrane fusion and osmotic homeostasis.
Disease: post-wound cell survival (wound repair failure in Stentor coeruleus)

title: Emerging genes implicated in human congenital heart disease: a 2023-2025 scoping review.
authors: Israel S, Morton SU.
ai_summary: This scoping review screened 2,834 articles published between 2023 and 2025 and identified 391 human studies reporting monogenic variants in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD), yielding 912 unique candidate CHD-associated genes. Frequently reported genes included PTPN11, NOTCH1, GATA4, JAG1, MYH6, GATA6, and LZTR1, and the implicated genes spanned all major stages of cardiogenesis, from developmental priming and cardiac progenitor specification through left-right axis formation, neural crest migration, outflow tract development, septation, and postnatal structural remodeling. The literature increasingly points to ciliary dysfunction, transcriptional regulation, ribosomal biology, and multigenic inheritance as contributing mechanisms, alongside emerging methods such as stem cell-derived cardiac models, machine learning-based gene prioritization, and epigenetic analyses. The authors conclude that the candidate gene catalog for CHD has expanded substantially, underscoring the biologic complexity of cardiac morphogenesis and the need to integrate genomic, developmental, and functional approaches to improve mechanistic understanding, genetic counseling, and precision medicine.

title: Modeling Inherited Disorders of Post-Lanosterol Cholesterol Biosynthesis: From Animal Models to Patient-Derived Stem Cells.
authors: Akhmetzyanova E, Nasybullina E, Rizvanov A, Mukhamedshina Y.
ai_summary: This review surveys experimental models for inherited post-lanosterol cholesterol biosynthesis disorders, a group that includes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, desmosterolosis, lathosterolosis, and CHILD syndrome. It describes how these conditions arise from both cholesterol insufficiency and toxicity of accumulated sterol intermediates, which drive oxidative stress, disrupted developmental signaling, membrane dysfunction, and impaired neurodevelopment. The authors compare genetically engineered animal models, patient-derived fibroblasts, immortalized and CRISPR/Cas9-edited cell lines, and induced pluripotent stem cell systems, with particular focus on Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, and discuss each platform's strengths and limitations for dissecting sterol metabolism and cell-type-specific disease mechanisms. They conclude by outlining future directions, including patient-specific iPSC models, genome editing, and next-generation multicellular systems, as a framework for selecting models and developing mechanism-based therapies.

title: DCDC2C Protein Expression in Human Spermatozoa: A Potential Molecular Marker for Asthenozoospermia.
authors: Adli O, Rachid E, Kbirou A, Rochdi C, Filali M, Louanjli N, Assou S, Aboutaieb R.
ai_summary:
Gene: DCDC2C
Finding: DCDC2C-positive spermatozoa were significantly more frequent in normozoospermic men (78.93 ± 1.67%) than in asthenozoospermic men (17.27 ± 2.23%), with reduced distal flagellar DCDC2C immunoreactivity associated with impaired sperm motility.
Disease: Asthenozoospermia

title: Pathways to enhancing prenatal diagnosis of skeletal dysplasias.
authors: Wang MJ, Jacobsen C, Arnold J, Wapner RJ, Krakow D.
ai_summary: This review addresses the challenges of prenatally diagnosing skeletal dysplasias, a heterogeneous group of Mendelian musculoskeletal disorders ranging from mild short stature to severe perinatal morbidity. Because ultrasound lacks the precision of postnatal radiographs and these conditions show marked allelic and phenotypic heterogeneity, historical sonographic phenotyping was genotype-nonspecific and counseling centered mainly on predicting perinatal lethality. Recent gains in genomic medicine and prenatal ultrasound resolution now permit more precise diagnosis and individualized counseling. The authors provide a comprehensive overview of best practices for prenatal ultrasonography and molecular work-up and propose a standardized, evidence-based framework for evaluation.

title: Loss of ABCA4 from photoreceptor discs is associated with glial transcriptomic changes in retinal organoids.
authors: Valenzano R, McDonald A, Gallego C, Andriessen CA, Moustakas I, Mulder AA, Mikkers HMM, Koning RI, Mei H, Wijnholds J.
ai_summary:
Gene: ABCA4
Finding: In human iPSC-derived retinal organoids carrying an ABCA4 exon-24 premature stop codon, ABCA4 protein was absent from mutant photoreceptor outer segment discs with no major transcriptional changes in rods and cones, but Müller glial cells and astrocytes showed disrupted neuronal development, glial microenvironment, intercellular communication, and programmed cell death pathways.
Disease: Stargardt disease (STGD1)

title: Inflamed Yet Immune-Evasive? A Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis Identifies Conserved Inflammatory, Developmental, and Neuronal Signatures Associated with Polyploid Giant Cancer Cells.
authors: Anatskaya OV, Vinogradov AE.
ai_summary: A meta-analysis of eight transcriptomic datasets from prostate, ovarian, and breast cancer models shows that polyploid giant cancer cells (PGCCs) share a conserved core program combining pro-inflammatory cytokine/chemokine signaling with immune evasion (PD-L1-associated and virus-like escape programs), alongside embryonic, reproductive, senescence, dormancy, and apoptosis-resistance signatures. PGCCs also activate neuronal differentiation and neurodegeneration pathways, including axon guidance, neurogenesis, and calcium signaling, which may reinforce immune privilege and long-term survival. The authors propose PGCCs represent an immune-adaptive polyploid survival state and highlight calcium signaling, neuronal mimicry, and checkpoint pathways as potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.

title: Omics signature of new-onset mild cognitive impairment and dementia in a population-based study.
authors: Lu Y, Tan CTY, Gwee X, Larbi A, Ng TP.
ai_summary: A population-based longitudinal study (Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Studies Wave 2) profiled plasma proteomics and metabolomics in participants followed 3–5 years for new-onset mild cognitive impairment and dementia. Of 1,892 assayed molecules, 463 were significantly associated with prevalent MCI/dementia at baseline. A predictive model for incident MCI and dementia retained 10 variables (ZSCAN18, PRKD3, SPANXN4, DDX43, saturated fatty acids, PPP3CA, NFATC4, IL-8, PAK6, PDGFB), implicating immune dysfunction and inflammation, protein coding, lipid metabolism, DNA-binding transcription factor activity, and nervous system development. The authors propose this circulating omics signature may improve diagnostic accuracy for new-onset MCI and dementia.

title: CDK10 loss primes tumor cells for transcriptional vulnerability and sensitizes to CDK12/13 inhibition.
authors: Islam S, Tarumoto Y, Takano M, Sugino S, Nishibuchi G, Mizutani A, Yamakawa H, Morishita D, Yusa K.
ai_summary:
Gene: CDK10
Finding: CDK10 loss, identified by genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening and validated in cell lines and xenografts, enhances sensitivity to CDK12/13 inhibition by prolonging transcriptional suppression and delaying RNA polymerase II re-engagement at sensitive gene loci, thereby increasing apoptosis and antitumor effects.
Disease: Breast and ovarian cancer

title: Diversity of molecular karyotypes of 234 pediatric patients with autism spectrum disorder in chromosomal microarray analysis.
authors: Ręka G, Wojciechowska K, Styka B, Janiszewska M, Lejman M.
ai_summary:
Gene: OTUD7A, CHRNA7
Finding: Chromosomal microarray analysis of 234 children with ASD found a diagnostic yield of 8.55% for pathogenic/likely pathogenic CNVs, with recurrent 15q13.3 duplications (OTUD7A, CHRNA7) observed four times and numerous other recurrent duplications and deletions at known ASD-associated loci.
Disease: Autism spectrum disorder

title: Carrier screening in the reproductive setting-Are there medical implications for the heterozygote?-A guide for clinicians.
authors: Rosenfeld EB, Kasatkin N, Yu BL, Velinov M, Brandt JS, Ashkinadze E.
ai_summary: This review challenges the traditional assumption that carriers of autosomal recessive conditions are asymptomatic, noting that recent evidence shows clinical implications in the heterozygous state—particularly in pregnancy. The authors examined three large panethnic commercial carrier screening panels covering 818 genes and found that 112 (13.7%) have definite or strong implications in carriers, with another 100 (12.2%) showing moderate or limited evidence; 19 genes may specifically affect pregnancy management. Prior studies cited indicate 9% of patients undergoing large panels carry a condition with heterozygous clinical implications, and an estimated 2.5% of women are heterozygous for a condition affecting their pregnancy management. The authors conclude that obstetric clinicians interpreting carrier screens must recognize these implications and incorporate them into counseling and management to improve outcomes.

title: A Rare De Novo Missense Mutation in IFT122 Confers a Genetic Susceptibility Factor of Idiopathic Pediatric Uveitis Via Trio-based Whole-Exome Sequencing.
authors: Zhou Q, Huang J, Wang Y, Li X, Liu X, Dai L, Li H, Wang Q, Liu J, Su G, Zhang W, Deng Y, Cao Q, Lai Y, Luo X, Huang C, Chen L, Hou S, Yang P.
ai_summary:
Gene: IFT122
Finding: A rare de novo missense mutation (A773E) identified by trio-based whole-exome sequencing enhanced interaction with IFT43, upregulated calcium channels, and activated the MEK/ERK/FRA1 axis, increasing inflammatory factor secretion and barrier damage in vivo and in vitro.
Disease: Idiopathic pediatric uveitis

title: Convergent mechanisms in Wnt and Hedgehog signaling.
authors: Myers BR, Zalatan JG, Virshup DM.
ai_summary: This review highlights that the Wnt and Hedgehog signaling pathways, despite being distinct cascades implicated in numerous diseases, share a core regulatory mechanism: tethered pseudosubstrate inhibition of kinases that controls intracellular signal transmission. The authors argue that this and other shared features—lipidated ligands, specialized ligand delivery systems, atypical G protein-coupled receptors, and phosphorylation-dependent inhibition of transcriptional effectors—indicate the two pathways converged on a common regulatory logic, allowing them to produce specific functional outputs while reusing molecules common to many other cascades. This signaling mode may extend to other pathways in which cell-surface receptors directly regulate kinase activity.

title: Beyond the Classics: The Synergy of AI and Genomics Reveals an Expanded Repertoire of Pigmentation Genes.
authors: Ahi EP, Karagic N.
journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part B, Molecular and developmental evolution
ai_summary: This review argues that combining AI-driven phenotyping (deep learning, self-supervised modeling, pattern recognition) with genomic mapping methods such as GWAS, QTL mapping, and structural variant analysis has expanded the known repertoire of pigmentation genes beyond the classical melanin-production and pigment-cell-differentiation loci. Across diverse animal taxa, these integrated approaches have uncovered non-classical regulators involved in membrane trafficking, intracellular signaling, structural organization, and non-coding regulation. The authors propose the term "AI-pigmentomics" for this integration of AI phenotyping with genomic mapping, positioning it within the broader AI-omics trend. Rather than replacing the classical pigmentation paradigm, these findings extend it and offer a framework for studying coloration in both model and non-model species.

title: Mechanical control in dental and jaw morphogenesis and remodeling.
authors: Yang X, Zhang X, Gao Q, Wang S, Wu X.
ai_summary: This review examines how mechanical forces shape the development and remodeling of teeth and jaw bones. It describes the sources and spatiotemporal distribution of mechanical stress during dentofacial development, then details the molecular mechanisms by which mechanical signals—converted to biochemical cues through cellular mechanotransduction—regulate proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis during crown formation, root morphogenesis, tooth eruption and replacement, and maxillomandibular bone development and remodeling. The authors also identify current research gaps and propose future directions for studying mechanical regulation of dentofacial development.

title: Computational analysis of treatment resistant cancer cells.
authors: Matov A.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary:
Gene: AR
Finding: Computational live-cell analysis of microtubule dynamics in prostate cancer cells suggests that androgen receptor content and specific AR splice variants influence sensitivity or resistance to different taxanes, which could guide selection of the most effective drug.
Disease: Prostate cancer

title: Gut microbiota-regulated cell death: a review on pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and related mechanisms.
authors: Shen Y, Zhou Y, Yuan Y, Chen W, Liang M, Liu X, Lu Y, Zheng Q.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes how the gut microbiota regulates regulated cell death (RCD), focusing on pyroptosis and ferroptosis, which are implicated in immune regulation, metabolic homeostasis, and disease progression. The authors describe how microbial metabolites, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, and immune-cell polarization mediate these effects across intestinal, metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative disorders. Noting that existing evidence is fragmented and often fails to distinguish direct microbial regulation from indirect associations driven by barrier dysfunction, inflammation, or metabolic remodeling, they propose grading evidence at four levels—from direct regulation of the death machinery to purely observational association—and use this framework to assess therapeutic strategies and identify evidence gaps for future mechanistic and translational work.

title: RFX3 Pathogenic Variants as a Rare Cause of Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
authors: Ceraolo G, Spoto G, Trivisano M, Federico C, Vinci M, Calì F, Treccarichi S, Musumeci A, Di Rosa G, Specchio N, Nicotera AG.
ai_summary:
Gene: RFX3
Finding: A de novo heterozygous ~147 kb microdeletion at 9p24.2 involving the initial exons of RFX3 was identified in a patient with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome who achieved complete remission on vigabatrin and ACTH but later showed global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and facial dysmorphisms.
Disease: Infantile epileptic spasms syndrome with neurodevelopmental disorder

title: Genomic characterization of aggressiveness in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors.
authors: Benanteur N, Villa C, Bioletto F, Birtolo MF, De Murat D, Masliah-Planchon J, Gravrand V, Lebib I, Benkhellat M, Boezennec R, Allassonnière S, Letourneur F, Martin Y, Bonnet Serrano F, Jacob J, Calugaru V, Barat M, Dohan A, Arrondeau J, Huillard O, Raffin-Sanson ML, Emile JF, Raverot G, Libé R, Guignat L, Garcia C, Groussin L, Bertagna X, Gaillard S, Bertherat J, Jouinot A, Baussart B, Assié G.
ai_summary:
Gene: LRP1B
Finding: LRP1B alterations, along with TP53 and CDKN2A alterations, were associated with aggressive features in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, whereas USP8 and GNAS alterations were not; a common aggressiveness signature combining a proliferative transcriptome and DNA hypermethylation was identified within each lineage.
Disease: Aggressive pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs)

title: Neurotoxic mechanisms of cadmium in neurodegenerative diseases.
authors: Zhang Z, Lu Y, Yang J, Li M, Yang M, Xu Y, Ullah MS, Wan Q, Bao B, Yu W, Liu X.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: Cadmium neurotoxicity is driven primarily by oxidative stress, which triggers ferroptosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium dyshomeostasis, and chronic neuroinflammation. The review details disease-specific effects: in Alzheimer's disease, Cd promotes amyloid-β deposition and tau hyperphosphorylation; in Parkinson's disease, it disrupts gut-liver-brain metabolic homeostasis and drives α-synuclein aggregation; and in the ALS-FTD spectrum, it contributes to TDP-43 proteinopathy and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Proposed interventions include metal chelation, restoration of autophagic flux, modulation of the neuroimmune microenvironment, and enhanced neuronal repair, though translating in vitro and organoid findings to real-world chronic exposure remains challenging.

title: Ferroptosis in bovine mastitis: multidimensional mechanisms, stratified assessment, and intervention prospects.
authors: Cheng L, Song G.
ai_summary:
Gene: GPX4
Finding: Restriction of the cysteine-GSH-GPX4 axis, together with increased oxidative load, altered iron flux, and membrane-lipid remodeling, can lower the ferroptotic threshold of mammary epithelial cells in the mastitic microenvironment, though direct in vivo causal evidence in bovine mastitis remains limited.
Disease: Bovine mastitis

title: Programmed cell death in metabolic syndrome: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies (Review).
authors: Zhong J, Zhang M, Zheng Y, Gong C, Deng Y, Sun L, Zhou D, Zhou Q, Chen Q.
ai_summary: This review examines how programmed cell death (PCD) drives the pathogenesis of metabolic syndrome (MetS), a condition marked by insulin resistance, central obesity, hyperglycemia, hypertension and dyslipidemia that raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atherosclerosis. It surveys established and emerging PCD forms — apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, ferroptosis, necroptosis, PANoptosis and disulfidptosis — focusing on their molecular mechanisms, tissue-specific roles, regulatory crosstalk and therapeutic potential. The authors argue that because current treatments (caloric restriction, exercise, and drugs targeting lipids, blood pressure and glucose) remain suboptimal, intervening in PCD networks offers a promising basis for new therapies to prevent and treat MetS and its complications.

title: Exploring pathogenetic mechanisms in subglottic stenosis: A narrative review toward an integrated molecular classification.
authors: Martella S, Cusumano G, Bondì G, La Via L, Fruciano M, Muscato G, Vancheri C, Terminella A.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current understanding of subglottic stenosis (SGS), a chronic fibroinflammatory airway narrowing with heterogeneous causes—iatrogenic/traumatic, autoimmune (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis), post-viral (including COVID-19-related COATS), and idiopathic (iSGS, predominantly affecting adult Caucasian women). Despite this etiologic diversity, all forms converge on a shared pathogenetic core of epithelial damage, immune activation, chronic inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. The key argument is that recent molecular studies reveal distinct biological signatures across SGS variants, implying the existence of molecular subtypes with differing clinical trajectories. The authors therefore advocate moving toward a biomarker-based molecular classification to enable precision medicine, with future treatment prospects including targeted immunotherapies (such as IL-17A/IL-23 inhibitors), anti-fibrotic agents, and epithelial regeneration strategies to complement existing surgical approaches and improve long-term prognosis.

title: On the Edge of Benefit and Harm: Reactive Oxygen Species in Cancer.
authors: Nikiforova AB.
ai_summary: This review examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in cancer, where physiological ROS levels support signaling, proliferation, and immune responses, while excessive ROS drives DNA damage, genomic instability, metabolic reprogramming, and tumor microenvironment remodeling that fuel initiation, progression, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Because many cancer cells already operate near their oxidative stress threshold, pushing ROS higher can trigger apoptosis, ferroptosis, and immunogenic cell death. The authors survey intracellular and microenvironmental ROS sources, redox signaling in malignant transformation, and antioxidant buffering systems, then review therapeutic strategies spanning both ROS suppression and ROS amplification—including redox-modulating small molecules, radiotherapy, photodynamic and sonodynamic therapy, catalytic nanomaterials, and ROS-responsive prodrugs and delivery systems. They emphasize context-dependent ROS effects, the antioxidant paradox, tumor heterogeneity, hypoxia, off-target toxicity, and the need for reliable redox biomarkers, concluding that exploiting tumor-specific redox vulnerabilities is key to effective ROS-oriented cancer therapy.

title: Research progress and applications of functional hydrogels in nasal wound healing.
authors: Wang C, Wang Z, Gan S, He B, Tong Y, Zhu Y, Ye D.
ai_summary: This review examines functional hydrogels as next-generation nasal wound dressings, motivated by the nasal cavity's demanding physicochemical environment (mildly acidic pH ~6.3–6.9, shear-thinning mucus, continuous mucociliary clearance, and lysozyme-dominated enzymatic activity) that conventional packing materials such as Vaseline gauze and polyvinyl alcohol sponges fail to meet due to poor biocompatibility, rigidity, and traumatic removal. It classifies hydrogels by polymer backbone (natural polysaccharides/proteins versus synthetic polymers) and crosslinking chemistry (dynamic covalent bonds including Schiff base, disulfide, and boronic ester, versus supramolecular host-guest and hydrogen bonding), and evaluates reaction pathways, degradation kinetics, and mechanical matching to nasal mucosa. Representative systems highlighted include the RADA16 self-assembling peptide hydrogel, which reduced postoperative adhesion by 91–100% versus gelatin-thrombin and bioresorbable controls in randomized trials; TSPBA/PVA ROS-responsive hydrogels that scavenge H₂O₂ via boronic ester cleavage and extend mucosal retention to 24 hours; and pNIPAAm-based thermoresponsive systems with an LCST near 32 °C relevant to the 30–34 °C nasal temperature range. The review also discusses cell-material interactions driving macrophage M1→M2 polarization, epithelial and fibroblast behavior, and ciliary function, and addresses ongoing clinical trials (NCT04970966, NCT05898074) alongside translational barriers including sterilization, long-term in vivo safety, and standardized large-scale production.

title: Narrative review-the emerging role, functions, and mechanisms of UFMylation in cancers.
authors: Fang L, Yang F.
ai_summary: UFMylation is a newly identified post-translational modification whose defects (genetic variants, abnormal expression, somatic copy number alterations) have been implicated in tumorigenesis, cancer progression, and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recently identified UFMylation substrates, discusses reported molecular mechanisms by which UFMylation influences tumorigenesis and cancer treatment responses and resistance, examines its roles across various cancers (mainly solid tumors), and considers possible crosstalk between UFMylation and ubiquitination. The authors conclude that UFMylation may serve as a biomarker for diagnosis and treatment-response assessment and as a potential therapeutic target in cancer therapy.

title: Lens aging and disease: Molecular mechanisms, functional consequences, and pharmacological implications.
authors: Fan X, Monnier VM.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
ai_summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in lens aging biology to explain how age-related cataract (ARC) develops. Because lens core fiber cells, crystallins, and lipids persist for decades without turnover, they accumulate oxidative and biochemical damage—crystallin oxidation, truncation, deamidation, racemization, glycation, and crosslinking—alongside membrane remodeling and nuclear stiffening, progressively eroding transparency and refractive precision. Declining glutathione synthesis and redox-repair capacity amplifies this damage, and emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis, rather than apoptosis, as the dominant regulated cell-death pathway threatening lens epithelial cell survival. ARC also has a complex polygenic architecture, with modifier genes affecting cytoskeletal resilience, protein stability, ion transport, and metabolic signaling, while environmental exposures such as UV radiation, smoking, heat stress, and air pollution interact with these pathways to accelerate opacity. The authors propose a cohesive framework linking these mechanisms and outline emerging therapies targeting redox buffering, crystallin stability, epithelial survival, and lens biomechanics.

title: Structural dynamics of kappa opioid receptor interactions with β-arrestin 1.
authors: Han J, Fine EJ, Jiang Q, Zhuang Y, Suomivuori CM, Chen ZW, Denn E, Whiddon K, Li K, Evers AS, Fuller J, Carter J, Fay JF, Chen M, Dror RO, Che T.
ai_summary: The study reports the 2.60 Å cryo-EM structure of the kappa opioid receptor (KOR) bound to β-arrestin1, revealing multiple phosphorylation sites and a phospholipid-binding site that enhances arrestin recruitment. The complex shows a core interaction distinct from other GPCR–β-arrestin1 complexes, and comparisons with KOR–Nb39 and KOR–Gi1 structures identify differences in the orthosteric pocket and transducer interface that influence signaling bias. 3D variation analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further reveal conformational dynamics in both receptor and β-arrestin1, suggesting an allosteric pathway for arrestin entry and exit.

title: Natural Products Targeting Airway Inflammation and Mucus Hypersecretion: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential for Respiratory Health.
authors: Lee SG, Lee JH, Kang H.
ai_summary: This review examines natural products as multitarget therapies for chronic respiratory diseases marked by airway inflammation and mucus hypersecretion. Marine-derived compounds and plant phytochemicals act on signaling pathways including NF-κB, MAPKs, PI3K/Akt, JAK/STAT, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and Nrf2, suppressing inflammation, oxidative stress, goblet cell differentiation, and MUC5AC overexpression. Nanoformulation, pulmonary drug delivery, multi-omics, AI-assisted drug discovery, and network pharmacology are expected to speed clinical translation, positioning natural products as candidates for functional foods, nutraceuticals, and novel therapies.

title: Vitamins as modulators of neonatal intestinal injury.
authors: Singh DK, Yamaguchi Y, Saito C, Cassidy OG, Nishiyama K, Huang L.
ai_summary: This review examines how vitamins modulate the pathophysiology of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in premature infants, a severe intestinal disease with 15-45% mortality. It describes multiple mechanistic roles: vitamins A and D promote epithelial barrier maturation and immune homeostasis by limiting excessive TLR4 activation; vitamins E and C reduce oxidative stress while supporting regulatory T-cell function and IgA-mediated mucosal immunity; vitamin K supports immune regulation and hemostasis via protein S-dependent anticoagulant activity and suppression of TLR-mediated inflammation, reducing microvascular injury; and folate attenuates lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation and may bolster defenses against Gram-negative bacteria. Collectively, these vitamins target TLR4 signaling, oxidative stress, barrier dysfunction, and dysregulated mucosal immunity, suggesting potential for NEC prevention and attenuation, though dosing and route of administration in preterm infants require careful consideration.

title: Coal Dust Nanoparticles Induce Colitis-Like Lesions in Rats via Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis and P53/SCO2/SLC7A11-Mediated Epithelial Ferroptosis.
authors: Zhang Y, Ma Y, Jiang C, Liu Y, Xu Y, Yang Q, Huang Y, Liu X, Zhou S, Zhang Y.
ai_summary: Respiratory exposure to coal dust nanoparticles in rats caused colitis-like colonic damage, inflammation, and loss of tight junction proteins, accompanied by gut microbiota dysbiosis and epithelial ferroptosis driven by the P53/SCO2/SLC7A11 pathway.

title: A Novel Hemizygous CDX4 Missense Variant Identified in a Taiwanese Man with Severe Teratozoospermia.
authors: Au CF, Wang YY, Lai TH, Chan CC, Ke CC, Chung SD, Lin YH.
ai_summary:
Gene: CDX4
Finding: A rare hemizygous missense variant (c.103G>T, p.Gly35Cys) in the conserved Caudal-like transactivation domain was identified in a man with severe teratozoospermia, whose sperm showed head defects and aberrant CDX4 localization along the midpiece and tail; CDX4 transcripts were elevated in teratozoospermic versus normozoospermic samples, and murine CDX4 localized to spermatogonia/spermatocyte nuclei and later to the sperm head and neck/tail during morphogenesis.
Disease: Severe teratozoospermia (male infertility)

title: Organic Nanozyme-Embedded Biotherapeutic Thermosensitive Hydrogel for Extracellular GSH Depletion and Postoperative Tumor Suppression.
authors: Jiang C, Yang Z, Guo R, Suo M, Wang G, Chen D, Su L, Wang F, Ning S, Fan K, Wang X.
ai_summary: A temperature-sensitive agarose hydrogel (SEH) co-loading a cyanine nanozyme and E. coli was developed to prevent postoperative tumor recurrence. Light irradiation triggers photothermal and photodynamic therapy that degrades the hydrogel, releasing the nanozyme and bacteria; the nanozyme's peroxidase-like activity combined with PDT cyclically generates reactive oxygen species that deplete extracellular glutathione and disrupt tumor cell redox balance, while killed E. coli release pathogen-associated molecular patterns that recruit immune cells and establish long-term antitumor immune protection.

title: Direct neuronal reprogramming for neurological diseases: applications, translational Challenges, and future directions.
authors: Chen Y, Zheng Z, Zhao P, Zhu J, Sun H, Zhu H, Zeng Y, Shang B, Zhang A, Pan Y, Wang K.
ai_summary: This review examines direct neuronal reprogramming, an approach that converts non-neuronal cells (notably glial cells) directly into functional neurons, bypassing the pluripotent intermediate stage that carries risks such as tumorigenicity, incomplete maturation, and immune rejection in induced pluripotent stem cell-based strategies. Key reprogramming factors discussed include transcription factors NeuroD1, Ascl1, and Sox2, as well as CRISPR activation of NGN2 and ISL1. The authors survey applications across several neurological diseases, highlight potential contamination issues in AAV delivery systems, and propose a code of conduct to avoid artifacts and pitfalls. They conclude by outlining future directions, including expanding reprogramming targets, integrating organoid-based disease modeling, and advancing reprogramming regulation techniques.

title: Itaconate and its derivatives in human health and diseases.
authors: Gu J, Zhang W, Zhang J, Zeng S, Xia R, Cai L, Zhong X, Guo S, Wang H, Chen ZS.
ai_summary: Itaconate, produced by IRG1/ACOD1-mediated decarboxylation of cis-aconitate, acts as an immunometabolic brake linking the TCA cycle to immune signaling and helping balance inflammation against tissue homeostasis. Across infectious, metabolic, ischemic-reperfusion, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and oncologic conditions, itaconate and its derivatives generally show anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective effects, though in some microenvironments pathogens can exploit them to evade clearance or drive immunosuppressive and protumorigenic responses. The authors call for further work on tissue- and lineage-specific functions, bidirectional regulation, and pharmacokinetic optimization of derivatives, anticipating that the IRG1/ACOD1-itaconate axis will become a key metabolic checkpoint and therapeutic target.

title: Integrin α5β1 Activation by PHSRN Peptide Elicits Neuroprotection and Functional Recovery in Parkinson's Disease Mice.
authors: Wu CC, Wang HK, Su YT, Ho YC, Hsieh YC, Liang CL, Lee YK, Chu TH, Lin YS, Chen JS.
ai_summary:
Gene: ITGA5 (integrin α5β1)
Finding: Rotenone-induced stress reduces integrin α5 expression, and its knockdown worsens oxidative stress, synaptic degeneration, and apoptosis, whereas the fibronectin-derived α5β1-activating peptide Ac-PHSRN-NH2 restores FAK-PI3K-AKT/ERK and NRF2 antioxidant signaling, raises NGF/BDNF, preserves dopaminergic neurons and dopamine release, and improves motor function in MPTP-lesioned mice.
Disease: Parkinson's disease

title: A single-nucleus multiomic study of preoptic area cells in prepubertal control vs prenatally androgenized female mice.
authors: Burger LL, Chikodikar RM, Moenter SM.
ai_summary: This study used single-nucleus multiome sequencing (snRNAseq plus snATACseq) of the mouse preoptic area on postnatal days 18–22 to compare prenatally androgenized (PNA) female mice, a model of hyperandrogenemic PCOS, with controls. Profiling 31 cell populations (17 neuronal, 14 non-neuronal, including a manually curated 41-cell GnRH neuron cluster) revealed that PNA animals showed enrichment of protein synthesis and oxidative phosphorylation pathways and suppression of TNF/NF-κB signaling and steroid responsiveness across several clusters. Differential chromatin accessibility analysis across ~30,600 peaks identified 15 FDR-significant differentially accessible regions, including two loci in GnRH neurons at genomic regions of unknown function, indicating that prenatal androgen exposure alters chromatin accessibility in GnRH and other cell types. Sex steroid receptor genes were unexpectedly accessible in GnRH neurons, and reduced Pgk1 promoter accessibility in multiple glial populations suggests PNA alters epigenetic regulation of glial energy metabolism. The findings support a model of developmental programming in which prenatal androgen exposure causes cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling underlying the PNA phenotype.

title: Molecular Determinants of Unexplained Stillbirth: Genetic, Immune-Mediated, and Pharmacogenomic Contributors.
authors: Priscakova P, Gergely L, Shawkatova I, Milosovicova L, Repiska V, Gbelcova H.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes genetic, immune-mediated, and pharmacogenetic evidence on unexplained stillbirth. Cytogenetic and sequencing approaches, including exome sequencing, improve detection of clinically relevant abnormalities beyond conventional chromosomal analysis, with monogenic contributors spanning cardiac electrophysiology, neuromuscular function, metabolic homeostasis, and early development. Immune-mediated placental dysfunction, especially obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome, is highlighted as a clinically actionable mechanism involving vascular and inflammatory injury with angiogenic imbalance, while emerging pharmacogenetic data suggest that variability in drug metabolism and receptor signaling may affect treatment response in placenta-mediated complications. The authors conclude that integrating genomic, immune, and pharmacogenetic data with phenotypic characterization could improve etiologic resolution, recurrence risk assessment, and precision prevention.

title: Nutritional modulation of male fertility: a molecular-focused scoping review.
authors: Ramgir-Naidu S, Abubakar YA, Soni M.
journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
ai_summary: This scoping review synthesizes molecular evidence linking nutrition to male fertility, focusing on how micronutrients and dietary fats regulate oxidative stress, gene expression, and cellular signaling pathways governing spermatogenesis and sperm quality. Vitamins C, D, E, zinc, selenium, folate, omega-3 fatty acids (especially DHA), and coenzyme Q10 were implicated in mechanisms such as testosterone biosynthesis, sperm membrane integrity, mitochondrial function, and DNA protection, while diets high in processed foods and saturated fats were associated with lipid peroxidation and inflammatory signaling that may impair spermatogenesis, possibly via epigenetic regulation. However, most evidence derives from preclinical and observational studies, with limited and heterogeneous randomized controlled trial data, so clinical translation remains uncertain. The authors identify gaps in long-term adaptation, nutrient-gene interactions, and dose-response relationships, and call for well-designed trials incorporating validated molecular biomarkers before targeted nutritional strategies can be recommended for routine male reproductive care.

title: Genetics of Congenital Heart Disease.
authors: Yasuhara J, Bigelow AM, Garg V.
ai_summary: This review summarizes the established genetic causes of congenital heart disease (CHD) and recent advances in understanding its underlying genetic architecture. It emphasizes that while new genomic technologies have uncovered novel variation associated with CHD, prioritizing and interpreting variants for pathogenicity remains challenging, and the molecular mechanisms driving CHD are still incompletely defined. The authors also discuss the clinical implications of these genomic advances and future research directions.

title: The Proteome of Bone Marrow Multipotent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Undergoes Significant Alterations in Acute Leukemia Patients at the Onset and During Treatment.
authors: Petinati NA, Sadovskaya AV, Shipounova IN, Drize NI, Vasilyeva AN, Aleshina OA, Paderina AS, Pokrovskaya OS, Kuzmina LA, Smirnov IP, Pobeguts OV, Arapidi GP, Lagarkova MA, Parovichnikova EN.
ai_summary: The study compared bone marrow multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) from acute leukemia patients (ALL and AML) with those from healthy donors, examining the proteome at disease onset, in remission, and before and after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient MSCs showed a proteome that differed significantly from donor MSCs at both onset and remission, with changes in extracellular matrix proteins that could affect cell adhesion and growth factor access, as well as alterations in mitochondrial and vesicular transport proteins. Unexpectedly, no differences were found between donor and patient MSCs before and after allo-HSCT, suggesting the stromal cell abnormalities persist despite transplantation.

title: Spatial Transcriptomics Unveils the Blueprint of Mammalian Lung Development.
authors: Chen 陈明月 M, Lv 吕俊杰 J, Zhang 张乔 Q, Gong 龚倩 Q, Zhao 赵婷 T, Chen 陈振平 Z, Xu 徐海深 H, Zhou 周南 N, Jiang 姜姗 S, Du 都建 J, Chen 陈雪鹏 X, Ke 柯玉文 Y.
ai_summary: This study built a spatial transcriptomic atlas of mouse lung development covering the pseudoglandular through alveolar stages, integrating spatial epigenome data to map transcription factor regulatory landscapes, including novel enhancer-driven regulons important for early epithelial progenitors. It identified hundreds of spatiotemporally dynamic cell-cell communication events, such as Bmp8b-mediated signaling enriched in airway branching, and traced the distinct developmental trajectories of alveolar AT1 and AT2 cells, showing that collagen pathways drive their spatial convergence to form primary alveoli during the canalicular-saccular transition.

title: Enterococcus and cancer: from mechanistic insights to clinical translation.
authors: Feng H, Huang X, Zhuang Y, Pu L, Dong R, Ren P.
ai_summary: The gut microbiota influences immunotherapy outcomes, and the genus Enterococcus plays a dual role in cancer: some strains enhance antitumor immunity, while others—notably Enterococcus faecalis—promote tumor progression through DNA damage and inflammatory cascades. Understanding these interactions with the host immune system could help optimize immunotherapy and support microbiome-based treatments.

title: Beyond Infection: Mitochondrial Reprogramming and Immunometabolic Adaptation in Helicobacter pylori-Associated Gastric MALT Lymphoma.
authors: Gargiulo Isacco C, Pham VH, Pham HT, Nguyen KCD, Tran TC, Le TH, Jirillo F, Jirillo E, Santacroce L.
ai_summary: This review proposes that chronic H. pylori infection drives gastric MALT lymphoma (GML) not only through antigenic stimulation and inflammation but through mitochondrial and immunometabolic reprogramming. H. pylori evades innate immunity via its lipid A structure, which fails to activate TLR4/MD2, while its CagA and VacA oncoproteins cause mitochondrial damage, reactive oxygen species production, and functional hypoxia. This stabilizes HIF-1α and forces a glycolytic shift, and defective mitophagy allows metabolically altered, apoptosis-resistant B-cell clones to survive and expand. The authors reinterpret the cytoplasmic sequestration of BCL10 and NF-κB p65 seen in GML as an adaptive state orchestrated by mitochondrial stress and metabolic programs involving MYC, NRF2, and BCL2, framing malignant transformation as a multi-step transition from chronic infection to monoclonal B-cell autonomy.

title: Exploring candidate biomarkers for nonobstructive azoospermia: A bioinformatics and machine learning approach.
authors: Liang M, Chi Y, Pan H, Wu C, Zeng J, Lv W, Luo X.
ai_summary: This bioinformatics and machine-learning study analyzed multiple GEO datasets to identify oxidative stress-related biomarkers for nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA). Five candidate markers emerged—IL1RN, NOSIP, PDYN, PRKCZ, and UTRN—of which IL1RN, NOSIP, PRKCZ, and UTRN were confirmed by qRT-PCR to match the bioinformatic predictions. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed stage-specific dysregulation of these four genes in NOA, broadening the known candidate biomarker landscape for this disorder.

title: Redox Homeostasis, Metabolic Pathways and Plasticity in Uveal Melanoma Compared to Other Cancers.
authors: Păsărică MA, Curcă PF, Dragosloveanu CDM, Nisipașu CI, Curcă GC.
ai_summary: This review integrates literature on redox homeostasis and metabolic plasticity in uveal melanoma (UM), a malignancy genetically and behaviorally distinct from cutaneous melanoma. UM cells maintain redox balance through glutathione, thioredoxin, peroxiredoxin, peroxisomal catalase, and mitochondrial antioxidant networks, with NADPH central to regenerating antioxidant capacity; NRF2, AMPK, mTOR, MAPK, and FoxO signaling are implicated but remain understudied relative to cutaneous melanoma, and PON2 is identified as a literature gap. UM displays high metabolic plasticity, readily switching between glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, and notably favors OXPHOS over the classic Warburg effect, generating excess lactate linked in experimental studies to immune escape. This OXPHOS capacity confers survival advantages and divides tumors into OXPHOS-high and OXPHOS-low subpopulations. UM cells are vulnerable to prooxidants, a metabolic weakness that promotes genetic pleomorphism and selection of more proliferative, disseminative variants. The authors conclude that UM is an oncogenic mutation- and mitochondrial metabolism-driven malignancy with metabolic parallels to several other cancers, and that better understanding of its redox and metabolic signaling could reveal new therapeutic targets and predictors of treatment response.

title: Special Issue: EACR 2026 Congress: Innovative Cancer Science, 8-11 June 2026.
ai_summary: This supplement publishes abstracts accepted by the Congress Organising Committee for the EACR 2026 Congress: Innovative Cancer Science, held 8-11 June 2026. The abstracts appear in Molecular Oncology, an affiliated journal of the European Association for Cancer Research.

title: Hydrogen Sulfide-Regulated NF-κB Signaling via Persulfidation: A Review.
authors: Xu L, Liang K, Wang R, Ta Y, Yang Y, Wang J, Zhang X, Wang Y, Xiao C, Wang Y, Li M.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence that hydrogen sulfide (H2S) fine-tunes NF-κB inflammatory signaling through persulfidation (S-sulfhydration) of key pathway components, including p65, IKKβ, IκBα, and upstream regulators. By modifying these proteins at specific cysteine sites, H2S modulates IKK activation, IκBα degradation, and p65 nuclear translocation, thereby limiting excessive NF-κB activation and inflammatory cytokine production. The authors integrate this mechanism across the TLR4/NF-κB, PI3K/Akt/NF-κB, and MAPK/NF-κB networks and discuss its involvement in oxidative stress, apoptosis, pyroptosis, and tissue repair, while noting challenges in identifying persulfidation sites, understanding endogenous H2S regulation, and improving detection methods. They propose H2S as a precision modulator of inflammatory signaling and a potential target for therapeutic development.

title: Technological advances in axonal regeneration and structural plasticity: optogenetics, single-cell omics, and tissue clearing.
authors: Shu X, Zhang J, Qin Z.
ai_summary: This review describes how three emerging technologies are advancing understanding of axonal degeneration and regeneration after spinal cord and optic nerve injury. Optogenetics provides precise spatiotemporal control of neuronal activity, revealing how targeted stimulation affects axonal growth and circuit reorganization; single-cell omics exposes heterogeneity in regenerative capacity among neuronal subtypes and identifies regeneration-associated genes driving structural remodeling; and tissue clearing with 3D imaging enables direct visualization of axonal trajectories, growth cone morphology, and pathfinding errors in intact tissue, overcoming conventional histology limits. Together these approaches offer new avenues for promoting functional recovery after CNS injury.

title: Functional Foods and Micro- and Nanoplastics: Advances in Precision Nutritional Medicine for Oral-Gut-Brain Axis Health.
authors: Concetta SM, Cinzia L, Giulia Z, Caterina L, Gaetano I, Nicolò M, Angela TS.
ai_summary: This review examines how functional foods rich in polyphenols—such as artichoke, spirulina, Opuntia ficus-indica, pterostilbene, hydroxycinnamic acids, and quinic acid—may counteract damage caused by micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) along the oral-gut-brain axis. These bioactive compounds, especially combined with probiotics and prebiotics, appear to work largely by activating Nrf2 signaling and cellular resilience enzymes, which may help preserve the oral epithelial, intestinal epithelial, and blood-brain barriers while modulating oral pathogens, gut dysbiosis, and neuroinflammation. However, the authors stress that most supporting evidence comes from in vitro and animal studies, with limited human data, so causal links to conditions such as Alzheimer's disease remain unproven. The review also discusses precision nutritional medicine concepts, including individual variability in dietary response and microbiome factors, and calls for further translational and clinical research.

title: Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and Its Supernatant Ameliorate Parkinson's Disease in Association with Modulation of Gut Microbiota and Its Tryptophan Metabolism.
authors: Su B, Meng F, Lu Y, Zhang Y, Wang T, Zhang Y, Liu J, Lin L.
ai_summary:
Gene: TH
Finding: Oral Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and its fermentation supernatant improved motor function, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, promoted neuronal survival, and restored neuroprotective tryptophan metabolites (kynurenic acid, xanthurenic acid, serotonin) in MPTP-treated mice, with live bacteria more effective than supernatant.
Disease: Parkinson's disease

title: Exosome-nanomaterial hybrid nanomedicine for ischemic stroke: microenvironment-informed design, therapeutic applications, and translational challenges.
authors: Zhu Q, Wu X.
ai_summary: This review proposes a microenvironment-informed design paradigm for exosome-nanomaterial hybrid nanomedicines in ischemic stroke, in which the ischemic lesion is treated not as a passive delivery target but as a staged design brief shaped by blood-brain barrier remodeling, thromboinflammation, oxidative stress, immune-cell trafficking, and neurovascular repair. The authors describe how exosome source, nanomaterial component, cargo loading, surface functionalization, administration route, and characterization strategy can be matched to these pathological cues, and they survey applications including BBB-penetrant delivery, neuroprotection, inflammatory modulation, imaging-guided therapy, and neurovascular recovery. They conclude that such hybrids will only become clinically meaningful if their design is microenvironment-informed, mechanism-driven, and translationally scalable, noting persistent safety, quality-control, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers.

title: α-tubulin N-acetyltransferase 1 regulates NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy and protects cancer cells from ferroptosis.
authors: Pellegrini FR, Iuzzolino A, De Palma C, Ambrosio F, Fianco G, Naso FD, Paone A, Rinaldo S, Cutruzzolà F, Degrassi F, Strappazzon F, Stagni V, Trisciuoglio D.
ai_summary:
Gene: ATAT1
Finding: ATAT1 silencing induces NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy and intracellular iron overload, reducing ATP production and oxygen consumption and sensitizing lung cancer cells to ferroptotic cell death, effects that depend on α-tubulin K40 acetylation.
Disease: Ferroptosis susceptibility in lung cancer

title: Overcoming hepatic tropism: Precision engineering of lipid nanoparticles for extrahepatic RNA delivery.
authors: Liu Y, Guo X, Hu Q, Gan C, Nie S, Xiang J, Liu Y, Zou J, Wu X, Li C, Tang Y.
ai_summary: This review addresses the liver tropism that limits lipid nanoparticle (LNP) use for RNA delivery to other organs, arguing that LNPs' "biological identity" must be reprogrammed through three interconnected factors: lipid composition, physicochemical properties, and protein corona modulation. It builds an integrated conceptual framework for extrahepatic targeting, classifying strategies by organ-accumulation mechanism into endogenous corona-mediated approaches (SORT, ENDO, POST, with POST distinguished by peptide-remodeled coronas), covalent active targeting via surface-conjugated ligands binding cell-surface receptors, and passive accumulation governed by vascular permeability. The review surveys recent delivery advances for the lungs, spleen, brain, heart, kidney, bone, and pancreas, discusses translational bottlenecks including species differences, immunogenicity, and manufacturing, and proposes a direction for predictive design.

title: Argonaute 2 stabilization of microRNAs controls adult neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis.
authors: Liu X, Pan W, Chopp M, Fan B, Wang X, Landschoot-Ward J, Wei M, Lu Q, Liu H, Golembieski W, Santra S, Zhang ZG.

title: Neutralization of pathogenic PC-OxPL by AAV-delivered scFv as a therapeutic strategy for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
authors: Gomes-Duarte A, Wong JK, Moro A, Pasteuning-Vuhman S, Pos W, Haselberg R, Sogorb-González M, Pascoal S, Borst L, Chatterjee M, Giera M, Tsimikas S, Sadiq SA, van Deventer S.
ai_summary: This study identifies oxidized phosphatidylcholines (PC-OxPL) as a mechanistic driver of ALS pathology. A distinct PC-OxPL signature was found in the CSF of sporadic ALS patients, carried primarily by apoE-containing particles, and PC-OxPL exposure induced disease-relevant transcriptional changes and TDP-43 pathology in human iPSC-derived motor neurons. To counter this, the authors engineered an AAV-delivered single-chain antibody fragment (PC-OxPL-VecTab) targeting PC-OxPL neoepitopes, which neutralized neurotoxicity, reduced TDP-43 aggregation, and prevented motor neuron death and behavioral deficits in a sALS CSF transfer mouse model. Intrathecal delivery in minipigs achieved broad CNS biodistribution, supporting feasibility for CNS delivery and positioning PC-OxPL-VecTab as a candidate therapeutic strategy for ALS and potentially other PC-OxPL-associated disorders.

title: The role of DNA methylation in directing treatment in medulloblastoma.
authors: Alsaedi MAH, Strathdee G.
ai_summary: This review discusses how DNA methylation profiling has become a key epigenetic tool for stratifying medulloblastoma, the most common malignant childhood brain tumor, into its four molecular subtypes (WNT, SHH, Group 3, and Group 4). Because traditional clinical and histological risk stratification fails to capture the disease's full biologic heterogeneity, methylation-based classifiers offer more precise subgroup and prognostic classification. The authors emphasize the clinical utility of these classifiers for guiding therapeutic decisions and informing clinical trial design, particularly for high-risk patients whose outcomes remain poor despite improved overall survival.

title: Multi-omics technologies: Novel tools and methods for assessing nerve injury and regeneration.
authors: Zhou Q, Zhao Z, Tan D, Fang C, Shen Z, Li S, Chen X.
ai_summary: This review describes how multi-omics approaches (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics) are being applied to nerve injury and regeneration research. Integrating these datasets allows comprehensive tracking of dynamic molecular changes after injury, such as abnormal gene expression, disrupted protein signaling, altered metabolic programs, and immune microenvironment shifts. Single-cell multi-omics resolves cellular heterogeneity among neurons, glial cells, and immune subpopulations, while spatially resolved transcriptomics preserves the spatial context of lesion and regeneration sites for targeted interventions. The authors note that these technologies can identify key molecular players in nerve regeneration and support personalized medicine, but data integration faces challenges including high dimensionality, batch effects, and algorithmic limitations, alongside ethical concerns around stem cell therapy and gene editing. They argue that future progress toward functional remodeling will require AI-driven data integration, organ-on-a-chip modeling, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.

title: Resveratrol and Curcumin in Stroke Therapy: From Experimental Evidence to Clinical Perspectives.
authors: Grabarczyk M, Szychowska A, Szczepańska W, Smolińska E, Glabinski A, Szpakowski P.
ai_summary: This review evaluates resveratrol and curcumin as adjunctive agents for ischaemic and haemorrhagic stroke. Preclinical and early clinical evidence indicates both polyphenols attenuate oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, blood-brain barrier disruption, and microglial activation, and may act partly through gut microbiota and the gut-brain axis. In animal models they reduce infarct volume and cerebral oedema, preserve neuronal viability, promote angiogenesis and neurogenesis, and improve neurological outcomes, with benefits seen both before and after injury. However, the authors caution that experimental stroke models do not capture human stroke heterogeneity, and that poor solubility, low bioavailability, and rapid metabolism limit clinical translation; novel formulations such as nanoparticles and exosome-based delivery may help. Both compounds remain investigational, requiring further clinical trials to establish dosing, timing, safety, and efficacy.

title: Human biomarker navigator.
authors: Li MY, Zhang Q, Wang Z, Gui Z, Liu J, Li J, Jiang M, Chang Z, Han Q, Yang B, Saeed T, Li J, Jia J, Song C, Shao T, Peng T, Zhang X, Guo P, Luo J, Yang G, Wan Y, Zengin G, Yuan Q, Li L, Fan X, Luo Y, Zhu L, Zheng Y, Mao W, Sun W.
ai_summary: This review proposes a "biomarker navigation system" that maps interaction networks of biomarkers across physiological systems, organs, and diseases, shifting from simple knowledge enumeration to a systems-level framework for understanding shared pathological foundations of comorbidities. It argues this integrated view supports a reorientation of medicine toward preventive intervention and systems-based rather than single-disease management. To enable practical use, the authors developed the Human Biomarker Navigator web platform (http://www.hbiomarker.com), which lets researchers and clinicians retrieve the functional characteristics and clinical significance of biomarkers across different disease contexts.

title: The Neanderthal-Derived 3p21 Haplotype at LZTFL1 in Modern-Day Moroccans Is Associated With COVID-19 Severity and Further Suggests the Presence of Neanderthals in North Africa.
authors: Bouhouche A, Skhoun H, Baghdadi JE, Yousfi FE.
ai_summary:
Gene: LZTFL1
Finding: The Neanderthal-derived 3p21 haplotype tagged by rs35044562-T and rs13078854-A was associated with a 2.5-fold increased risk of severe COVID-19 in Moroccans, while sub-Saharan African and rare local haplotypes carrying rs11385942 did not influence outcomes.
Disease: COVID-19 severity

title: DirectContacts2: a wiring diagram of human physical protein interactions.
authors: Claussen ER, Woodcock-Girard MD, Fischer SN, Drew K.
ai_summary:
Gene: OFD1
Finding: A machine-learning model (DirectContacts2) that distinguishes direct from indirect protein interactions was used to structurally model the orofacial digital syndrome (OFDS) complex, providing insight into the molecular consequences of pathogenic OFD1 mutations.
Disease: Orofacial digital syndrome (OFDS)

title: PML as a neuroprotective guardian: Leveraging nuclear protein quality control to mitigate neurotoxicity of an ALS-associated NEK1 variant.
authors: Stark T, Müller S.
ai_summary:
Gene: NEK1
Finding: An ALS-linked NEK1 truncation mutant is recruited to PML nuclear bodies where it likely undergoes SUMOylation and ubiquitylation; in mice, PML loss exacerbates ALS-like symptoms while induced PML expression delays disease onset.
Disease: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)

title: Recent advances in etiology and treatment of von Hippel-Lindau Disease (VHLD).
authors: Pirestani S, Nicolas E, Broadrup RL, Clapper ML, Golemis E.
ai_summary:
Gene: VHL
Finding: Loss of VHL-dependent degradation of HIF-1α and HIF-2α drives tumor formation in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, supporting the use of HIF signaling inhibitors such as belzutifan, though HIF-independent and ubiquitin-ligase-independent VHL functions (microtubule stability, mitotic progression, ciliation, extracellular matrix formation) may also contribute to disease.
Disease: Von Hippel-Lindau disease (clear cell renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, hemangioblastomas)

title: Phytochemical Characterization and Mechanistic Insights into the Cytotoxic Effects of Bougainvillea glabra Bract Extract in Caco-2 Colorectal Adenocarcinoma Cells.
authors: Leal-Alcazar MC, Bautista-Palestina F, Rocha-Pizaña M, Monribot-Villanueva JL, Guerrero-Analco JA, Mojica L, Contreras J, Luna-Vital DA.
journal: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)
ai_summary: The study characterized a Bougainvillea glabra bract extract, identifying 21 phenolic compounds (including rutin and quercetin) and two major betacyanins by UPLC-MS. The extract showed ABTS radical scavenging activity, reduced intracellular ROS under basal and LPS-stimulated conditions, decreased Caco-2 colorectal adenocarcinoma cell viability, and enhanced cisplatin cytotoxicity. These effects were linked to apoptosis- and autophagy-related markers such as p53 and Bcl-2, along with differential regulation of genes involved in caspase activation and NF-kB signaling, supporting the extract's potential as a source of bioactive compounds for colorectal cancer research.

title: Pml loss worsens NEK1-linked ALS and Pml induction drives NEK1 degradation, precluding disease onset.
authors: Georgiadou P, Erkaya B, Niwa-Kawakita M, Oltan M, Keskin YK, Sahin E, Öztürk H, Tiryaki F, Yildiz K, Özgenç I, Odabasi E, Pekbilir E, Dogan SA, Lallemand-Breitenbach V, Vargas S, Prochiantz A, Firat-Karalar EN, de Thé H, Sahin U.
ai_summary:
Gene: NEK1
Finding: The ALS-linked Nek1 Arg812Ter truncation is aggregation-prone in alpha-motoneurons and causes disease when bi-allelic, while Pml loss permits ALS in heterozygotes and Pml induction (via poly(I:C)-triggered interferon signaling) promotes SUMO-mediated degradation of mutant Nek1, clearing puncta and extending survival by 5 months.
Disease: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)

title: Comparative genomic analysis of pigs differing in survival following African swine fever virus infection.
authors: Świerczek N, Ropka-Molik K, Piórkowska K, Małopolska M, Tyra M, Szmatoła T, Muszyński S, Quembo CJ.
ai_summary: Whole-genome sequencing of 32 Mozambican Landim pigs (16 survivors, 16 non-survivors) naturally exposed to African swine fever virus identified 4,804 polymorphisms that significantly differentiated the two groups, including missense variants in TTC12 and WWC1, with annotated genes implicated in immune regulation, T-cell activation, signaling, cytoskeletal organization, vesicular transport, proteostasis, and lipid metabolism. However, because the survivor and non-survivor groups showed marked genetic stratification, the authors caution that variant effects cannot be unambiguously separated from underlying population structure, so the findings are exploratory and require validation in larger, independent, genetically comparable populations.

title: Compound Heterozygous PCDH15 Variants Associated With Cone-Rod Dystrophy in a Chinese Pedigree.
authors: Zhang L, Wang Q, Wang H, Jia W, Zhang B, Wang R, Qiang W, Bai S.
ai_summary:
Gene: PCDH15
Finding: Two novel compound heterozygous PCDH15 variants (c.4903_4906del, p.Glu1635Lysfs*4 and c.3470C>A, p.Ala1157Glu) were identified in a Chinese pedigree and co-segregated with disease; both variants affect highly conserved residues and structural modeling predicted altered protein structure.
Disease: Autosomal recessive cone-rod dystrophy

title: The Regulatory Army of Plant Defense: Transcription Factors in the War for Plant Immunity.
authors: Ferreira-Neto JRC, de Barros AAG, de Melo ALTM, Amorim LLB, de Luna Aragão MA, Bezerra-Neto JP, Maciel LS, da Silva MD, da Silva PVG, Benko-Iseppon AM.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes recent advances positioning transcription factors (TFs) as central regulators of plant immunity, linking pathogen perception to immune signaling and defense reprogramming. Combining a literature synthesis with NLP analysis of 1,647 PubMed abstracts (2021–2026), the authors found that WRKY, MYB, AP2/ERF, bHLH/MYC, and NAC families dominate recent research, while NF-Y, Trihelix, PLATZ, TCP, and GRAS are emerging actors. TFs integrate pattern- and effector-triggered immunity, hormone crosstalk, chromatin dynamics, non-coding RNA regulation, post-translational modifications, and metabolic remodeling, with function shaped by cell type, pathogen lifestyle, and host genetic background; pathogens also manipulate TFs to weaken defense. The review proposes TF-centered strategies for engineering durable crop resistance.

title: Regenerative strategies for ALS: stem cells and extracellular vesicles.
authors: Raghunathan T, Parthasarathy B, Prabhu P, Mahesh P, Dhanushkodi A.
ai_summary: This review discusses the limited treatment options for ALS, a late-onset disease with a 5-year survival rate and no early diagnostic method. Extracellular vesicles released from the degenerative environment propagate ALS by transporting misfolded proteins, proinflammatory cytokines, and neurotoxins, making them potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. The authors highlight stem cell-based therapies and extracellular vesicles as promising biotherapeutic strategies that offer hope for slowing or halting ALS progression.

title: Transcending genome-wide association studies to create useful multi-omic views of glaucoma.
authors: Li K, Kang JH, Khawaja AP, Jardines S, Vergroesen J, Ramdas W, Stuart K, Luben R, Hysi P, Hanyuda A, Zeleznik O, Segrè AV, Vallabh NA, Leung YYR, Wiggs JL, Pasquale LR.
journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
