ai_summary: This review synthesizes the current multi-omic landscape in glaucoma, covering genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, microbiome, and phenomic approaches, and evaluates the strengths and limitations of each modality. The authors argue that integrating these data types can identify biomarkers, molecular endotypes, and pathways underlying glaucoma susceptibility and progression, moving beyond genome-wide association studies. They propose conceptual and methodological frameworks for using multi-omics to characterize the full spectrum of glaucoma, with emphasis on optic nerve integrity, mechanistic insight, and precision medicine.

title: Post-translational modification of proteins in the human testis development pathway.
authors: Idris FP, Ferreira LGA, Houston B, Humphrey SJ, Sinclair AH, Ayers KL.
ai_summary: This review examines how post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate proteins critical for human foetal testis development and how their disruption contributes to congenital disorders such as differences of sex development (DSD). Drawing on databases including PhosphoSitePlus, ClinVar and the Human Gene Mutation Database, the authors find that proteins required for testis development undergo extensive PTM, and that several PTM sites and PTM-mediated pathways (such as the MAPK pathway) are disrupted in DSD patients. The review also surveys emerging proteomic and stem cell-based organ modelling technologies that could overcome the technical, ethical and logistical barriers currently limiting large-scale proteomic study of human foetal gonads, arguing that closing this knowledge gap has clinical relevance for genetic diagnosis and patient outcomes.

title: From environmental signals to adaptive phenotypes: signal-responsive regulation and network logic of bacterial small RNAs.
authors: Yi Z, Xiao X, Zou L, Cen C, Shentu X, Yu X, Wang W.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes current understanding of bacterial regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) as central nodes in posttranscriptional networks. It outlines sRNA biogenesis and the pathways controlling their expression—including environmental signal sensing and regulation by sigma factors and transcription factors—showing how sRNAs respond dynamically to changing conditions. It further covers their roles in metabolic adaptation, stress responses, and virulence, emphasizing how they link environmental cues to cellular phenotypes, and reviews experimental and computational methods for sRNA discovery and target identification.

title: Unraveling the Pathogenetic Potential and Immune Crosstalk of Yersinia spp. in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
authors: Sabzehali F, Zerbato V, Bella SD, Morabito S, Zali MR, Yadegar A.
ai_summary: Yersinia enterocolitica and Y. pseudotuberculosis are candidate microbiological contributors to IBD, but the evidence linking them to disease remains circumstantial: PCR-based detection of Yersinia DNA in IBD intestinal tissue and epidemiological associations with prior infection are limited by scarce culture confirmation and infrequent amplicon sequencing, so active infection or causality is unproven. These pathogens use type III/VI secretion systems to exploit epithelial barrier defects and compromised mucosal immunity, activating inflammasomes and inducing pyroptosis, while polymorphisms in autophagy-related genes such as NOD2 and ATG16L1 impair clearance and raise susceptibility. Antibiotics remain effective for invasive disease but resistance is rising, and probiotics show immunomodulatory, antimicrobial, and barrier-protective effects in preclinical models, though clinical validation in IBD is still needed.

title: A multiplex tissue resource for high-resolution spatial protein profiling in the Human Protein Atlas.
authors: Katona B, Schutten R, Bertilsson F, Hikmet F, Adelsköld P, Forsberg M, von Feilitzen K, Méar L, Uhlén M, Lindskog C.
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
ai_summary: This paper describes a new multiplex immunohistochemistry resource within version 25 of the Human Protein Atlas that adds high-resolution spatial context to antibody-based protein profiling. Using eight iterative multiplex antibody panels across nine tissue settings (including testis, motile ciliated epithelia, salivary gland, endocrine pancreas, and kidney), the authors analyzed 1,106 proteins, interpreting candidate protein expression directly within intact tissue architecture via overlap with markers of cell identity, tissue organization, cellular state, and subcellular structure. The panels resolve contexts such as spermatogenesis stages, Sertoli cell and ciliary subcellular compartments, salivary gland acinar/ductal structures, pancreatic endocrine cell types, and nephron segments, providing a publicly available framework for refining spatial protein annotation and generating hypotheses about protein function in normal tissue biology.

title: Uncovering Potential Druggable Targets in Coronary Atherosclerosis: A Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization Study With Cross-Platform and Experimental Validation.
authors: Gao D, Lin H, Wang S, Wang Y, Yang H, Wang Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: SDCCAG8
Finding: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization with colocalization and SMR/HEIDI analyses prioritized SDCCAG8 as one of five candidate plasma proteins for coronary atherosclerosis, and it was among the proteins included in the druggable genome list.
Disease: Coronary atherosclerosis

title: Microglia-Mediated Ependymal Injury in Bacille Calmette-Guérin-Induced Meningitis Is Attenuated by Sodium Butyrate with Restoration of Hmgcs2 Expression.
authors: Ren Y, Chen D, Xie S, He Y, Zhuang X, Ye D, Fei Z, Xia L, Wang Y, Li F.
ai_summary:
Gene: Hmgcs2
Finding: In a murine BCG-induced meningitis model, microglia amplified ependymal transcriptional dysregulation, and BCG challenge downregulated Hmgcs2, causing ciliary shortening and increased apoptosis, while sodium butyrate restored Hmgcs2 expression, preserved ciliary structure, and reduced apoptosis.
Disease: Tuberculous meningitis

title: Genetic Insights Into Retinitis Pigmentosa: A De Novo RPGR Mutation in an Iranian-Azeri Family.
authors: Ghezelbash N, Bonyadi M, Bonyadi MHJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: RPGR
Finding: Whole-exome sequencing in a 40-year-old Iranian-Azeri Turkish man with retinitis pigmentosa identified a hemizygous c.194G>T mutation in exon 3 of RPGR, predicted in silico to create a new cryptic donor site; segregation analysis showed the variant was absent in his mother and healthy siblings, indicating it arose de novo, and it was not found in 430 healthy controls from the same ethnic group.
Disease: Retinitis pigmentosa

title: Editorial: Use of bioinformatics in pharmacogenetics to optimize drug efficacy.
authors: Jaafari A, Tilaoui M.

title: Beyond hypoxia and ccRCC: the expanding universe of VHL novel targets and next-generation therapeutics.
authors: Deng R, Wang B, Zou M, Mao K, Shang J, Qiu J, Zhou J, Xu H, Ma X, Wang Y, Cai L, Gong K.
ai_summary: This review argues that the therapeutic relevance of VHL extends well beyond the canonical VHL–HIF axis that underlies current HIF-2α inhibitors like belzutifan, whose intrinsic non-responsiveness and acquired resistance limit ccRCC treatment. It synthesizes evidence on non-canonical VHL substrates across epigenetic regulation (ZHX2, SETDB1, METTL3/METTL14), metabolic reprogramming (NDRG3, TFAM), extracellular matrix architecture (fibronectin, COL4A2), and immune modulation (TBK1), with evidence quality ranging from direct biochemical ubiquitination to indirect downstream observations, mostly from preclinical cell-line and xenograft models. These findings suggest two therapeutic directions: in VHL-deficient cancers, small-molecule inhibition of unshielded downstream effectors as vulnerability-targeted salvage therapy; and in VHL-proficient cancers, VHL-recruiting PROTACs that hijack the ligase to degrade oncogenic drivers, including previously undruggable targets. The authors caution that clinical translation remains distant, with unresolved questions about substrate directness, tissue tropism, and resistance trade-offs.

title: A Stimulus-Resolved Framework for Investigating Putative Neurotrophic Secretome-Metabolome Coupling in Aging Skeletal Muscle: CNTF and CLCF1 as Non-Equivalent Nodes.
authors: Tong F, Chen Y, Gui H, Li A, Li H, Pei Y, Wu Z, Wang M.
ai_summary: This narrative review argues that resting myokine levels are insufficient to interpret muscle neurotrophic signaling, since they cannot separate adaptive signaling from compensation, injury, or non-muscle sources. Comparing CNTF and CLCF1 across basal, insulin-stimulated, exercise, recovery, and training states, the authors find CNTF has a well-established CNTFRα-LIFR-gp130 receptor model with pharmacological links to AMPK activation, glucose uptake, ceramide handling, and insulin responsiveness, whereas CLCF1's receptor usage and muscle tissue source remain unresolved and its extracellular availability depends partly on CRLF1. Only one recent study offers preclinical and exploratory human evidence for exercise-responsive CLCF1, and no direct human studies pair CNTF/CLCF1 kinetics with muscle metabolomics or isotope-resolved flux. The authors therefore frame neurotrophic secretome-metabolome coupling as a hypothesis-generating construct rather than a validated system, specifying that testing it requires synchronized measurement of ligand, receptor-proximal signaling, and metabolic output within the same physiological challenge, using targeted/untargeted metabolomics, lipidomics, quality-controlled annotation, paired tissue and plasma sampling, and stable isotope tracing to assess reproducibility, muscle relevance, and aging-related change.

title: Let the female tract choose: finding the sperm to enhance in vitro embryo production.
authors: Saint-Dizier M, Ehrhardt L, Perez-Gomez A, Souza-Fabjan JMG, Mahé C.
ai_summary: This review argues that conventional sperm selection for in vitro embryo production, based mainly on motility and morphology, captures only part of sperm functional competence, which helps explain why only about 25% of fertilized oocytes yield transferable embryos and why outcomes trail in vivo-derived embryos. In vivo, the female tract filters sperm through the utero-tubal junction, the oviductal sperm reservoir, and guided navigation to the oocyte, allowing fewer than 0.01% of inseminated sperm to reach the fertilization site; these selective mechanisms are largely missing from standard IVF. Emerging biomimetic approaches, especially microfluidic platforms and oviduct cell-based selection, show promise for improving IVEP in cattle, but limited throughput, standardization, and scalability still restrict routine use.

title: Multi-genomics data mining identified critical transcription factors and immune response pathways in traumatic optic nerve injury and retinal injury.
authors: Li J, Zhang Y, Zhou S.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: STAT3 was identified as one of six hub genes with diagnostic relevance in experimental retinal injury datasets and, together with STAT1, was predicted to act as a transcriptional regulator within the hub gene regulatory network.
Disease: Traumatic optic nerve injury and retinal injury

title: Interleukin-6 in complications of prematurity: from biomarker to targeted therapy.
authors: Xiao S, Zheng Q, Wang L, Wang Z, Bi G, Yang J.
ai_summary: This review examines the role of interleukin-6 (IL-6) in complications of prematurity, covering its mechanisms and clinical implications across various neonatal conditions. It discusses current and emerging therapies targeting IL-6, its receptor, and the trans-signaling pathway as potential treatments. While IL-6 is consistently valuable as an early predictive biomarker, its translation into targeted therapy for preterm infants remains preliminary, with substantial gaps in safety and pharmacokinetic data requiring further investigation.

title: S14G-humanin attenuates renal ischaemia-reperfusion injury, potentially through activation of STAT3 and ERK1/2 signalling pathways in rats.
authors: Abueid L, Torun AF, Golal E, Acar N, Basrali F.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: S14G-humanin reduced oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction in renal ischaemia-reperfusion injury, with increased STAT3 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation suggesting involvement of these pathways, although blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine were unaffected.
Disease: Renal ischaemia-reperfusion injury

title: Dysregulation of liquid-liquid phase separation: from molecular mechanisms to targeted therapies in cardiovascular diseases.
authors: Zhang X, Ma X, Cao N, Zhou Y, Zhang Z, Ma R.
ai_summary: This review proposes that m6A modification-mediated phase separation of RNA with intrinsically disordered proteins acts as a conserved regulatory axis across diverse cardiovascular diseases, and that the irreversible liquid-to-gel/solid transition of biomolecular condensates drives the pathological irreversibility of end-stage CVD. It further describes synergy between m6A RNA modification and protein post-translational modifications in controlling this axis, and outlines four emerging LLPS-targeted therapeutic strategies: small-molecule modulators, biomaterial-based delivery systems, chiral nanomaterial interventions, and PTM-focused modulation.

title: S100A9 as a Candidate Molecular Bridge in Hepato-Ocular Crosstalk.
authors: Wang P, Li Y, Xia B, Lin Y, Tuo Q, Lin L, Peng Q.
ai_summary: This narrative review assesses whether S100A9-related signals mediate crosstalk between liver and eye disease. Across human, ocular fluid, animal, and cellular studies, evidence supports disease-associated hepatic expression and ocular responsiveness, with stronger support for local S100A9-TLR4 effects than for S100A9-specific RAGE signaling. Clinical associations with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, diabetic retinopathy, chronic liver disease, dry eye disease, and uveitis are heterogeneous and confounded, and interpretation is limited by the non-equivalence of S100A9, S100A8/A9, calprotectin, and higher-order complexes. The authors conclude that S100A9-related species are best regarded as exploratory indicators of inflammatory activity or local amplifiers rather than established liver-derived causal signals, and call for analyte-specific measurement, source tracing, and selective perturbation.

title: Natural flavonoid dihydroquercetin blocks Trim14-JAK1-STAT3 signaling and relieves pain-depression comorbidity in rheumatoid arthritis.
authors: Ni XW, Chai B, Li ZM, Li XP, Sun C, Yuan XL, Zhang YB, Zhang Y, Qian WJ, Zhang HL.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: The natural flavonoid dihydroquercetin binds Trim14 with sub-micromolar affinity and inhibits the spinal Trim14-JAK1-STAT3 axis, while intrathecal Trim14 knockdown reduces synovial inflammation, inflammatory pain, and anxiety-depressive behaviors in collagen-induced arthritis mice; serum Trim14 is elevated in RA patients and correlates with symptom severity.
Disease: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated pain-depression comorbidity

title: Maternal-fetal interface abnormalities in unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss: mechanisms, models, and a framework for subtype identification.
authors: Tokuoka A, Iida K, Yamada M, Ono M, Irie N.
ai_summary: This mini review argues that unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (URPL) should be viewed as an exclusion-based clinical category rather than a single disease, and examines the hypothesis that a subset of cases arises from abnormalities in specific cellular and molecular components of the maternal-fetal interface. It surveys maternal compartments (endometrial epithelial lineage states, decidual stromal dysfunction, stromal-immune interactions) and fetal/trophoblast compartments (trophoblast lineage defects and broader maternal-fetal interactions), drawing on recent single-cell, spatial, organoid, assembloid, implantation model, trophoblast stem cell, and placental explant studies from 2024-2026. The authors note that current data do not establish clinical subtypes of URPL or support treatment selection in routine practice, but propose that these technologies now allow interface phenotypes to be defined at higher resolution and patient-derived abnormalities to be tested for reproducibility and perturbability, offering an interface-centered framework to move the field toward experimentally testable subtype identification.

title: Uterine factor infertility-current understanding and limitations.
authors: Cornish T, Chowdhury I.
ai_summary: Uterine factor infertility is an underrecognized contributor to recurrent implantation failure and recurrent pregnancy loss, yet current diagnostics (ultrasonography, hysteroscopy, ERA) detect only structural pathology and timing-based receptivity deficits, missing underlying molecular and cellular endometrial dysfunction. This review examines how estrogen- and progesterone-driven cyclical endometrial remodeling and cytokine signaling networks regulate receptivity, how their disruption contributes to implantation failure and pregnancy loss, and proposes emerging molecular and spatial profiling technologies as future tools for more precise assessment of endometrial competence.

title: Extracellular vesicles and acetylation: reciprocal regulation in disease progression.
authors: Liu Y, Wu S, Wang Y, Zhu X, Kang L.
ai_summary: This review describes a bidirectional regulatory relationship between extracellular vesicles (EVs) and acetylation. Acetylation controls EV biogenesis, cargo loading, secretion, and protein trafficking, while EVs transferred to recipient cells can alter acetyl-CoA metabolism, acetylation writers and erasers, and acetylated protein signaling via non-coding RNAs, proteins, and metabolites. The authors discuss implications for cancer immunity (antigen presentation, macrophage polarization, CD8+ T-cell dysfunction, regulatory T cells, natural killer cells, immune checkpoint regulation), evaluate EV-associated acetylation signatures as biomarkers, and assess histone deacetylase inhibitors and EV-based interventions, along with current methodological and translational limitations.

title: The regulatory role of post-translational modifications in the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis.
authors: Ji Y, Wei B.
ai_summary: This review examines how post-translational modifications (PTMs)—including phosphorylation, glycosylation, acetylation, methylation, ubiquitination, citrullination, and palmitoylation—contribute to the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis. The authors synthesize evidence that PTMs regulate immune function, epithelial barrier integrity, and inflammatory signaling, positioning these modifications as potential therapeutic targets, though the precise pathogenesis of UC remains incompletely understood.

title: Exercise-induced osteoimmune crosstalk: a virtuous cycle between bone remodeling and immune regulation.
authors: Wang L, Guo W.
ai_summary: This review describes how exercise initiates a feed-forward osteoimmune circuit: mechanical loading activates osteocytes and osteogenic progenitors, remodels the bone marrow niche, and promotes anti-inflammatory immune polarization, which in turn shifts the balance toward bone formation over resorption. The authors propose that this virtuous cycle between bone remodeling and immune regulation offers new therapeutic strategies for preventing and treating bone metabolic diseases such as osteoporosis.

title: The neuro-immune-vascular landscape of lung cancer brain metastasis: insights from organoid models.
authors: Li J, Xu M, Wang L, Yu Y.
ai_summary: This review discusses how organoid-based models are advancing understanding of lung cancer brain metastasis, a process shaped by coordinated neural, immune, and vascular interactions within the brain metastatic niche. Conventional models cannot recreate this multicellular, spatially organized ecosystem, but newer platforms—cerebral organoid assembloids, vascularized microfluidic systems, and blood-brain barrier models—reconstruct key niche components and their dynamic interactions. These systems have revealed regulatory axes such as astrocyte-driven colonization, neurovascular remodeling, and metabolic-immune coupling, and they allow functional testing of patient-specific drug and immunotherapy responses. Despite remaining limitations, organoid models offer a framework for dissecting the neuro-immune-vascular landscape of LCBM and translating mechanistic findings into personalized treatment.

title: Thyroid Cancer: From Potential Drivers to Real Modulators.
authors: Rafiqi SI, Jaume JC.
ai_summary: This review argues that thyroid cancer research has focused disproportionately on tumor genetics while under-exploring the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), which comprises macrophages, lymphocytes, natural killer cells, mast cells, and signaling molecules and evolves with tumor growth and metastasis. The authors describe how oncogenic signaling, stromal remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming interact with the TIME to shape the clinical and biological heterogeneity of thyroid cancers, ranging from aggressive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma to indolent papillary thyroid carcinoma. They conclude that mapping spatial and temporal changes in the TIME could enable therapies that counter immune evasion, and that thyroid cancer treatment is shifting from mutation-directed strategies toward integrated, combinatorial approaches incorporating personalized immunotherapy.

title: Anti-inflammatory efficacy of diosgenin in an oxazolone-induced model of ulcerative colitis in mice via suppression of Th2 pathways and pSTAT3 expression: A prospective study.
authors: Narayan A, Babu Shubha P, Baker S, Sathyanarayana NR, Ahmed F, Shivananju NS.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: Diosgenin reduced colitis severity in oxazolone-induced ulcerative colitis mice, with effects attributed to cytokine modulation and inhibition of pSTAT3 expression.
Disease: Ulcerative colitis

title: The Impact of Plant-Derived Foods and Medicines on the Lung-Gut Axis and Microbiota Cross-Talk.
authors: Vivatvakin S, Werawatganon D.
ai_summary: This narrative review examines bidirectional communication along the gut-lung axis, focusing on how gut microbiota and their metabolites—especially short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate) produced by fermentation of dietary fiber and polysaccharides—influence respiratory immunity through immune cell trafficking and epithelial barrier regulation. It also covers the less-established reverse direction, in which respiratory infection, smoking, or lung injury disrupt gut barrier integrity and microbiota composition. Plant-derived interventions such as dietary fibers, polysaccharides, and polyphenols show promise, primarily via SCFA-dependent immune modulation and enrichment of metabolite-producing bacteria, with some compounds acting through microbiota-independent antioxidant and barrier-protective mechanisms. The authors conclude that SCFA-mediated immune regulation is the best-supported mechanism, that lung-to-gut signaling remains poorly established, and that most evidence is preclinical, underscoring the need for standardized human trials assessing dose, safety, and respiratory outcomes.

title: Utility of the Inflammatory Bowel Disease Serology, Genetics, and Inflammation (IBD-SGI) Panel in the Evaluation of Atypical Ulcerative Colitis With Active Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug Use: A Case Report.
authors: Guo LZ, Bryant R, Perry K.
ai_summary: This case report describes a 39-year-old man with hematochezia, diarrhea, and chronic high-dose NSAID use who developed anemia, elevated fecal calprotectin, and colonoscopic inflammation. Because biopsies showed overlapping features of NSAID injury and IBD, an IBD-SGI blood panel was used as an adjunct; interpreted alongside the clinical, endoscopic, and histopathologic findings, it supported a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis, and the patient was treated with vedolizumab with good recovery by three-month follow-up. The authors conclude the panel may be a useful supportive tool when biopsy findings are inconclusive and multiple etiologies coexist, though it remains outside routine practice due to guideline restrictions, lack of FDA clearance, and limited insurance coverage.

title: From gut microbiota-driven mucosal barrier disruption to myeloid-dominant immunosuppressive niches in colorectal cancer.
authors: Lu N, Zhang L, Sun H, Zhou Y, He P, Zhao C, Wang Y.
ai_summary: This review argues that poor immunotherapy response in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer is not merely a consequence of low antigenicity but reflects a spatially structured, drug-resistant niche built along a microbiota–barrier–myeloid axis. Dysbiosis involving Fusobacterium nucleatum and enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis, together with microbial metabolites and tight junction disruption, drives cytokine and eicosanoid signaling through IL-6/STAT3, NF-κB, TNF-alpha, and COX-2/PGE2, remodeling the tumor microenvironment toward myeloid dominance via tumor-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, neutrophil polarization, dendritic cell dysfunction, regulatory T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, CXCL12-mediated T-cell exclusion, and hypoxia. The authors propose that incorporating this axis into biomarker development and mechanism-matched combination therapy design is a more rational strategy for overcoming immunotherapy resistance in colorectal cancer, particularly MSS disease, than empirical drug combinations.

title: Low Dose Ketamine Preconditions Astrocyte Mitochondria to Achieve Antidepressant Efficacy via Adenosine, Humanin, and Melatonin Upregulation and Efflux.
authors: Anderson G.
ai_summary: This hypothesis-driven review proposes that ketamine's antidepressant efficacy stems not from synaptic NMDAR antagonism but from direct preconditioning of astrocyte mitochondria, mediated via NMDARs on the inner mitochondrial membrane. Developmental stress and trauma are proposed to epigenetically prime astrocytes in specific CNS regions, increasing their reactivity and dysregulating mitochondrial function while raising local blood-brain barrier permeability. At these stress-vulnerable sites, ketamine is proposed to upregulate and efflux adenosine, humanin, and melatonin, restoring astrocyte function and dampening local inflammation involving microglia, neurons, and oligodendrocytes; melatonin and humanin are further proposed to suppress microglial activation, promote remyelination, and restore neuronal and interregional communication. No gene-disease link is experimentally established.

title: Precision nanomedicine for pulmonary diseases: from molecular targeting to clinical translation.
authors: Deng Z, Gao W, Do J, Aragam S, Dawd O, Belthur M, Shi D, Kalin TV, Kalinichenko VV.
ai_summary: This review surveys precision nanomedicine for pulmonary diseases, covering how nanoparticle platforms can overcome the limitations of conventional gene and drug therapies (viral vector safety, therapeutic instability, poor cellular uptake, and lack of tissue- and cell-specific targeting) by improving stability and bioavailability, enabling controlled release and endosomal escape, and targeting specific lung compartments. It examines nanoparticle physicochemical properties and design strategies for targeted delivery, compares pulmonary versus systemic administration routes given the lung's unique architecture, and reviews applications across pulmonary fibrosis, COPD, infections, pulmonary vascular disease, cystic fibrosis, asthma, lung cancers, and neonatal pulmonary disorders. It also assesses clinical trial status and translational barriers such as biological barriers, long-term safety, and manufacturing, proposing interdisciplinary strategies to advance clinical translation.

title: Broad-spectrum host-targeting antivirals for rhinovirus infections: mechanisms and future perspectives.
authors: Shang W, Luo H, Li S, Yu S, Wang X, Fu D, Wang L, Meng F, Gao M.
ai_summary: This review discusses host-targeting antivirals (HTAs) as an alternative strategy against rhinovirus infection, which is difficult to treat with conventional direct-acting antivirals due to the virus's many serotypes and lack of conserved viral targets. HTAs work by interfering with host cell factors and pathways required for viral entry, biosynthesis, assembly, release, and immune regulation. While promising, the approach still faces challenges in clinical translation, including safety, delivery efficiency, and individual variability, but is seen as a potentially transformative treatment, particularly for high-risk patients.

title: Research Status and Prospects of Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis: From Mechanisms to Traditional Chinese Medicine Treatment.
authors: Fan Z, Jin Z, Liu C, Hu R, Li W.
ai_summary: This review examines Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis (HPAG), a chronic gastric mucosal inflammation that underlies peptic ulcers and gastric precancerous lesions. Because high global infection rates and rising antibiotic resistance are undermining conventional eradication therapy, the authors synthesize the molecular pathogenesis of HPAG — covering bacterial virulence factors, host immune responses, aberrant signaling pathways, oxidative stress, epigenetic regulation, and mucosal barrier damage — and review traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interventions through the lens of microecological homeostasis regulation. They describe how TCM monomers and formulas contribute to immunomodulation, mucosal repair, and antibacterial synergism, and use this evidence to build a whole-course intervention framework spanning susceptibility prevention, active treatment, and posteradication repair. The review also critiques clinical translation bottlenecks and the "black-box" nature of TCM research, proposing multiomics-driven directions for future work.

title: Tissue-Specific Transcriptomic Insights into Myxozoan Infections: Immune and Stress Responses in the Kidney and Head Cartilage of Rainbow Trout.
authors: Akram N, Ertl R, Ghanei-Motlagh R, Secombes CJ, El-Matbouli M, Saleh M.
ai_summary: This study used RNA sequencing to profile transcriptomic responses in the kidney and head cartilage of rainbow trout during single and sequential co-infections with the myxozoan parasites Myxobolus cerebralis and Tetracapsuloides bryosalmonae. Infection order altered host transcriptional profiles in a tissue-dependent manner: kidney responses to T. bryosalmonae involved chronic inflammation, immune complex clearance, and IL-8-mediated signaling, while subsequent M. cerebralis infection (Tb+) produced broad, dysregulated immune activation; kidney responses in Mc+ fish centered on macrophage and IL signaling. In head cartilage, M. cerebralis activated Th17, IL-23, phagolysosome, and IL-6 pathways, whereas Mc+ fish showed enhanced pathogen processing and metabolic responses with suppressed cytokines and tissue repair, and Tb+ fish shifted toward IL-23/Th17-driven responses with reduced developmental and extracellular matrix processes. The authors conclude that host responses to myxozoan co-infection depend on tissue tropism and infection sequence, offering a basis for tissue-specific biomarkers and improved monitoring of these infections in salmonids.

title: Oxidative stress-driven epigenetic reprogramming of immune cells in COPD: from epitranscriptomic and metabolic crosstalk to treatable traits.
authors: Pan CF, Wan Q, Ni FX, Xu P, Huang DH, Jiang ZB.
ai_summary: This review proposes an integrated framework in which oxidative stress in COPD reprograms immune cells through both classical epigenetic mechanisms (DNA methylation, histone modifications) and epitranscriptomic regulation (m6A RNA methylation), locking cells into pathogenic states. Metabolic intermediates such as S-adenosylmethionine, α-ketoglutarate, succinate, and NAD+ act as key nodes linking immunometabolism to epigenetic enzymes and the m6A machinery, connecting redox status to RNA fate. Using NETosis as a paradigm, the authors show how oxidative-epigenetic-metabolic loops sustain neutrophilic inflammation and failed resolution, and they outline a treatable traits framework for precision combination therapies aimed at mechanism-driven disease modification rather than symptom control.

title: The microbiome-EBV axis in carcinogenesis bridges commensal influence and viral oncogenesis.
authors: Tian X, Ji K, Feng M.
ai_summary: This review proposes the "microbiome-EBV axis" as a framework for how host microbial communities influence Epstein-Barr virus-associated carcinogenesis, moving beyond the classical virus-host paradigm. It synthesizes four interrelated mechanisms: microbial regulation of EBV latency and lytic reactivation, microbiome-driven remodeling of the immune microenvironment, microbial contributions to genomic and epigenetic instability, and potential translational applications of microbial signatures or microbiome-targeted interventions. The authors emphasize distinguishing mechanistic evidence from in vitro and animal studies, observational associations from clinical cohorts, and clinically validated findings, concluding that microbiome-derived biomarkers and therapies remain promising but incompletely validated.

title: Advances in FGF/FGFR Signaling: Implications for Disease and Therapy.
authors: Song M, Liu X, Xiao Y, Li Y, Zhao H.
ai_summary: This review summarizes FGF/FGFR signaling, which involves FGFs, FGFRs, and the Klotho co-receptor and governs embryogenesis, tissue homeostasis, metabolism, and neurodevelopment. Both hyperactivation and loss-of-function of this pathway contribute to diseases including skeletal dysplasia, metabolic disorders, cancers, and neurological disorders, making it an attractive therapeutic target. The authors discuss cellular and physiological functions of the pathway, its links to disease, and strategies for targeting dysregulated signaling, while noting remaining clinical challenges such as side effects, acquired resistance to pathway blockade, and safety concerns with FGF analogs.

title: Multifaceted roles of S100A6 in neurological disorders: expression, interaction networks, and clinical implications.
authors: Zhang J, Tang P, Huang L, Lv J, Chen Y, Wang Y, Luo Y.
ai_summary: S100A6 (calcyclin) is a Ca2+/Zn2+-binding S100-family protein expressed in neurons and glia in a developmentally regulated, cell-type-specific manner. This review describes its interactome—spanning cytoskeletal regulators, chaperones, nuclear transport proteins, and cell surface receptors—which positions it as a central signaling hub. Its involvement in neurological disease is context-dependent: in Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis it acts as a glial-derived factor linking protein aggregation, metal dyshomeostasis, and neuroinflammation; in neuro-oncology it promotes malignancy and immunosuppression in glioblastoma, is an epigenetically silenced marker in medulloblastoma, and aids diagnosis of peripheral nerve sheath tumors; and its expression is altered in epilepsy, traumatic brain injury, and autoimmune encephalitis. The authors conclude that clarifying these functions could yield new diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapies.

title: Gut-liver axis molecular mechanisms in alcohol-associated liver disease.
authors: Jiang Y, Llorente C.
ai_summary: This review examines how the gut-liver axis drives alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). Chronic alcohol use disrupts intestinal homeostasis, causing microbial dysbiosis, impaired barrier integrity, and translocation of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) into the portal circulation and liver, where they engage pattern-recognition receptors on hepatic immune and parenchymal cells to promote inflammation and fibrosis. Microbial metabolites—short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, indole derivatives, and vitamin B—also modulate hepatic and immune pathways relevant to liver homeostasis. The review further highlights the roles of central interleukins (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, IL-10, IL-22, IL-23) in ALD pathogenesis and concludes that modulating gut microbiota composition and signaling is a promising avenue for developing safe, novel ALD therapies.

title: The Immunomodulatory Role of Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in the Treatment of Asthma.
authors: You F, Gao Q, Li W, Ma N, Guo J, Li X.
ai_summary: This review discusses mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exos), particularly from human umbilical cord MSCs, as a potential immunomodulatory therapy for asthma. Through molecules such as proteins, miRNAs, lncRNAs, and lipids, MSC-Exos can correct Th1/Th2 and Th17/Treg imbalance, inhibit ILC2 activation and inflammasome activity, modulate macrophage polarization, and promote epithelial repair while reducing airway remodeling and oxidative stress. Animal and in vitro studies show anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and tissue-protective effects with low immunogenicity and good biocompatibility, suggesting promise for severe and steroid-resistant asthma. However, evidence remains preclinical, and large-scale randomized controlled trials are still needed to confirm safety, efficacy, and standardized administration.

title: Microbial Signals in Cancer: Dissecting Host-Microbiota-Tumor Interactions and Potential Therapeutic Strategy.
authors: Lu J, Xuan M, Yu L, Xie Z, Chu Q, Wei S, Wang T, Xue C, Li L.
ai_summary: This review examines how the host-microbiota-tumor axis influences cancer, covering the origins and colonization of intratumoral bacteria, fungi, and viruses, and the signaling pathways they engage (TLR-NF-κB, cGAS-STING, Wnt/β-catenin, JAK-STAT, PI3K-AKT). It discusses how microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and tryptophan derivatives reshape immune cell phenotypes and tumor metabolism, and synthesizes evidence linking microbiota to immune checkpoint blockade response, chemotherapy resistance, radiotherapy toxicity, diagnosis, and prognosis. The authors also compare translational strategies—fecal microbiota transplantation, engineered bacteria, oncolytic viruses, and bacteriophages—along with their safety and standardization barriers, arguing that the field must move from fragmented descriptive associations toward causal, biomarker-guided microbiota interventions.

title: The dual roles of Prevotella in gastrointestinal tumorigenesis: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic prospects.
authors: Lu Z, Tang D.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that the genus Prevotella plays context-dependent, dual roles in gastrointestinal tumorigenesis rather than acting in a single direction. Pro-tumorigenic strains such as Prevotella intermedia correlate with malignant progression, though human causal evidence remains limited, while other strains may be protective, largely via production of short-chain fatty acids, especially butyrate, as suggested by preclinical and correlational human data. The review emphasizes that this duality is shaped by strain-level heterogeneity, diet, microbial community context, and anatomical localization, and it distinguishes associative from causal evidence while exploring translational strategies that exploit these opposing effects for cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Intranasal essential oils in therapy: advances in clinical applications and delivery mechanisms.
authors: Yong L, Qiuyan G, Yi C, Wei WU, Ming Y, Fangrui T, Yawen W, Deng P, Xiaoying H, Huiting LI.
journal: Journal of traditional Chinese medicine = Chung i tsa chih ying wen pan
ai_summary: This review summarizes preclinical and clinical evidence on intranasal delivery of essential oils (EOs) for neurological, respiratory, cardiovascular, and metabolic disorders. Advanced formulations such as nanoemulsions, liposomes, and in situ nasal gels improve EO stability, bioavailability, and targeted release, while mechanistic effects appear to operate through neurotransmission modulation, anti-inflammatory pathways, and vascular regulation via the olfactory and trigeminal nerves. Clinical evidence supports efficacy in anxiety, depression, allergic rhinitis, and hypertension, though irritation and patient adherence remain challenges; the authors call for better in vivo pharmacokinetic tools, optimized delivery systems, and safety assessment to enable broader clinical translation.

title: The lung microbiome and asthma: from inflammatory phenotype differentiation to microbe-based immunomodulatory strategies.
authors: Ren S, Li H, Dong Z, Fang M.
ai_summary: This review examines how the lung microbiome shapes asthma's inflammatory phenotypes and how it might be targeted therapeutically. Distinct asthma inflammatory phenotypes show altered microbial diversity and dominant species, notably colonization by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Tropheryma whipplei. These communities influence CD4+ T-cell subset differentiation and activate or suppress inflammatory pathways, thereby interacting with eosinophilic and neutrophilic phenotypes. Microbial products such as lipopolysaccharide, exosomes, and bacterial lysates activate or suppress host immune cells and mediate airway inflammation. The authors map specific bacterial species to asthma endotypes and critically assess methodological heterogeneity in the field, highlighting immunomodulatory strategies including bacterial lysates, probiotics, and microbial exosome therapy as a basis for standardizing research and advancing microbiome-based precision prevention.

title: Tissue-Resident Macrophage in Inflammation and Cancer.
authors: Huang S, Fan J, Liu W, Liu D, Wang R, Wang Y, Sun J, Zhang H, Cai Q, Xu Z, Xu F, Jiang J, Wang Z, Zeng L.
ai_summary: This review examines tissue-resident macrophages (TRMs), long-lived immune cells whose functional plasticity supports both organ homeostasis and disease. It describes how organ-specific niche signals shape TRM heterogeneity and vulnerability, then traces macrophage dysfunction in sepsis from protective anti-infectious immunity through tipping points to immunoparalysis, and surveys their roles in sterile, autoimmune, Type 2, and metabolic inflammation. In cancer, the tumor microenvironment chronically co-opts TRMs into tumor-associated macrophages that promote angiogenesis, suppress antitumor immunity, drive metastasis, and support cancer stem cells. A cross-disease comparison identifies shared regulatory mechanisms behind macrophages' opposing roles in inflammation versus cancer, and the authors propose shifting therapy from functional blockade toward precise recalibration of macrophage function to restore immune balance in both disease settings.

title: From Symbiont to Potential Carcinogenic Contributor: Examining the Pathogenic Evolution of Morganella morganii in Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Soleymanpour K, Shokouhi B, Kafil HS.
ai_summary: This narrative review evaluates evidence that *Morganella morganii*, a common gut Enterobacteriaceae member, may contribute to adenomatous polyps and colorectal cancer. Its distinguishing feature is production of the genotoxin indolimine, which acts independently of the pks gene cluster and clbI/clbP genes and causes a distinct DNA-damaging pattern (DNA smearing); strains lacking the aat gene show no detectable genotoxic activity, implicating aat in this effect. Drawing on in vitro experiments, animal models, and limited human observational data, the authors propose that M. morganii may drive genetic damage, metabolic changes, and polyp growth, framing CRC as involving activation of genotoxic bacteria and their interaction with the intestinal epithelial microenvironment rather than dysbiosis alone. However, the scarcity of longitudinal human studies means it remains unresolved whether the bacterium is predisposing, initiating, or merely consequential in CRC, and larger human studies of colonization and CRC development are needed to clarify causality.

title: Macular telangiectasia type 2: An update.
authors: Wu L, Chen-Li G, Sanabria MDM.
journal: The Journal of international medical research
ai_summary: Macular telangiectasia type 2 is a genetically complex disorder in which most cases lack an identified causative gene, though dysregulated serine and lipid metabolism—leading to cytotoxic 1-deoxysphingolipid accumulation that damages Müller cells, photoreceptors, and retinal pigment epithelium—is implicated in pathogenesis. Optical coherence tomography angiography indicates vascular changes may arise earlier and in parallel with neurodegeneration rather than as a secondary consequence, and the strong correlation between ellipsoid zone loss and retinal sensitivity supported FDA acceptance of ellipsoid zone loss area as a structural surrogate endpoint for approval of the ciliary neurotrophic factor implant. Therapeutic strategies under investigation include serine supplementation, fenofibrate, gene replacement, and targeting mitochondrial dysfunction.

title: Epigenetic Skeletal Muscle Memory: The Impact of Physical Activity on Aging and Post-Injury Regeneration.
authors: Godlewski A, Wróblewski M, Kuk J, Moritz M, Dobrak F, Kołodziejska R, Woźniak A.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the cellular and epigenetic mechanisms of skeletal muscle memory—including myonuclear retention, persistent DNA methylation changes, chromatin remodeling, transcriptional priming, non-coding RNA regulation, and mitochondrial epigenetic adaptations—and how these interact with satellite cells, fibro-adipogenic progenitors, immune cells, and extracellular matrix remodeling to preserve regenerative competence. Aging progressively erodes this plasticity through epigenetic drift, chronic inflammation, altered macrophage states, satellite cell dysfunction, persistent fibro-adipogenic progenitor activity, fibrosis, mitochondrial impairment, and anabolic resistance, contributing to sarcopenia. Training-detraining-retraining studies show that parts of the exercise-induced epigenetic landscape persist after training cessation and can be reactivated by renewed loading, though the durability and functional significance of individual signatures remain unclear. Exercise is the best-established intervention for preserving muscle function and epigenetic responsiveness, while caloric restriction, nutrient-sensing pathway modulation, senolytics, and direct targeting of epigenetic regulators remain promising but less translationally mature; preserving epigenetic plasticity may be a key determinant of healthy muscle aging and regeneration.

title: Intratumoral microbiota in the growth of CRC and lung cancer: Comprehensive insights from etiology to therapy.
authors: Wang Y, Li J, Du X, Li W, Wang D, Li Y.
ai_summary: This review compares the intratumoral microbiota (ITM) of colorectal and lung cancer, two anatomically distinct cancers connected by the gut-lung axis, and surveys detection methods from cultivation and sequencing to spatial and single-cell technologies. Oral pathobionts including Fusobacterium nucleatum, Streptococcus, and Veillonella accumulate in both tumor types and drive tumorigenesis via chronic inflammation, immune evasion, genotoxic damage, and metabolic reprogramming, with venous drainage and systemic dissemination linking them to colorectal cancer lung metastasis. Microbial signatures in stool, saliva, blood, and tumor tissue may serve as non-invasive tools for detection, prognosis, and predicting immunotherapy resistance, while antibiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, and engineered live biotherapeutics offer ways to remodel the tumor microenvironment. The authors position the gut-lung axis as a systemic driver of metastasis and outline a path toward precision microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

title: Differential Modulation of Keratinocyte Proliferation, Differentiation, and Barrier Function by Hemp Oil, Blackcurrant Seed Oil, and Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> Under Atopic-Associated Cytokine Stimulation.
authors: Tortolani D, Scipioni L, Anselmucci A, Ciaramellano F, Di Leonardo M, Fusaro I, Oddi S, Gramenzi A.
ai_summary: An in vitro canine keratinocyte model of atopic-like inflammation (cytokine cocktail of IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-13) was used to compare hemp oil, blackcurrant seed oil, vitamin D3, and their combination. The cocktail reproduced an AD-like phenotype (increased Ki-67, reduced CLDN1, nitrosative stress, NRF2/BACH1 induction, and secretion of STAT1/NF-κB-dependent mediators). The treatments showed distinct, pathway-specific effects: vitamin D3 (alone or combined) was the strongest modulator of proliferation and acted on the downstream redox arm (inducing HMOX1, reducing BACH1) with broad anti-inflammatory activity; hemp oil preferentially improved tight-junction integrity (CLDN1), the upstream NRF2 arm, STAT1 chemokines, and wound closure; blackcurrant seed oil mainly reduced NF-κB-dependent IL-8 and affected early wound closure. These differential profiles support further study of these formulations as nutraceutical adjuncts in canine atopic dermatitis.

title: The microbiome as a systems-level regulator of immune, metabolic, neural, and endocrine signaling in cancer.
authors: Bautista J, López-Cortés A.
ai_summary: This review argues that the human microbiome acts as a systems-level regulator of cancer biology by integrating immune, metabolic, neural, and endocrine signals. Microbial dysbiosis is linked to sustained inflammation, genomic instability, and epigenetic reprogramming, while microbiome-derived metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and tryptophan derivatives mediate host signaling through shared pathways including NF-κB, STAT3, and WNT/β-catenin, thereby influencing tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic response. Microbiome profiles are proposed as diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarkers, though clinical use is limited by methodological variability, cohort heterogeneity, and lack of causal validation.

title: Clinical pearls and pitfalls in inborn errors of immunity: An expert-derived framework for diagnostic pattern recognition.
authors: Vásquez Echeverri E, Bustamante-Ogando JC, Castano-Jaramillo LM, Vélez Tirado N, Venegas Montoya E, Gómez Tello H, Palma A, Guaní-Guerra E, Ale H, Yamazaki-Nakashimada MA, Sullivan KE, Lugo Reyes SO.
journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
ai_summary: This expert survey compiled over 150 clinical pearls for diagnosing inborn errors of immunity, organized into six categories (red flags, category-suggestive signs, highly specific and highly sensitive findings, expected phenotypes, and practical wisdom). Key pearls included disseminated BCG/mycobacterial disease, very early-onset IBD, and infant lymphopenia as red flags; microthrombocytopenia for Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, catalase-positive infections for chronic granulomatous disease, and ataxia with telangiectasias for ataxia-telangiectasia as highly specific findings. Important caveats were that normal mean platelet volume does not exclude Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, normal IgG may mask antibody deficiency in older ataxia-telangiectasia patients, and absent fever during serious bacterial infection suggests IRAK4/MyD88 deficiency. The authors note that phenotypes evolve over time and that general-purpose large language models underrepresented this type of experiential clinical wisdom.

title: Integrative management of gastric cardia cancer and precancerous lesions: prospects and mechanistic rationale for Banxia Xiexin Tang.
authors: Liang X, Yang L, Zhang Y, Yuan S, Hong Y.
ai_summary: This narrative review examines the integrative management of gastric cardia cancer and its precancerous lesions, emphasizing the inflammation-metaplasia-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence and the distinct biology of tumors at the gastroesophageal junction compared with non-cardia gastric cancer and esophageal adenocarcinoma. It evaluates Banxia Xiexin Tang (BXT), a seven-botanical formula, whose preclinical and supportive-care studies suggest possible modulation of inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier injury, and treatment-related gastrointestinal toxicity. The authors stress that the evidence base is uneven and largely extrapolated from gastritis, reflux injury, or non-cardia gastric disease models rather than human gastric cardia cancer, and they synthesize findings narratively due to heterogeneity across studies, explicitly flagging what the data do and do not support and identifying remaining research gaps.

title: Balancing act of cytokines in controlling the severity of Clostridioides difficile infection.
authors: Mears KS, Abt MC.
ai_summary: This review examines how the innate immune response, particularly cytokine signaling, determines the severity of Clostridioides difficile infection. It emphasizes that effective immunity requires a careful balance: controlling C. difficile pathology and preventing systemic spread of opportunistic bacteria while avoiding collateral immunopathology, and simultaneously promoting repair of toxin-induced intestinal barrier damage. The authors focus specifically on the role of innate immune-induced cytokines in shaping these outcomes.

title: Targeting pyroptosis for skeletal muscle atrophy: mechanistic insights and therapeutic perspectives.
authors: Sun CC, Peng TJ, Zhang P, Fan XL, Lu CT, Jiang HL, Tang CF.
ai_summary: This review examines the role of pyroptosis—a Gasdermin-mediated form of programmed cell death accompanied by intense inflammation—in skeletal muscle atrophy. It describes how the core NLRP3–caspase-1–GSDMD signalling axis drives release of inflammatory cytokines, creating and sustaining a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that promotes protein degradation. The authors conclude that pyroptosis exacerbates muscle atrophy both by directly damaging myofibres and by fostering this chronic inflammatory milieu, and they summarise potential intervention strategies targeting pyroptosis while discussing challenges and prospects for clinical translation.

title: Virobiome-mediated regulation of microbiota-gut-brain axis signaling and neuroimmune homeostasis.
authors: Afkhamian A, Saffari Natanzi A, Jafaridarabjerdi M, Aghaei S, Haghjou A, Shafiei M, Bashkandi AH, Shahraki S, Reiter RJ, Haddad Kashani H, Yang Y.
ai_summary: This narrative review argues that the gut virome is an underappreciated regulator of microbiota-gut-brain axis signaling and neuroimmune homeostasis. Bacteriophages shape microbial community structure via lytic/lysogenic cycles, horizontal gene transfer, and metabolic modulation, indirectly affecting neuroactive metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids and tryptophan derivatives that influence blood-brain barrier integrity and microglial activation. Eukaryotic viruses including Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus are linked in human and experimental studies to systemic inflammation, molecular mimicry, and cytokine dysregulation, amplifying neuroimmune cascades implicated in Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, autism spectrum disorder, and major depressive disorder. The authors propose a transkingdom signaling model and discuss emerging interventions (precision phage therapy, CRISPR-based antiviral probiotics, fecal virome transplantation) and the need for multiomics plus AI-driven modeling to clarify temporal and mechanistic links between virome dynamics and neurological function.

title: Regulation of macrophage polarization in chronic airway inflammatory diseases: immune interactions, metabolic reprogramming, and beyond.
authors: Zhang H, Meng C, Zhu D.
ai_summary: This review examines how macrophage polarization contributes to chronic upper and lower airway inflammatory diseases such as allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis, and bronchial asthma. It summarizes the crosstalk between polarized macrophages and other immune cells in driving persistent inflammation, and highlights metabolic reprogramming as a central mechanism governing macrophage phenotype and function. The authors propose that targeting these metabolic pathways could offer new strategies for precise treatment of chronic airway inflammatory diseases.

title: Natural polysaccharides as immune adjuvants to overcome immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance: mechanistic insights, clinical evidence, and translational challenges.
authors: Li Y, Qian J, Zhou S, Wang C, Cai.
ai_summary: Natural polysaccharides can act as immune adjuvants to overcome immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) resistance, which otherwise limits efficacy in most solid tumors. The review details four mechanisms: repolarizing tumor-associated macrophages toward anti-tumor phenotypes, alleviating CD8+ T cell exhaustion, regulating gut microbiota-immune crosstalk, and inhibiting tumor-intrinsic immune escape. Preclinical and early-phase clinical evidence suggests synergy between polysaccharides and ICIs, but large randomized Phase III evidence is lacking, and translational barriers remain (structural heterogeneity, nonstandard quality control, low oral bioavailability, inconsistent trial protocols). The authors propose AI-assisted glycomics, synthetic biology, and a biomarker-guided precision medicine workflow to advance clinical translation.

title: Molecular mechanisms of bacteria-mediated cancer immunotherapy: from intratumoral microbiota to engineered therapeutics.
authors: Guo J, Li Y, Yang Y, Wang B.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms by which intratumoral bacteria influence malignancy—through genotoxicity, epigenetic reprogramming, metabolic competition, and modulation of the tumor-immune interface—and surveys engineering strategies (quorum-sensing circuits, thermo-inducible switches, molecular mimicry, biohybrid microrobots) that turn commensal or attenuated strains into precision delivery vehicles for cytokines, checkpoint inhibitors, and neoantigens. It critically evaluates translational bottlenecks including safety, pharmacokinetics, regulatory science, and inter-patient heterogeneity, and proposes an AI-guided, microbiome-integrated framework to accelerate clinical translation and convert immunologically "cold" tumors into therapy-sensitive "hot" lesions.

title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis in rheumatoid arthritis: mechanisms linking intestinal barrier dysfunction to synovial inflammation.
authors: Hafezi S, Saheb Sharif-Askari F, Saheb Sharif-Askari N, Wed Eladham M, S Zayat A, Halwani R.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence for a gut-joint axis in rheumatoid arthritis, positioning gut microbiota dysbiosis as one contributor within a broader mechanistic network rather than a sole initiating factor. Compromised intestinal barrier integrity and microbial imbalance are proposed to permit translocation of microbial products, driving immune activation and loss of tolerance via molecular mimicry, protein citrullination, and Th17/Treg imbalance, thereby connecting mucosal immunity to synovial inflammation. RA patients frequently show reduced short-chain fatty acid production—especially butyrate—linked to lower abundances of SCFA-producing bacteria such as Faecalibacterium and Roseburia and reduced fecal and circulating butyrate, which may worsen inflammation and impair immune homeostasis. Gut-imprinted immune cells may also migrate to joints through shared homing pathways, amplifying local inflammation. The authors conclude that the gut-joint axis is a promising framework for understanding RA immune dysregulation and that microbiota-targeted interventions warrant consideration as adjunctive therapies.

title: Single-cell genomics, metagenomics, and transcriptomics of Rhizophydium megarrhizum, an obligate fungal parasite of Planktothrix agardhii.
authors: McKindles K, Seto K, Ahrendt S, Salamov A, Chovatia M, Wang M, Barry K, Grigoriev IV, McKay RM, James TY.
ai_summary: This study generated the first reference genomes for chytrid fungi infecting the cyanobacterium Planktothrix agardhii, using single-cell sequencing and metagenomic assembly of isolates collected from Lake Erie's Sandusky Bay across two bloom years. The ~15.36 Mbp genomes were about 75% complete, and a pangenome revealed conserved gene content across isolates, with gene ontology categories related to cellular structure, biosynthetic regulation, and interspecies interactions. Preliminary RNA sequencing indicated that the chytrids consistently express high levels of cytoskeletal genes and many hypothetical proteins, with zoospores possibly upregulating carbohydrate-binding proteins for host recognition, while the host showed transcriptional shifts in buoyancy and nutrient-acquisition pathways that could reflect defense or parasite manipulation.

title: High-fructose diet-induced gut dysbiosis as a mechanistic driver of chronic inflammation and accelerated biological aging: a comprehensive review.
authors: Xu XZ, Dong MS, Dai JY, Wang QY, Dong XC, Jin Y.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes the mechanistic cascade by which a high-fructose diet drives accelerated biological aging. Excess fructose is rapidly metabolized via ketohexokinase (KHK), depleting ATP and generating uric acid and ROS, which activate NLRP3 and NF-κB and promote hepatic de novo lipogenesis. In parallel, fructose selectively depletes butyrate-producing taxa (Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Roseburia spp.) while enriching Gram-negative Proteobacteria, raising luminal LPS; butyrate loss downregulates tight junction proteins (ZO-1, occludin, claudin-1), causing barrier failure and metabolic endotoxemia. Circulating LPS then sustains TLR4-MyD88-NF-κB signaling and chronic TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β expression, forming a self-reinforcing dysbiosis → leaky gut → endotoxemia → NF-κB → NLRP3 "inflammaging" loop. This sustained inflammation accelerates aging through five pathways: cellular senescence/SASP propagation, ROS-mediated telomeric and DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction via the mtROS-cGAS-STING axis, epigenetic clock acceleration (DNMT3A/B, H3K27ac/me3 remodeling), and immunosenescence (TEMRA accumulation, Treg dysfunction, M1 polarization). The authors outline five intervention categories—dietary fructose restriction/Mediterranean diet, probiotics/prebiotics, bile acid FXR/TGR5 modulation with SCFA supplementation, senolytics/NAD⁺ precursors/mTOR-AMPK agents, and fecal microbiota transplantation—noting clinical improvements in glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, and SASP attenuation, though responses vary with baseline microbiota composition.

title: The Association Between Gut Microbiome and Cachexia in Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review.
authors: Hachani M, Gwenzi T, Schöttker B, Puschhof J, Stein-Thöringer C, Panagiotou G, Brenner H, Hoffmeister M.
ai_summary: This systematic review of 15 studies (13 preclinical, 2 clinical) found that colorectal cancer cachexia is associated with gut microbiome alterations, including reduced alpha diversity, depleted butyrate-producing taxa, and enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae and other pathobionts in murine models; some changes occurred independently of food intake and correlated with inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and muscle wasting. Limited clinical evidence from a single cohort linked higher pre-surgical Fusobacterium nucleatum and lower Porphyromonas and Actinomyces abundance to cachexia onset. Causality, directionality, and clinical relevance remain uncertain.

title: Citrullination-associated transcriptional states identify a non-canonical invasive program in malignant epithelial cells and correlate with SPP1-CD44 immune microenvironment niches in thyroid cancer.
authors: Tian Z, Zhu P, Zhao X, Yang F.
ai_summary: This study integrated single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data from thyroid cancer to define a citrullination-associated malignant epithelial state, quantified by a PADI-family-based CitrScore that was enriched in malignant cells. This state was linked to a non-canonical invasive transcriptional program and correlated with SPP1-CD44 signaling in the immune microenvironment. Functional experiments in TPC-1 and 8505C cells showed that CD44 knockdown and overexpression modulated pro-tumorigenic behavior, and in silico CD44 knockout supported the SPP1-CD44 axis as a macrophage-malignant communication hub, nominating CD44 as a candidate therapeutic target.

title: Does the ERBB/EGF Signaling Network Serve as a Nexus for Oncogenic Signals in Uveal Melanoma?
authors: Raeesian N, Riese DJ.
ai_summary: This review examines the biology and pharmacotherapy of uveal melanoma, focusing on the ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase/EGF growth factor signaling network and its crosstalk with G protein-coupled receptors. It highlights signaling changes thought to drive uveal melanoma, particularly increased signaling through the CYSLTR2/Gαq/Gα11 pathway, and proposes that some oncogenic signaling in this cancer may arise from crosstalk between that pathway and the ERBB/EGF network. The authors conclude that the ERBB/EGF signaling network may represent a novel therapeutic target for uveal melanoma.

title: The CCHCR1-UBAP2L Interaction Promotes UBAP2L Release from P-Bodies for Stress Granule Assembly.
authors: Ye Z, Xu M, Lin C, Sze SCW, Li C.
ai_summary:
Gene: CCHCR1
Finding: CCHCR1 directly binds UBAP2L in a stress-intensity-dependent manner, retaining it in P-bodies under mild oxidative stress and releasing it to enable stress granule assembly as stress intensifies; CCHCR1 deficiency traps UBAP2L in P-bodies via enhanced DDX6 association, causing defective and delayed stress granule assembly and increased P-body–stress granule fusion.
Disease: Stress granule biogenesis defects (cellular stress response phenotype)

title: Insights into IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling in the tumor microenvironment: Implications for cancer therapy.
authors: Thuya WL, Cao Y, Ho PC, Wong AL, Wang L, Zhou J, Nicot C, Goh BC.
ai_summary:
Gene: STAT3
Finding: The IL-6/JAK/STAT3 axis drives tumor growth, immune evasion, metabolic reprogramming, and therapy resistance by shaping an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and its inhibition (via anti-IL-6/IL-6R antibodies, JAK inhibitors, or STAT3-specific inhibitors) can suppress tumor growth, reverse immune suppression, and enhance immunotherapy efficacy.
Disease: Cancer

title: Microbiome-Driven Mechanisms in Breast Cancer: Emerging Evidence From Gut Microbial Signatures to Therapeutic Response.
authors: Wali AF, Talath S, Rangraze IR, El-Tanani M, Khan S.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on the gut–breast cancer axis, organizing it around four proposed mechanisms: immune modulation, estrobolome-mediated estrogen recycling, chronic inflammatory signaling, and microbial metabolite-driven epigenetic and metabolic regulation. It reports that microbial dysbiosis, reduced diversity, and enrichment of proinflammatory taxa are associated with tumor progression, subtype-specific biology, and variable therapeutic response, and that microbiome composition can affect the efficacy and toxicity of chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. The review also surveys microbiome-targeted interventions—probiotics, dietary modulation, postbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation—while noting unresolved challenges in mechanistic validation, profiling standardization, cross-cohort reproducibility, and clinical implementation, and calls for longitudinal multiomics and functional studies to enable clinically actionable microbiome interventions.

title: Pervasive relaxed selection on spermatogenesis genes coincident with the evolution of polygyny in gorillas.
authors: Bowman JD, Silva N, Schüftan E, Almeida JM, Brattig-Correia R, Oliveira RA, Tüttelmann F, Enard D, Navarro-Costa P, Lynch VJ.
ai_summary: This study investigated the molecular basis of the eroded male reproductive system in gorillas, whose polygynous mating system sharply reduces sperm competition. Comparing 13,310 orthologous protein-coding genes across 261 Eutherian mammals, the authors found 578 genes under relaxed purifying selection in the gorilla lineage versus only 96 positively selected genes. The relaxed genes accumulated deleterious amino acid substitutions, were preferentially expressed in male germ cells, and were enriched for meiosis and sperm biology functions. Using Drosophila, they identified 41 novel spermatogenesis genes required for normal fertility, and in exome/genome data from infertile men with severe spermatogenic impairment, human orthologs of the gorilla relaxed genes were enriched for loss-of-function variants. The authors conclude that reduced sperm competition in gorillas is associated with relaxed purifying selection on male reproductive genes, and that the resulting accumulation of deleterious mutations likely explains the low efficacy of gorilla spermatogenesis while nominating new candidate genes for human male infertility.

title: Targeting Plasma Membrane Ca<sup>2+</sup>-ATPases in Cancer: Current Insights and Future Perspectives.
authors: Lisek M, Tomczak J, Bochenska N, Duraj J, Boczek T.
ai_summary: This review examines the emerging roles of plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase (PMCA) isoforms in cancer. Beyond their classical function as calcium extrusion pumps, PMCAs organize compartmentalized calcium signaling microdomains by interacting with receptors, channels, and scaffold proteins, thereby selectively influencing tumor growth and metastasis. The authors highlight isoform-specific, context-dependent functions: PMCA1 contributes to basal calcium homeostasis and has been implicated in tumor progression, angiogenesis, and the tumor immune microenvironment; PMCA2 promotes survival and oncogenic signaling in HER2-positive breast cancer via stabilization of receptor signaling complexes; PMCA3 is linked mainly to endocrine tumors with limited mechanistic evidence; and PMCA4 shows the greatest functional diversity, acting as either tumor suppressor or promoter depending on cancer type. The review also discusses PMCAs as potential prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, emphasizing the need for isoform-specific strategies.

title: Differential effects of environmental enrichment and physical exercise on glial biology in aging and aging-related conditions: a systematic review.
authors: Singhal G, Baune BT.
ai_summary: This systematic review compared how environmental enrichment (EE), physical exercise (PE), and their combination affect glial cells during aging, synthesizing rodent and other preclinical studies identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar (PRISMA 2020, SYRCLE risk-of-bias assessment). EE was consistently linked to increased microglial number and morphological complexity and to modulation of peripheral T cell subsets, especially after long-term exposure, whereas PE more reliably reversed age-related microglial gene expression changes and produced region-specific astrocytic remodeling. Combining EE and PE gave additive benefits for neurogenesis but variable, non-superior effects on glial modulation. BDNF-TrkB signaling and inflammatory cascades mediated these outcomes, with neuroimmune crosstalk (notably peripheral T cells) influencing central glial states. The authors conclude that EE and PE have distinct but partially overlapping effects—EE acting more on glial-immune interfaces, PE more on metabolic/anti-inflammatory glial remodeling—and that methodological heterogeneity and limited sex-specific analyses restrict generalizability.

title: All-optical visualization of specific molecules in the ultrastructural context of brain tissue.
authors: M'Saad O, Cairns A, Gulcicek J, Kasula RK, Liao J, Kondratiuk I, Bewersdorf EH, Kidd P, Falahati H, Gentile JE, Niescier RF, Watters K, Sterner RC, Lee SI, Guo X, Liu X, Desir G, De Camilli P, Rothman JE, Koleske AJ, Biederer T, Kuan AT, Bewersdorf J.
ai_summary: This paper introduces pan-ExM-t, an all-optical imaging method that combines 16-24-fold linear tissue expansion with fluorescent pan-staining of proteins and lipids to provide electron-microscopy-like ultrastructural context, alongside immunolabeling for molecular specificity. The authors used it to image synaptic and cell-type-specific antibodies within the 3D nanoscale context of pre- and postsynaptic densities, neuropil architecture, and organelles in cultured neurons and mouse brain sections, and further showed that neuronal circuitry can be traced from the resulting image volumes. The approach allows any lab with a confocal microscope to localize specific molecules within nanoscale cellular and circuit contexts.

title: Spatial niche remodeling of senescent liver-resident immune cells and its role in chronic liver diseases.
authors: Mao F, Shan K.
ai_summary: This review proposes a "spatial niche remodeling" framework to explain how liver-resident immune cells (Kupffer cells, LSECs, HSCs, DCs, TRM, innate-like T cells, ILCs, and neutrophils) undergo senescence-associated reprogramming along the portal-to-central axis of the hepatic lobule during aging and chronic injury. It integrates cell-intrinsic senescence mechanisms—telomere dysfunction and p53/p21 and p16/Rb activation, mtDNA leakage driving SASP via cGAS-STING, epigenetic age acceleration such as H3K27me3 heterochromatinization, and glycolytic/lipid metabolic reprogramming—with lobular context and rewired intercellular communication, linking these changes to the progression from steatosis through steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors also assess senotherapeutic strategies targeting specific immune subsets, barriers to clinical translation, and priorities such as spatial multi-omics, humanized models, and epigenetic clock-guided trials.

title: Postbiotics Against Breast Cancer: A Narrative Review Bridging Preclinical Evidence with Potential Clinical Application.
authors: Luongo C, Di Santillo R, Cadavere A, Oglio F, Pisapia L, Gaeta A, Scocco C, López-Cánovas JL, Michelini M, De Aloe M, Lintura A, Chumsri S, Canani RB.
ai_summary: This narrative review summarizes preclinical evidence that postbiotics—non-viable microbial cells, their components, and metabolites—exert dose- and time-dependent anticancer effects across multiple breast cancer subtypes by modulating oncogenic pathways such as PI3K/AKT and NF-κB and by inhibiting histone deacetylases. Postbiotics also reshape the tumor microenvironment, altering cytokine networks, suppressing pro-metastatic inflammation, and activating NK and T cell antitumor responses, with emerging links to microbiome composition, estrobolome activity, and subtype-specific biology. However, clinical translation lags: only one registered postbiotic oncology trial exists (in melanoma) and none in breast cancer, underscoring the need for tumor-specific clinical trials to validate safety and efficacy.

title: Regulatory T cell induction strategies and applications in the treatment of immune and non-immune diseases.
authors: Chen Y, Shi Y, You J.
ai_summary: This review surveys strategies for inducing regulatory T cells (Tregs), spanning antigenic stimulation, cytokine modulation, metabolic pathways, epigenetic regulation, drug induction, and engineered technologies. The authors argue that no single approach adequately resolves challenges of Treg stability, target specificity, and large-scale production, and propose that integrating multiple induction strategies is key to developing more functional and broadly applicable Treg therapies. The paper also reviews therapeutic applications of Tregs in immune diseases (autoimmune disease, organ transplantation, allergic asthma, cancer) and non-immune diseases (insulin resistance, tissue repair, fibrotic diseases, osteoporosis), and discusses current research bottlenecks and future directions for Treg-based cell therapy.

title: Role of Oral-Lung Infection Axis on Respiratory Health.
authors: Unlu O, Demirci M, Kantarci A.
ai_summary: This review examines the oral-lung infection axis, arguing that oral dysbiosis—particularly proliferation of the red complex pathogens (Porphyromonas gingivalis, Treponema denticola, Tannerella forsythia)—drives chronic systemic inflammation that contributes to respiratory disease. It evaluates three pathways (metastatic infection, injury, and inflammation) by which oral pathobionts and their bioactive components (lipopolysaccharides, outer membrane vesicles, matrix metalloproteinases) reach the lower respiratory tract via microaspiration and hematogenous spread. The authors link reduced oral microbial diversity to COPD pathogenesis, modulation of the pulmonary virome and mycobiome, and maladaptive trained immunity, and assess contributions of immunosenescence, inflammaging, and reflex decline. They conclude by proposing clinical translation through saliva-based nano-theranostics, metatranscriptomic profiling, professional oral biofilm management in intensive care, and precision microbiome engineering to preserve respiratory function and restore immune homeostasis.

title: Genetic testing in liver diseases: Clinical applications.
authors: Keitel V, Mentzinger A, Dröge C, Vilarinho S.
ai_summary: This review summarizes the expanding role of genetic testing in adult hepatology, covering cholestatic disorders, unexplained hepatic steatosis, cryptogenic cirrhosis, idiopathic portal hypertension, and acute liver failure. It highlights high-yield, actionable clinical insights for real-world practice and stresses the value of specialized genomic hepatology centers and multidisciplinary Hepatology Genome Rounds. The authors also outline the near-term future of an integrative, liver-centered genomic ecosystem and its expected impact on hepatology training and practice.

title: Mechanisms and Manifestations of Ligand Bias in Signaling: Focus on Receptor Tyrosine Kinases.
authors: Schuck RJ, Roy T, Bondar AN, Krejci P, Hristova K.
ai_summary: This review examines ligand bias—the ability of different ligands to preferentially activate distinct signaling pathways through the same receptor—in the context of receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), the largest family of single-pass membrane receptors. The authors review established protocols for identifying and quantifying biased signaling, summarize evidence that RTKs engage in biased signaling, and discuss how this bias can be exploited in therapeutic design. They draw parallels with the more extensively studied GPCR field, applying lessons learned there to RTK biology, and propose that RTK ligand bias arose during evolution to diversify morphogen signaling pathways governing tissue and organ development in mammals.

title: Retinal glial cells in glaucoma and age-related retinal diseases: Inflammatory responses, disease transitions, and translational perspectives.
authors: Salkar A, Palanivel V, Basavarajappa D, Heng B, Schulz A, Gupta V, Graham S, Mirzaei M, You Y.
ai_summary: This review examines how retinal glial cells (microglia, Müller cells, and astrocytes) are reprogrammed in disease to drive chronic inflammation and neurodegeneration, focusing on shared triggers such as oxidative stress, metabolic dysfunction, aging, and systemic inflammation, and on key signaling pathways including NF-κB, MAPK, JAK/STAT, the inflammasome, and complement. It compares disease-specific glial responses across glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, and vascular occlusions, emphasizing the heterogeneity of gliosis and its contributions to neuronal and vascular pathology.
