The authors highlight emerging human-derived platforms and proteomics for mechanistic and biomarker discovery, while noting major gaps in understanding glial-glial communication, state transitions, and their temporal relationship to neurodegeneration, as well as a shortage of models designed to study glia directly. They argue for a strategic shift toward glia-centered models, integrative multi-omics, and human-relevant systems to reposition glial cells as central drivers of retinal disease and to enable targeted therapies that preserve vision.

title: The Dual Role of Macroglia in Glaucoma: Deciphering the Contributions of Astrocytes and Müller Cells to Retinal Neurodegeneration and Neuroprotection.
authors: Teixeira GR, Costa AGA, Mattos ACL, Souza Monteiro de Araújo D, Brito R, Calaza KDC.
ai_summary: This review examines how astrocytes and Müller cells shape retinal outcomes in glaucoma. Under healthy conditions these macroglia provide structural, homeostatic, and metabolic support to retinal ganglion cells, but sustained pathological stress triggers reactive gliosis with a dichotomous phenotype: initially adaptive and neuroprotective, then shifting to a deleterious state marked by extracellular matrix remodeling, complement activation, and neuroinflammation that worsens RGC death. Mechanosensitive pathways, particularly Piezo1 and TRP channels, are highlighted as key sensors converting physical stress into these reactive cascades within interconnected multicellular networks. The authors conclude by discussing the therapeutic potential of macroglia-directed pharmacological or gene therapies to reprogram the retinal environment.

title: FOXP3 Stability-Adaptation Paradox: Reshaping Treg-Based Therapies for Intestinal Diseases.
authors: Ren Y, Liu X, Wang B, Yin H, Zhao J, Xin S, Wang H, Zhang Y, Liu X, Liu J, Hua R, Tian X, Bian Y, Gu S, Zhang H, Wei T, Gao L, Lu X, Shang H, Gao H, Xu J.
ai_summary:
Gene: FOXP3
Finding: Microbial metabolites and retinoic acid stabilize FOXP3 and promote RORγt⁺/GATA3⁺ Treg specialization, whereas inflammatory cytokines and succinate drive ER stress and post-translational FOXP3 degradation, causing Treg lineage instability that limits current Treg-based therapies and motivates next-generation strategies such as gut-restricted HDAC inhibitors and exhaustion-resistant CAR-Tregs.
Disease: Inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, and celiac disease

title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic characterization of EGFR G719X/S768I double-mutant lung adenocarcinoma identifies an immunosuppressive niche defined by COL4A3-CD44 interaction.
authors: Zhang C, Liu L, Deng R, Lv J, Mei C, Zhang W, Yang L, Yang F, Yang R, Cun Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: CD44
Finding: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of EGFR G719X/S768I double-mutant lung adenocarcinoma revealed an EMT-like malignant subpopulation with a lipid-glycosylation metabolic profile that stabilizes CD44, driving enhanced COL4A3-CD44 crosstalk with immunosuppressive alveolar macrophages that was confirmed by multiplex immunohistochemistry and linked to drug sensitivity vulnerabilities.
Disease: EGFR G719X/S768I double-mutant lung adenocarcinoma

title: Intratumoral microbiota in colorectal cancer: roles, therapeutic potential, and challenges.
authors: Zhang X, Qi J, Dong C, Zhang L, Chen J, Liu J, Jiang T, Song J.
ai_summary: This review examines the emerging role of intratumoral microbiota in colorectal cancer, distinguishing it from the better-studied gut microbiota. It describes a dual role: some intratumoral microbes promote cancer through inflammatory pathways, metabolic alterations, and chemotherapy resistance, while others suppress tumors by modulating immune responses and inducing apoptosis. The authors highlight that specific intratumoral microbial communities are associated with treatment resistance or sensitivity, and that manipulating the microbiota—via probiotics, phage therapy, or fecal microbiota transplantation—could enhance immunotherapy efficacy. They conclude that targeting intratumoral microbiota, supported by multi-omics and clinical research, is a promising strategy for improving CRC treatment and overcoming resistance, while stressing the need for personalized approaches based on microbial biomarkers.

title: Non-caveolar caveolin - 1 in retinal Müller glia promotes innate immune responses.
authors: Enyong EN, Bankole OO, Gurley JM, McClellan ME, Liu L, Ding SY, Agbaga MP, Chucair-Elliott AJ, Ash JD, Elliott MH.
ai_summary:
Gene: CAV1
Finding: In retinal Müller glia, CAV1 exists predominantly outside caveolae (due to minimal CAVIN1/PTRF expression) and promotes TLR4 signaling and LPS-induced IL-6 upregulation via NF-κB activation, whereas CAV1 silencing or CAVIN1/PTRF-mediated sequestration into caveolae suppresses this pro-inflammatory response—an effect opposite to that seen in retinal endothelial cells, where caveolar CAV1 is anti-inflammatory.
Disease: Ocular inflammatory diseases (e.g., primary open angle glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration)

title: O-GlcNAcylation: A molecular switch linking brain health to neurodegeneration.
authors: Shao N, Zhang X, Ge Y, Tang J, Gao H, Si W, Cai B.
ai_summary: O-GlcNAcylation is a post-translational modification balanced by OGT and OGA that regulates protein behavior, cell signaling, and energy metabolism, supporting neuronal function and survival in healthy brains while contributing to neurodegeneration when dysregulated. This review highlights disease-specific effects: in Alzheimer's disease it blocks toxic changes in tau and amyloid-beta; in Parkinson's disease it reduces alpha-synuclein aggregation but may disrupt dopamine production; and in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis it protects nerve fiber transport. It also discusses roles in Huntington's disease, aging, Machado-Joseph disease, multiple sclerosis, and giant axonal neuropathy, and evaluates emerging therapies such as glucosamine supplements and O-GlcNAcase inhibitors, which show clinical promise but face translational challenges.

title: Interleukin 4-driven loss of stromal LIF signaling affects immune responses and cell-cell adhesion in atopic dermatitis.
authors: Feller Y, Malovitski K, Assaf S, Stein Y, Friedman S, Tussia-Cohen D, Khair L, Ishtewy R, Hagai T, Unterman A, Sarig O, Sprecher E, Samuelov L.
ai_summary:
Gene: LIF
Finding: IL-4-driven loss of fibroblast-derived LIF elevates keratinocyte IL-6 production and ERK1/2 activation, reducing desmoglein 1 membrane expression and impairing epidermal cohesion in a self-amplifying inflammatory circuit that can be rescued by blocking IL-6 or ERK1/2.
Disease: Atopic dermatitis

title: DAMPs, PAMPs, and Alarmins: From Mechanism to Therapy.
authors: Yu X, Jin Y, Li B, Deng J, Zhou Y, Zhang J, Li H.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes the molecular sources, sensing mechanisms, and regulatory networks governing pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs)/alarmins, integrating their classical roles in local host defense and maladaptive inflammation with newer concepts such as trained immunity and interorgan communication. It emphasizes the often-overlooked interplay between PAMPs and DAMPs, examines their context-dependent contributions to human disease, and evaluates their emerging potential as biomarkers and targets for immunomodulatory therapy.

title: From Joint Loading to Osteoarthritis: A Multiscale Review of Knee Mechanobiology and Digital Modelling.
authors: Stańczak M, Kacprzak B, Hagner-Derengowska M.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: TRPV4 and PIEZO1/2 mediate overlapping, context-dependent calcium signalling in joint mechanotransduction, but most causal evidence linking these channels to osteoarthritis remains preclinical.
Disease: Osteoarthritis

title: TRPV4-driven ATP release activates CFTR through ADORA2B and P2RY2 receptors in the airway epithelium.
authors: Genovese M, De Santis M, Giordano A, Marotta P, Galietta LJV.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPV4
Finding: TRPV4 activation triggers apical ATP release, and the resulting extracellular ATP/adenosine activates CFTR via P2RY2 and ADORA2B receptors in a paracrine manner, since TRPV4 and CFTR are expressed in distinct epithelial cell types.
Disease: Airway surface hydration and mucociliary clearance defects (airway disease)

title: From mechanical adaptation to innate immune reprogramming in osteoarthritis: a load-immunity framework.
authors: Zuo S, He L, Hou Z, Tian Q, Yang Y, Huang W.
ai_summary: This mini review proposes a "load-immunity" framework for osteoarthritis, asking how specific mechanical loading conditions shift joint-resident cells from reversible mechanoadaptation into persistent innate immune dysregulation, defined as a load-induced change in activation threshold, metabolic state, secretory output, or intercellular behavior that outlasts the initiating mechanical episode. Evidence is organized into three levels: initiating mechanical events; intracellular amplification via calcium overload, mitochondrial stress, NLRP3, and cGAS-STING signaling; and tissue-specific consequences propagated among chondrocytes, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, subchondral bone cells, and sensory neurons. Piezo1, TRPV4, NLRP3, and cGAS-STING are framed as context-dependent nodes rather than uniformly pathogenic switches, and the authors distinguish causal preclinical experiments from human association studies and proposed joint-level networks. They highlight recent evidence that mitochondria-derived extracellular vesicles from infrapatellar fat pad mesenchymal stromal cells can transfer mtDNA to chondrocytes, illustrating extracellular propagation of mitochondrial danger signals, though its quantitative importance in human OA is unresolved. Translationally, load correction has the strongest immediate rationale, while molecular interventions require tissue-specific delivery, disease-stage selection, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and preservation of physiological mechanoadaptation.

title: Molecular and neurovascular mechanisms of thermal sensitivity in teeth.
authors: Kádár K, Al-Khrasani M, Medgyes RA, Acsády S, Kirchlechner-Farkas JM, Shahbazi A, Lohinai ZM, Köles L, Zsembery Á.
ai_summary: This review examines how teeth sense thermal stimuli, particularly cold, through the dentin-pulp complex. It contrasts the direct neural theory (stimuli directly activate trigeminal nerve endings) with the hydrodynamic theory (temperature changes move dentinal fluid within tubules, creating mechanical forces that stimulate pulpal afferents). Growing evidence supports an integrated model in which odontoblasts act as mechanosensory transducers: thermal stimuli generate dentinal fluid movement and mechanical stress that activate ion channels and enzymes in odontoblasts, triggering release of signaling molecules such as ATP, glutamate, and possibly nitric oxide. This thermomechanical coupling mechanism—linking dentinal fluid dynamics, odontoblast mechanotransduction, and neuronal activation—is the most widely accepted explanation for thermal pain and dentin hypersensitivity, and understanding it may improve diagnosis and management of thermal dentin hypersensitivity.

title: Soft tissue mechanosensing and remodeling: the core regulatory role of Piezo/TRPV4 ion channels.
authors: Fan X, Shi M, Wang Z, Zhao C, Zhao Y, Zhou Y, Xu H.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review presents a multiscale framework linking mechanosensitive Piezo1/2 and TRPV4 ion channels to soft tissue fibrosis and chronic pain. It describes how these channels convert membrane tension and integrin-mediated traction into Ca2+ and other ionic signals that, alongside Ca2+-independent pathways, engage YAP/TAZ, NF-κB, and TGF-β signaling to reshape transcriptional programs. The authors conceptualize healthy ECM as a "spatial filter" whose viscoelasticity buffers superficial loads, whereas fibrotic cross-linking erodes this protection, chronically exposing fibroblasts and sensory endings to elevated mechanical and inflammatory cues and driving pathological "stiffness-inflammation-fibrosis/pain" loops. They propose a mechanical therapeutic window in which channel modulation and/or viscoelastic biomaterials reset the local environment toward a near-physiological state, preferentially engaging reparative and inflammation-resolving pathways while minimizing damage and pain amplification.

title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of Survival-Associated CpG Biomarkers in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Zhang BA.
ai_summary: This study integrated DNA methylation data from TCGA and ICGC cohorts to identify epigenetic biomarkers associated with survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Samples were stratified by survival time, yielding 688 differentially methylated CpG sites and 224 CpG biomarkers significantly associated with patient survival. A random forest model predicting survival achieved 85.2% accuracy for short-survival patients and 70.0% for long-survival patients in validation, with external dataset validation confirming robustness. De novo motif analysis implicated TWIST1 and FOXA2 as key transcriptional regulators enriched at survival-associated CpG sites. The findings provide epigenetic biomarkers and a predictive model for post-surgery PDAC risk stratification and personalized therapy.

title: The role of calcium homeostasis dysregulation in allergic rhinitis.
authors: Xiao L, Chen K, Wen Y, Fang Y, Tian L.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes molecular evidence that dysregulated calcium homeostasis acts as a downstream effector and integrative regulatory node across multiple pathological pathways in allergic rhinitis, amplifying and sustaining inflammation. It summarizes Ca2+ signaling roles in maintaining the nasal mucosal barrier, driving immune cell activation, and mediating neurogenic inflammation, along with Ca2+ signaling-related epigenetic modifications in AR. Integrating cross-disease evidence on transgenerational transmission in allergic diseases, the authors propose that calcium homeostasis may modulate offspring susceptibility to AR via epigenetic mechanisms, offering new avenues for understanding AR's transgenerational transmission.

title: From Load-Bearing Tissue to Failed Filter: A Conceptual Framework for Trabecular Meshwork Breakdown in Pseudoexfoliation Glaucoma.
authors: Rao A.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from trabecular meshwork biology, pseudoexfoliation material science, and glaucoma pathophysiology to propose a five-stage conceptual framework for trabecular meshwork failure in pseudoexfoliation glaucoma. It frames the trabecular meshwork as an active load-bearing filtration sieve whose structural breakdown in PXG is driven by pseudoexfoliation fibrillar material deposition and extracellular matrix dysregulation, with both mechanical obstruction and ischemic/oxidative stress implicated. This distinguishes PXG pathogenically from primary open-angle glaucoma and may explain its more severe clinical course and higher intraocular pressure, though the precise mechanism of trabecular dysfunction remains unresolved.

title: The Role of Biomechanical Regulation in Physiological and Pathological Pregnancy: From Mechanotransduction to Clinical Implications.
authors: Wang T, Chen W, Yang H, Yan J.
ai_summary: This review examines how mechanical forces at the maternal-fetal interface shape pregnancy outcomes. It describes how uterine adaptive remodeling in response to fetal growth and increasing amniotic fluid involves extracellular matrix remodeling and altered mechanical properties of the maternal-fetal interface, and it highlights mechanotransduction pathways including PIEZO1, integrins, and YAP/TAZ as key mediators of mechanical signals such as stiffness, shear stress, tension, and compression in both normal and complicated pregnancies. The authors also survey emerging technologies for studying uterine biomechanics and propose that targeting these mechanical signaling pathways could yield new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for pregnancy complications.

title: TP53-META, a meta-analysis tool for comparative transcriptomics of TP53 dependency: examples from target silencing and liver fibrosis.
authors: Keskus AG, Kumak E, Vural-Ozdeniz M, Aftab AM, Tirkayi S, Darde T, Konu O.
ai_summary: TP53-META is a new interactive R Shiny web tool for uploading and jointly analyzing RNA-seq datasets to assess how TP53 depletion or induction shapes the transcriptome, with visualization of expression clusters and transcription factor, pathway, disease-gene, and treatment-gene networks. The authors demonstrated it in two case studies: in MCF7 cells, comparing CHRNA5 knockdown alone versus combined CHRNA5/TP53 knockdown against public datasets separated transcriptomic changes dependent on TP53 signaling from those occurring independently of it; and using user-uploaded public datasets, they identified commonly modulated TP53-related genes in liver fibrosis. The tool is intended to help researchers integrate TP53-related transcriptomic data across sources and uncover robust, context-specific expression patterns.

title: Mapping Leak Electron Pathways from Mitochondria to the Outer Cell Membrane in Human Embryonic Lung Fibroblasts.
authors: Gao G, Wang H, Ding Y, Guo J, Zhou J, Ke L, Rao P, Zhang S, Chen T, Shaw C, Gu H.
ai_summary: The study used human embryonic lung fibroblasts expressing the superoxide indicator cpYFP on microtubules, actin, and integrin to track reactive oxygen species. All three transgenic strains fluoresced, revealing a ROS pathway extending from mitochondria to the outer cell membrane. Fluorescence intensity correlated positively with mitochondrial superoxide content and aerobic respiratory intensity but was independent of cytosolic ROS levels, suggesting that electrons leaking from the electron transport chain are transported out of the cell in electron form rather than being fully disposed of intracellularly. The authors propose this challenges current understanding of ROS generation and homeostasis.

title: Crosstalk of noradrenergic Ca<sup>2+</sup> and cAMP signaling in astrocytes of the murine olfactory bulb.
authors: Sauer J, Beiersdorfer A, Schmidt FL, Nordbeck M, Constantin O, Hirnet D, Gee CE, Lohr C.
ai_summary: This study dissects how noradrenergic signaling engages both Ca²⁺ and cAMP pathways in mouse olfactory bulb astrocytes. Norepinephrine raises both messengers through α₁ and α₂ adrenergic receptors, while β receptors elevate cAMP alone. The α₁ agonist phenylephrine increases cAMP via α₁A/α₁D receptors and the Ca²⁺/calmodulin-dependent adenylyl cyclases AC1 and AC3, an effect that requires intact Ca²⁺ signaling and is lost when Ca²⁺ is depleted. α₂ receptor stimulation also raises Ca²⁺ and promotes cAMP production through AC1/AC3, yet simultaneously inhibits adenylyl cyclase via Gi, as shown by reduced forskolin-induced cAMP responses. The findings reveal intricate, subtype-specific crosstalk between Ca²⁺ and cAMP signaling in these astrocytes.

title: Intestinal muscularis in health and disease.
authors: Yang W, Yang J, Zou Q, Tu H.
ai_summary: This review describes the intestinal muscularis as a multifunctional tissue in which enteric neurons, smooth muscle cells, and immune cells interact to coordinate motility, immune responses, and tissue homeostasis. It argues that beyond peristalsis, the muscularis acts as an active regulatory hub integrating neural, immune, and microbial signals, and it surveys how disruption of these integrated neuromuscular and immune networks drives pathological remodeling in inflammatory bowel diseases, irritable bowel syndrome, infection, and Hirschsprung disease.

title: Proteomic Analyses of Early Versus Advanced Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Uncover Biochemical Signatures Associated With Disease Staging.
authors: Zhou TE, Mathew DJ, Wigg K, Chan D, Zhang JW, Balian C, Kherani IN, Schlenker MB, Jurisica I, Sivak JM.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRPC6
Finding: Large-scale proteomic profiling of aqueous humor from patients with mild versus advanced primary open-angle glaucoma revealed stage-specific enrichment of proinflammatory and immune pathways and identified soluble TRPC6 as a novel biomarker correlating with clinical parameters such as intraocular pressure and retinal outcomes.
Disease: Primary open-angle glaucoma

title: Micro/Nanorobots (MNRs) at the Intersection of Mechanobiology and Artificial Intelligence: An Emerging Frontier for Precision Nanomedicine.
authors: Afsari T, Harmouch J, Sharma R, Liu R, Mohapatra S, Mohapatra SS.
ai_summary: This review argues that micro/nanorobots (MNRs) should be understood not merely as propelled drug carriers but as mechanobiology-driven systems, since their propulsion-generated forces and flows act as mechanical cues that engage cellular mechanosensing—membrane tension, ion-channel activation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and downstream transcriptional signaling. The authors propose "force-to-function coupling" as a unifying design principle that links propulsion dynamics to defined mechanotransduction outcomes at the nano-bio interface, rather than classifying MNRs by actuation modality alone. They further describe how artificial intelligence can contribute predictive modeling, imaging-guided feedback, and closed-loop optimization for programmable biological outputs under physiological uncertainty, and outline translational challenges for biology-aware, intelligent MNRs in precision nanomedicine.

title: The airway epithelial-immune axis: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
authors: Zhu Z, Li Q, Hua B.
ai_summary: This review describes how the airway epithelium actively regulates mucosal immunity rather than serving only as a passive barrier. Environmental allergens, pollutants, and pathogens disrupt epithelial tight junctions and trigger release of alarmins (TSLP, IL-33, IL-25), which drive reciprocal crosstalk with innate (ILC2) and adaptive (Th2) immune networks, creating self-perpetuating inflammatory loops that contribute to asthma, COPD, and upper airway inflammatory disorders. The authors highlight therapeutic strategies targeting this axis, including alarmin-neutralizing biologics, upstream receptor inhibition, and barrier restoration, and discuss how single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, organoid models, and multi-omics are revealing cellular heterogeneity and spatial niches to advance precision medicine.

title: Central nervous system lymphatic network: from the maintenance of brain homeostasis to emerging therapeutic perspectives in neurodegenerative diseases.
authors: Ding S, Yang J, Wang Z, Bai R, Yin K, Jin L, Kueckelhaus M, Meuth SG, Xiao M, Hu G.
ai_summary: This review describes the central drainage network — comprising the glymphatic system, meningeal lymphatic vessels, and cranial perineural drainage pathways — which clears metabolic waste from the brain and helps maintain brain homeostasis, aided by immune cells in the meninges and perivascular spaces. Dysfunction of this network is widely seen in aging and neurodegenerative disorders, marked by mislocalized aquaporin-4 on astrocytic endfeet, impaired lymphatic valvular integrity, and altered meningeal immune cell populations. The authors review its anatomy, regulatory mechanisms, and physiology, summarize its pathological roles across neurodegenerative conditions, and discuss emerging multimodal imaging and liquid biomarker assessments, as well as therapeutic strategies such as restoring meningeal lymphatic function, targeting glymphatic drainage, and modulating the meningeal immune microenvironment.

title: Motion as Medicine: Physical Activity, Joint Sensitivity, and Pain Management-A Narrative Review.
authors: Labusca L, Puha B, Dmour BA, Onu I, Tirnovanu MC, Tîrnovanu ȘD, Dmour A.
ai_summary: This narrative review reframes physical activity as a continuous physiological regulator of synovial joint biology rather than merely a strengthening or weight-control intervention. Synthesizing evidence across mechanical, fluidic, immune-metabolic, and sensory domains, it describes the joint as a dynamic mechano-fluidic organ in which movement promotes synovial fluid exchange, lubrication, cartilage nutrition, matrix turnover, anti-inflammatory signaling, proprioception, and exercise-induced hypoalgesia, whereas inactivity and unloading impair fluid dynamics and promote stiffness, inflammation, and sensory deconditioning, and excessive loading disrupts homeostasis via matrix injury and nociceptive sensitization. The authors propose an "adaptive loading window"—a hypothesis-generating framework, not a validated threshold—within which joint function and pain regulation are supported without tissue or symptom aggravation, concluding that clinical benefit depends on identifying an individualized loading range that avoids both underloading and overload.

title: Magnetoreceptive CRY/MagR complexes: linking circadian redox signalling to protein aggregation in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
authors: Alipour M, Hajipour-Verdom B, Ashrafi F, Roodsari SR, Nohesara S, Zali A, Ashrafi F.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes literature across neuroscience, biophysics, and circadian biology to assess whether CRY/MagR-based magnetoreceptor complexes are relevant to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. It first outlines core neuropathological mechanisms (amyloid-β and tau pathology in AD; α-synuclein aggregation and dopaminergic vulnerability in PD) and the biophysical basis of magneto-protein function, particularly cryptochrome-mediated radical pair mechanisms and iron-sulphur cluster-dependent magnetic sensitivity. Evidence from cellular and animal models suggests CRY/MagR-associated pathways can modulate oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetics, protein aggregation, autophagy, and circadian control of neuronal metabolism—processes that overlap with determinants of neuronal vulnerability in AD and PD. However, the authors stress that direct validation in mammalian and human systems is limited and controversial, so the proposed mechanistic convergence remains largely speculative and requires rigorous mammalian validation.

title: Unraveling stress fractures: from cellular and molecular mechanisms to therapeutic approaches.
authors: Pu P, Zhang X, Zhang S, Chen H, Lei Q, Song T, Wang C, Xie Y, Chen L.
ai_summary: This review examines the pathogenesis and healing of stress fractures, which arise when repetitive mechanical loading exceeds the bone's adaptive repair threshold, causing microdamage to accumulate and disrupting the balance between bone resorption and formation. Healing occurs mainly through intramembranous ossification, beginning with periosteal woven bone formation to stabilize the fracture followed by remodeling to repair cracks, and involves dynamic changes in cell types, tissue constituents, and signaling. The authors call for future research using larger animal models (rabbits, minipigs) and clinically representative fracture models, and for exploring additional physical therapy modalities beyond anti-osteoporotic agents, NSAIDs, and low-intensity pulsed ultrasound to clarify their mechanisms and role in management.

title: Thermal challenge and food intake: Mutual regulatory mechanisms.
authors: Alpár A.
ai_summary: This review examines the mutual regulatory links between thermoregulation and food intake. In the arcuate nucleus, anorexigenic POMC/MSH and orexigenic NPY/AgRP neurons receive diet-derived and hormonal signals and are sensitive to temperature, while projecting to sympathetic and endocrine effectors; ambient temperature influences feeding via spinobrachial-preoptic pathways targeting AgRP neurons. Tanycytes are highlighted as central integrators: they dynamically regulate the blood-brain barrier and neurohormone access, carry thermosensitive and metabolic receptors (notably TRPV1, glucose, and cytokine receptors), reduce feeding during heat exposure through a parabrachial-tanycyte-hypothalamic circuit, and act as neural stem cells supplying new arcuate neurons in temperature- and diet-responsive ways—a regenerative capacity compromised by extreme heat or diet-induced obesity. The authors also discuss hibernation as an extreme fasting state with specific body temperature control, suggesting possible medical applications such as artificial induction of a hibernation-like hypometabolic state.

title: Ecological and genomic signatures of the convergent evolution of planktivory in fossil and living reef fishes over deep time.
authors: Santaquiteria A, Arcila D, Carnevale G, Rincon-Sandoval M, Melendez-Vazquez F, White WT, Baldwin CC, Westneat MW, Ortí G, Tyler JC, Betancur-R R.
ai_summary: This study uses genomic data from 80 living acanthuriform fishes and morphological data from 32 fossils to reconstruct a total-evidence, tip-dated phylogeny and trace dietary evolution across deep time. The authors identify at least seven independent origins of planktivory and four reversals, concentrated in the Tethys and Indo-Pacific, and find that planktivory is not an evolutionary dead end: planktivores show higher reversal rates and lower extinction than benthic feeders, with both climate and phylogeny shaping their diversification. Using a new chromosome-level genome plus 44 additional assemblies, they identify 39 genes under convergent positive selection in planktivorous lineages, six of which show accelerated evolution linked to metabolism and dietary specialization and display codon-level parallelism or convergence.

title: Investigating the coupled effects of stiffness and stretch on the trabecular meshwork cells using a hydrogel-integrated microfluidic system.
authors: Choi K, Kim M, Lakk M, McDonnell FS, Krizaj D, Kim J.
ai_summary:
Gene: MYOC
Finding: A hydrogel-integrated microfluidic platform enabling simultaneous control of substrate stiffness and equibiaxial stretch revealed that glaucomatous trabecular meshwork cells show elevated α-SMA, reduced mechanical regulation of MMP2, and diminished stretch-mediated COL1 suppression compared with normal cells, while retaining stiffness-dependent FAK phosphorylation and MYOC responses.
Disease: Glaucoma

title: Proteomic Profiling of Endothelial Cells Under Laminar Shear Stress Confirms the Importance of KLF4 in the Regulation of Membrane Protein Expression Compared to Oscillatory Flow.
authors: Réthoré L, Barré B, Guihot AL, Grimaud L, Proux C, Boissard A, Henry C, Guette C, Guillonneau F, Henrion D, Legros C, Legendre C.
ai_summary:
Gene: KLF4
Finding: Laminar shear stress induces a membrane and extracellular matrix proteomic signature in endothelial cells in which KLF4 acts as a key transcriptional regulator, promoting flow-induced cell alignment and elongation by increasing expression of CD34, HEG1, PI16, and ITGB4.
Disease: Cardiovascular disease (endothelial dysfunction)

title: Congenital hepatic fibrosis and related ciliopathies across the life course: current management, disease burden, and unmet needs in the era of genomic diagnosis and translational therapeutics.
authors: Wang A, He J, Liu K, Fu J, Chen J.
ai_summary: This narrative review covers congenital hepatic fibrosis (CHF), a rare autosomal recessive hepatobiliary developmental disorder marked by portal tract fibrosis and ductal plate malformation that is a major cause of portal hypertension in children and adolescents. It synthesizes current knowledge of pathophysiology, genetics, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, complication management, and therapeutics, and critically appraises the disease burden and gaps in care. The authors highlight the wide clinical heterogeneity (from asymptomatic to severe portal hypertension), the absence of targeted therapies addressing the underlying disease process, and persistent deficiencies in multidisciplinary coordination, individualized treatment, and long-term follow-up. The review's distinctive emphasis is on life-course management, patient burden, and translational gaps in the era of genomic diagnosis, aiming to inform future research and integrated care models.

title: Setmelanotide Response Variability in Two Genetically Confirmed Pediatric Kidney Transplant Recipients with Bardet-Biedl Syndrome.
authors: Kondou A, Siolos P, Sotiriou G, Agakidis C, Dotis J, Christoforidis A, Printza N.
ai_summary:
Gene: SDCCAG8
Finding: In a 17-year-old male kidney transplant recipient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome and a homozygous pathogenic SDCCAG8 exon deletion, 12 months of setmelanotide improved weight, BMI z-score, hunger, and HbA1c, whereas a second patient with a BBS5 splice-site variant showed only transient benefit and continued BMI gain.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: Biallelic WDR19 Variants: Systematic Analysis of Genotype-Phenotype Correlations.
authors: Webster Z, Woods L, Dalziel R, Drake K, de Valles-Ibáñez G, Poke G.
ai_summary:
Gene: WDR19
Finding: In the largest review of WDR19-associated ciliopathy to date (93 published cases plus one new patient), truncating variants were associated with increased likelihood of skeletal involvement and reduced likelihood of hepatobiliary disease compared with missense-only genotypes, while missense variants outside repeat protein domains correlated with early onset (before age 16) and ocular manifestations, and recurrent variants showed considerable phenotypic variability.
Disease: WDR19-associated ciliopathies (renal, ocular, skeletal and hepatic manifestations)

title: Evidence for a tubular basement membrane-cilia connection in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease pathogenesis.
authors: Sussman CR, Harris PC.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Cilia-dependent, PKD1-mediated regulation of the tubular basement membrane links cilia-dependent tubule dilation and basement membrane thinning to early cystogenesis, with PC1 loss compromising basement membrane stiffness.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Defective neuronal differentiation in Lowe syndrome is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired cilia-related Sonic Hedgehog signaling.
authors: Walkiewicz G, Chen S, Lo C, Zhao J, Liu Z, Wang B, Wang Q, Kowal TJ, Lawson B, Sun Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: OCRL
Finding: OCRL loss causes reduced mitochondrial activity, mtDNA and mitochondrial content with increased oxidative stress, shifts differentiation toward astrocytes rather than impairing neurogenesis, and impairs cilia-related Sonic Hedgehog signaling, phenotypes conserved across patient iPSC neurons, Ocrl knockout mice, and zebrafish.
Disease: Lowe syndrome (neurodevelopmental dysfunction)

title: Isolated rod-cone dystrophy in homozygous IFT140 missense allele p.Tyr923Asp.
authors: Eiselen C, Shanks M, Sperring S, Cehajic-Kapetanovic J.
ai_summary:
Gene: IFT140
Finding: Homozygosity for the missense variant c.2767T>G (p.Tyr923Asp), absent from gnomAD and classified as likely pathogenic, segregated with autosomal-recessive disease in two consanguineous siblings who showed classic rod-cone dystrophy (parafoveal hyperautofluorescent rings, ellipsoid zone loss, reduced scotopic and photopic ERG responses) but normal renal, skeletal, and auditory function at diagnosis and eight years later.
Disease: Isolated rod-cone dystrophy (retinal dystrophy without systemic ciliopathy features)

title: Analysis of motor-based transport in primary cilia by dynamic mode decomposition of live-cell imaging data.
authors: Campestre F, Lauritsen L, Pedersen LB, Wüstner D.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF13B
Finding: A KIF13B deletion mutant retaining only the motor domain and part of the FHA domain leaves steady-state IFT velocity and frequency unchanged, but prevents the reduction in both anterograde and retrograde IFT velocities normally seen when retrograde dynein-2 is inhibited by Ciliobrevin D or Tanespimycin; KIF13B localizes to the ciliary membrane, periciliary membrane region, and centriolar subdistal appendages below FBF1.
Disease: Primary cilia motor-based transport (ciliary protein trafficking)

title: From Guidelines to Practice: Pilot Implementation and Analytical Boundaries of a Focused ADPKD-Spectrum Gene Panel.
authors: Babici RG, Ivanov IC, Agavriloaei BD, Mititiuc IL, Dodi G, Dragoș ML, Racoviță S, Savuca A, Apetrii M, Popescu R, Covic AC, Rusu C.
ai_summary: This pilot study evaluated a 28-gene ADPKD-spectrum hybrid-capture panel across 16 samples, using 694 analytical target intervals per sample, with MLPA for dosage assessment and selective whole-exome sequencing for short-read verification. Most interval observations (82.7%) achieved mean depth ≥20×, and nine genes (including GANAB, HNF1B, and TSC2) met mean-depth criteria throughout, though PKD1 exon 1 remained undercovered and nominal depth in duplicated sequence did not confirm authentic-locus callability. Among nine panel-first cases, one HNF1B and one unique-locus PKD1 finding were supported, while four duplicated-sequence PKD1 findings remained confirmation-dependent. The authors conclude that responsible implementation of such panels requires explicit analytical boundaries and staged complementary testing.

title: Protocol for optogenetic control of cAMP in human telencephalic organoids using an easy-to-build Arduino-driven LED system.
authors: Shimada IS, Kato Y.
ai_summary: This protocol describes a low-cost, Arduino-driven LED stimulation system for optogenetic control of cAMP in human telencephalic organoids. It covers assembly of the hardware, code for regulating LED output, preparation of iPS cells for optogenetic experiments, and photoactivation of cAMP via bPAC to control cell-fate decisions, offering an affordable alternative to commercial optogenetic setups.

title: The power of five - inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase gene mutations at the intersection of development and disease.
authors: McGrath MJ, Davies EM, Ooms LM, Nanayakkara R, Gurung R, Jones EI, Mitchell CA.
ai_summary: This review covers the inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase family (10 mammalian enzymes that dephosphorylate the 5-position phosphate of PtdIns(4,5)P2, PtdIns(3,5)P2, and/or PtdIns(3,4,5)P3). Despite overlapping substrate specificity, family members act nonredundantly, as shown by mouse and zebrafish knockout studies. Mutations in several family members cause multisystem developmental and congenital syndromes, and emerging evidence links gene variants to diabetes and metabolic syndrome, neurodegenerative disease, and, rarely, cancer. The review discusses disease modeling and mechanistic advances.

title: Emerging roles of the ciliary-mitochondrial axis in cellular homeostasis and neuroprotection.
authors: Miller E, Bambakidis P, Templin P, Paul BD, Pieper AA.
ai_summary: This review argues that primary cilia and mitochondria should be viewed as a single coupled signaling and metabolic hub rather than separate organelles. The bidirectional ciliary-mitochondrial axis integrates extracellular sensing, calcium dynamics, bioenergetics, and organelle quality control, with ciliary signaling influencing mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy, and mitochondrial metabolic states in turn affecting cilia. Disruption at any point in this axis is proposed as a potential trigger of neurodegeneration, and the authors highlight the axis as a promising, tractable target for therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring brain homeostasis and neuroprotection.

title: CFAP100 forms phase-separated condensates required for ciliary transition zone assembly.
authors: Sun S, Li K, Sun X, Tian R, Zhu LE, Liu K, Yue Y, Li W, Ran J, Zhou J, Liu M.
ai_summary:
Gene: CFAP100
Finding: CFAP100 forms phase-separated condensates at the distal end of centrioles that stimulate transition zone assembly and recruit NPHP3, with Cfap100 knockout mice showing ciliary defects in brain, trachea, and kidney.
Disease: Ciliary defects (ciliopathy-associated phenotypes in brain, trachea, and kidney)

title: A comprehensive overview of genetic mutations in Iranian patients with Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
authors: Khalilian S, Fathi M, Entezam M, Farbood Z, Ghafouri-Fard S, Dastgheib SA, Miryounesi M.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS10
Finding: In a whole-exome sequencing study of 26 unrelated Iranian patients with Bardet-Biedl syndrome, causative or potentially causative autosomal recessive variants were identified in all probands across 13 genes, with BBS10, BBS2, BBS5, BBS12, and CEP290 each mutated in three cases and consanguinity present in 88.4% of families.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: The utility and advantages of exome and genome sequencing in pediatric kidney disease diagnosis.
authors: Jang S, Lee H.
ai_summary: This review compares genetic testing modalities for pediatric kidney disease, where roughly 30% of cases are inherited. It argues that exome and genome sequencing outperform fixed targeted gene panels by enabling unbiased analysis of all disease-associated genes and detecting structural, copy-number, and non-coding variants that panels miss, while also allowing discovery of novel disease genes through periodic reanalysis. A diagnostic gap nonetheless persists because short-read sequencing struggles with complex genomic regions and variants of uncertain significance are hard to interpret; the authors recommend integrating long-read sequencing and systematic reanalysis protocols to close it.

title: Sequential liraglutide and setmelanotide therapy in Bardet-Biedl Syndrome: metabolic and renal outcomes in a real-world case report and literature review.
authors: Pasquariello T, Secondulfo F, Roscini AR, Nardi E, Prosperi E, Capasso G, Perna AF, Zacchia M.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBS10
Finding: In an adult with compound heterozygous likely pathogenic BBS10 variants, sequential liraglutide then setmelanotide produced 10.5% weight loss, normalized liver transaminases, reduced liver stiffness, and sustained improvement in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio with stable eGFR, alongside improved insulin resistance and discontinuation of metformin and a statin.
Disease: Bardet-Biedl syndrome (obesity, MASLD, albuminuria)

title: Primary hyperaldosteronism in patient with Bardet-Biedl syndrome: unmasking secondary hypertension.
authors: Marinova E, Stoyanova L, Todorova T, Dimova M.
ai_summary:
Gene: BBSome (Bardet-Biedl syndrome)
Finding: A 35-year-old man with Bardet-Biedl syndrome presenting with treatment-resistant hypertension and hypokalaemia was found to have primary hyperaldosteronism due to a unilateral aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma, with normalization of potassium and improved blood pressure control after laparoscopic adrenalectomy.
Disease: Primary aldosteronism (secondary hypertension) in Bardet-Biedl syndrome

title: Loss of ADAMTS9 disrupts ciliogenesis and collagen homeostasis resulting in Nephronophthisis-like polycystic kidneys.
authors: Fischer S, Robert KL, Ahmed M, Kane GI, Kavanaugh MA, Wang W, Tran PV, Atukorale PU, Nandadasa S.
ai_summary:
Gene: ADAMTS9
Finding: Proximal nephron deletion of ADAMTS9 in mice impairs cleavage of the ciliary transition zone protein TMEM67, disrupting ciliogenesis and the MKS/B9 module, and causing interstitial collagen deposition that drives cystogenesis and the small, non-enlarging cystic kidney phenotype; all eight known ciliopathy patient ADAMTS9 variants failed to localize TMEM67's C-terminus to the transition zone.
Disease: Nephronophthisis-like polycystic kidney disease (ciliopathy)

title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia from Embryogenesis to Adulthood: Micro-CT Analysis of Stage-Dependent Upper Airway Abnormalities in Odad3 Loss-of-Function Mouse Models.
authors: Orsini T, Putti S, Chiani F, Gambadoro A, Pasquini M, Ermakova O.
ai_summary:
Gene: Odad3
Finding: Constitutive Odad3 loss causes embryonic and early postnatal craniofacial remodeling and turbinate hypoplasia, whereas adult-induced ablation produces localized caudal nasal turbinate atrophy with massive mucus accumulation, while heterozygous loss yields no upper airway phenotype.
Disease: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (chronic rhinosinusitis-like upper airway pathology)

title: Primary cilia: master conductors of cellular communication in development and disease.
authors: Thomsen OK, Pigino G, Pedersen LB, Pazour GJ, Wachten D, Christensen ST.
ai_summary: Primary cilia act as cellular antennae that integrate multiple signalling pathways (including Hedgehog, GPCR, TRP, receptor tyrosine kinase and TGFβ signalling) to coordinate development, proliferation, differentiation, metabolism and tissue homeostasis. Their composition is dynamically shaped by intraflagellar transport, ciliary gating and cargo adaptors, which determine the strength, duration and specificity of signalling. Disruption of ciliary architecture, trafficking or signalling causes ciliopathies with tissue-specific phenotypes such as polycystic kidney disease, retinal degeneration, skeletal abnormalities, cardiovascular disease, neurodevelopmental disorders and obesity. Cell-type-specific and temporally dynamic ciliary signatures appear to determine signalling competence and disease susceptibility, and defining these signatures and their plasticity may open new therapeutic avenues.

title: CDK4/6 Inhibitor Abemaciclib Arrests and Reverses Kidney Cyst Progression in Preclinical Models of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Cao Y, Sun X, Huang Y, Chen C, Ji B, Chen R, Li Y, Liang Y, Aghevli A, Yang N, Patel V, Harris P, Ling K, Hu J, He K.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
ai_summary:
Gene: CDK6
Finding: The CDK4/6 inhibitor abemaciclib, at doses below those used in oncology, arrested cyst progression more effectively than tolvaptan in Pkd1R3277C/R3277C mice and reversed cyst growth in males, restoring axonemal polyglutamylation and ciliary polycystin levels via CDK6 inhibition.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: ALMS1 regulates primary cilia signaling in adipogenesis.
authors: Lee MD, Giagnocavo SD, Campora KJ, Menon R, Hilgendorf KI.
ai_summary:
Gene: ALMS1
Finding: Loss of ALMS1 in visceral (but not subcutaneous) mouse preadipocytes and adipocyte progenitor cells reduces ciliation and centriole cohesion and impairs adipogenesis, with cells retaining ciliary GPCR localization but failing to respond to receptor activation, indicating a defect in ciliary signal transduction downstream of receptor localization.
Disease: Alström syndrome (obesity, hyperphagia, early-onset type 2 diabetes)

title: Clinical Characteristics of Patients With Fontan Circulation and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: A Case Series From the SV-ONE Registry.
authors: Aldawsari KA, Bucholz E, Saba TG, Schidlow D, Chen S, Spurgin SB, Khalid O, Jaggers J, Chatfield KC.
ai_summary: This retrospective case series from the Single-Ventricle Outcomes Network registry identified only 5 patients with both Fontan physiology and reported primary ciliary dyskinesia among 1,535 Fontan patients. Median age at Fontan completion was 3 years with 7 years of median follow-up; 2 patients developed chylous pleural effusions, while none developed plastic bronchitis or protein-losing enteropathy. The authors conclude that Fontan completion was achieved in only a small cohort of PCD patients and emphasize the need for multidisciplinary collaboration to describe and manage these multiorgan comorbidities.

title: CFTR correctors suppress Ca²⁺-cAMP signaling and cyst growth in primary cultures of ARPKD cholangiocytes.
authors: Sharma A, Afshani M, Sharma T, Cebotaru L.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: In Pkhd1-mutant mouse cholangiocytes, the CFTR correctors VX-809 and VX-445 increased CFTR expression, partially restored PC1 and PC2, attenuated elevated cytosolic Ca²⁺ and cAMP signaling, and reduced proliferation and cyst growth, whereas the CFTR inhibitor CFTRinh-172 did not reproduce these effects.
Disease: Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) / hepatobiliary disease

title: Biallelic DAW1 variants reveal a tissue-specific role in heterotaxy without primary ciliary dyskinesia.
authors: Urbatsch D, Jeyaraj A, Bedekar S, Rao V, White SC, Thomas MJ, Garrod A, Peroutka C, Ratan A, Kulkarni SS.
journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
ai_summary:
Gene: DAW1
Finding: Compound heterozygous DAW1 variants (a splice-site variant causing complete loss of function and a missense variant acting as a context-dependent hypomorph) were identified in a proband with heterotaxy and complex congenital heart disease; Xenopus tropicalis models showed that Daw1 depletion disrupted left-right patterning, cardiac looping, and mucociliary flow, with the missense allele rescuing mucociliary flow but not left-right patterning.
Disease: Heterotaxy/laterality defect spectrum with complex congenital heart disease, without primary ciliary dyskinesia

title: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease in children and adolescents.
authors: Mun E, Baek HS.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1, PKD2
Finding: ADPKD, though traditionally considered adult-onset, often begins with in utero cystogenesis and childhood structural changes; pediatric patients are mostly asymptomatic but 20%-40% develop hypertension and some have albuminuria, with ultrasonography as the preferred diagnostic tool, genetic testing reserved for very-early-onset or atypical cases, and management centered on renin-angiotensin system inhibitor-based blood pressure control plus sodium restriction and hydration.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: [Bronchiectasis in children: An underdiagnosed disease with accessible screening and etiological assessment].
authors: Mansouri I, Benchaji D, Errami A, Zridi S, Ailal F, El Bakkouri J, Benhsaien I, Adnane F, Salam S, Bousfiha AA, Amenzoui N.
ai_summary: Pediatric non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis is an emerging but underdiagnosed cause of chronic respiratory morbidity, with incidence varying from 0.2–2.3 per 100,000 children in high-income countries to over 700 per 100,000 in highly deprived settings. Registry data (Child-BEAR-Net) show post-infectious forms (~30%) and immunodeficiencies (~20%) predominate, with primary ciliary dyskinesia accounting for ~10–15% and rarer causes including congenital malformations and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis. In low-resource settings it is often misdiagnosed as asthma or tuberculosis, delaying care; however, the pediatric airway retains remodeling capacity, so early lesions may regress with prompt treatment. Chronic productive cough is the cardinal symptom, and early screening plus multidisciplinary management (physiotherapy, targeted antibiotics, immunoglobulin replacement, nutritional support) improves outcomes. Priorities include adopting ERS 2021 guidelines, national registries, and tailored screening programs, since some forms—especially post-infectious—may be preventable.

title: Effects of hypertonic saline and/or carbocisteine on sputum rheology in bronchiectasis: CLEAR-EME.
authors: McKelvey MC, Einarsson GG, Carson J, Kadoom A, Brown RR, Campbell C, Jackson A, McDowell C, Clarke M, Copeland F, Ferguson K, McLeese RH, Convery R, Hill AT, De Soyza A, Shahidi M, Kelly M, Carroll M, Gatheral T, Anwar M, Duckers J, Flight W, Hurst JR, Ionescu AA, Loebinger MR, Sullivan AL, Chalmers JD, Downey DG, Tunney MM, O'Neill B, McAuley DF, Elborn JS, Bradley JM, Taggart CC.
ai_summary: Neither hypertonic saline nor carbocisteine, alone or in combination, reduced sputum viscoelasticity or altered sputum biomarker levels or bacterial community composition in patients with bronchiectasis after 2 or 8 weeks of treatment. At baseline, sputum viscoelasticity correlated positively with interleukin-8 levels and greater relative bacterial dominance, but these properties were unchanged by treatment, arguing against the use of these mucoactives to modify sputum properties in bronchiectasis.

title: Nasal Mucociliary Clearance Assessment: Historical Evolution, Methodological Approaches, and the Role of Activated Charcoal as a Visible Marker.
authors: Dinev SD, Atanasov TD.
ai_summary: This narrative review traces the evolution of nasal mucociliary clearance assessment from early direct-observation and dye-based methods through saccharin transit time testing, visible particle and charcoal-based tracers, radiolabeled and scintigraphic techniques, and modern specialized tests such as ciliary beat frequency analysis, high-speed video microscopy, nasal nitric oxide measurement, transmission electron microscopy, immunofluorescence, and genetic testing. It compares these approaches by physiological relevance, practicality, objectivity, cost, reproducibility, and patient tolerance, noting that saccharin testing is simple and inexpensive but relies on subjective taste perception, while radiolabeled and scintigraphic methods are more objective but technically demanding and poorly suited to routine use; advanced ciliary and genetic tests are valuable in selected contexts such as primary ciliary dyskinesia but are not equivalent to direct nasal transport-time measurement. The authors position activated charcoal not as a new or universally substitutive technique but as a topical, low-cost, dark visible marker that allows examiner-observed endpoint recognition, and they conclude that its added value, including standardized endoscopic control, still requires prospective comparative validation, with particular relevance to pediatric otorhinolaryngology.

title: GPCR signaling from a primary cilium perspective.
authors: Idevall-Hagren O, Hughes J.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence that the primary cilium functions as a privileged, modular signaling hub where a distinct subset of GPCRs, along with their effectors (G proteins, GPCR kinases, β-arrestins, RGS proteins, and AKAPs), is concentrated by dedicated trafficking machinery. The cilium's unique geometry, membrane composition, voltage, pH, and cytoskeletal architecture shape signaling outcomes, enabling autonomous, highly sensitive microdomains of cAMP and Ca2+ signaling that integrate and hierarchically control multiple GPCR inputs. The authors highlight the physiological roles of ciliary GPCR signaling in neural, renal, adipose, pancreatic, and developmental tissues, where its disruption contributes to metabolic disease, impaired morphogenesis, loss of tissue homeostasis, and ciliopathies, concluding that subcellular localization is a key determinant of receptor function and signaling specificity.

title: Floppy Mitral Valve/Mitral Valve Prolapse: Diagnosis and Clinical Classification in This Continuing Odyssey.
authors: Boudoulas KD, Triposkiadis F, Marmagkiolis K, Iliescu C, Cilingiroglu M, Pitsis A, Stefanadis C, Boudoulas H.
ai_summary: This review argues that floppy mitral valve (FMV)/mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is a complex, heterogeneous entity with multiple genotypes and phenotypes, lacking a precise definition, and that clinical manifestations often do not track with the severity of mitral regurgitation. It advocates a diagnostic approach centered on FMV rather than on MVP alone, since MVP is frequently a non-specific finding, and proposes a clinical classification that distinguishes patients whose symptoms are not directly related to mitral regurgitation severity (termed FMV/MVP syndrome) from those whose symptoms arise directly from mitral regurgitation and its complications. The authors anticipate that genetic variants will eventually be integrated into the diagnostic classification and management of this entity.

title: Exome Sequencing and MRI in Prenatal Diagnosis: A Case Report of Joubert Syndrome in Colombia.
authors: Annicchiarico W, Peña-Pardo LX, Redondo AM, Cruzate KF, Castro M, Betin G, Miranda J.
ai_summary:
Gene: CSPP1
Finding: A homozygous pathogenic canonical splice-site variant (c.2968+1G>A) was identified by exome sequencing in a fetus with occipital meningocele, cerebellar vermis agenesis, bilateral cleft lip and palate, and the molar tooth sign on fetal MRI, with postnatal evaluation confirming the prenatal diagnosis.
Disease: Joubert syndrome 21

title: Somatostatin analogues for ADPKD: ending the confusing story of mGFR and eGFR.
authors: Gansevoort RT, Bais T.
ai_summary: This commentary reviews the LIPS trial, the final randomized evaluation of somatostatin analogues in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Lanreotide showed no benefit on the primary outcome of measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) decline, though it suggested an effect on creatinine-estimated GFR (eGFR) slope. This discrepancy underscores the challenges of interpreting kidney function endpoints and statistical modeling. Overall, the findings support the current KDIGO recommendation against prescribing somatostatin analogues solely to preserve kidney function in ADPKD.

title: Airway Clearance and Pediatric Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia: A Clinical Framework for Children and Adolescents.
authors: Zhao J, Chen L, Yang W, Liu H.
ai_summary: This narrative review addresses airway clearance failure as the central treatment problem in pediatric primary ciliary dyskinesia, evaluating airway clearance techniques, mucoactive adjuncts, and pulmonary rehabilitation for children and adolescents. The authors note that no single airway clearance technique has proven universally superior and that pediatric rehabilitation evidence remains limited, so they propose a clearance-anchored dual-pillar framework in which airway clearance techniques directly target mucus retention while pulmonary rehabilitation complements them by improving fitness, muscle performance, participation, and self-management. Treatment response should be assessed across four domains: clinical stability, treatment performance, physiological and functional outcomes, and patient and family experience. The authors call for prospective multicenter comparative trials and harmonized pediatric outcome measures.

title: Novel human neutralizing monoclonal antibodies against Pregnancy-Associated Plasma Protein A for the treatment of Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Hu E, Gardener MJ, Wang X, Luo G, Kotzer C, Jiang L, Mallick E, Srinivasan A, Ouro-Gnao L, Firczuk H, Chandler S, Chung CW, Goswami P, Madi S, Lenhard S, Alsaid H, Doan M, Nanayakkara K, Swerdlow DI, Roberts J, Torres VE.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Novel human pan-selective monoclonal antibodies against PAPPA blocked cleavage of IGFBP2, 4, and 5, showed excellent target engagement even at low doses, and ameliorated cystic disease, inflammation, fibrosis, and IGF1Rβ signaling in mouse models of both early and advanced PKD, though female Pkd1RC/RC mice were less protected than males.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

title: Large-scale organoid-derived cyst cultures as a drug discovery platform for polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Vanichapol T, Wangford R, Mishra S, Takemoto M, Uesugi M, Davidson AJ, Sander V.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD2
Finding: Large-scale suspension cultures of ureteric bud organoids from PKD2-deficient hiPSCs form cysts efficiently within 7-20 days, respond to cyst-reducing compounds (JQ1, QNZ, and the TLR4 antagonist M1/TAK-242) but not tolvaptan, and enable small-molecule screening for cyst reduction.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Nowak KL, Chonchol M.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Nephrectomy in Kidney Transplant Candidates With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
authors: Atitallah N, Martin D, Golshayan D, Zingg T, Matter M.
ai_summary: This retrospective single-center study of 109 ADPKD kidney transplant recipients found that native nephrectomy was performed in 72% of patients, most commonly before transplantation and predominantly bilaterally. The leading indication was insufficient intra-abdominal space for graft implantation, followed by cyst infection, chronic pain, and hemorrhagic cysts. Nephrectomy patients had higher body weight and were more often dialysis-dependent pre-transplant. Post-transplant nephrectomy was uncommon. Although complication rates (bleeding requiring transfusion, fluid collections, incisional hernias, reinterventions) did not differ significantly between strategies, bilateral pre-transplant nephrectomy accounted for most postoperative complications. No malignancy was found in available histopathology. The authors conclude that practice varies widely and support individualized, anatomy- and symptom-based decision-making.

title: Spectrum of Hydrometrocolpos in Pediatric Patients: A Pictorial Essay and Authors' Experience.
authors: Gupta R, Soni P.
journal: Journal of Indian Association of Pediatric Surgeons
ai_summary: This pictorial essay and ambispective review of 17 pediatric patients with hydrometrocolpos describes its diverse etiologies and presentations, including imperforate hymen, vaginal atresia, transverse vaginal septum, urogenital sinus, cloacal malformations, and rare syndromic associations such as Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich and McKusick-Kaufman syndromes. Patients presented with a vestibular bulge, abdominal mass, or anorectal malformation, and all had varying degrees of hydroureteronephrosis from lower urinary tract obstruction. Management was individualized, ranging from incision and drainage for simple causes to abdominal vaginostomy for complex ones, underscoring the need for early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach.

title: A rapid automated segmentation method for total kidney volume measurement on unenhanced computed tomography in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Hu Y, Zhao T, Gao Y, Zhang P, Liu T, Lin Y, Gao S, Zhang T, Xu Y, Li B, Zhang Y, Xie S, Zhou L, Sun H.
ai_summary: A fully automated nnU-Net-based segmentation model was developed and validated for measuring total kidney volume from unenhanced CT in ADPKD patients. Across an independent validation cohort (including longitudinal scans), automated segmentation showed excellent spatial agreement with expert-corrected reference segmentation (mean Dice 0.96) and near-perfect volumetric agreement (ICC 0.999, minimal bias), with similarly robust agreement for longitudinal kidney growth assessment. The method reduced processing time from about 30 minutes per case to roughly 5 seconds, offering a fast, accurate, and reproducible alternative to manual volumetric analysis.

title: Imaging Pitfalls in Evaluating Liver Metastases in Breast Cancer With Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease-Associated Polycystic Liver: A Case Report.
authors: Aso S, Sasaki R, Kawano H, Onagi H, Saeki H, Okazaki M, Ijima K, Kutomi G.
ai_summary: In a patient with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and extensive polycystic liver, diffuse infiltrative breast cancer liver metastases were radiologically underestimated on conventional whole-body imaging because the cysts obscured the true hepatic tumor burden. The authors highlight that persistent discordance between biomarkers and imaging should prompt reassessment of progression at known disease sites and evaluation of other organs, using organ-specific imaging when clinically indicated.

title: A novel frameshift variant in TTC29 associated with total asthenozoospermia and male infertility.
authors: Li L, Wan F, Feng K, Qu X, Xia Y, Dong J, Liu Y, Zhao Y, Zhu G, Yin B, Guo H.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary:
Gene: TTC29
Finding: A novel frameshift variant (c.121dupA; p.Ile41Asnfs*21) produced little or no detectable protein, reduced TTC29 signal along the sperm flagellum, and caused disruption of the 9+2 axonemal architecture with midpiece and principal piece abnormalities; two ICSI cycles achieved fertilization but no clinical pregnancy.
Disease: Total asthenozoospermia and male infertility

title: Genomic spectrum of congenital heart disease combined with kidney and urinary tract anomalies uncovered by exome sequencing and array-CGH.
authors: Zlotina A, Zhuk S, Kozyrev I, Sorokina M, Nikitina E, Shagimardanova E, Melnik O, Vershinina T, Petrova N, Kagantsov I, Vasichkina E, Pervunina T, Kostareva A.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary:
Gene: ROBO1
Finding: Two children with combined congenital heart disease and kidney/urinary tract anomalies carried ROBO1 loss-of-function variants, and in vitro studies in patient cardiac mesenchymal cells showed markedly diminished or moderately reduced ROBO1 expression, suggesting haploinsufficiency.
Disease: Combined congenital heart disease and anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CHD-CAKUT)

title: From phenotypic screening to target and compound prioritization for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Araripe DA, Iljin M, Bange H, Price LS, Liu R, van der Es D, Heitman LH, Peters DJM, van Westen GJP.
journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: A multi-step workflow combining phenotypic screening in a Pkd1-/- cyst-swelling assay with target database cross-referencing, QSAR modeling, and radioligand binding identified A1AR affinity and subtype selectivity as a common feature of cyst-swelling-reducing ligands (with the positive allosteric modulator MIPS521 most effective), while GLUT1 inhibitors also reduced swelling and the MR antagonist Esaxerenone was a compound-specific hit.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

title: Beyond the Kidney: A Systematic Review of Extrarenal Manifestations in MAPKBP1-Related Nephronophthisis.
authors: Ambrosini E, Luberto A, Busciglio S, Baroni MC, Taiani A, Cannizzaro IR, Gandolfini I, Maggiore U, Martorana D, Uliana V, Barili V, Percesepe A.
ai_summary:
Gene: MAPKBP1
Finding: In a systematic review of 19 patients with biallelic MAPKBP1 variants, most had at least one extrarenal manifestation, most commonly skeletal abnormalities such as scoliosis (8/19), along with short stature, patellar subluxation, long fingers or feet, craniofacial dysmorphisms, and cardiovascular abnormalities; pathogenic variants were predominantly stop-gain, splice-site, and frameshift.
Disease: Nephronophthisis type 20 (NPHP20)

title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Landscape of Sitosterolemia in China: Including a Rare Case With Nephronophthisis.
authors: Ding D, Wu H, Zhao F, Zheng B, Chen Q.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHP1
Finding: A Chinese boy with sitosterolemia due to biallelic ABCG8 mutations also carried a homozygous NPHP1 deletion, presenting with renal dysfunction alongside recurrent fever, thrombocytopenia, and splenomegaly, initially misdiagnosed as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
Disease: Nephronophthisis (concurrent with sitosterolemia)

title: CRISPR activation of endogenous PKD1 increases polycystin-1 levels and suppresses cellular features of ADPKD.
authors: Chakraborty A, Varghese MM, Wallace DP, Ward CJ, Yu ASL.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: CRISPR activation of the endogenous PKD1 promoter raised polycystin-1 levels and reduced proliferation, in vitro cyst formation, aerobic glycolysis, and cystogenic signaling (cAMP, cMyc, pCreb, pErk) in ADPKD cell models, with successful activation also demonstrated in human primary renal epithelial cells.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Pkd1 Deficiency Causes Intrinsic Renal Circadian Clock Dysfunction.
authors: Jamadar A, Douma LG, Maser RL, Gumz ML, Rao R.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: Pkd1 loss blunts core clock gene oscillations in synchronized renal epithelial cells and dampens/desynchronizes circadian clock gene expression and PER2::LUC bioluminescence in cystic kidneys, with progressive disruption of diurnal water intake and urine output paralleling cystic burden in both slow- and rapid-progressing ADPKD mouse models.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Polycystic Kidney Disease-Related Mortality in the US (1999-2024): A Nationwide Joinpoint Analysis of Trends, Disparities, and Comorbidity Structure.
authors: Amir HB, Uzair M, Khan ZM, Siddiqi HA, Sidhwa AY.
ai_summary: This nationwide analysis of 17,141 US PKD-related deaths (1999–2024) found that age-adjusted mortality declined steadily until 2013, then reversed and rose significantly through 2024 (APC +2.34%), a two-segment trajectory masked by the overall average annual change. The rebound occurred across nearly all demographic strata, was steepest among non-Hispanic Black decedents (roughly double the non-Hispanic White rate), and was absent only in the Northeast. Co-mention of renal failure and ischemic heart disease declined while hypertension co-mention rose, and the reversal preceded approval of ADPKD-specific therapy, arguing against a link to the 2014 kidney allocation policy revision.

title: HOXD13 links positional identity to primary cilia-dependent signalling in synovial fibroblasts.
authors: Mirrahimi M, Klein K, Cebrián CC, Khmelevskaya A, Houtman M, Ezen E, Saadat MH, Vogetseder A, Retamosa EC, Rothenfluh E, Wang J, Hajdari L, Berli M, Rauer T, Catanzaro S, Andersson J, Distler O, Ospelt C.
ai_summary:
Gene: HOXD13
Finding: Silencing of 5' HOXD genes in synovial fibroblasts produced transcriptional changes mirroring joint-specific differences in rheumatoid arthritis, with HOXD13 identified as a key regulator of primary cilia function, cell-cycle control, DNA damage responses, and genome stability.
Disease: Rheumatoid arthritis

title: Very-early-onset autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease coexisting with congenital adrenal hyperplasia in a newborn: a case report.
authors: Kim C, Kim HY, Jung YH, Choi CW, Kim J, Kim JH.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: A de novo truncating PKD1 variant was identified in a newborn with prenatally detected kidney cysts who also had salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to two CYP21A2 variants; hypertension developing at 3 years 7 months resolved after mineralocorticoid dose reduction.
Disease: Very-early-onset autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease coexisting with congenital adrenal hyperplasia

title: Pirfenidone treatment attenuates fibrosis in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
authors: Remadevi V, Jamadar A, Varghese MM, Yang H, Gunewardena S, Wallace DP, Rao R.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: In ADPKD, fibroblasts are the predominant source of fibrous and adhesive extracellular matrix, and pirfenidone suppressed myofibroblast activation and ECM production in vitro and reduced renal fibrosis, myofibroblast accumulation, profibrotic signaling, and kidney enlargement while improving kidney function in the Pkd1RC/RC mouse model (cyst burden was reduced only in females).
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: CiliaIO: Machine learning reveals spatial patterns of cilia beating dynamics in the zebrafish spinal cord.
authors: Atayeter E, Ho J, Blottin TG, Joe IB, Sistrunk R, Zhang B, Solnica Krezel L, Gerstlauer A, Wallingford JB, Gray RS.
ai_summary:
Gene: bbs2
Finding: A machine learning tool (CiliaIO) quantified motile cilia morphodynamics and revealed subtle, highly significant regional differences in ciliary waveforms in the zebrafish spinal cord, and captured subtle ciliary defects in a novel bbs2 allele.
Disease: Late-onset scoliosis (motile ciliopathy)

title: Association Between Tolvaptan Exposure and Venous Thromboembolism Risk in ADPKD: A Real-World Propensity-Matched EHR Study.
authors: Chen TP, Tsai SF.
ai_summary: In a large propensity-matched retrospective cohort of adults with ADPKD, tolvaptan exposure was associated with significantly lower risks of venous thromboembolism (2.1% vs 3.9%) and all-cause mortality (1.28% vs 3.9%) compared with no tolvaptan. The authors caution that the observational design and possible residual confounding mean these findings are associative and hypothesis-generating rather than causal, and warrant prospective confirmation.

title: Dishevelled drives disassembly of primary cilia through an unusual PDZ domain-mediated binding mode with Girdin-L.
authors: Renko M, Beitia GJ, Rutherford TJ, Bienz M, Gammons MV.
ai_summary:
Gene: DVL2
Finding: The PDZ domain of DVL2 binds with high affinity to extended C-terminal PDZ-binding motifs in Girdin-L (and its paralog Daple), clusters around basal bodies, recruits endogenous Girdin to primary cilia, and promotes cilia disassembly, a process accelerated by Wnt5a.
Disease: Primary cilia disassembly (β-catenin-independent Wnt signaling)

title: Genes, kidneys, and the future: transforming chronic kidney disease management through genomic insights.
authors: Kil SY, Yang WS, Kim YN, Shin HS, Jung Y, Rim H.
ai_summary: Genetic diagnostics are reshaping chronic kidney disease (CKD) management: over 600 genes are linked to inherited kidney disorders, and monogenic variants explain 10–20% of adult and up to 50% of pediatric CKD. Gene panels, whole-exome, and whole-genome sequencing improve diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized care across conditions such as autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, Alport syndrome, congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract, autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease, and monogenic nephrotic syndromes, while also guiding treatment, enabling familial risk assessment, and sometimes removing the need for renal biopsy. Polygenic risk scores from genome-wide association studies remain of unproven clinical utility, and barriers persist, including variants of uncertain significance, limited clinician genetics knowledge, and poor access to genetic counseling.

title: Open Cholecystectomy in a Patient With Situs Inversus Totalis and Symptomatic Cholelithiasis: A Case Report.
authors: Gillani SFP, Javaid MH, Ali RN, Irfan W, Irfan S, Mahato RK.
ai_summary: A patient with situs inversus totalis and symptomatic cholelithiasis underwent open cholecystectomy via a left subcostal (mirror-image Kocher) incision. Because SIT reverses the normal anatomical landmarks, the authors emphasize the need for careful preoperative imaging, a mirror-image surgical strategy, and strict attainment of the critical view of safety before dividing any ductal or vascular structures. The case demonstrates that open cholecystectomy can be performed safely despite visceral transposition.

title: Follow-up of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract from the antenatal period to the first year of life: a retrospective study from Turkey.
authors: Fil NI, Onay OS, Velipasaoglu M, Tufan AK, Cetin N, Kaya TB, Aydemir O.
ai_summary: This retrospective cohort of 55 infants with antenatally detected CAKUT found that collecting system anomalies (mainly hydronephrosis) were more common than renal parenchymal malformations, in which multicystic dysplastic kidney predominated. While AKI incidence did not differ between groups, CKD was significantly more prevalent in the renal parenchymal malformation group, and loss of corticomedullary differentiation on postnatal ultrasound emerged as an important predictor of AKI.

title: Rare Complications of Chronic Rhinosinusitis Associated With Nasal Polyps and Osseous Metaplasia.
authors: Ritz M, Rubenacker-O'Dell A, Olson F, Fonarov I.
journal: Journal of community hospital internal medicine perspectives
ai_summary: An 18-year-old man with asthma and prior polypectomy developed an unusually aggressive form of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, complicated by osseous metaplasia, anterior skull base erosion, and intracranial and orbital extension, presenting with headaches, visual changes, and proptosis. Endoscopic surgery with bilateral Draf IIb frontal sinus decompression revealed fibrotic polyps, bone expansion, and purulent intracranial collections, and led to resolution of proptosis and symptom improvement. The case underscores the need for early recognition, multidisciplinary care, and close follow-up to prevent neurological and ophthalmic complications.

title: Correction to "Tolvaptan: a possible preemptive treatment option in children with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease?"
authors: Baek HS, Cho MH.
ai_summary: This is a correction notice for an article published in volume 27, page 76, concerning tolvaptan as a possible preemptive treatment option in children with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. No substantive research findings are presented in the correction notice itself.

title: Kartagener syndrome with partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage: a case report.
authors: Firmanda DR, Putri AY, Ghea C, Fadila AN, Prabowo E, Valentine V, Hamadah F.
ai_summary: A 34-year-old woman with previously undiagnosed Kartagener syndrome presented with an acute respiratory exacerbation and severe hypoxemia. Imaging revealed situs inversus totalis, bilateral bronchiectasis, and a rare coexisting partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (two right pulmonary veins draining into the right atrium) with severe tricuspid and moderate pulmonary regurgitation. She improved with pulmonary vasodilators, a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor, and antibiotics. The case underscores the value of multimodality imaging in recognizing this rare combination of anomalies and guiding management.

title: Atelectasis secondary to two separate video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection of the lung lobe and pleurodesis under general anesthesia in the same patient: a case report.
authors: Wang JY, Li Y.
ai_summary: A 15-year-old with recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax developed obstructive atelectasis from copious viscous mucus plugs during each of two successive video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resections and pleurodesis, despite having no preoperative respiratory symptoms. Persistent subclinical inflammation from prior mycoplasma pneumoniae and human rhinovirus infections, together with surgical stress and one-lung ventilation injury, was proposed to drive intraoperative mucus hypersecretion. Real-time video-assisted airway surveillance during the second surgery allowed timely bronchoscopic lavage and clearance, supporting preoperative evaluation of subclinical inflammation and individualized intraoperative airway management in adolescents undergoing thoracic surgery.

title: Side-Specific Concordance Between Nasal Endoscopy and Computed Tomography Severity in Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis.
authors: Kasprzyk A, Franczak-Józefkiewicz E, Mielnik-Niedzielska G, Niedzielski A.
ai_summary: This retrospective study of 73 children surgically treated for chronic rhinosinusitis found that a graded nasal endoscopic score (Lund-Kennedy) correlated strongly with CT severity (Lund-Mackay) at the patient level (ρ = 0.76) and side-specifically, with good sensitivity and specificity for detecting severe disease. However, Bland-Altman analysis showed that endoscopy cannot quantitatively substitute for CT at the individual level. The authors conclude that endoscopy is best used as a non-ionizing surrogate to grade severity, monitor disease, and select which children need CT, while CT remains necessary for surgical planning; generalizability to milder disease requires confirmation.

title: Ferroptosis in kidney disease.
authors: Wang T, Sun S, Linkermann A, Min J, Wang F.
ai_summary: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lethal lipid peroxidation, is implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, renal cell carcinoma and autosomal-dominant polycystic kidney disease.
