Ferroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells and intrarenal immune cells interacts with other regulated cell death pathways, amplifying tissue damage. Early kidney injury biomarkers such as NGAL and KIM1 are associated with ferroptotic features and may serve as indirect indicators of early ferroptotic lesions, while multimodal imaging (optical, MRI, photoacoustic, radionuclide) enables in vivo detection of ferroptotic hallmarks for early diagnosis. Preclinical studies show that synthetic small molecules, natural phytochemicals and metabolic modulators targeting ferroptotic signalling can mitigate renal injury or suppress malignant kidney cell proliferation, supporting ferroptosis as a promising therapeutic target.

title: Defining minimum media requirements for ex vivo respiratory cilia studies using mouse tracheal tissue.
authors: Francis R.
ai_summary: A simple NaCl/KCl solution approximating physiological extracellular ion concentrations preserves mouse tracheal ciliary motility for up to 2 hours at 37.5 °C, whereas storage in 0.9% saline rapidly and significantly impairs motility, especially at 4 °C. Beyond 2 hours, all solutions lacking an energy source showed small but significant declines in cilia beat frequency, which were prevented by 10 mM glucose supplementation, maintaining CBF for up to 12 hours. Ciliated cells were more susceptible to storage-associated injury and death than non-ciliated epithelial cells, a vulnerability worsened by 0.9% saline and 4 °C storage. Simplified media thus offer a standardized, cost-effective basis for mechanistic studies of motile cilia.

title: Cystic Pancreatic Lesions Diagnosed on Endoscopic Ultrasound: Frequency, Morphology, and Factors Associated with Malignant Nature of these Lesions.
authors: Tasneem AA, Luck NH, Majid Z, Ahsam S, Siddiqui M, Khan RT, Laeeq M.
ai_summary: This observational study of 56 patients with cystic pancreatic lesions (CPLs) evaluated by endoscopic ultrasound found that serous cystadenoma was the most common lesion (19.6%), followed by intraductal papillary neoplasm (17.9%) and mucinous cystic neoplasm (16.1%); most lesions were pure cystic (73.2%) and located in the pancreatic head (53.6%). Malignancy was identified in seven patients (cystic degeneration of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine cancer, and one malignant IPMN). Factors associated with malignant histology were age >55 years, solid-cystic morphology, and size >4 cm on univariate analysis, with solid-cystic morphology remaining significant on multivariate analysis, suggesting that solid-cystic morphology predicts a higher likelihood of malignancy.

title: A patient with ROHHAD syndrome and leptin-melanocortin pathway gene variations. Correlation or just a coincidence? Case report.
authors: Kostopoulou E, Efthymiadou A, Giannakopoulos A, Chrysis D.

title: Protein kinase D1 regulates innate immune signaling pathways to promote hepatitis C virus replication.
authors: Lee J, Chuang Y-C, Lee JA, Ou J-HJ.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1
Finding: HCV activates PKD1 via PKC early in infection and cleaves it later via caspase-3; PKD1 silencing reduces HCV RNA without affecting entry, induces IFN/ISG expression, augments TNF-α signaling, and compromises inflammasome induction, indicating PKD1 suppresses antiviral IFN and TNF-α responses while promoting the inflammasomal response to support viral replication.
Disease: Hepatitis C virus infection

title: A Cell Type-Specific Role for Tubb6 in Ciliogenesis of Xenopus Epidermal Multiciliated Cells.
authors: Xu X, Ross J, Clark F, Wei S, Sun J.
ai_summary:
Gene: Tubb6
Finding: Tubb6 mRNA is selectively expressed in Xenopus epidermal multiciliated cells and its protein localizes to ciliary axonemes; its depletion markedly reduces cilia number and length and impairs multiciliated cell function, while mono-motile cilia in the gastrocoel roof plate are unaffected.
Disease: Defective motile ciliogenesis in epidermal multiciliated cells (cell type-specific ciliary defect)

title: Metabolic Syndrome and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Pediatric Kidney Transplant Recipients-A Cross-Sectional Study.
authors: Saha A, Champaneri B, Patel V, Shah H, Kapadia S, Vala K, Bhatt D, Patel H, Gera D, Modi M, Modi P.
ai_summary: This cross-sectional study of 32 pediatric kidney transplant recipients in India found that 28.1% had metabolic syndrome at a median of 21.5 months post-transplant, with hypertension (68.8%) and hypertriglyceridemia (53.1%) being the most common components. Post-transplant weight gain (ΔBMI height-age Z-score) was an independent predictor of metabolic syndrome, while acute rejection independently predicted left ventricular hypertrophy; metabolic syndrome itself did not predict LVH. Graft function, LVMI, triglyceride index, and hand grip strength did not differ between MS and non-MS groups, though all patients had elevated carotid intima-media thickness.

title: Beyond Sequencing: Integrating MLPA Reveals Hidden Structural PKD2 Variants and Enhances Mutation Detection in a Highly Selected ADPKD Greek Cohort.
authors: Papachristopoulou A, Margoni A, Simoudis AC, Mylona A, Kroupi OI, Nikolopoulos P, Papavassiliou AG, Vlahakos DV, Kroupis C.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD2
Finding: In six well-characterized ADPKD patients who started kidney replacement therapy after age 70, targeted Sanger sequencing plus MLPA identified pathogenic PKD2 variants in 33%, including the recurrent nonsense variant p.Arg872Ter and a novel multi-exonic deletion of exons 1–9 detectable only by MLPA, plus a VUS (p.Leu273Gln).
Disease: Late-onset autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Congenital Nephrotic Syndrome in Oman: A 20-year single-centre experience.
authors: Al Hashmi M, Al Maskari A, Al Saidi S, Al Ghaithi B, Al Riyami M, Al Kalbani N.
ai_summary:
Gene: NPHS1
Finding: In a 20-year single-centre cohort of 26 Omani children with congenital nephrotic syndrome, genetic workup in 19 patients was positive for NPHS1 in 73.6%, with consanguinity in 61.5% and a family history of renal disease in 46.2%.
Disease: Congenital nephrotic syndrome

title: Cerebellar Contributions to Cerebral Connectivity in Severe Mental Illness: A Developmental Cascade and Predictive-Modeling Framework with Autistic Disorder as the Focal Case.
authors: Lincoln AJ.
ai_summary: This review argues that severe mental illness, including psychotic spectrum disorders and autism, should be understood as neurodevelopmental conditions arising from early perturbations rather than processes beginning at clinical presentation, though they differ in the nature and timing of the perturbation. Focusing on autistic disorder as defined under DSM-III/IV (whose diagnostic criteria enriched for a subgroup with cerebellar vermal lobules VI and VII abnormality, posterior callosal reduction, and atypical predictive processing), it hypothesizes that deviation of vermal lobules VI and VII from typical development—in either the hypoplastic or hyperplastic direction, with evidence pointing to prenatal origin—initiates a developmental cascade that shapes postnatal cerebral connectivity via disinhibition of deep cerebellar nuclei and altered excitatory drive to thalamocortical circuits during sensitive periods. Cross-condition evidence shows vermal abnormality also occurs in Joubert syndrome, fragile X, Rett syndrome, Williams syndrome, and schizophrenia, but produces the autistic-disorder cluster only when the upstream perturbation also affects cortical context-integration substrates at the relevant developmental window; these conditions are treated as instances of a common neurodevelopmental class. The framework positions the cerebellum as a substrate for predictive internal models scaffolding auditory, social, and contextual learning, and is proposed as testable through infant connectivity and event-related potential studies and stratified re-analysis of multisite samples.

title: Stepwise Humanization of the Yeast TRAPP Core Enables Functional Analysis of TRAPP Variants.
authors: Abboud C, Shokohi R, Pape O, Mehranfar M, Baple EL, Damseh N, Sacher M.
ai_summary:
Gene: TRAPPC3
Finding: A humanized yeast strain in which five TRAPP core subunits were replaced by their human orthologues enabled functional testing of TRAPPC3 variants of uncertain significance, which produced pronounced growth defects and predicted structural clashes.
Disease: TRAPPopathy disorders (TRAPP complex-related rare genetic disorders)

title: Community-acquired pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia in immunocompetent children: a study of 7 cases.
authors: Lu F, Li Y, Chen X, Chen Y, Li C, Nong G, Liu J, Wei Q.
ai_summary: This retrospective case series describes seven immunocompetent boys (median age 18 months) with community-acquired Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia, confirmed by culture or BAL mNGS. All presented acutely with fever and cough, and disease was frequently severe: lobar or mass-like consolidation, empyema or pyopneumothorax in most, bacteremia in two, and respiratory failure within 72 hours in two. Three needed intensive care, two invasive ventilation, and one decortication; there were no deaths, but four children had residual lung injury from necrotizing pneumonia. Isolates were susceptible to anti-pseudomonal β-lactams (except aztreonam), and the authors conclude that although rare, this infection causes severe disease and complications in immunocompetent children, that initial anti-pseudomonal β-lactam therapy appears effective, and that repeat cultures are warranted in persistently symptomatic patients.

title: Mechanistic Insights into the Role of Adenoid Hypertrophy and Chronic Adenoiditis in the Pathogenesis of Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Systematic Review.
authors: Pratomo GRA, Trihandoko F.
ai_summary: This systematic review of nine studies (927 children) examined how adenoid disease contributes to pediatric chronic rhinosinusitis. Evidence for mechanical obstruction was mixed, since adenoid size did not consistently correlate with CRS severity. Stronger support existed for the adenoid acting as a microbial reservoir and biofilm-bearing tissue, with pathogenic bacterial colonization and extensive adenoidal biofilm reported in affected children. Limited molecular evidence suggested reduced surfactant protein-D expression, while epithelial barrier dysfunction and mucociliary impairment rested mainly on indirect findings. Adenoidectomy improved symptoms and quality of life in selected children with medically refractory CRS. The authors conclude that adenoid hypertrophy and chronic adenoiditis likely contribute through combined obstructive, microbial, biofilm-related, inflammatory, and immunological pathways, though causality cannot be established, and that further prospective mechanistic studies are needed.

title: Child with genetically confirmed Prader-Willi syndrome.
authors: Kahssay MG, Oyieke K, Hoybye C.
ai_summary:
Gene: chromosome 15 (maternal uniparental disomy)
Finding: A boy in his early teens with short stature and early-onset obesity was genetically confirmed to have Prader-Willi syndrome due to maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 15, with modest improvement from food restriction and increased physical activity.
Disease: Prader-Willi syndrome

title: The spectrum of copy number variation in the Pan-Canadian HostSeq databank.
authors: Aujla N, Thiruvahindrapuram B, Casalino S, Frangione E, Mahajan R, Di Iorio D, Fung CYJ, Jayachandran L, MacDonald G, Morgan G, Wolday D, Young J, Arshad M, Clausen M, Arnoldo S, Binnie A, Borgundvaag B, Chowdhary S, Dagher M, Devine L, Friedman SM, Gingras AC, Goneau LW, Khan Z, Lapadula E, Mazzulli T, McGeer A, McLeod S, Mighton C, Pugh TJ, Richardson D, Simpson J, Stern S, Taher A, Strug L, Bombard Y, Faghfoury H, Greenfeld E, CGEn HostSeq Initiative, Scherer SW, Taher J, Noor A, Lerner-Ellis J.
ai_summary: This study integrated copy number variant (CNV) analysis into genome sequencing pipelines for 10,488 participants in the Canadian HostSeq cohort, generating over 8.5 million CNV calls. After filtering for rare variants (36,631 CNVs), the authors identified 82 CNVs in neurodevelopmental disorder regions and 206 putatively pathogenic CNVs based on ClinGen dosage sensitivity or DECIPHER overlap, stratifying deletions into inheritance-based tiers. The work demonstrates the value of incorporating CNV workflows into sequencing analysis and provides a population-scale CNV resource for medical genomics in Canada.

title: Comparison of Nasal Mucus Metabolites in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With and Without Polyps and Healthy Controls.
authors: Armstrong MF, Bartemes KR, Hunter DE, Griesel MD, Voss SG, Choby GW, Pinheiro Neto CD, Hagan JB, Divekar RD, O'Brien EK.
ai_summary: Nasal mucus from patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with polyps (CRSwNP), without polyps (CRSsNP), and healthy controls was compared using untargeted LC-MS metabolomics. Glycerophosphocholine and glycerol-3-phosphate (glycerophospholipid pathway) were significantly elevated in controls versus both CRS groups, while the sphingolipid metabolites C24-OH sulfatide and dihydroceramide were significantly elevated in CRSwNP compared to CRSsNP and controls. These metabolite differences suggest nasal mucus profiling may help distinguish CRS subtypes.

title: Prevalence and Correlates of Sinonasal Symptom Burden in Young Adult Males: A Cross-Sectional Population-Based Study (PrENT Study).
authors: Maitz E, Domanyi R, Schwantzer G, Sendlhofer G, Andrianakis A, Thurnher D, Weiland T.
ai_summary: Over one third (38.2%) of 500 young male adults reported at least moderate sinonasal symptom burden (SNOT-22 ≥21), with a mean score of 18.8. Higher symptom scores correlated significantly with elevated CRP and reduced relative FEV1%, while eosinophil percentages showed a non-significant numeric gradient across severity categories. The findings link sinonasal symptom burden to systemic inflammation and impaired pulmonary function, supporting the unified airway concept and the use of SNOT-22 in preventive health examinations.

title: A Novel Device to Improve the Tolerability of Intranasal Corticosteroid Sprays for Allergic Rhinitis and Postoperative Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Crossover Trial.
authors: Ranasinghe S, Berger X, Kimita W, Biswas K, Kim R, Douglas R.
journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
ai_summary: A nasal adaptor for metered-dose inhalers was developed to reduce the unpleasant sensations of intranasal corticosteroid delivery. In two crossover trials (16 allergic rhinitis and 16 postoperative chronic rhinosinusitis participants), symptom improvement was comparable between the adaptor-based fluticasone MDI and a standard fluticasone nasal spray, but 69% of participants in both groups preferred the novel device, citing fewer unpleasant sensations, with significantly greater satisfaction improvement in the CRS cohort and higher reported likelihood of compliance. The improved tolerability may enhance adherence and long-term symptom control.

title: Assessment of functional capacity in children with chronic kidney disease using various field tests.
authors: Firat M, Aksel-Uylar AA, Saglam M, Topaloglu R, Ozaltin F, Duzova A, Vardar-Yagli N, Gulhan B.
ai_summary: This study assessed functional capacity in 51 children with chronic kidney disease (mean age 13.7 years) using three field tests: the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), 2-minute walk test (2MWT), and 3-minute step test (3MST), alongside dynamometer measures of quadriceps and hand grip strength. No significant differences in field test performance were found between early and advanced CKD groups, but the early CKD group had significantly greater dominant quadriceps muscle strength, indicating that peripheral muscle strength deteriorates with advancing disease. The 6MWT and 2MWT were moderately positively correlated, and most children preferred the walking tests (43.1% each) over the step test (13.8%). The authors conclude that the 2MWT is a practical, time-efficient alternative to the 6MWT, while the 3MST remains a viable option when walking tests are not feasible.

title: Adhesion GPCRs in Kidney: New Insights into Development, Physiology and Disease.
authors: Myrzatayeva A, Singh AK, Engel FB.
ai_summary: This review compiles the literature on adhesion G-protein-coupled receptors (aGPCRs) in kidney development, physiology, and disease, summarizing their expression profiles, validation status, and knockout phenotypes. It highlights specific roles: Celsr1/Adgrc1 is expressed early in metanephric development and its deletion causes aberrant oriented cell division and simplified ureteric trees; GPR116/ADGRF5 maintains glomerular filtration barrier integrity and regulates renal acid secretion; Gpr56/Adgrg1 deletion ameliorates diabetic kidney disease, whereas GPR97/ADGRG3 upregulation exacerbates acute kidney injury and hypertensive nephropathy. Notably, no function has been proposed for roughly two-thirds of kidney-expressed aGPCRs, so the authors generate hypotheses about their potential roles based on functions in other tissues, aiming to clarify how these receptors contribute to the molecular mechanisms of kidney development and disease.

title: Five-year outcomes of next-generation sequencing implementation at a Brazilian public health system reference centre for rare diseases.
authors: Rabelo NC, Gomes ME, de Moraes IC, Abdala BB, Junior DC, Barth A, Correia P, Vieira DKR, Rolemberg F, Gomes N, Magalhães TSPC, Horovitz DDG, Llerena JC, Gonzalez S.
ai_summary: This five-year study evaluated the implementation of next-generation sequencing (clinical or whole-exome sequencing) in 385 patients with suspected genetic disorders at a Brazilian public health reference centre for rare diseases. The overall diagnostic yield was 38.7% (149/385 cases), with 249 variants identified across 165 genes, including 75 previously unreported variants. Actionable secondary findings were found in 3.2% of cases, involving genes linked to cardiac disease, cancer predisposition, and anesthesia risk. The authors conclude that NGS is feasible and impactful in the Brazilian public health system, reducing the diagnostic odyssey, but that success depends on multidisciplinary care, standardized HPO-based phenotyping, and clinical-laboratory integration, while highlighting challenges in interpreting variants of uncertain significance in Brazil's admixed, underrepresented population.

title: The frequent exacerbator phenotype in bronchiectasis revisited: data from EMBARC registry.
authors: Sibila O, Perea L, Burgel PR, Polverino E, Hull RC, Long MB, Chotirmall SH, Shteinberg M, Pollock J, Stobo J, Lind H, Haworth C, Dimakou K, Bossios A, Loebinger MR, Dhar R, Xu JF, Mersch P, Rademacher J, Choi H, Lorent N, Blasi F, Vendrell M, Goeminne P, Ringshausen F, De Soyza A, Aliberti S, Chalmers JD.
journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
ai_summary: This large EMBARC registry analysis of 19,324 patients with bronchiectasis across 30 countries shows that each prior exacerbation incrementally raises the risk of future exacerbations and severe (hospitalized) exacerbations, with no clear threshold defining a "frequent exacerbator" phenotype. The association was highly consistent across etiologies and geographic regions, suggesting that exacerbation history should be treated as a continuous risk gradient rather than a binary ≥3-per-year cutoff.

title: In the wisdom of Odin: modular architecture, receptor trafficking and therapeutic implications.
authors: Pennacchietti V, Malagrinò F, Gianni S.
ai_summary: Odin (ANKS1A) is a multidomain adaptor protein originally identified as a receptor tyrosine kinase substrate, now recognized to coordinate receptor signaling and membrane trafficking. Through its conserved modular architecture, Odin contributes to ependymal cell development, ciliogenesis, and neurovascular homeostasis, and its dysfunction has been linked to cancer, neurodevelopmental disorders, neurodegeneration, ciliopathies, and cardiovascular disease. This review synthesizes current knowledge of Odin structure and function, proposes a model in which its multidomain architecture underlies its role in receptor trafficking and membrane homeostasis, and argues that Odin remains a promising but largely unexplored therapeutic target for which few strategies currently exist.

title: Zebrafish larvae swim bladder serves as a model to study Mycobacterium abscessus infection kinetics, host-pathogen interactions and drug efficacy.
authors: Basnet RM, Gupta S, Olivier KN.
ai_summary: A new zebrafish larva model injects Mycobacterium abscessus directly into the swim bladder, which resembles the human lung histologically and physiologically, to better mimic respiratory NTM infection than the commonly used caudal vein route. Bacteria formed localized biofilm-like growth with minimal systemic spread, recruited neutrophils and macrophages into granuloma-like structures, and raised TNF-α. Clarithromycin and omadacycline both significantly reduced this biofilm-like growth, establishing the model for studying localized infection, host-pathogen interactions, and drug efficacy.

title: Neuron-specific enolase and brain-derived neurotrophic factor as developmental neurovascular markers in chronic kidney disease and kidney transplantation.
authors: Hernandez L, Strizzi CT, Lindblad YT, Stenvinkel P, Barany P, Chromek M, Kublickiene K.
ai_summary: This prospective cohort study of 75 children (12 with normal kidney function, 31 with non-dialysis CKD stages G2–G5, and 32 kidney transplant recipients) examined circulating neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) as markers of the pediatric kidney-brain axis. NSE correlated inversely with age rather than reflecting CKD status, indicating it primarily tracks developmental stage; group comparisons therefore require age adjustment. Kidney transplantation altered the NSE-age relationship beyond what kidney function alone could explain. BDNF tracked kidney function in pediatric CKD. The authors conclude that age-stratified reference intervals are needed before either marker can guide clinical decisions.

title: Ciliary Ift20 and Wwtr1 Coordinate Transforming Growth Factor-β Receptor II Signaling to Maintain Bone-Fat Balance in Skeletal Homeostasis.
authors: Li Y, Yang Y, Yang S, Chang H, Li YP, Yang S.
ai_summary:
Gene: Ift20
Finding: In osteoblast-lineage cells, Ift20 localizes to primary cilia and protects TβRII from c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination and degradation, while Wwtr1 transcriptionally activates TβRII; combined loss of Ift20 and Wwtr1 suppresses TGF-β signaling, impairing osteoblast differentiation and enhancing adipogenesis and osteoclastogenesis, causing severe bone loss and excess marrow adipose tissue that worsens under ovariectomy and high-fat diet.
Disease: Osteoporosis and metabolic bone loss

title: Reporter-guided photoreceptor differentiation in 2D culture using PGP1-hIPSCs: A comparable alternative to 3D organoid systems?
authors: Beaver D, Cioanca AC, Barnett NL.
ai_summary:
Gene: TMEM138
Finding: A xeno-free 2D differentiation protocol generated photoreceptor-like cells from PGP1 hIPSCs that expressed cilium markers including TMEM138 and CX36, alongside ultrastructural features of developing cilia and disc-like whorls, with transcriptomic profiles comparable to 3D retinal organoid cultures.
Disease: Photoreceptor differentiation (retinal cell therapy development)

title: Post-translational protein S-palmitoylation in renal tubular injury: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
authors: Li M, Zhu H, Zhao H, Liu C, Wang Y, Zuo L.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review discusses how S-palmitoylation, a reversible lipid modification, influences renal tubular injury in AKI and CKD. In tubular epithelial cells it normally supports polarity, ciliary function, ion transport, and receptor signaling, but dysregulated palmitoylation during injury can worsen cell damage, inflammation, and fibrosis, while other changes are protective—outcomes depending on the specific protein, enzyme, and cell type. The authors conclude that therapies should target specific pathogenic enzyme-substrate pairs with cell-specific delivery rather than globally modulating palmitoylation, which risks disrupting protective pathways.

title: An antioxidant therapy elicits distinct transcriptome responses in 22q11-deleted upper layer cortical projection neurons.
authors: Rukh S, Meechan DW, Roberts A, Siggins C, Erwin ZD, Maynard TM, LaMantia AS.
ai_summary: NAC improves the growth, connectivity, and cognitive performance of upper-layer cortical projection neurons in a 22q11.2 deletion syndrome mouse model, but it does so by inducing growth and antioxidant-defense gene programs rather than by restoring wild-type expression of 22q11 downstream targets. The transcriptional response to NAC differs between primary culture and postnatal cortex and includes gene sets that respond only in the context of the 22q11 deletion, indicating a distinct in vivo therapeutic signature.

title: Comparative Genomic Screening Identifies Developmental Constraint Loci Underscoring the Phenotypic Evolution of Syngnathids.
authors: Dong Z, Wang C, Dong S, Peng Y, Guo J, Zhang C, Xu Z, Wu Z, Wang B, Qu Q.
ai_summary: Comparative genomic screening of syngnathids (seahorses and relatives) identified loci underlying their distinctive morphology. A convergent amino acid change in lat4a, shared with some flying fishes, was confirmed in vitro to drive fin size reduction in both lineages. Tooth loss appears to result from loss of regulatory elements such as pitx2 rather than changes in tooth-development genes, which remain conserved. The study also implicates col6a3 in spinal curvature development in seadragons, highlighting developmental constraints shaping syngnathid phenotypic evolution.

title: Bone Aging and Glycative Stress: Convergent and Divergent Mechanisms Driving Skeletal Deterioration.
authors: Peñarrubia S, Martín-Guerrero E, Gortázar AR, Ardura JA.
ai_summary: This review compares how aging and glycative stress drive skeletal fragility through shared versus distinct pathways. Both converge on oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, senescence, impaired autophagy, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and ferroptosis, reducing osteocyte viability and disrupting RANKL/OPG-mediated remodeling. They diverge in primary drivers: aging involves hormonal decline and stem-cell exhaustion with progressive loss of bone mass and microarchitecture, whereas glycative stress acts via AGE-RAGE signaling and collagen cross-linking, impairing bone quality and mechanosensitivity while often preserving bone mineral density—explaining the elevated fracture risk in diabetes. Because current anabolic and anti-resorptive therapies do not target AGE-related pathways, the authors argue that combined senolytic, antiglycative, and mechanoprotective strategies plus lifestyle interventions may be needed to reduce fracture risk in aged and diabetic populations.

title: Ulcerative colitis-driven gut dysbiosis exacerbates periodontal bone loss through the gut-oral axis /Th17/Treg imbalance.
authors: Huang Y, Hu Y, Zhao Y, Li Y, Liu Y, Wang M, Wang Q, Hu H.
ai_summary: Ulcerative colitis-driven gut dysbiosis acts as a transmissible causal factor in periodontitis. In a mouse model combining ligature-induced periodontitis with DSS colitis, UC doubled alveolar bone loss and increased systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and osteoclastogenesis. Microbiome and metabolome analyses showed enriched oral pathogens, depleted gut Firmicutes, expanded Bacteroides, and suppressed amino-acid/bile-acid biosynthesis. Fecal microbiota transplantation from colitis donors into antibiotic-pretreated periodontitis-prone mice reproduced aggravated bone loss, gut-barrier leakage, and Th17/Treg imbalance, whereas healthy-donor FMT was protective. Short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate) fell by 35-60%, with keystone taxa Parabacteroides and Muribaculum inversely correlating with SCFAs and inflammatory genes. SCFA-producing microbes or supplementation are proposed as potential therapeutics for UC-associated periodontitis.

title: Proceedings of the 33rd European Paediatric Rheumatology Congress.
Liver disease reveals KIF12 as a regulator of mitochondria, lysosome and cilia localisation in human cholangiocytes.
authors: Seth A, Brancale J, Dashti-Gibson N, Florentino RM, Faccioli LAP, Liu Z, Konkwo C, Hong H, Soto-Gutierrez A, Vilarinho S.
ai_summary:
Gene: KIF12
Finding: The patient-derived homozygous p.Arg219∗ KIF12 mutation reduced KIF12 transcript and protein, and caused perinuclear clustering of mitochondria and lysosomes, mislocalisation of primary cilia, and increased GGT activity in human cholangiocyte-like cells and biliary organoids, all rescued by wildtype KIF12 re-expression.
Disease: High gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) cholestatic liver disease

title: Multi-omics analyses reveal steroid hormone and antioxidant pathways regulating sperm storage capacity in female Muscovy ducks (Cairina moschata).
authors: Wu Z, Chao X, Chang Z, Lan L, Ma XR, Zhu W, Liu A, Liang W, Zhang X, Fang C, Ji C, Luo Q.
ai_summary: This study investigated the physiological and molecular basis of sperm storage capacity in female Muscovy ducks by phenotyping roughly 1,500 birds across three generations, focusing on peak and late laying stages, and comparing high- versus low-storage individuals using histology plus transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. Sperm storage capacity declined significantly with age and was linked to the integrity of ciliated cells in the uterovaginal junction (UVJ) microenvironment. Multi-omics analyses highlighted steroid hormone biosynthesis, glutathione metabolism, and tryptophan metabolism, with cholesterol and progesterone emerging as candidate biomarkers. Down-regulation of LIMA1 and CYP2R1 pointed to coordinated regulation of antioxidant balance, immune response, and steroid synthesis in the UVJ, providing a multi-omics framework and candidate biomarkers for improving fertility duration in poultry.

title: Craniofacial development: genetics, signaling pathways, teratogenic mechanisms, and clinal significance.
authors: Lv X, Du J.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes the cellular and molecular mechanisms of normal craniofacial development, centered on the coordinated regulation of cranial neural crest cells by transcription factors, signaling pathways, and epigenetic programs. It summarizes pathogenic mechanisms of craniofacial disorders such as cleft palate and craniosynostosis, and explores how maternal endogenous and external environmental teratogens interact with genetic factors to reshape developmental trajectories. Emphasizing gene-environment interactions as central to craniofacial pathogenesis, the authors integrate evidence from developmental biology, multi-omics, and clinical studies, and outline current diagnostic techniques and management strategies along with existing challenges and future directions.

title: Divergent microtubule-organizing center strategies in mammalian gametogenesis.
authors: Skinner MW, Jordan PW.
ai_summary: This review contrasts how male and female mammalian gametes build the microtubule-organizing centers (MTOCs) that drive meiotic spindle assembly. Spermatocytes retain canonical centrosomes with meiosis-specific biogenesis, yet these centrosomes are dispensable for chromosome segregation, which can instead be carried out by a noncentrosomal MTOC pathway. Oocytes, in contrast, eliminate centrioles and build bipolar MTOCs by coalescing pericentriolar material, aided by a chromosome-driven spindle assembly pathway. The review also covers species-specific differences in MTOC regulation between mouse and human oocytes and argues that defects in these pathways are a primary cause of aneuploidy and infertility.

title: The kinesin motor Kif9 regulates centriolar satellite positioning during interphase.
authors: Vicente JJ, Wagenbach M, Decarreau J, Zelter A, MacCoss MJ, Davis TN, Wordeman L.
ai_summary:
Gene: Kif9
Finding: The microtubule plus-end-directed kinesin Kif9 localizes to centriolar satellites and controls their pericentrosomal positioning during interphase; loss of Kif9 causes satellites to aggregate closer to the centrosome, increases centrosomal protein degradation, disrupts centrosome maturation, and leads to chromosome congression and segregation defects in mitosis.
Disease: Centrosome maturation defects and chromosome missegregation (mitotic defects)

title: Coordinated neural progenitor adaptations contribute to primate neocortical downscaling.
authors: Tynianskaia L, Bastidas-Betancourt CM, Grewe EM, Kniep JM, Liutikaite N, Esiyok N, Göloğlu İB, Heide S, Rüger N, Lindenwald D, Drummer C, Petkov S, Di Donato N, Heide M.
ai_summary: The study investigates why the common marmoset, unlike most primates, has a small, smooth (lissencephalic) neocortex, likely reflecting an evolutionary reduction from the ancestral folded primate condition. Using marmoset and human cerebral organoids alongside analyses of fetal marmoset neocortical tissue and published histological data, the authors identify coordinated adaptations in neural progenitor cells. Multiple changes in apical and basal progenitors converge on reduced progenitor capacity and altered early progenitor dynamics, which likely constrain neuronal output and thereby limit the size and folding of the marmoset neocortex.

title: Retbindin Dynamically Redistributes to Preserve Retinal Flavin-Dependent Homeostasis in Response to Riboflavin Availability and Circadian Demand.
authors: Zhao X, Makia MS, Moiseyev GP, Naash MI, Al-Ubaidi MR.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
ai_summary:
Gene: RTBDN
Finding: RTBDN abundance and localization are dynamically regulated by developmental stage, riboflavin availability, and the light-dark cycle—redistributing from the outer segment-RPE interface toward cone-associated domains during fasting or darkness and returning to outer segment tips upon riboflavin repletion or light onset—thereby adapting retinal flavin-dependent homeostasis to nutrient flux and circadian demand.
Disease: Cone degeneration

title: CRISPR-Cas technologies: Emerging tools from research to clinical application.
authors: Hyeon H, Hwang S, Luo Y, Shin E, Yeom JH, Kim HM, Ryu M, Lee K.
ai_summary: This review surveys the expanding CRISPR-Cas toolkit for gene therapy, covering SpCas9 alongside engineered variants, alternative Cas enzymes, base and prime editors, RNA-targeting Cas13, and CRISPRa/i systems for gene regulation. It describes delivery options such as electroporation, adeno-associated viruses, and lipid nanoparticles for DNA, RNA, or ribonucleoprotein cargo, and reviews clinical progress. The authors conclude that CRISPR-based therapeutics hold major potential for treating many diseases, including rare congenital diseases, through permanent genomic DNA correction, but that further advances in targeted delivery, safety, and stability are needed to maximize therapeutic efficiency.

title: Regional signaling controls stem cell-mediated regeneration in an invertebrate chordate.
authors: Gordon T, Levy T, Yu CJ, Rosental B, Lubeck L, Manni L, Weissman IL, Voskoboynik A.
ai_summary: This study uses the ascidian Ciona robusta, in which bottom body fragments regenerate after injury while upper fragments do not, to investigate how local signals control stem cell activation. Combining flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, transplantation, and fate mapping, the authors identified a candidate stem cell population with strong proliferative and differentiation potential upon transplantation. However, regenerative success was not determined by stem cell abundance alone but by region-specific signaling cues, with local expression of metabolic, immune, and differentiation-related factors shaping divergent outcomes from a shared injury response.

title: Spatial and single-cell dissection of medulloblastoma identifies developmental hierarchies and a prognostic PPIA-BSG tumor-immune axis.
authors: Chen M, Duan B, Zhang J, Daniels C, Hu C, Yuan J, Guo J, Taylor MD, Shi X, Zhang L, Li D, Sun T.
ai_summary:
Gene: PPIA-BSG
Finding: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of medulloblastoma revealed infiltrating immune cells with an activated regulatory T-cell phenotype and identified the PPIA-BSG co-receptor signaling axis as an independent prognostic factor.
Disease: Medulloblastoma

title: Spatially patterned kidney assembloids recapitulate progenitor self-assembly and enable high-fidelity in vivo disease modeling.
authors: Huang B, Medina P, He J, Zeng Z, Kim S, Romo J, Koppitch K, Zhang CC, Gyarmati G, Park Y, Bohovyk R, N'Guetta PY, Guo J, Ma T, Schreiber ME, Xu C, Pham J, Parvez RK, Su J, Xia MW, Liu Z, Perin L, El-Nachef D, Murry CE, Kumar S, O'Brien L, Zimmerman KA, Ichida J, Lindström NO, Pastor-Soler NM, Hallows KR, Staruschenko A, Peti-Peterdi J, Jiang C, McMahon AP, Li Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKD1/PKD2 (ADPKD-associated genes; genome-edited human KPAs)
Finding: Spatially organized mouse and human kidney progenitor assembloids (KPAs) recapitulate nephron progenitor self-assembly with fusion to a central collecting system, show improved maturity and kidney functions, and when genome-edited and grown in vivo model ADPKD cystic phenotypes and cyst-stroma-macrophage crosstalk.
Disease: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)

title: Comparative proteomic characterization of seminal plasma and sperm proteins associated with reproductive function in the Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus).
authors: Fahrudin M, Witri BW, Arifiantini I, Prasetyaningtyas WE, Indrawati A, Karja NWK.
ai_summary: This study provides the first proteomic characterization of seminal plasma and sperm in the Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin. Of 199 proteins identified, seminal plasma proteins (84) were enriched for catabolic, proteolytic, and endopeptidase-regulatory functions supporting sperm protection and survival, while sperm proteins (119) were enriched for oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial ATP synthesis, spermatogenesis, and flagellar motility, with only four proteins shared between fractions. The findings reveal distinct functional specialization of the two semen fractions and suggest oxidative phosphorylation is the principal energy pathway supporting sperm function in this species, offering a resource for fertility biomarkers and assisted reproduction in a Near Threatened cetacean.

title: Mitochondrial outer membrane protein FUNDC2 contributes to ferroptosis as a potential upstream regulator in retinitis pigmentosa.
authors: Chen JY, Huang YF, Hong Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: FUNDC2
Finding: FUNDC2 is upregulated in the retinal pigment epithelium of a sodium iodate-induced rat model and in ARPE-19 cells, and its knockdown rescues cell viability loss and restores GPX4 expression, indicating it acts as an upstream regulator of ferroptosis by negatively regulating GPX4.
Disease: Retinitis pigmentosa

title: Programmed cell death in degenerative skeletal diseases: molecular crosstalk and combinatorial therapeutic strategies.
authors: Zhao R, Zhao J, Yin H, Zhan Y, Ma D, Xue X, Yang W.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review argues that apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis and autophagy-associated cell death are rarely independent in osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration and osteoporosis, but are instead shaped by cell type, anatomical niche, disease stage and stress intensity. It proposes an evidence-graded framework that distinguishes genuine mechanistic crosstalk (shared upstream triggers, convergent regulatory nodes, sequential transitions, direct molecular conversion) from mere functional coexistence, warning that detecting multiple death markers together is often wrongly read as causal interaction. The authors also assess therapies targeting the cell death–inflammation–metabolism axis, including multi-target agents, nanomaterials, extracellular vesicles, biomaterials and tissue engineering, but note that most evidence is preclinical and requires human validation and confirmation of causal targets.

title: Itraconazole induced ferroptosis in acute myeloid leukemia cells through TP53INP1.
authors: Qi Y, Han C, Lin Y, Cheng S, She Y, Zhang M, Xie H, Yang G, Zeng D.
ai_summary:
Gene: TP53INP1
Finding: Itraconazole induces ferroptosis in AML cells via upregulation of TP53INP1, whose knockdown attenuates ferroptosis by altering iron metabolism and elevating SLC7A11 and GPX4, while also impairing AML progression in vivo.
Disease: Acute myeloid leukemia

title: Cr(VI) and DON co-exposure triggers intestinal epithelial cells ferroptosis and pyroptosis through Nrf2/NF-κB/NLRP3 to impair intestinal barrier function.
authors: Gu Y, Miao X, Fan L, Cai G, Song R, Zou H, Gu J, Yuan Y, Liu X, Liu Z, Bian J.
journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
ai_summary: This study investigated how the environmental pollutants Cr(VI) and deoxynivalenol (DON), which co-occur naturally, damage the intestinal barrier. Using network toxicology plus cell experiments in broiler intestinal epithelial cells with pathway activators/inhibitors (TBHQ for Nrf2, PDTC for NF-κB, MCC950 for NLRP3), the authors found that Cr(VI) and/or DON caused oxidative stress, suppressed Nrf2, and abnormally activated NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling, triggering ferroptosis and pyroptosis and disrupting tight junctions. Overexpressing Nrf2 or silencing NLRP3/NF-κB reversed these effects, indicating that bidirectional imbalance of the Nrf2/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis and the resulting cross-regulation of ferroptosis and pyroptosis is the core mechanism of intestinal barrier dysfunction from combined Cr(VI) and DON exposure.

title: High-altitude hypoxia and male reproductive dysfunction: testicular oxygen homeostasis, microenvironmental injury and spermatogonial niche vulnerability.
authors: Li J, Meng D, Zhang B, Yang C, Ma F, Li F, Wang Y, Zheng Z, Wang Z, Li M, Liu L, Chang D.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes human high-altitude exposure studies, mountaineering observations, and animal hypobaric hypoxia models showing that high-altitude hypoxia is associated with reduced sperm concentration, total count, motility, viability, and normal morphology, alongside testicular structural injury, oxidative stress, and reproductive endocrine changes in experimental models. Because the magnitude and reversibility of these effects vary widely, the authors argue that altitude-related reproductive dysfunction is not a simple linear consequence of hypoxia but a dynamic process shaped by exposure intensity and duration, acclimatization, systemic stressors, and local testicular compensatory capacity. They propose an integrated framework centered on testicular oxygen homeostasis, dual microenvironmental injury, and spermatogonial niche vulnerability, in which failed compensation propagates injury through two interconnected compartments—the interstitial vascular endothelial niche–Leydig-cell–immune axis and the seminiferous Sertoli-cell–blood-testis barrier–germ-cell support system—with peritubular myoid cells, basement membrane, and extracellular matrix linking them and contributing to the spermatogonial stem-cell niche. Rete testis/efferent ductules, the epididymal microenvironment, blood-epididymis barrier, and seminal extracellular vesicles are positioned as downstream or modifying layers rather than primary mechanisms, and whether injury reaches spermatogonia or their niche may determine whether recovery is rapid and complete or delayed and incomplete. The review also highlights evidence gaps, including direct measurement of local testicular oxygen tension, compartment-specific designs, niche-targeted endpoints, and longitudinal high-altitude/lowland return cohorts.

title: TRAIL of Hope: Bioactive Dietary Component-Driven Carrier-Free Nanoplatforms for Synergistically Enhanced Tumor Multimodal Therapy.
authors: Yang L, Song X, Wang Z.
ai_summary: This review surveys carrier-free nanoplatforms built from bioactive dietary components (e.g., capsaicin, curcumin, epigallocatechin gallate, quercetin, ursolic acid) as a strategy for multimodal cancer therapy, drawing on 2024–2025 literature. Using dietary molecules themselves as self-assembled building blocks avoids inert carrier materials, yielding higher drug loading, optimized drug ratios, simpler fabrication, and better biosafety. Such platforms can be combined with chemotherapy, chemodynamic, immuno-, photodynamic, photothermal, and sonodynamic therapies, and the authors discuss remaining challenges and prospects for clinical translation.

title: Kinesins in Cancer Drug Resistance: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Targeting, and Translational Potential.
authors: Tan Y, Feng Y, Jiang Y, Li M, Xie Z.
ai_summary: This review examines how kinesin superfamily proteins contribute to cancer drug resistance through roles in mitotic regulation, intracellular transport, and stress-response pathways. While aberrant kinesin expression is frequently associated with aggressive disease, poor prognosis, and treatment resistance across cancers, the authors stress that expression changes alone do not prove functional dependency, and mechanistic validation is needed to separate true resistance drivers from adaptive tumor states. The review covers kinesin classification and biology, resistance mechanisms, and targeting strategies including natural-product inhibitors, small-molecule development, rational combinations, and structure-guided optimization, along with biomarker potential and advanced preclinical models. It concludes that clinical translation is hindered by limited target specificity, compensatory resistance, insufficient biomarker validation, and tumor heterogeneity, and that progress will require integrating functional genomics, multiomics, and mechanism-guided strategies to establish when kinesin inhibition is clinically actionable.

title: Mixed-Culture Fermentation of Coffee Pulp Induces Metabolomic Changes and Enhances Multi-Target Bioactivity Relevant to Androgenetic Alopecia.
authors: Muangsanguan A, Ruksiriwanich W, Panti N, Sawangrat K, Pummara P, Rachtanapun P, Sringarm K, Sommano SR, Krobthong S, Arjin C, Satsook A, Castagnini JM.
ai_summary:
Gene: GLI1
Finding: Mixed-culture fermentation of coffee pulp (MIX-CP) upregulated Sonic Hedgehog pathway genes including GLI1, SHH, and SMO in human hair follicle dermal papilla cells, alongside increased cell proliferation, reduced oxidative stress, and downregulation of SRD5A1/SRD5A2 and TGFB1.
Disease: Androgenetic alopecia

title: Peroxiredoxin 4 Involved in Spermatogenesis by Affecting Oxidative Stress and Ferroptosis.
authors: Yuan S, Wei N, Ma W, Hu M, Zhang B, Gao L, Gao C, Yang X, Meng Y, Liu J, Cui Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: PRDX4
Finding: Prdx4 deficiency in mice and Leydig cells increased oxidative stress and ferroptosis (with decreased GPX4 and SLC7A11 and increased ACSL4 and COX2), impairing spermatogenesis and fertility, effects partially rescued by deferoxamine or SLC7A11 overexpression.
Disease: Impaired spermatogenesis and male infertility associated with aging and oxidative stress

title: The interaction between oxidative stress and Schwann cells.
authors: Yang S, Zhang Z, Liao Q, Ouyang Q, Ye Y, Lu W, Jiang Z.
ai_summary: This review discusses the dual role of reactive oxygen species in peripheral nerve injury: moderate ROS levels promote Schwann cell proliferation, differentiation, and signal transduction, whereas excessive ROS cause oxidative stress that induces Schwann cell apoptosis, activates inflammation, and disrupts the regenerative environment. Because Schwann cells are central to peripheral nerve repair, alleviating oxidative damage to them is proposed as a route to more precise nerve regeneration. The article surveys emerging tissue engineering approaches—functionally designed neural scaffolds and conduits—that exploit or target this Schwann cell–oxidative stress interaction, aiming to provide new treatments for temporary or permanent functional deficits in peripheral nerve injury and peripheral neuropathies.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: pathogenic mechanisms and exercise-induced molecular adaptations.
authors: Lei S, Tao J, Chen X, Li X, Zhong S.
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenic mechanisms of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), emphasizing that progression from steatosis to steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma is driven by interconnected disturbances in lipid handling, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, immune-inflammatory activation, programmed cell death, autophagy-lysosomal homeostasis, and gut-liver communication. Impaired lipid storage, oxidation, export, and detoxification interact with organelle stress, macrophage activation, inflammasome and cell-death signaling, defective autophagic clearance, and bidirectional gut-liver inputs to promote hepatocellular injury and fibrogenesis. The authors also review how exercise modality, intensity, dose, and timing influence MASLD, concluding that exercise may enhance lipid mobilization and fatty acid oxidation, improve mitochondrial and autophagic quality control, restrain inflammatory and programmed cell-death pathways, and reshape gut-liver axis function. They argue that defining disease-stage- and phenotype-specific responses, along with reliable metabolic and molecular biomarkers, will be essential for translating exercise-induced adaptations into individualized MASLD management.

title: From Traditional Remedy to Evidence-Based Phytotherapeutic Agent: Hedera helix L. in Respiratory Medicine.
authors: Pawłowska AM.
ai_summary:
Gene: GRK2
Finding: In β2-adrenergic receptor cell models, Hedera helix constituents such as α-hederin reduced agonist-induced receptor internalisation, increased ligand binding and cAMP responsiveness, and altered GRK2/β-arrestin signalling, supporting the extract's expectorant and antitussive effects in productive cough.
Disease: Productive cough/bronchitis

title: Phloretin as a functional feed bioactive in livestock: Biological role, biosynthesis, and practical applications.
authors: Areb E, Zhu Q, Han L, Pan C, Li W, Lan X.
journal: Animal nutrition (Zhongguo xu mu shou yi xue hui)
ai_summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence on phloretin, a dihydrochalcone polyphenol found mainly in apples, as a functional feed bioactive in livestock. Phloretin exerts antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting the NF-κB inflammatory pathway, activating the Nrf2 antioxidant response, and regulating glucose and lipid metabolism through AMPK-related signaling. These mechanisms are linked to improved intestinal barrier integrity, reduced lipopolysaccharide-induced oxidative stress, and better resilience to environmental and metabolic stressors, with potential gains in growth performance and reproductive function. However, the authors note that current research is fragmented and largely confined to in vitro or non-livestock models, with insufficient data on optimal dosage and links to economically important production traits, and they call for nutrigenomics and controlled feeding trials to establish evidence-based applications.

title: A mutation in Bicdl1 (BICD family-like cargo adaptor 1) leads to mild outer retina thinning and late retinal dysfunction in a mouse model.
authors: Ulker-Yilmazer G, Kirman DC, Yu T, Turpin ER, Shrestha S, Yuksel S, He YG, Ludwig S, Kumar A, Xing C, Moresco EMY, Beutler BA, Aredo B, Ufret-Vincenty RL.
ai_summary:
Gene: Bicdl1
Finding: A point mutation in Bicdl1 causes mild outer retina and rod outer segment thinning, increased fundus spots and Iba1+/Tmem119+ cells on RPE flat mounts, reduced a-wave amplitudes in aging mice, and fewer RPE mitochondria, with transcriptomics linking low Bicdl1 expression to increased oxidative phosphorylation in photoreceptors.
Disease: Mild outer retinal thinning and late retinal dysfunction

title: An Optimized Diagnostic Approach for Adults With Suspected Inherited Metabolic Disorders.
authors: Oud MM, Ferreira EA, van Karnebeek CDM, Wijngaard R, Wolf NI, Engelen M, Datema M, Ferdinandusse S, van Kuilenburg ABP, Steinbusch L, van der Crabben SN, Langeveld M, ZOEMBA Study Group.
ai_summary: A reanalysis study of 31 adults who remained undiagnosed with suspected inherited metabolic disorders after standard care used deep phenotyping by a clinical geneticist, adult metabolic specialist, and neurologist, followed by exome reanalysis with multidisciplinary variant prioritization. This yielded a (partial) diagnosis in nine participants from six families (25% diagnostic yield). The authors identified four reasons the causal variants were missed initially; beyond technical advances and new disease-gene knowledge, the most impactful factor was organizational. They conclude that reviewing all strong genetic variants within a multidisciplinary team, enabling bidirectional exchange of expertise, improves diagnostic accuracy, especially when the underlying cause is not immediately apparent.

title: Changes in gut microbiota and plasma metabolites in patients with symptomatic degenerative rotator cuff tendinopathy.
authors: Liu Y, Liu Z, Zhang B, Wang W, Tian X, Cheng W.
ai_summary: This case-control multi-omics study compared gut microbiota and plasma metabolites in 61 patients with symptomatic degenerative rotator cuff tendinopathy (dRCT) and 61 matched healthy controls. dRCT patients showed significant gut microbiota dysbiosis (altered β-diversity), with enrichment of pro-inflammatory taxa (Bacteroidota, Pseudomonadota, Segatella, Megamonas, Klebsiella, Desulfovibrio, Agathobacter, Alistipes) and depletion of short-chain fatty acid/butyrate-producing genera (Gemmiger, Eubacterium_ruminantium group). Functional prediction indicated upregulated pro-inflammatory microbial pathways (LPS biosynthesis, flagellar assembly) in dRCT versus amino acid synthesis and tissue-repair pathways in controls. Untargeted plasma metabolomics revealed numerous differential metabolites, with KEGG enrichment implicating tryptophan metabolism, ferroptosis, unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, bile secretion, and steroid hormone biosynthesis. Correlation analysis linked Segatella and Megamonas negatively with indole-3-acetaldehyde and vitamin E, and Gemmiger positively with quininic acid. The authors propose a "gut-tendon axis" in which gut-derived endotoxin production, reduced tryptophan-to-indole conversion, and ferroptosis-related oxidative stress may contribute to tendon degeneration.

title: Impact of Microgravity on Cytoskeletal Dynamics, Protein Transport, and Signaling Networks: Potential Therapeutic Opportunities for Skin Health.
authors: Ballard JM, Chiguru R, Deeb MB, Swatsburg RB, Lau AY, Davis GH, Demiri M, Keller JT, Nourachi B, Abu Shihadeh TA, Schneider R, Articulo E, Daye NM, Awwad TA, Lamko B, Bailey SM, Guerra BL, Guerra SL, Quarterman C, Nanjundan M.
ai_summary: This review surveys PubMed findings on how microgravity affects cytoskeletal components, intracellular protein trafficking, and signaling cascades in mammalian model systems, with attention to the cell culture technologies used in actual spaceflight and simulated microgravity conditions. The authors identify gaps in current knowledge and propose that mechanistic insights from microgravity research could inform new therapeutic approaches for skin disorders such as atopic dermatitis and psoriasis, for which existing treatments carry adverse effects.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals a pro-fibrotic epithelial subpopulation contributing to endometrial dysfunction in polycystic ovary syndrome.
authors: Wang Q, Zhi Y, Xie H, Lang J, Yang W, Liang A, Zhu X, Fu Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: DCN
Finding: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified a DCN-high/ECM1-high endometrial epithelial subpopulation with elevated epithelial-mesenchymal transition propensity that is expanded in PCOS, driven by reduced anti-fibrotic BMP signaling from fibroblasts and increased pro-fibrotic TGFβ signaling from immune cells, with worsening in obese versus non-obese PCOS.
Disease: Endometrial dysfunction and reduced endometrial receptivity in polycystic ovary syndrome

title: Lineage relationships in muscle stem cells: linking functional fate to molecular state.
authors: Ashekyan O, Catenacci MJ, Guilhot C, Lin T, Rudnicki MA.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review examines the heterogeneity of muscle stem cells (MuSCs/satellite cells) during the transition from quiescence to activation, contrasting two models of lineage progression: classical lineage-tracing and transplantation studies, which revealed functional heterogeneity and suggested a hierarchical organization, and next-generation sequencing/single-cell approaches, which resolved molecular heterogeneity and suggested continuous dynamic state transitions. The authors argue these models are typically interpreted independently and that their interrelationship is overlooked. They propose a lineage progression model in which functional fate and molecular state are not mutually exclusive but intertwined, depending on the level and specific transition, and call for future work combining lineage tracing and transplantation with single-cell multi-omics to better understand MuSC deficits in disease and aging and to guide therapeutic strategies.

title: Unveiling the Mechanisms of Ozone-Induced Male Reproductive Toxicity: Insights from Testicular Proteomics and CTD Database.
authors: Zhuge R, Ren J, Zhu Y, Wang S, Chen R, Lai B, Yan Z, Li Y, Guo C.
ai_summary:
Gene: HIF1A
Finding: Short-term ozone exposure in mice impaired sperm quality and testicular histology and disrupted cholesterol, steroid hormone, and retinol metabolism; proteomics and CTD mining implicated HIF-1α/mTOR signaling, and in vitro air-liquid interface coculture showed ozone triggered ROS-mediated oxidative stress that inactivated HIF-1 signaling and impaired Leydig cell steroidogenesis.
Disease: Ozone-induced male reproductive toxicity (impaired spermatogenesis and steroidogenesis, reduced sperm quality)

title: Single-cell and multi-omics integration delineates the landscape of gene-wise intratumor heterogeneity and identifies prognostic biomarkers for immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Yuan J, Weng Z, Li Z, Chen R, Cheng C, Yang W, Xie X, Luo C, Wang T, Zhang S, Tan Z.
ai_summary:
Gene: AKR1B10
Finding: A low-intratumor-heterogeneity-derived prognostic signature (LITHrisk: PD-L1, CDK11B, CXCL13, RPS4Y1, AKR1B10, CRLF1) predicted immunotherapy prognosis and response across cancers, with AKR1B10 suppressing anti-tumor immunity via SPP1 regulation and CRLF1 promoting a fibroblast-enriched microenvironment.
Disease: Non-small cell lung cancer (immunotherapy response)

title: Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction in bone formation and fracture repair.
authors: Wu R, Zhuang Y, Yang H, Dong Q, Wang S, Zhang J, Chen Y.
ai_summary: This review describes how the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 converts mechanical forces into biological signals that drive skeletal development and fracture repair, acting mainly through endochondral ossification. Piezo1 regulates chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transdifferentiation, osteogenic fate determination in skeletal stem/progenitor cells, and activation of mature osteoblasts; genetic models show that Piezo1 deficiency in these lineages causes severe skeletal defects and fragility. Piezo1 is also required for fracture healing, coordinating periosteal stem cells, chondrocyte fate, and macrophage regulation in the repair callus. The authors highlight emerging Piezo1-targeted therapies, including low-intensity pulsed ultrasound and biomaterial-based or pharmacological approaches, as potential treatments for bone disorders and to improve fracture repair.

title: From Host-Microbiome Symbiosis to Clinical Translation: A Gut Microbiome Perspective on Radiation Enteritis.
authors: Zhuang J, Zhong Y, Lin Z, Lu Y, Wang H, Chen L, Yang K, Tan D, Qiu Y, Zhang Y, Wang H, Ge Z.
ai_summary: This review reframes radiation enteritis (RE) through a host-microbiome lens, summarizing how radiotherapy reshapes gut microbial composition and metabolism and how microbial metabolites—short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and tryptophan derivatives—contribute to barrier repair, immune homeostasis, and stem-cell regeneration. It discusses microbiome heterogeneity across disease phases, tumor types, and host factors, and microbiota-mediated gut-brain, gut-cardiopulmonary, gut-skin, and gut-bone-marrow axes in systemic radiation injury. The authors outline microbiome-based approaches to individualized risk stratification and early prediction, and assess probiotics/synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, dietary and lifestyle interventions, drugs and natural products, and engineered microbes with novel delivery systems, concluding that the gut microbiome is a promising target for preventing and treating RE and systemic radiation toxicity.

title: Nanomedicine for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: From Pathophysiological Mechanisms and Disease Heterogeneity to Precision Therapy.
authors: Li W, Guo W, Wang H, Yu J.
ai_summary: This review discusses how the heterogeneity of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) — with distinct clinical and biological subphenotypes differing in inflammation, molecular signatures, and treatment response — complicates therapy, since existing pharmacological options are limited by poor lung drug accumulation and systemic side effects. It examines how nanomedicine, through tunable physicochemical properties, surface functionalization, and microenvironment-responsive designs, can improve drug stability, pulmonary targeting, and controlled release, and can exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, barrier-protective, anticoagulant, and antifibrotic effects via passive/active targeting, biomimetic delivery, and stimuli-responsive mechanisms. The authors also highlight challenges in biosafety, large-scale manufacturing, regulatory approval, and clinical translation, framing a rationale for precision nanomedicine development in ARDS.

title: Optimization Strategies and Synergistic Applications of Engineered Salmonella Typhimurium in Cancer Therapy: From Synthetic Biology to Nanobiotechnology.
authors: Sheng Z, Bai J, Huang M.
ai_summary: This review examines engineered Salmonella Typhimurium as a tumor-targeting therapeutic, covering its intrinsic anti-tumor mechanisms (direct tumor cell killing and immune activation), genetic modification strategies, and four nanobiotechnology-based surface-engineering approaches—chemical conjugation, biomineralization, physical adsorption, and biomimetic/polymeric coating. Bacteria-nanomaterial hybrid systems synergize with genetic editing to improve tumor targeting and therapeutic potential under controllable biosafety conditions. The authors also review combination regimens pairing the bacterium with chemoradiotherapy, immunotherapy, and emerging nanotechnology-mediated therapies, which overcome monotherapy limitations through multi-mechanism complementarity. They identify translational bottlenecks including interspecies model gaps, administration limitations, and industrial production obstacles, and propose future directions for precision bacterial cancer therapeutics.

title: Interactions of LINE-1 ORF1p with proteins and chromatin suggest a role in neuronal physiology.
authors: Sinnassamy S, Massiani Beaudoin O, Lombard B, Loew D, Bonnifet T, Fradet M, Monnet H, Caille T, Servant N, Joshi RL, Fuchs J.
ai_summary:
Gene: ORF1p (LINE-1)
Finding: In differentiated mouse and human neurons, ORF1p interacts with proteins involved in gene regulation and neuron-specific processes, binds chromatin in nuclei and localizes to neurites; its loss alters chromatin accessibility, down-regulates long neuron-specific genes, and changes neurite morphology.
Disease: Neuronal physiology (post-mitotic neuron function)

title: Biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration: Niche reprogramming, precision therapeutics, and structural reconstruction.
authors: Jiang Y, Li H, Wang W, Guo Q, Wang C, Li Y, Lu H, Chen J, Yang H, Zhao X, Zheng L, Qiao Y.
ai_summary: This review argues that intervertebral disc degeneration is driven by multiple coupled pathological processes (redox imbalance, inflammation, senescence, nutrient limitation, matrix loss, mechanical failure), yet most biomaterial studies still target only one mechanism or one disc compartment in isolation. The authors organize current strategies into three interdependent layers: niche reprogramming (redox control, immunomodulation, metabolic rescue, and delivery of extracellular vesicles, cells, genes, or biologics); precision therapeutics (endotype- and stage-matched platform selection, image-guided delivery, response monitoring); and structural reconstruction of the nucleus pulposus, annulus fibrosus, and cartilaginous endplate using compartment-specific hydrogels, fibrous scaffolds, and whole-disc constructs. They critically compare evidence strength, material parameters, animal models, manufacturability, biosafety, regulatory pathways, and clinical applicability, and propose a dual-axis decision framework linking disease endotype and degeneration stage to treatment choice. Their central conclusion is that durable disc regeneration will require coordinated control of the pathological niche, patient selection, and compartment-specific mechanics rather than any single universal material.

title: Mitochondrial-Targeted Phytochemicals in Reproductive Aging: Mechanisms and Translational Potential.
authors: Halim B, Lubis HP, Syahputra RA.
ai_summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction—impaired ATP production, excessive reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial DNA damage, and disrupted homeostasis—is a central driver of reproductive aging in both sexes, contributing to reduced oocyte competence, sperm motility, and embryonic development. Several mitochondrial-targeted phytochemicals (resveratrol, quercetin, epigallocatechin gallate, astaxanthin, lycopene, berberine, and coenzyme Q10) showed protective effects via SIRT1-PGC-1α, AMPK, Nrf2, and PINK1-Parkin pathways, suggesting a promising but not yet clinically validated strategy for preserving fertility and extending reproductive lifespan.

title: Piezo1 as a Key Mechanosensitive Ion Channel Linking Mechanical Overload to Mitochondrial Dysfunction, Mitophagy, and Immunometabolic Dysregulation in Osteoarthritis.
authors: Toumi H, Almhdie-Imjabbar A, Lespessailles E.
ai_summary:
Gene: PIEZO1
Finding: Persistent Piezo1 activation under pathological mechanical loading drives mitochondrial calcium overload, ROS production, ATP depletion, and impaired mitophagy, which in turn trigger cGAS-STING and NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated immunometabolic reprogramming and pro-inflammatory cytokine release, creating a self-perpetuating cycle of cartilage destruction.
Disease: Osteoarthritis

title: Assessment of methylene blue and NAD on LPS-induced acute brain injury: effects on neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-brain barrier integrity in a rat endotoxemia model.
authors: Doganay S, Üstündağ H, Erbaş E, Yanar S, Hayme S, Kurt N.
ai_summary: This study tested methylene blue (MET) and NAD, alone and combined, in a rat LPS-induced sepsis model of brain injury. Both agents individually reduced neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neuronal damage, with MET and NAD each significantly lowering IL-6 and IL-8; the combination produced the greatest improvements in antioxidant capacity (elevated SOD), clinical and histopathological outcomes, and reduced myeloperoxidase activity, and preserved BDNF levels comparable to controls. LPS disrupted the blood-brain barrier (reduced occludin, increased aquaporin-4 and GFAP reactivity), and the treatments showed incremental benefits on these outcomes, suggesting therapeutic potential for sepsis-associated encephalopathy.

title: A dependency map enhanced with next-generation 3D cancer models.
authors: Neiswender JV, Maffa S, Brenan L, ElHarouni D, Yun Y, Boyle I, Wienand K, Inam H, Bertea T, Anderson A, Wong M, Enriquez M, Lenz E, Villafranca B, Shanks N, Hager M, Lloyd N, Shadmany H, Wie SJ, Liang H, Yunghans K, Zhang X, Golden L, Harris H, Day S, Montgomery P, Stokes S, Giglio RM, Hajal C, Whittle JR, Garcia G, Mills CE, Touat M, Pelton K, Li H, Prabhakar PS, Herter S, Kamrat ZH, Gui D, Dilly J, Wong CK, Guo JA, Pal S, Baidi Y, Johnston R, Brown DD, Bhatia S, Winter PS, Raghavan S, Beroukhim R, Colas E, Spector DL, Bass AJ, Sorger PK, Chen Y, Hill SJ, Oesterreich S, Lee AV, Beltran H, Boehm JS, Tseng YY, Root DE, Hahn WC, Aguirre AJ, Campbell CD, Ligon KL, Dempster JM, Shibue T, Vazquez F.
ai_summary: This study expands the Cancer Dependency Map by performing 147 genome-scale CRISPR screens alongside multi-omic characterization of next-generation cancer models (organoids and spheroids) spanning 10 cancer types. Compared with traditional cell lines, these models capture additional genomic and molecular subtypes, preserve transcriptional programs that are silenced in conventional culture, and reveal new biomarker-associated gene dependencies. The authors also show that growth format and culture medium independently influence gene essentiality, and they integrate the new data with existing DepMap resources into a publicly accessible portal.

title: Oxidative stress and inflammation in neurodegenerative disorders.
authors: Jomova K, Alomar SY, Valko R, Nepovimova E, Kuca K, Valko M.
ai_summary: This review examines how oxidative stress and inflammation drive neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, detailing disease-specific mechanisms such as Aβ-metal interactions and tau aggregates in Alzheimer's, iron accumulation and complex I dysfunction in Parkinson's, huntingtin polyglutamine expansion in Huntington's, and SOD1 mutations in ALS. Although low-molecular-weight antioxidants show promise in preclinical and animal studies, clinical translation is limited by poor bioavailability and blood-brain barrier penetration. The authors highlight emerging strategies including nanoparticle-based delivery, mitochondrial-targeted agents, Nrf2 pathway activation, polyphenol supplementation (quercetin, resveratrol, curcumin), and autophagy-modulating compounds, while noting that epidemiological links between vitamins C/E intake and reduced Parkinson's risk have not yet translated into effective human therapies.

title: Phosphoinositides and inositol phosphates-functions and cellular dynamics.
authors: Rao F, Haucke V.

title: Phosphoinositides in membrane remodeling during infections and cellular stresses.
authors: Alemany C, Morel E.
ai_summary: This review discusses how phosphoinositides—phosphorylated phosphatidylinositols best known for defining endomembrane identity—also act as signaling hubs that integrate diverse cellular stress cues, including nutrient deprivation, mechanical strain, osmotic imbalance, and DNA damage. It highlights conserved adaptation programs such as vacuolar remodeling, endosomal trafficking, and autophagosome biogenesis, which are controlled by a network of phosphoinositide kinases, phosphatases, and regulatory partners. The authors emphasize compartment-specific regulation, enzymatic diversity, and organelle crosstalk, and propose phosphoinositide signaling as a potential therapeutic target in diseases characterized by defective stress resolution.

title: The instructive scar - the dynamic role of extracellular matrix in biliary pathophysiology.
authors: Waddell SH, Brennan E, Boulter L.
ai_summary: This review discusses how the extracellular matrix (ECM) actively shapes biliary pathophysiology rather than serving as a passive scar. Cholangiopathies—congenital and acquired diseases of the intrahepatic bile ducts—progress with inflammation and fibrosis, and the fibrotic tissue surrounding diseased ducts shows aberrant changes in ECM molecular composition that vary between different cholangiopathies and reflect contributions from different cell types. The authors highlight that while the ECM's broad composition is fairly well characterized, it remains poorly understood how it transmits biochemical and biomechanical signals to cholangiocytes and how these interactions guide ductular cells to coordinate tissue-level regeneration and drive the molecular pathology of these diseases. The review explores these mechanisms and discusses current and future therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting ECM-related processes in the clinic.

title: A novel homozygous variant causing fatal neonatal adenylosuccinate lyase (ADSL) deficiency presenting with respiratory failure and encephalopathy.
authors: Wolfe K, Armstrong L, Wambach C, Leon E, Ohrtman K, Miller I, Pyle T, Schroeder J, Fraser J, Kousa Y.
ai_summary:
Gene: ADSL
Finding: A novel homozygous loss-of-function variant in ADSL was identified in a term neonate with respiratory failure and encephalopathy, with neuroimaging showing microencephaly, a simplified gyral pattern, and diffuse white matter edema, consistent with the rare fatal neonatal phenotype.
Disease: Fatal neonatal adenylosuccinate lyase (ADSL) deficiency

title: A microprotein atlas of the human frontal cortex in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Miller B, Vieira de Souza E, Lau C, Vaughan JM, Pai VJ, Giraldez S, Rocha A, Diedrich JK, O'Shea CC, Bennett DA, Saghatelian A.
ai_summary:
Gene: MKKS
Finding: A small ORF within MKKS encodes a 63-amino-acid microprotein that is the locus's predominant translation product and is downregulated in Alzheimer's disease; its loss impairs microglial mitochondrial respiration.
Disease: Alzheimer's disease

title: Sperm subpopulations differing in mitochondrial abundance show divergent nuclear allele frequencies.
authors: Weide T, Koltes J, Steibel J, Kerns K.
ai_summary: Sperm from a single boar were sorted by mitochondrial abundance (MitoTracker Green fluorescence) into low- and high-mitochondrial subpopulations, with microscopy confirming that high-fluorescence sperm had longer mitochondrial sheaths. Whole-genome sequencing of paired subpopulations from three boars revealed allele-frequency differences at 182 candidate SNPs (≥30 reads in both fractions) relative to heterozygous baseline populations, indicating non-random segregation of nuclear alleles within ejaculates. The authors propose sperm mitochondrial abundance as a potential high-throughput marker of nuclear genomic heterogeneity within sires.

title: Retinoic acid in health and disease.
authors: De Angelis MT, Dattilo V, Vono N, Lise V, Reda M, De Marco C, Rizzuto A, Trapasso F, Viglietto G, Santamaria G.
ai_summary: Retinoic acid (RA), the active vitamin A metabolite, regulates embryonic patterning, epithelial integrity, stem-cell behavior, immune homeostasis, and metabolism, and disruption of its synthesis, degradation, receptor signaling, or pathway crosstalk contributes to a wide range of diseases including congenital malformations, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular, pulmonary and ophthalmic disease, and cancer. In tumors, RA signaling is highly context-dependent, acting either as a differentiation inducer or a stemness-maintaining factor according to genetic, metabolic, and microenvironmental cues. Retinoid therapy has transformed acute promyelocytic leukemia treatment, but broader use is limited by resistance, pharmacokinetics, tissue-specific effects, and the pathway's dual nature. Emerging organoid, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and epigenomic approaches reveal highly localized, cell-type-specific retinoid responses, supporting a systems-level framework of "retinoid endotypes" — tissue- and stage-specific states defined by metabolic niches, chromatin state, and microenvironment — that could guide patient stratification and precision retinoid therapy.

title: Crosstalk between innate immune signaling pathways and integrated TLR, NLRP3 inflammasome, cGAS-STING, and NF-κB networks in sepsis.
authors: Du X, Qiao H.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
ai_summary: This review synthesizes evidence that sepsis pathogenesis arises not from any single innate immune pathway but from extensive crosstalk among TLR, NLRP3 inflammasome, cGAS-STING, and NF-κB signaling networks, which together govern pathogen recognition, cytokine production, inflammasome activation, type I interferon signaling, pyroptosis, and immune cell reprogramming. It highlights shared adaptor proteins, feedback loops, and signaling hubs that drive the transition from protective host defense to hyperinflammation and subsequent immunosuppression, and discusses how mitochondrial dysfunction, ROS, DAMPs, epigenetic modifications, and non-coding RNAs modulate these circuits and contribute to organ-specific injury. The authors also review systems-level approaches (single-cell transcriptomics, spatial multi-omics) for identifying biomarkers and therapeutic targets, and summarize emerging strategies including inhibitors of TLRs, NLRP3, STING, and NF-κB, as well as combination and precision medicine approaches.

title: BRD2 bridges TFIID and MOF-H4K16ac-containing nucleosomes to promote transcriptional initiation.
authors: Zheng B, Qiu R, Gold S, Iwanaszko M, Aoi Y, Howard BC, Das M, Shilatifard A.
ai_summary:
Gene: BRD2
Finding: BRD2 promotes transcriptional initiation in a bromodomain-dependent manner at promoters and enhancers; its bromodomains preferentially bind histone H4 with MOF-mediated H4K16ac while its C-terminal domain recruits TFIID, distinguishing it from BRD4's bromodomain-independent role in elongation.
Disease: Gene expression regulation (transcriptional initiation control)

title: Progress and challenges in CRISPR/Cas applications in microalgae.
authors: Tran QG, Le TT, Choi DY, Cho DH, Yun JH, Choi HI, Kim HS, Lee YJ.
ai_summary: This review summarizes recent progress in applying CRISPR/Cas genome-editing systems to microalgae, a field that has historically been hampered by low transformation efficiency, limited target selection, and interspecies genetic variation that restricts the transfer of genetic tools between species. It highlights successful uses of class 2 Cas proteins such as Cas9 and Cas12a, along with emerging CRISPR-based strategies designed to overcome microalgal cellular barriers, with the overall goal of improving editing precision and efficiency. The authors also outline future perspectives for CRISPR/Cas strategies in microalgal biotechnology.

title: P-STAT3-dependent SPP1 transcription in cholangiocytes drives hepatic stellate cells activation in congenital hepatic fibrosis.
authors: Jiao M, Sun Y, Liu R, Yin X, Hou X, Yuan H, Dai Z, Chen Q, Zhu C.
ai_summary:
Gene: PKHD1
Finding: PKHD1 deficiency in cholangiocytes upregulates SPP1/osteopontin via p-STAT3-dependent transcription, and secreted OPN activates PI3K/Akt signaling in hepatic stellate cells to promote their activation and fibrosis; cholangiocyte-specific Spp1 knockdown attenuates hepatic fibrosis in vivo.
Disease: Congenital hepatic fibrosis
